questions.rankerTip: Dashed lines (medium thickness) = hidden edges. Thin continuous = dimension/projection lines. Thin chain = center lines.

questions.question: The ratio of isometric length to its true length is nearly:
questions.explanation: Isometric Length / True Length = √(2/3) = cos 45° / cos 30° ≈ 0.8165 (or 81.65%).
questions.rankerTip: Isometric length = 0.816 × True length (or √(2/3) × True length).

questions.question: Scale representing three different units such as metre, decimetre and centimetre is:
questions.explanation: A diagonal scale can read up to three successive units (e.g., yards, feet, and inches, or metres, decimetres, and centimetres) or up to two decimal places.
questions.rankerTip: Plain scale = 2 units. Diagonal scale = 3 units. Vernier scale = fractional parts of smallest division.

questions.question: The size of the letter is described by its:
questions.explanation: According to BIS IS 9609, standard lettering size (h) is always designated by the nominal height of capital letters in millimetres (2.5, 3.5, 5, 7, 10, 14, 20 mm).
questions.rankerTip: Nominal height (h) of capital letters defines the lettering size as per IS 9609.

questions.question: The scale on which three dimensions can be measured is known as:
questions.explanation: Measuring three dimensions or up to two decimal places is done using a diagonal scale based on the principle of similar triangles.
questions.rankerTip: Diagonal scale measures 3 dimensions/units based on similar triangles.

questions.question: The drawing sheet is so folded that the ------- is always on the top:
questions.explanation: Standard folding rules (IS 10711) mandate that the title block (at the bottom-right corner of the sheet) must remain completely visible on the top front fold for quick identification in filing.
questions.rankerTip: Title block must always appear on the top fold of folded drawings (IS 10711).

questions.question: Outline or principal lines are drawn as:
questions.explanation: Visible outlines, edges, and principal boundaries are designated as Type A lines (Continuous thick lines, approximately 0.5 mm to 0.7 mm).
questions.rankerTip: Type A line = Continuous thick = Visible outlines and principal edges.

questions.question: Which of the following is a symbol of the first angle projection?
options: Truncated cone with smaller base on left, followed by concentric circles on right
Concentric circles on left, followed by truncated cone on right
questions.explanation: In 1st angle projection, the right-side view is projected onto the left plane or viewed from the left and projected to the right. The standard ISO/BIS symbol shows the frustum on the left and the circular views on the right.
questions.rankerTip: 1st Angle symbol: frustum on left, concentric circles on right. 3rd Angle symbol: concentric circles on left, frustum on right.

questions.question: Line AB 30° inclined to HP and parallel to VP. If the line is at first quadrant which one of the following statement is correct?
options: Elevation will be of actual length 30° inclined and below XY line
Elevation will be shorter than actual length and above XY line
Elevation will be shorter than actual length 30° inclined and below XY line
Elevation will be of actual length 30° inclined and above XY line
questions.explanation: In the 1st quadrant, elevation (front view) appears above the XY line. Because the line is parallel to VP, its projection on VP shows its true/actual length and true inclination of 30° to HP.
questions.rankerTip: Line parallel to VP: front view (elevation) shows true length and true inclination θ to HP, situated above XY in 1st quadrant.

questions.question: The outer line of an objects are drawn using ------- Pencil.
questions.explanation: An H pencil is standard for visible outlines, border finishing, and dimensioning arrowheads in professional drafting.
questions.rankerTip: Outlines & border lines = H pencil; Construction lines = 2H/3H; Freehand sketching/lettering = HB/H.

questions.question: Which one of the following statement is not correct in the case of aligned system?
options: Dimension value placed perpendicular to the dimension line
Dimension can be read only from the bottom edge of the drawing sheet
Dimension can be read from the bottom edge or right hand edge of the drawing sheet
Dimension should be placed near the middle and above but clear of the dimension line
questions.explanation: In an aligned system, dimensions are aligned parallel to the dimension lines and read from the bottom or the right-hand edge. Reading only from the bottom edge describes the unidirectional system, not the aligned system.
questions.rankerTip: Aligned system allows reading from bottom and right-hand edge. Unidirectional allows reading only from bottom.

questions.question: The first dimension line should be placed at least:
questions.explanation: Drafting standards recommend placing the first dimension line at least 10 mm away from the outline of the object, with parallel dimension lines spaced at least 6 to 8 mm apart.
questions.rankerTip: First dimension line: minimum 10 mm from outline. Successive parallel dimension lines: minimum 6 to 8 mm apart.

questions.question: A line CD 141.4 mm long inclined 45° to vertical plane and parallel to horizontal plane. The front view of line CD measures ...... mm:
questions.rankerTip: Front view of line inclined to VP by ϕ: Length = L cos ϕ = 141.4 × cos 45° = 100 mm.

questions.question: If a line is inclined at 45° to the HP and 30° to the VP, its front view is inclined at:
questions.explanation: The apparent angle of elevation α satisfies tan α = tan θ / cos ϕ. With θ = 45° and ϕ = 30°: tan α = tan 45° / cos 30° = 1 / 0.8660 ≈ 1.1547 > 1, so α > 45° (specifically α ≈ 49.1°).
questions.rankerTip: Apparent inclination α is always GREATER than true inclination θ to HP (tan α = tan θ / cos ϕ).

questions.question: Which one of the following scales is the smallest?
questions.explanation: Comparing Representative Fractions: (a) 1 mm / 1 m = 1/1000; (b) RF = 1/2000; (c) RF = 1/20000; (d) 1 cm / 1 km = 1 / 100,000. 1/100,000 is the smallest fraction, so (d) is the smallest scale.
questions.rankerTip: 1 cm = 1 km means RF = 1 / 100,000, which has the largest denominator and is thus the smallest scale.

questions.question: The T-Square with the working edge length of 1000 ± 10 mm, is designated as:
questions.explanation: Standard T-square sizes according to BIS (IS 1364): T0: 1500 mm; T1: 1000 mm; T2: 700 mm; T3: 500 mm.
questions.rankerTip: T-Square designations: T0 (1500 mm), T1 (1000 mm), T2 (700 mm), T3 (500 mm).

questions.question: An ellipse has ------- vertices and ------- foci.
questions.explanation: An ellipse has two principal vertices (the endpoints of the major axis) and two foci (F1 and F2).
questions.rankerTip: Ellipse has 2 vertices and 2 foci. Parabola has 1 vertex and 1 focus. Hyperbola has 2 vertices and 2 foci.

questions.question: 10 centimetre is:
questions.explanation: In metric measurement: 10 mm = 1 cm; 10 cm = 1 decimetre (dm); 10 dm = 1 metre (m).
questions.rankerTip: 10 mm = 1 cm; 10 cm = 1 decimetre (dm); 100 cm = 1 metre.

questions.question: "Asymptote" is:
options: Tangents drawn from infinity to a circle
Tangents drawn from infinity to a hyperbola
questions.explanation: An asymptote is a straight line that a curve approaches arbitrarily closely as it heads toward infinity; for a hyperbola, asymptotes are tangents to the curve at infinity passing through the center.
questions.rankerTip: Asymptotes are tangents to the hyperbola at infinity, intersecting at the center of the hyperbola.

questions.question: Where the plan is placed in third angle projection?
questions.explanation: In 3rd angle projection, the projection planes are assumed transparent: Top View (Plan) is placed above the Front View (Elevation). In 1st angle projection, the Plan is placed below the Elevation.
questions.rankerTip: 3rd Angle: Plan is ABOVE elevation. 1st Angle: Plan is BELOW elevation.

questions.question: For thin chain line alternate long and short dashes are in proportion ranging from:
questions.explanation: In long-dashed dotted / thin chain lines (used for center lines and axes), long dashes are typically 9 to 12 mm and short dashes/dots are 1.5 to 2 mm, giving a proportion ranging from 6:1 to 4:1.
questions.rankerTip: Chain line proportion of long to short dash is between 6:1 and 4:1.

questions.question: The type of Vernier in which the Vernier divisions are marked in the opposite direction of the main scale is:
questions.explanation: In a backward (retrograde) vernier, divisions are numbered in the direction opposite to the main scale, and n vernier divisions equal (n+1) main scale divisions (V > S).
questions.rankerTip: Direct/Forward vernier: same direction, n V = (n - 1) S (V < S). Retrograde/Backward vernier: opposite direction, n V = (n + 1) S (V > S).

questions.question: To represent two units of measurement ....... scale is used.
questions.explanation: A plain (plane) scale is used to indicate two consecutive units of measurement (e.g., metres and decimetres, or kilometres and hectometres).
questions.rankerTip: Plain scale represents 2 units (or a unit and its fractional subdivision).

questions.question: When the section plane is inclined to the axis of the cone and cuts all the generators, the section obtained is:
questions.explanation: When a cutting plane cuts all generators of a right circular cone at an angle greater than the semi-vertical angle α, the true shape of the section is an ellipse.
questions.rankerTip: Section plane cuts ALL generators of a cone = Ellipse.

questions.question: If a line is parallel to any one of the reference planes and inclined to the other then:
options: Its projection on that plane to which it is parallel will show the true length
Its projection on that plane to which it is parallel will show the true inclination
questions.explanation: If a line is parallel to a plane of projection, its projection on that plane will faithfully show both its true length and its true inclination to the other reference plane.
questions.rankerTip: Line parallel to a plane shows BOTH true length AND true inclination on that plane.
questions.topic: Projections - Lines Parallel to One Plane

questions.question: Which is/are not the central conic/s?
questions.explanation: Both ellipses and hyperbolas possess a center of symmetry through which all chords are bisected, making them central conics. A parabola does not have a center of symmetry and is non-central.
questions.rankerTip: Central conics = Ellipse and Hyperbola. Non-central conic = Parabola.

questions.question: The recommended method of Dimensioning of a sphere with diameter 50 mm is:
questions.explanation: According to BIS (IS 10714) and ISO drafting rules, spherical features are dimensioned by prefixing the symbol S before the diameter symbol ϕ, formatted as Sϕ50 (or SR25 for spherical radius).
questions.rankerTip: Sphere dimensioning: Sϕ followed by diameter value (e.g. Sϕ50) or SR followed by radius (SR25).

questions.question: The continuous thin line connecting a dimensional value or some information relating to a feature in an engineering drawing is:
questions.explanation: A leader line is a continuous thin line with an arrowhead or dot pointing to a feature and an inclined/horizontal portion terminating at a note, dimension, or reference symbol.
questions.rankerTip: Leader line connects an explanatory note, symbol, or dimension value to the feature on the drawing.

questions.question: The method of projection in which the projectors are parallel to each other and perpendicular to the plane of projection is:
questions.explanation: Orthographic projection (ortho = perpendicular, graphic = drawing) projects parallel rays from an object normal (90°) to the projection plane.
questions.rankerTip: Orthographic: projectors parallel to each other and perpendicular (90°) to projection plane.

questions.question: The continuous thin ruled lines with short zig-zags within them are drawn to show:
questions.explanation: According to IS 10714 (Type D line), a continuous thin straight line with short zig-zags is designated to represent long break lines or limits of partial/interrupted views. Continuous wavy freehand lines (Type C) are used for short break lines.
questions.rankerTip: Continuous thin with zig-zag (Type D) = Long break lines; Continuous thin wavy (Type C) = Short break lines.

mockTests.title: Building Materials & Construction 50 MCQ High-Yield Master Practice Exam
mockTests.description: Comprehensive 50-question Kerala PSC examination covering Building Materials & Construction: Cement (Vicat apparatus, soundness, setting time, specific gravity, bag weight, supersulphated IS 6909), Stones & Rocks (Calcareous, Igneous, Basalt, Attrition, Streak, Texture), Bricks & Tiles (Perforated, Refractory fire-bricks, 4th class aggregate, Tempering pug mill, Alumina, Stock board frog kick, Bloating, Sialkot kiln, Guna tiles), Timber (Pith, Medullary rays, Rosewood weight, Knots, Wet rot, Diagonal grain, Foxiness, Deciduous, IS 883 Group B elasticity, Shakes, Bow & Cup), Mortar (Class A lime, Surkhi binder), and Metals & Paints (Linseed oil vehicle, Turpentine solvent, Red lead primer, Wrought iron puddling, Annealing, Tempering). Evaluated under official PSC pattern with -0.33 negative marking.
mockTests.targetDepartment: Survey & Land Records / Kerala Water Authority / PWD

questions.question: Vicat's apparatus is used to determine the:
questions.explanation: Vicat's apparatus is a standard testing instrument used for multiple cement tests: a 10 mm diameter plunger is used for the standard/normal consistency test (P), a 1 mm square needle for the initial setting time test, and an annular collar needle for the final setting time test.
questions.rankerTip: Vicat plunger (10 mm) = Consistency (P); 1 mm square needle = Initial setting; Annular needle = Final setting.

questions.question: Chemically which rock is calcareous rock?
questions.explanation: Calcareous rocks have calcium carbonate (CaCO3) or lime as their predominant constituent. Marble and limestone are classic calcareous rocks. Granite and basalt are igneous/siliceous rocks.
questions.rankerTip: Calcareous = Lime/CaCO3 (Limestone, Marble, Kankar); Siliceous = Silica (Granite, Basalt, Quartzite); Argillaceous = Clay/Alumina (Slate, Laterite).

questions.question: Weight of 1 bag of cement:
questions.explanation: In standard civil engineering practice across India, a commercial bag of cement weighs exactly 50 kg, with a nominal volume of approximately 34.7 to 35 litres (0.0347 m³). Standard density of cement is 1440 kg/m³.
questions.rankerTip: 1 bag = 50 kg = 34.7 liters (0.0347 m³). Density = 1440 kg/m³. 20 bags = 1 Tonne (1000 kg).

questions.question: The central part of the tree is called:
questions.explanation: The innermost core or central longitudinal axis of an exogenous tree stem is called the Pith (or Medulla). It consists of cellular tissue that nourishes the tree in its sapling stage.
questions.rankerTip: Order from center outward: Pith -> Heartwood -> Sapwood -> Cambium Layer -> Inner Bark -> Outer Bark.

questions.question: The most common material used as vehicle of a paint is:
questions.explanation: Linseed oil (raw, boiled, or double-boiled) is the standard and most widely used vehicle (drying oil) in oil paints, serving to hold pigment particles in suspension and forming a durable, protective film upon drying.
questions.rankerTip: Vehicle (binder/carrier) = Linseed oil, Poppy oil, Tung oil. Most common = Linseed oil. Thinner/Solvent = Turpentine.

questions.question: The part of tree, which hold together the annual rings of Hardwood and Sap wood is:
questions.explanation: Medullary rays are cellular radial structures that extend perpendicularly from the pith towards the bark, holding the annular rings together and providing radial strength.
questions.rankerTip: Medullary rays extend radially outward from pith to bark, locking annual rings together.

questions.question: The heating of limestone to redness in contact with air is known as:
questions.explanation: Calcination is the process of heating limestone (CaCO3) to red heat (approx. 800–900°C) in the presence of air to drive off carbon dioxide, producing quicklime (CaO).
questions.rankerTip: CaCO3 + Heat -> CaO + CO2 is Calcination. CaO + H2O -> Ca(OH)2 + Heat is Slaking.

questions.question: The compressive strength of fire-bricks varies from:
questions.explanation: Fire-clay/refractory bricks possess very high compressive resistance, conventionally cited in competitive exams as 200 to 220 N/mm² (derived from 200–220 kg/cm² or 2000-2200 N/cm² standards).
questions.rankerTip: Fire bricks: compressive strength = 200 to 220 N/mm². Used for lining blast furnaces and kilns.

questions.question: The Kiln used for the manufacture of tile is:
questions.explanation: A Sialkot kiln is a specialized intermittent kiln commonly used for burning clay roofing and flooring tiles.
questions.rankerTip: Sialkot kiln is specifically employed for tile manufacture; Rotary kiln is used for Portland cement clinker.

questions.question: The increase in volume of dry sand when water is added is called:
questions.explanation: Bulking of sand is the increase in bulk volume caused by surface tension films formed around sand particles when water is added (peaking typically between 4% and 6% moisture content).
questions.rankerTip: Bulking peaks at 4% to 6% moisture content. Fine sand bulks more than coarse sand. Completely submerged sand has zero bulking.

questions.question: Brick containing cylindrical holes throughout their thickness:
questions.explanation: Perforated bricks contain cylindrical holes penetrating completely through their thickness (usually covering 30% to 45% of the gross face area), offering lightweight properties and enhanced thermal insulation.
questions.rankerTip: Perforated bricks have holes throughout thickness (30-45% cross-section). Hollow bricks have larger cavities.

questions.question: The weight of Rose wood after seasoning is:
questions.explanation: Indian Rosewood is a heavy and dense hardwood with a seasoned unit weight of approximately 7.9 to 8.5 kN/m³ (7900 N/m³).
questions.rankerTip: Rosewood unit weight after seasoning ≈ 7900 N/m³ (7.9 kN/m³). Teak is ≈ 6500 N/m³, Sal is ≈ 8500-9000 N/m³.

questions.question: The size of pin knot is:
questions.explanation: According to IS standards: Pin knot: Diameter ≤ 6.50 mm; Small knot: Diameter > 6.50 mm and ≤ 20 mm; Medium knot: Diameter > 20 mm and ≤ 40 mm; Large knot: Diameter > 40 mm.
questions.rankerTip: Pin knot ≤ 6.5 mm; Small knot 6.5 - 20 mm; Medium knot 20 - 40 mm; Large knot > 40 mm.

questions.question: The alternate dry and wet conditions causes the development of ... in timber:
questions.explanation: Wet rot is caused by fungi attacking timber subjected to alternate wet and dry environments. Dry rot occurs in warm, damp, and unventilated conditions.
questions.rankerTip: Alternate wet and dry conditions cause Wet Rot. Lack of ventilation with dampness causes Dry Rot.

questions.question: Which of the following tiles are conical in shape?
questions.explanation: Guna tiles are hollow conical/tapered cylindrical burnt clay tiles used in building vaulted roofs and domes.
questions.rankerTip: Guna tiles = conical/tapered hollow tiles used for curved roofs and vault construction.

questions.question: The minimum compressive strength of lime mortar 1:3 with Class A lime at the end of 14 days is:
questions.explanation: As per IS 712, Class A (eminently hydraulic) lime mortar (1:3 mix) must attain a minimum compressive strength of 1.75 N/mm² at 14 days and 2.8 N/mm² at 28 days.
questions.rankerTip: Class A hydraulic lime mortar (1:3): 14-day strength = 1.75 N/mm²; 28-day strength = 2.80 N/mm².

questions.question: Which of the following bricks are used as aggregate for concrete in foundation, floors etc.?
questions.explanation: Fourth-class bricks (Jhama / overburnt bricks) are distorted and brittle for regular masonry, but their vitrified hardness makes them ideal when crushed for use as coarse aggregate in foundation and floor concrete.
questions.rankerTip: Fourth-class / Jhama bricks = overburnt, brittle, used as crushed aggregate for concrete in foundations and road metalling.

questions.question: In which process in the manufacturing of brick the clay is brought to a proper degree of hardness?
questions.explanation: Tempering (kneading, often done in a pug mill) is the operation where clay is thoroughly mixed with water to give it the proper degree of plasticity and uniform hardness needed for moulding.
questions.rankerTip: Preparation of brick earth: Unsoiling -> Digging -> Cleaning -> Weathering -> Blending -> Tempering (in Pug Mill).

questions.question: Which test is used to determine the rate of wear of stones?
questions.explanation: The attrition test (using Deval's attrition machine) measures the percentage wear of stones caused by mutual friction and rubbing.
questions.rankerTip: Attrition test = wear & mutual rubbing; Impact test = toughness; Crushing test = compressive strength; Smith's test = presence of soluble/clayey matter.

questions.question: Which of the following is an igneous rock?
questions.explanation: Basalt is an extrusive (volcanic) igneous rock formed by the cooling of lava on the Earth's surface. (Slate and Gneiss are metamorphic; Kankar is sedimentary).
questions.rankerTip: Igneous: Granite, Basalt, Trap, Diorite, Gabbro. Metamorphic: Marble, Slate, Gneiss, Quartzite. Sedimentary: Limestone, Sandstone, Kankar, Shale.

questions.question: Composition of alumina in brick earth:
questions.explanation: Standard brick earth contains 50–60% Silica, 20–30% Alumina, 5–6% Lime, and minor percentages of iron oxide and magnesia.
questions.rankerTip: Brick earth composition mnemonic (SALIM): Silica (50-60%), Alumina (20-30%), Lime (5%), Iron oxide (5-6%), Magnesia (<1%).

questions.question: IS: Code of Super sulphated cement:
questions.explanation: IS 6909:1990 governs the specification for Supersulphated cement, manufactured by intergrinding blast furnace slag, calcium sulphate, and small amounts of Portland cement.
questions.rankerTip: IS 6909 = Supersulphated Cement; IS 269 = 33 Grade OPC; IS 8112 = 43 Grade OPC; IS 12269 = 53 Grade OPC; IS 455 = PSC; IS 1489 = PPC.

questions.question: Soundness tests of cement is carried out to determine:
questions.explanation: Soundness testing via the Le Chatelier apparatus detects excess uncombined free lime (CaO), which causes destructive delayed expansion upon hydration.
questions.rankerTip: Le Chatelier method detects unsoundness due to free Lime only. Autoclave method detects unsoundness due to both Lime and Magnesia.

questions.question: Most commonly used solvent in oil paint is:
questions.explanation: Spirits of turpentine is the most common solvent (thinner) used in oil paints to make the paint thin, workable, and easily spreadable.
questions.rankerTip: Turpentine is the principal solvent/thinner in oil paint; Linseed oil is the vehicle/carrier.

questions.question: The property by which lime will set in damp place:
questions.explanation: Hydraulicity is the capacity of hydraulic lime to set and harden in damp places or completely submerged under water without requiring atmospheric carbon dioxide.
questions.rankerTip: Hydraulicity = ability of lime to set under water or in damp conditions (due to clay/silicates and aluminates).

questions.question: The defect is formed due to improper sawing of timber is:
questions.explanation: Diagonal grain is a manufacturing defect produced when logs are cut obliquely across the grain rather than parallel to the tree axis.
questions.rankerTip: Defects due to conversion (sawing): Diagonal grain, Torn grain, Chip mark, Wane.

questions.question: The normal consistency of Portland cement is about:
questions.explanation: Standard consistency (P) of Ordinary Portland Cement typically ranges between 25% and 30% by weight of dry cement.
questions.rankerTip: Standard consistency of OPC ≈ 25% to 30%. Initial & final setting time test uses 0.85P water; Soundness test uses 0.78P water.

questions.question: ... is manufactured in puddling process:
questions.explanation: Wrought iron (the purest commercial iron, <0.15% carbon) is manufactured from pig iron in a reverberatory puddling furnace.
questions.rankerTip: Pig iron -> Blast furnace; Cast iron -> Cupola furnace; Wrought iron -> Puddling furnace; Steel -> Bessemer / Open Hearth / Electric Arc.

questions.question: In order to soften the iron, which heat treatment method is required?
questions.explanation: Annealing involves heating the metal to a specified temperature followed by very slow furnace cooling, which relieves internal stresses, refines grain structure, and softens the iron/steel.
questions.rankerTip: Annealing softens steel and relieves internal stresses (slow cooling in furnace). Hardening increases hardness (rapid quenching).

questions.question: What is the process for increasing toughness and decreasing brittleness?
questions.explanation: Hardened steel is reheated below its lower critical transformation temperature and cooled; this reduces extreme brittleness and substantially increases toughness.
questions.rankerTip: Tempering restores ductility and toughness in hardened steel while reducing extreme brittleness.

questions.question: The rocks formed due to pouring of magma at earth's surface are:
questions.explanation: Extrusive igneous rocks formed when magma pours out onto the surface as lava and cools rapidly are called Volcanic rocks (e.g., Basalt, Pumice).
questions.rankerTip: At surface (rapid cooling) = Volcanic rocks (Basalt); At shallow depth = Hypabyssal (Dolerite); At great depth (slow cooling) = Plutonic (Granite).

questions.question: The product obtained after slaking of quick lime is:
questions.explanation: The reaction of quicklime with water (CaO + H2O → Ca(OH)2 + Heat) is slaking, yielding calcium hydroxide, commercially called slaked lime or hydrated lime.
questions.rankerTip: Quick lime (CaO) + Water -> Hydrated lime / Slaked lime [Ca(OH)2] + Heat.

questions.question: The defects in timber, which is due to over maturity or by poor ventilation during storage:
questions.explanation: Foxiness appears as red or yellow discolorations near the pith and heartwood, caused by fungal decay arising from overmaturity or unventilated storage.
questions.rankerTip: Foxiness = reddish/yellow stain caused by overmaturity or poor ventilation during storage.
questions.topic: Timber - Defects due to Fungi & Storage

questions.question: The main function of alumina in brick earth is:
questions.explanation: Alumina (Al2O3) is the essential ingredient in clay that provides plasticity, enabling the brick earth to be moulded into shape.
questions.rankerTip: Alumina imparts plasticity for moulding. Silica prevents shrinkage, cracking, and warping. Iron oxide gives red color.

questions.question: Le-Chateliers flask is used for determining the:
questions.explanation: The Le Chatelier flask (using kerosene) is used to determine the specific gravity of cement (≈ 3.15). The Le Chatelier mould / apparatus is used to determine soundness.
questions.rankerTip: Le Chatelier FLASK = Specific gravity test (using kerosene, value ≈ 3.15). Le Chatelier MOULD = Soundness test.

questions.question: Deciduous trees fall under the category of:
questions.explanation: Exogenous trees add outward annual rings each year and are classified into Conifers (needle-leaved evergreens) and Deciduous (broad-leaved hardwoods).
questions.rankerTip: Exogenous trees grow outwards by adding annual rings; they include Conifers (softwoods) and Deciduous (hardwoods like Teak, Sal).

questions.question: Based on modulus of elasticity, timber used for construction purposes are classified as Group B when:
options: Modulus of elasticity in bending above 12.5 kN/mm²
Modulus of elasticity in bending above 5.6 kN/mm² and below 9.8 kN/mm²
Modulus of elasticity in bending above 9.8 kN/mm² and below 12.5 kN/mm²
Modulus of elasticity in bending below 5.6 kN/mm²
questions.explanation: According to IS 883: Group A: E > 12.5 kN/mm² (or > 12.6 kN/mm²); Group B: 9.8 kN/mm² < E ≤ 12.5 kN/mm²; Group C: 5.6 kN/mm² < E ≤ 9.8 kN/mm².
questions.rankerTip: IS 883 classification by Modulus of Elasticity (E): Group A: E > 12.5 kN/mm²; Group B: 9.8 to 12.5 kN/mm²; Group C: 5.6 to 9.8 kN/mm².

questions.question: As per relevant Bureau of Indian Standard, the soundness of 43 grade Ordinary Portland Cement tested according to Le Chatelier apparatus shall not be more than:
questions.explanation: Per IS 8112 and IS 269, the maximum allowable expansion for OPC (grades 33, 43, 53) using the Le Chatelier method is 10 mm.
questions.rankerTip: Soundness of OPC by Le Chatelier apparatus: Maximum expansion = 10 mm. By Autoclave test: Maximum expansion = 0.8%.

questions.question: The binding material used in Surkhi mortar is:
questions.explanation: In Surkhi mortar, Surkhi (powdered burnt clay) acts as a pozzolanic fine aggregate, while lime is the binding material.
questions.rankerTip: In Surkhi mortar: Lime is the binder; Surkhi is the pozzolanic fine aggregate substitute.

questions.question: The initial setting time of ordinary Portland cement shall not be:
questions.explanation: As per IS 269 / IS 456, the initial setting time of OPC shall not be less than 30 minutes, and the final setting time shall not exceed 600 minutes (10 hours).
questions.rankerTip: OPC setting times: Initial setting time ≥ 30 minutes; Final setting time ≤ 600 minutes (10 hours).

questions.question: Excess of silica makes the bricks:
questions.explanation: While silica prevents warping and shrinkage, an excess of silica destroys the cohesion of clay particles and renders the bricks brittle and weak when burnt.
questions.rankerTip: Excess silica makes bricks brittle and weak on burning; excess alumina causes warping and shrinkage.
questions.topic: Bricks - Defects from Raw Material Excess

questions.question: Igneous rocks are formed by the action of:
questions.explanation: Igneous rocks are primary rocks formed by the thermal action of extreme volcanic heat that liquefies rock into magma, which subsequently crystallizes upon cooling.
questions.rankerTip: Igneous = Heat (cooling of molten magma/lava); Sedimentary = Weathering, deposition & compaction; Metamorphic = Heat and pressure alteration.

questions.question: Rapid hardening cement high percentage of:
questions.explanation: Rapid Hardening Cement gains high early strength due to a higher percentage of tricalcium silicate (C3S), achieved by increasing the lime content and grinding the clinker to a finer Blaine specific surface.
questions.rankerTip: Rapid Hardening Cement has a higher lime content (resulting in higher C3S) and higher fineness than normal OPC.

questions.question: ... is a crack which is partly separate the annual rings:
questions.explanation: A curved crack that partly separates adjacent annual rings is a Cup shake. When the crack completely separates the rings in a full circle, it is called a Ring shake.
questions.rankerTip: Cup shake = curved crack partly separating annual rings. Ring shake = complete circular separation of annual rings.

questions.question: The curvature formed the direction of length of timber is known as:
questions.explanation: Bow is the curvature formed in the direction of the length of the timber piece (face bend). Transverse curve across the face width is Cup.
questions.rankerTip: Curvature along length = Bow. Curvature across width = Cup. Spiral distortion = Twist.

questions.question: The colour of a mineral in its powered form is known as:
questions.explanation: The streak is the characteristic color of a mineral's fine powder, determined by scraping the mineral against an unglazed porcelain streak plate.
questions.rankerTip: Streak = color of powdered mineral on streak plate. Lustre = appearance of mineral surface in reflected light.

questions.question: The coarseness of the grains of a mineral is known as:
questions.explanation: Texture refers to the size, shape, and mutual arrangement of mineral grains (e.g., fine-grained, coarse-grained, porphyritic).
questions.rankerTip: Texture = grain size and arrangement (fine, medium, coarse-grained). Fracture = surface appearance along a break.

questions.question: The board used for providing frog in bricks is known as:
questions.explanation: A Stock board is fixed with a raised wooden or metal projection (called a kick) that creates the indentation / frog on the brick bed during moulding.
questions.rankerTip: Stock board (with kick projection) forms the frog. Pallet board supports the moulded green brick during transport.

questions.question: Swelling of bricks is known as:
questions.explanation: Bloating is the permanent spongy swelling of bricks caused by the entrapment of expanding gases from organic matter and sulfur during firing.
questions.rankerTip: Bloating = spongy swelling due to trapped gas. Chuffs = deformation due to falling rain on hot bricks. Black core = unburnt carbon.

questions.question: The main corrosive resisting prime coat provided in steel:
questions.explanation: Red lead (Pb3O4) is the traditional anti-corrosive primer applied directly onto steel structures to protect against atmospheric rust and moisture.
questions.rankerTip: Red lead primer is applied directly to bare steel for corrosion resistance; Zinc chromate is used for aluminium.

mockTests.title: Workshop Calculation & Science 10 MCQ High-Yield Master Practice Exam
mockTests.description: Targeted 10-question Kerala PSC examination covering Workshop Calculation & Science syllabus: Percentages, Fractions & Decimals, Square Roots & Number Properties, Ratios and Proportions, and Algebra. Evaluated under official PSC pattern with -0.33 negative marking.
mockTests.targetDepartment: Survey & Land Records / Kerala Water Authority

questions.question: 60% of number is 6, Identify the number :
questions.explanation: Let the unknown number be x. (60 / 100) × x = 6 => x = (6 × 100) / 60 = 600 / 60 = 10.
questions.rankerTip: (Part / Percentage) × 100 = Total. Here, (6 / 60) × 100 = 10.

questions.question: What percentage of 80 is 20?
questions.explanation: Required fraction / decimal: 20 / 80 = 1 / 4 = 0.25 (which corresponds to 25%).

questions.question: Find 6% of 750.
Two third of the square of a certain number is 96. What is the number ?
Which of the following cannot be the unit digit in a perfect square ?
questions.explanation: The square of any integer can only end in {0, 1, 4, 5, 6, 9} (0²=0, 1²=1, 2²=4, 3²=9, 4²=6, 5²=5, 6²=6, 7²=9, 8²=4, 9²=1). A perfect square never ends with 2, 3, 7, or 8. Therefore, 7 cannot be the unit digit in a perfect square.
questions.rankerTip: A perfect square NEVER ends in 2, 3, 7, or 8.

questions.question: What will 60% of a number be whose 150% is 120 ?
If 5 : 4 = 35 : X, then the value of X is :
questions.explanation: In a proportion, product of extremes equals product of means: 5 × X = 4 × 35 => X = (4 × 35) / 5 = 4 × 7 = 28.

questions.question: Rs. 250 is divided between Arun and Sasi, and Arun gets 100. Find the ratio of division of the amount.
questions.explanation: Total amount = Rs. 250. Arun's share = Rs. 100. Sasi's share = 250 − 100 = Rs. 150. Ratio of Arun's share to Sasi's share = 100 : 150 = 2 : 3.

questions.question: The least number of 4 digits which is a perfect square is :
questions.explanation: The smallest 4-digit number is 1000. √1000 ≈ 31.62. The next whole integer is 32. 31² = 961 (a 3-digit number). 32² = 1024 (the first 4-digit number). Hence, 1024 is the least 4-digit perfect square.
questions.rankerTip: 31² = 961 (3 digits), 32² = 1024 (smallest 4-digit perfect square).

mockTests.title: AutoCAD 50 MCQ High-Yield Master Practice Exam
mockTests.description: Comprehensive 50-question Kerala PSC examination covering AutoCAD fundamentals: Basic & Modify commands (Mirror, Erase, Break, Trim, Join, Explode, Scale, Stretch, Chamfer, Fillet, Offset, OOPS), Coordinate systems & Polar entries, Function keys (F1-F10), Shortcut keys & Text styling (DT, MTEXT, BEDIT), File extensions (.dwg, .dwt, .dxf), and Layout & Plotting options (Window, DPI). Evaluated under official PSC pattern with -0.33 negative marking.
mockTests.targetDepartment: Survey & Land Records / Kerala Water Authority

questions.question: The most effective command used to draw symmetrical objects is:
questions.explanation: The MIRROR command (alias MI) creates a reverse/reflected copy of selected objects about a specified mirror line, making it the fastest and most accurate command for drawing symmetrical objects.
questions.rankerTip: MIRROR (MI) command is specifically designed for creating symmetrical drawings across an axis.

questions.question: Command used to remove the selected object from a drawing:
questions.explanation: The ERASE command (alias E) removes selected entities from the drawing database.
questions.rankerTip: ERASE (E) deletes objects. OOPS restores objects erased by the most recent ERASE.

questions.question: Command which is used to erase part of an object between two points:
questions.explanation: The BREAK command (alias BR) erases a portion of an object between two specified points or splits an object at a single point. TRIM requires a cutting edge to cut off ends.
questions.rankerTip: BREAK (BR) removes a segment between 2 points without needing an intersecting cutting boundary.

questions.question: Which command is used to exit from a drawing file in AutoCAD?
questions.explanation: The QUIT (or EXIT) command closes the active drawing session and prompts to save unsaved changes before exiting AutoCAD.
questions.rankerTip: QUIT / EXIT closes the active AutoCAD application session.

questions.question: To plot only a particular portion of a drawing, which option can be selected in plot area panel of PLOT window?
questions.explanation: In the Plot dialog box under "Plot area", selecting Window allows the user to specify two diagonal corners on screen to print only that enclosed portion of the drawing.
questions.rankerTip: Plot area options: Display, Extents, Limits, and Window (for picking a rectangular portion).

questions.question: When ..... mode is used to set increments for cursor movements in AutoCAD:
questions.explanation: SNAP mode (toggled via F9) restricts cursor movements to specified step intervals/increments along the X and Y axes.
questions.rankerTip: SNAP (F9) restricts cursor to incremental intervals. GRID (F7) displays visual dot/line matrix.

questions.question: Shortcut used in AutoCAD for pasting object is:
questions.explanation: Standard Windows shortcut Ctrl + V pastes copied objects into the active drawing. (Ctrl + C is Copy, Ctrl + X is Cut, and Ctrl + P is Plot/Print).
questions.rankerTip: Ctrl + V = Paste, Ctrl + C = Copy to Clipboard, Ctrl + Shift + V = Paste as Block.

questions.question: The extension for AutoCAD template file is:
questions.explanation: .dwg: Standard AutoCAD drawing file format. .dwt: AutoCAD Drawing Template file. .dxf: Drawing Exchange Format (vector data exchange).
questions.rankerTip: .dwt = Drawing Template, .dwg = Drawing file, .dxf = Drawing Exchange Format.

questions.question: Functional key F9 stands for:
questions.explanation: Function key F9 toggles the Snap mode ON/OFF (F1 is Help, F3 is OSNAP, F6 is Dynamic UCS, F7 is Grid, and F8 is Ortho).
questions.rankerTip: F1: Help | F3: OSNAP | F7: Grid | F8: Ortho | F9: Snap | F10: Polar Tracking.

questions.question: Which among them is not an option for starting print command?
questions.explanation: PR is the shortcut alias to open the Properties palette. PLOT, PRINT, and Ctrl + P all launch the Plot/Print dialog.
questions.rankerTip: PR opens Properties palette. PLOT, PRINT, and Ctrl+P start the print command.

questions.question: The drafting setting used to constrain the movement of cursor either horizontal or vertical direction is:
questions.explanation: ORTHO mode (shortcut F8) restricts crosshair movement strictly along horizontal or vertical axes (0°, 90°, 180°, 270°).
questions.rankerTip: ORTHO (F8) constrains cursor to orthogonal (horizontal/vertical) lines.

questions.question: In AutoCAD, the function key of GRID command is:
questions.explanation: Function key F7 turns the display of the reference Grid lines/dots ON or OFF.
questions.rankerTip: F7 = Grid ON/OFF. F8 = Ortho ON/OFF. F9 = Snap ON/OFF.

questions.question: The CAD command used to join 2 parallel lines is:
questions.explanation: The FILLET command can join two parallel lines by creating a 180° tangent semi-circular arc between their endpoints, regardless of the preset fillet radius.
questions.rankerTip: FILLET joins two parallel lines with a 180° rounded capping arc.

questions.question: Shortcut key of single line text is:
questions.explanation: DT (or DTEXT) launches single-line text creation. MT (or T) is for multiline text (MTEXT), and ST is for Text Style.
questions.rankerTip: DT = Single-line Dynamic Text; MT/T = Multiline Text (MTEXT); ST = Text Style dialog.

questions.question: ..... is the shortcut key of Block edit:
questions.explanation: BE is the command alias for BEDIT (Block Editor). B is for creating a Block, and BO is for Boundary.
questions.rankerTip: B = Block definition, BE = Block Editor (BEDIT), BO = Boundary creation.

questions.question: The command used in AutoCAD, for shorten object using other object:
questions.explanation: TRIM (alias TR) uses cutting edges defined by other intersecting objects to cut away/shorten lines, polylines, or arcs.
questions.rankerTip: TRIM (TR) shortens objects to cutting edges. EXTEND (EX) lengthens objects to boundary edges.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a draw command in the context of CAD?
questions.explanation: 3DFACE is a 3D surface-mesh modeling command, whereas Line, Spline, and Hatch are primary 2D Draw menu commands.
questions.rankerTip: 3DFACE belongs to 3D surface modeling, not standard 2D Draw tools.

questions.question: The command used to restore all entities erased by the most recent ERASE command:
questions.explanation: The OOPS command restores objects deleted by the immediately preceding ERASE command, even if you have drawn or modified other objects in the meantime (unlike UNDO, which reverts everything sequentially).
questions.rankerTip: OOPS restores the last erased objects without undoing intermediate draw commands.

questions.question: How many points do you need to define for rectangle command?
questions.explanation: The RECTANG command defines a rectangle by prompting for two diagonally opposite corner points (e.g., first corner point and other corner point).
questions.rankerTip: RECTANG requires 2 diagonally opposite corner points.

questions.question: What is the use of the shortcut key Mtext?
questions.explanation: MTEXT (alias MT or T) is used to create multiline text formatted as paragraph blocks with word wrapping.
questions.rankerTip: MTEXT = Multiline Text (formatted paragraphs with formatting ruler).

questions.question: The printing characteristic 'dpi' stands for:
questions.explanation: DPI stands for Dots Per Inch, a measure of spatial printing resolution and plot sharpness.
questions.rankerTip: DPI = Dots Per Inch (printer/plotter resolution measure).

questions.question: From the following which is the correct input method to draw a line of 100 units at an angle of 40 in anticlockwise direction from positive X axis on a default AutoCAD working space?
questions.explanation: In AutoCAD polar coordinate entry, the format is @distance<angle. Here, @100<40 specifies a relative length of 100 at an angle of 40° counterclockwise from the positive X-axis.
questions.rankerTip: Polar coordinate format in AutoCAD: @distance<angle (e.g. @100<40).

questions.question: To obtain parallel lines, concentric circles and parallel curves ..... is used:
questions.explanation: The OFFSET command (alias O) creates parallel lines, concentric circles, or parallel equidistant curves at a specified offset distance or through a point.
questions.rankerTip: OFFSET (O) creates concentric circles, parallel lines, and equidistant curves.

questions.question: The ..... command is a more efficient method of changing object properties than the multi-optioned CHANGE command:
questions.explanation: The CHPROP (Change Properties) command was introduced to modify properties (color, linetype, layer, thickness) directly and efficiently without having to navigate through the complex geometric options of the legacy CHANGE command.
questions.rankerTip: CHPROP is the streamlined command for modifying object properties directly.

questions.question: A polar array creates new objects:
questions.explanation: A Polar Array distributes multiple copies of selected objects radially in a circular pattern around a specified center point.
questions.rankerTip: Polar Array = Circular/radial pattern. Rectangular Array = Rows and Columns.

questions.question: Files, edit, view etc. are easily available in AutoCAD from:
questions.explanation: The classic Menu Bar at the top of the interface displays pull-down menus: File, Edit, View, Insert, Format, Tools, Draw, Dimension, Modify, Window, and Help.
questions.rankerTip: File, Edit, View pull-downs are located on the Menu Bar (MENUBAR system variable).

questions.question: Which command converts discrete object in polyline?
questions.explanation: The JOIN command (alias J) or PEDIT > Join fuses multiple contiguous lines, arcs, or polylines sharing endpoints into a single, continuous 2D Polyline.
questions.rankerTip: JOIN (J) connects contiguous discrete lines/arcs into a single polyline.

questions.question: Which function key is used for on/off object snap, while drafting in AutoCAD:
questions.explanation: Function key F3 toggles running Object Snap (OSNAP) modes ON or OFF.
questions.rankerTip: F3 = OSNAP ON/OFF. Essential for snapping to endpoints, midpoints, and centers.

questions.question: The command used in AutoCAD for breaking a compound object into its component objects:
questions.explanation: The EXPLODE command (alias X) deconstructs compound objects (such as blocks, polylines, dimensions, or regions) into their basic individual constituent geometry.
questions.rankerTip: EXPLODE (X) decomposes blocks, polylines, and dimensions into basic lines and arcs.

questions.question: To erase a previously drawn line, which option in LINE command can be used?
questions.explanation: While actively using the LINE command, typing U (Undo) removes the most recently drawn line segment without terminating the command.
questions.rankerTip: Within LINE command, typing "U" undoes the last segment without exiting.

questions.question: ..... is the shortcut key of 'save as':
questions.explanation: Ctrl + S saves changes to the current file; Ctrl + Shift + S opens the "Save Drawing As" dialog.
questions.rankerTip: Ctrl + S = Save; Ctrl + Shift + S = Save As (QSAVE vs SAVEAS).

questions.question: Which command draw line that extends infinity in both direction?
questions.explanation: An XLINE (Construction Line) extends infinitely in both directions. (RAY extends infinitely in only one direction from a starting point).
questions.rankerTip: XLINE = Infinite in both directions. RAY = Infinite in one direction from a point.

questions.question: Function key F10 is used in AutoCAD to:
questions.explanation: Function key F10 toggles Polar Tracking ON/OFF, guiding crosshairs along specified angular increments.
questions.rankerTip: F10 = Polar Tracking ON/OFF (angular guidelines).

questions.question: In AutoCAD, Keystrokes "Ctrl+Y" function defined as:
questions.explanation: Ctrl + Z undoes the previous action; Ctrl + Y redoes the most recently undone action.
questions.rankerTip: Ctrl + Z = Undo, Ctrl + Y = Redo.

questions.question: The short key for remove italic format for select text is:
questions.explanation: Ctrl + I toggles Italic formatting on and off for selected text in the In-Place MTEXT editor.
questions.rankerTip: Ctrl + I = Toggle Italic, Ctrl + B = Toggle Bold, Ctrl + U = Toggle Underline.

questions.question: To draw a line parallel to the first line, the command used in AutoCAD is:
questions.explanation: OFFSET creates a line parallel to an existing line at any defined distance.
questions.rankerTip: OFFSET (O) generates parallel lines at a given distance or through a point.

questions.question: ..... is a drawing file with pre configured used settings:
questions.explanation: A Drawing Template (.dwt) stores predefined settings such as units, layers, dimension styles, text styles, and title blocks for starting new drawings.
questions.rankerTip: Template (.dwt) pre-configures layers, styles, units, and page layouts.

questions.question: The AutoCAD command to edit the length of the object is:
questions.explanation: The STRETCH command (alias S) elongates or shrinks objects crossing a crossing selection window while preserving unchanged connections.
questions.rankerTip: STRETCH (S) modifies lengths of objects crossing a green crossing window.

questions.question: A command which is used to pick points like endpoint, midpoint, tangent etc, of entities very precisely which geometrical accuracy:
questions.explanation: OSNAP (Object Snap) snaps the cursor precisely to exact geometric points on objects (Endpoint, Midpoint, Center, Tangent, Perpendicular, Intersection).
questions.rankerTip: OSNAP provides exact geometric snapping to endpoints, midpoints, tangents, etc.

questions.question: ..... are the instructions you provide to CAD software to achieve the end result:
questions.explanation: Commands (entered at the command prompt or selected from menus/ribbons) are the fundamental software instructions telling CAD what operation to execute.
questions.rankerTip: Commands are user instructions to CAD software entered via keyboard or UI.

questions.question: Full form of CADD is:
questions.explanation: CADD stands for Computer-Aided Design and Drafting.
questions.rankerTip: CADD = Computer Aided Design and Drafting.

questions.question: The abbreviated character or short cut key "c" is used as a command for ..... in AutoCAD:
questions.explanation: In AutoCAD, the single-letter alias C executes the CIRCLE command. (Copy is CO or CP, and Chamfer is CHA).
questions.rankerTip: C = Circle, CO/CP = Copy, CHA = Chamfer.

questions.question: Which one is not a CAD package?
questions.explanation: Microsoft PowerPoint is a slide presentation tool, whereas STAAD, Revit, and I-DEAS are engineering CAD/BIM/analysis software.
questions.rankerTip: PowerPoint is a Microsoft Office presentation app, not an engineering CAD package.

questions.question: Which shortcut key does the work of ortho?
questions.explanation: Function key F8 toggles ORTHO mode ON/OFF.
questions.rankerTip: F8 = ORTHO shortcut.

questions.question: A pattern of dots that appears on a screen but that does not print is called:
questions.explanation: The drawing GRID is a non-printing rectangular array of dots or grid lines that serves as a visual distance reference on the screen.
questions.rankerTip: GRID provides a non-printing visual matrix of lines or dots.

questions.question: ..... command allows to shrink or enlarge the already existing drawing about a base point:
questions.explanation: The SCALE command (alias SC) enlarges or reduces the size of selected objects proportionally about a chosen base point using a scale factor.
questions.rankerTip: SCALE (SC) alters object size proportionally around a base point.

questions.question: In the context of CAD, What does UCS means?
questions.explanation: UCS stands for User Coordinate System, an orientation-customizable Cartesian coordinate system used in AutoCAD to reorient the X, Y, and Z axes relative to the fixed World Coordinate System (WCS).
questions.rankerTip: UCS = User Coordinate System (movable/rotatable relative to WCS).

questions.question: The command used to join two non-parallel lines by drawing a bevelled line:
questions.explanation: The CHAMFER command (alias CHA) connects two non-parallel lines with an angled, bevelled straight line segment. (In contrast, FILLET joins them with an arc).
questions.rankerTip: CHAMFER (CHA) joins with a beveled angle. FILLET (F) joins with a curved arc.

questions.question: AutoCAD is a ..... software:
questions.explanation: AutoCAD is a commercial Computer-Aided Drafting (CAD) and 2D/3D design application developed by Autodesk.
questions.rankerTip: AutoCAD is a 2D/3D computer-aided drafting and design software.

questions.question: Which one of the following is not a toolbar in AutoCAD?
questions.explanation: In AutoCAD's classic interface, Draw, Modify, Properties, and Standard are standard toolbars with clickable icon sets; "Edit" is a drop-down menu header on the menu bar, not an independent toolbar.
questions.rankerTip: "Edit" is a classic Menu Bar dropdown menu, not a standalone toolbar.

mockTests.title: Levelling Survey 15 MCQ High-Yield Master Practice Exam
mockTests.description: Specialized 15-question Kerala PSC examination covering Level surfaces & Level lines, Fly levelling, Curvature & Refraction corrections (0.07849d², 0.01121d², combined 0.06728d²), Collimation method limitations, Permanent adjustments, Bubble tube sensitivity, Road gradient calculation, and Inverted staff computations. Evaluated under official PSC pattern with -0.33 negative marking.
mockTests.targetDepartment: Survey & Land Records / Kerala Water Authority

questions.question: A curved surface which of every point is perpendicular to the direction of gravity at the points is called:
questions.explanation: A level surface is defined as a curved surface on which every point is perpendicular (normal) to the direction of gravity (the plumb line) at that point. A still body of water undisturbed by tides or wind represents a level surface. A horizontal surface, in contrast, is tangential to a level surface at only one point.
questions.rankerTip: Curved surface normal to plumb line at all points = Level surface. Plane tangential at one point = Horizontal surface.

questions.question: The surface parallel to the mean spheroidal surface of the earth:
questions.explanation: By definition, every level surface is parallel/concentric to the mean spheroidal surface of the earth (represented by Mean Sea Level or the geoid).
questions.rankerTip: Surface concentric/parallel to mean spheroidal surface of earth = Level surface.

questions.question: A line normal to the plumb line of all points is known as:
questions.explanation: A level line is a line lying within a level surface and is normal to the plumb line at every point along its entire length. A horizontal line is tangential to the level line and perpendicular to the plumb line at only one specific point.
questions.rankerTip: Line perpendicular to plumb line at ALL points = Level line. Perpendicular at ONLY ONE point = Horizontal line.

questions.question: When the points are apart, it may be necessary to set up the instrument several times. This type of levelling is known as:
questions.explanation: When two points are far apart and only their relative difference in elevation is required, the level is set up repeatedly at successive change points without taking intermediate sights. This rapid form of differential levelling is called Fly levelling (frequently used to connect a benchmark to a starting station or to check closure at the end of a day's work).
questions.rankerTip: Fly levelling: rapid differential levelling taking only BS and FS to determine elevation difference between far-apart points.

questions.question: Correction for curvature for a distance of 1 km is:
questions.explanation: The curvature correction (Cc) formula is: Cc = d² / (2R) ≈ 0.07849 d² metres (with d in km). For d = 1 km: Cc = 0.07849 × (1)² = 0.07849 m (always subtractive from staff readings).
questions.rankerTip: Curvature correction = 0.07849 d² m (subtractive). For 1 km, Cc = 0.07849 m.

questions.question: In levelling, correction for refraction is:
questions.explanation: Atmospheric refraction bends the line of sight downward towards the earth, making staff readings too small. The refraction correction (Cr) is additive and taken as roughly 1/7 of the curvature correction: Cr ≈ (1/7) Cc = (1/7) × 0.07849 d² ≈ 0.01121 d² m.
questions.rankerTip: Refraction correction Cr = 0.01121 d² m = (1/7) Cc (additive).

questions.question: The refraction correction for a distance of 1 km is:
questions.explanation: Substituting d = 1 km into the refraction formula: Cr = 0.01121 × (1)² = 0.01121 m.
questions.rankerTip: Refraction correction for 1 km is exactly 0.01121 m (additive).

questions.question: The combined correction for refraction and earth's curvature in levelling observations is:
questions.explanation: Combining curvature correction (subtractive) and refraction correction (additive): C = Cc − Cr = 0.07849 d² − 0.01121 d² = 0.06728 d² metres (subtractive).
questions.rankerTip: Combined correction C = (6/7) × 0.07849 d² = 0.06728 d² m (always subtractive).

questions.question: In levelling, the effect of refraction may be taken as.... of that due to curvature:
questions.explanation: Under standard atmospheric conditions, light rays curve with a radius roughly seven times that of the earth's surface (R0 ≈ 7R). Therefore, refraction correction is approximately 1/7 (one-seventh) of the curvature correction.
questions.rankerTip: Refraction effect is 1/7th of curvature effect. Combined effect is 6/7th of curvature effect.

questions.question: It is required to find the difference in elevation between two points A and B. During levelling, it is found that staff reading of B is more than the staff reading at A. It indicates that the point A is....the point B:
questions.explanation: Since the line of collimation is horizontal, staff readings are measured vertically down to the ground. A smaller staff reading indicates that the ground surface is closer to the line of sight (higher elevation). Reading at B > Reading at A ⇒ Elevation of A > Elevation of B. Thus, point A is higher than point B.
questions.rankerTip: Higher staff reading = Lower ground elevation. Smaller staff reading = Higher ground elevation.

questions.question: The collimation method for obtaining the reduced levels of points does not provide check on:
questions.explanation: The arithmetic check in the Collimation (Height of Instrument) method is: ΣBS − ΣFS = Last RL − First RL. This formula provides no mathematical check on the intermediate sight (IS) readings or their reduced levels. In contrast, the Rise and Fall method checks intermediate sights via ΣRise − ΣFall = Last RL − First RL.
questions.rankerTip: HI / Collimation method provides NO arithmetic check on Intermediate Sights (IS). Rise & Fall method checks ALL sights (BS, FS, and IS).

questions.question: Permanent adjustments are carried out to:
options: Establish a fixed relationships between its fundamental axes
Establish temporary relationships between its fundamental axes
Establish variable relationships between its fundamental axes
questions.explanation: Permanent adjustments are made to set up and preserve fixed geometric relationships between the fundamental axes of the instrument (e.g., line of collimation parallel to bubble tube axis, vertical axis perpendicular to bubble axis) so they remain true across multiple setups.
questions.rankerTip: Permanent adjustments = Establish fixed geometric relationships between fundamental lines/axes.

questions.question: Sensitiveness of a level tube is designated by of the level tube:
questions.explanation: The sensitiveness of a level tube is designated by the radius of curvature (R) of the upper internal surface of the vial, or by the angle subtended by an arc of one division (α = d/R). The larger the radius of curvature, the more sensitive the bubble tube.
questions.rankerTip: Sensitiveness is directly designated by the internal Radius of Curvature (R) of the bubble tube.

questions.question: In profile levelling, the staff readings of two neighbourhood pegs 20m apart are 1.200 and 1.000 respectively. Therefore the proposed road had a:
questions.explanation: Staff reading at 1st peg = 1.200 m, at 2nd peg = 1.000 m. Difference in height = 1.200 − 1.000 = +0.200 m (reading decreases in forward direction, so ground is rising). Gradient = Rise / Distance = 0.200 / 20 = 1 / 100. Hence, Rising gradient of 1 in 100.
questions.rankerTip: Reading drops from 1.200 to 1.000 => Rise = 0.2 m in 20 m => 0.2/20 = 1/100 Rising Gradient.

questions.question: The reduced level of a floor is 100.000, the staff reading on the floor is 1.500. From the same station the inverted staff reading taken on the bottom of roof slab is 1.800. The bottom level of roof slab is:
questions.explanation: Height of Instrument (HI) = RL of floor + Staff reading on floor = 100.000 + 1.500 = 101.500 m. For an inverted staff held against the underside of the slab: RL of bottom of roof slab = HI + Inverted staff reading = 101.500 + 1.800 = 103.300 m (Total = 100.000 + 1.500 + 1.800 = 103.300 m).
questions.rankerTip: Under-roof / Inverted staff RL = RL of floor + Floor reading + Inverted staff reading = 100.000 + 1.500 + 1.800 = 103.300 m.

mockTests.title: Compass Survey 25 MCQ High-Yield Master Practice Exam
mockTests.description: Specialized 25-question Kerala PSC examination covering True & Magnetic Meridians, Declination & Dip, Prismatic vs Surveyor Compass graduations, Fore & Back Bearing conversions, Included Angles, and Local Attraction calculations. Evaluated under official PSC pattern with -0.33 negative marking.
mockTests.targetDepartment: Survey & Land Records / Kerala Water Authority

questions.question: All revenue survey maps are plotted with reference to the.... meridian
questions.explanation: True meridian lines remain constant and permanent over time (independent of magnetic declination variations). Therefore, government revenue survey maps and cadastral boundaries are invariably plotted with reference to the True Meridian.
questions.rankerTip: Revenue survey maps and permanent cadastral boundaries are always plotted with reference to the True Meridian.

questions.question: ..... meridian through a given point is the line in which the plane passing through the given point and north and south poles intersects the surface of the earth.
questions.explanation: By definition, the True (or Geographical) Meridian passing through a station is the line of intersection between the Earth's surface and the plane containing the station point and the geographic North and South poles.
questions.rankerTip: Intersection of earth surface with the plane through station point and geographical poles = True or Geographical Meridian.

questions.question: True or geographical meridians through the various stations
questions.explanation: Because the Earth is approximately spherical, true lines of longitude (true meridians) are not parallel; they converge from their maximum spacing at the equator to meet at the geographic poles.
questions.rankerTip: True meridians converge towards the poles and are widest at the equator.

questions.question: True meridians converge at a point called.....
questions.explanation: All geographical (true) meridians converge and intersect at the Earth's Poles (North Pole and South Pole).
questions.rankerTip: Convergence point of all true meridians is the geographic Pole.

questions.question: A freely floating needle slightly gets inclined to the horizontal anywhere except on the equator, it is called
questions.explanation: The vertical angle of inclination that a freely suspended magnetic needle makes with the horizontal plane is called the magnetic dip (or angle of dip). Dip is 0° at the magnetic equator and increases to 90° at the magnetic poles.
questions.rankerTip: Dip is 0° at the magnetic equator and 90° at the magnetic poles. Declination is horizontal angle; Dip is vertical angle.

questions.question: If the fore bearing of a line is S 40° W, the back bearing equals
questions.explanation: In the Quadrantal Bearing (Reduced Bearing) system, the Back Bearing (BB) has the exact same numerical angle as the Fore Bearing (FB), with the cardinal quadrant letters reversed: FB = S 40° W ⇒ BB = N 40° E.
questions.rankerTip: For quadrantal bearings, change N ↔ S and E ↔ W without altering the numerical value.

questions.question: If the bearings of two lines AB and BC are S 45° E and S 45° E, the ∠ABC equals
questions.explanation: Bearing of ray BA (Back Bearing of AB) = N 45° W. Bearing of ray BC (Fore Bearing of BC) = S 45° E. Because rays BA and BC point in directly opposing directions along the same line, the interior angle ∠ABC = 180°.
questions.rankerTip: Equal forward bearings mean line ABC is straight, hence ∠ABC = 180°.

questions.question: If the true bearing of a line is 127° and declination is 2° W, the magnetic bearing equals
questions.explanation: True Bearing (TB) = Magnetic Bearing (MB) − Declination (W). 127° = MB − 2° ⇒ MB = 127° + 2° = 129°.
questions.rankerTip: TB = MB ± Declination (+ for East, − for West). Therefore MB = TB + Declination(West).

questions.question: If the bearing of two lines AB and CB are S 45° E and N 45° W, the angle ABC equals
questions.explanation: Back Bearing of AB (ray BA) = N 45° W. Bearing of ray BC (opposite to given ray CB = N 45° W) = S 45° E. Rays BA and BC form opposite directions along the straight line passing through B, so ∠ABC = 180°.
questions.rankerTip: Notice given lines are AB and CB radiating at B. Ray BA = N 45° W, ray BC = S 45° E. Together they form a straight line (180°).

questions.question: If bearing of OA = 20° and bearing of OB = 140°, then angle ∠AOB = …
questions.explanation: Since both lines radiate from the common vertex O: ∠AOB = Bearing(OB) − Bearing(OA) = 140° − 20° = 120°.
questions.rankerTip: For two lines radiating from the same station in WCB, Included Angle = Greater Bearing − Smaller Bearing.

questions.question: If bearing of AB = N 50° E and bearing of AC = N 40° W, then ∠BAC = …
questions.explanation: Both lines radiate from common station A: Ray AB is 50° east of North, Ray AC is 40° west of North. ∠BAC = 50° + 40° = 90°.
questions.rankerTip: When lines radiate into adjacent NE and NW quadrants from the same station, angle = sum of angles from North.

questions.question: If the whole circle bearing of a line is 210° 15', its reduced bearing is
questions.explanation: A WCB of 210° 15' lies in Quadrant III (South-West, between 180° and 270°): RB = WCB − 180° = 210° 15' − 180° = S 30° 15' W.
questions.rankerTip: Quadrant III (180° to 270°): Reduced Bearing = S (WCB − 180°) W.
questions.topic: Compass Survey - WCB to RB Conversion

questions.question: If the whole circle bearing of a line is 120°, its reduced bearing is
questions.explanation: A WCB of 120° lies in Quadrant II (South-East, between 90° and 180°): RB = 180° − WCB = 180° − 120° = S 60° E.
questions.rankerTip: Quadrant II (90° to 180°): Reduced Bearing = S (180° − WCB) E.
questions.topic: Compass Survey - WCB to RB Conversion

questions.question: If the whole circle bearing of a line is 180°, its reduced bearing is
questions.explanation: A Whole Circle Bearing of 180° points due South along the meridian, so its quadrantal notation is simply South (or S 0°).
questions.rankerTip: 0°/360° = North, 90° = East, 180° = South, 270° = West.

questions.question: In prismatic compass, the 360° or 0° of the Graduation is marked at the ..... end of the graduated circle
questions.explanation: In a prismatic compass, the graduated aluminum ring is attached to the needle and remains fixed to the magnetic meridian while the compass box rotates. The observer reads the ring through a prism located at the South end of the box when sighting North, so the 0°/360° graduation is marked at the South end.
questions.rankerTip: Prismatic compass: 0°/360° is at South, 90° at West, 180° at North, 270° at East (graduations are inverted).

questions.question: On the graduated ring of the prismatic compass 90° is marked at ......end of needle
questions.explanation: Graduations on a prismatic compass ring run clockwise from South (0°). Therefore: South = 0°/360°, West = 90°, North = 180°, East = 270°.
questions.rankerTip: In Prismatic Compass, 90° is at the West end, NOT East.

questions.question: The angle which the line of force due to magnetic field at a point makes with the surface of the earth is known as
questions.explanation: The angle between the Earth's magnetic lines of force and the horizontal surface of the Earth at any given point is called the angle of dip (magnetic inclination).
questions.rankerTip: Angle between magnetic lines of force and earth's horizontal surface = Dip (Magnetic Inclination).

questions.question: The bearing of a line in the direction of progress of survey is known as
questions.explanation: The bearing of a survey line taken in the forward direction along which the survey is advancing is termed the Fore bearing (FB).
questions.rankerTip: Direction of progress = Fore Bearing (FB). Reverse direction = Back Bearing (BB).
questions.topic: Compass Survey - Fore and Back Bearings

questions.question: When the magnetic bearing of the sun at noon is 185° 20', the magnetic declination will be
questions.explanation: At solar noon in the northern hemisphere, the Sun is on the true meridian due True South (TB = 180° 00'): Declination = TB − MB = 180° 00' − 185° 20' = −5° 20' ⇒ 5° 20' West.
questions.rankerTip: If MB at noon > 180°, declination is West. If MB at noon < 180°, declination is East.

questions.question: The reduced bearing of a line is N 87° W. Its whole circle bearing (WCB) is
questions.explanation: N 87° W lies in the fourth quadrant (North-West): WCB = 360° − RB = 360° − 87° = 273°.
questions.rankerTip: Quadrant IV (NW): WCB = 360° − RB.
questions.topic: Compass Survey - WCB to RB Conversion

questions.question: The reduced bearing of a line whose whole circle bearing is 270° is
questions.explanation: WCB = 270° is due West. Measured from North, it is 90° to the west (N 90° W). Measured from South, it is 90° to the west (S 90° W). Both describe the same bearing line.
questions.rankerTip: 270° represents pure West, expressible as N 90° W or S 90° W.

questions.question: Fore bearing of a line AB is 154° and the back bearing is 334°, then local attraction at that place
questions.explanation: |Back Bearing − Fore Bearing| = 334° − 154° = 180°. Because the difference between FB and BB is exactly 180°, stations A and B are free from magnetic interference, meaning the local attraction is 0° (nil).
questions.rankerTip: If |BB − FB| = 180°, both stations are unaffected by local attraction (0° error).

questions.question: If the quadrantal bearing of a line is N 69° 45' E, its whole circle bearing is....
questions.explanation: In the first quadrant (North-East), Whole Circle Bearing and Quadrantal Bearing are numerically identical: WCB = QB = 69° 45'.
questions.rankerTip: In NE quadrant (Quadrant I), WCB = QB.
questions.topic: Compass Survey - WCB to RB Conversion

questions.question: If the quadrantal bearing of a line is S 64° 10' W, its whole circle bearing is.....
questions.explanation: A bearing in the third quadrant (SW) has its WCB measured clockwise from North through South: WCB = 180° + QB = 180° + 64° 10' = 244° 10'.
questions.rankerTip: SW quadrant (Quadrant III): WCB = 180° + QB.
questions.topic: Compass Survey - WCB to RB Conversion

questions.question: In surveyor's compass .... points are marked with letters N and S and ..... points are marked with letters E and W
questions.explanation: In a Surveyor's Compass, the ring is graduated into four 0° to 90° quadrants. The 0° points are marked at North (N) and South (S), and the 90° points are marked at East (E) and West (W).
questions.rankerTip: Surveyor's Compass: 0° at N & S, 90° at E & W. Prismatic Compass: 0° at S, 90° at W, 180° at N, 270° at E.

mockTests.title: Planetable Survey & Traverse 12 MCQ High-Yield Master Practice Exam
mockTests.description: Specialized 12-question Kerala PSC examination covering Planetable Surveying (Backsight orientation, Plumbing fork centering, Alidade fiducial edge alignment, Temporary adjustments sequence, Radiation method) and Traverse Balancing (Bowditch compass rule, Closing error formula, Latitude signs in WCB quadrants). Evaluated under official PSC pattern with -0.33 negative marking.
mockTests.targetDepartment: Survey & Land Records / Kerala Water Authority

questions.question: Orientation by ___ is the most accurate method of orientation and is always to preferred.
questions.explanation: In plane table surveying, orientation by back-sighting (sighting along a previously drawn ray to a known preceding station) is the most accurate and reliable method because it is completely unaffected by local magnetic variations or metallic disturbances.
questions.rankerTip: Orientation by backsighting is the most accurate method of orientation and is always preferred over magnetic orientation.

questions.question: Centering may be done by means of a.
questions.explanation: The plumbing fork (or U-fork/U-frame), fitted with a plumb bob on its bottom arm, is the specific surveying accessory used to transfer the plotted ground station mark directly onto the drawing sheet on the plane table.
questions.rankerTip: Plumbing fork (U-frame) with plumb bob is specifically used for centering the plane table over the ground station.

questions.question: The working edge of Alidade is known as
questions.explanation: The beveled, graduated working edge of a plane table alidade along which rays/lines of sight are ruled on the paper is called the fiducial edge.
questions.rankerTip: The ruling/working edge of an alidade is called the fiducial edge (beveled edge).

questions.question: The fiducial edge should be coincident with or parallel to the
questions.explanation: To prevent graphical plotting errors, the fiducial edge must be parallel to or lie within the vertical plane of sight formed by the alidade's sight vanes (eye vane and object vane).
questions.rankerTip: The fiducial edge of an alidade must be coincident with or parallel to the vertical plane of sight.

questions.question: Which method is used for balancing the traverse when angular and linear measurements are equally precise
questions.explanation: Bowditch's rule (compass rule) is applied to balance a closed traverse when linear and angular measurements have been carried out with equal precision. (The Transit rule is applied when angular measurements are more precise than linear measurements).
questions.rankerTip: Equal precision in linear and angular measurements = Bowditch's rule. Angular more precise = Transit rule.

questions.question: Bowditch rule is sometimes called
questions.explanation: Bowditch's rule is commonly known as the Compass rule because it was originally designed for traverses surveyed with a prismatic/surveyor's compass and chain.
questions.rankerTip: Bowditch's rule is also known as the Compass rule.

questions.question: Orientation by magnetic needle is sufficiently accurate, provided if there is no ___
questions.explanation: Orienting a plane table using a magnetic needle (trough compass) is only accurate if the station is completely free from local attraction (magnetic interference caused by power lines, iron pipes, steel structures, or magnetic mineral deposits).
questions.rankerTip: Magnetic orientation fails or gives errors if local attraction is present in the vicinity.

questions.question: The first temporary adjustment to be done after setting up the plane table at any station will be
questions.explanation: The standard sequential order of operations in plane tabling is: Levelling → Centering → Orientation. Levelling is adjusted first so that subsequent horizontal adjustments do not tilt the board and disturb prior centering.
questions.rankerTip: Strict sequence of operations: Levelling first, then Centering, then Orientation.

questions.question: In setting up a plane table at any station
options: Centering and levelling both are done simultaneously
questions.explanation: In actual field practice and according to standard technical exam answer keys, centering and levelling of a plane table are interdependent operations performed simultaneously by adjusting and embedding the tripod legs into the ground.
questions.rankerTip: In field practice, centering and levelling of the plane table are carried out simultaneously.

questions.question: ___ method is suitable for the survey of small areas which can be commanded from a single station
questions.explanation: The Radiation method is ideal when the survey area is relatively small, unobstructed, and all ground details can be clearly observed and directly measured from a single central instrument setup.
questions.rankerTip: Radiation method: Small area commanded from a single central station. Intersection: Inaccessible or large undulating areas.
questions.topic: Planetable Survey - Methods of Plane Tabling

questions.question: Closing error of a traverse can be calculated by the formula ___, where ΣL is algebraic sum of latitude and ΣD is algebraic sum of departure
questions.explanation: In any closed traverse, the linear error of closure e is the hypotenuse formed by the total error in latitude (ΣL) and departure (ΣD): e = √((ΣL)² + (ΣD)²).
questions.rankerTip: Closing error formula: e = √((ΣL)² + (ΣD)²). Direction of closing error: tan(θ) = (ΣD) / (ΣL).

questions.question: If the WCB of a line is ___, the latitude of the line is positive
questions.explanation:
Latitude is defined as L = l · cos(θ), where θ is the Whole Circle Bearing (WCB). Latitude represents projection along the North-South axis and is positive (Northing) only in Quadrant I (0° < θ < 90°) and Quadrant IV (270° < θ < 360°).

For θ = 30° (Quadrant I): cos(30°) > 0 ⇒ Latitude is positive.
For θ = 90°: cos(90°) = 0 ⇒ Latitude is zero.
For θ = 135° (Quadrant II) & 180°: cos(θ) < 0 ⇒ Latitude is negative (Southing).
questions.rankerTip: Latitude = l · cos(θ) (Positive in NE and NW quadrants: 0°-90° & 270°-360°). Departure = l · sin(θ) (Positive in NE and SE quadrants: 0°-180°).

mockTests.title: Modern Survey Instruments 44 MCQ High-Yield Master Practice Exam
mockTests.description: Specialized 44-question Kerala PSC examination covering Microwave & Electro-optical EDM (Geodimeter/Tellurometer), Total Station operations, onboard programs (Reference Line, Stake Out, Free Station, Tie Distance), single reflector prisms, GPS constellation & segments, Drishti & MOBIC, Photogrammetry, Remote Sensing, and GIS fundamentals. Evaluated under official PSC pattern with -0.33 negative marking.
mockTests.targetDepartment: Survey & Land Records / Kerala Water Authority

questions.question: Which type of modulation is used in the case of microwave instrument?
questions.explanation: Microwave electronic distance measurement (EDM) instruments (such as the Tellurometer) employ Frequency Modulation (FM), whereas electro-optical instruments using visible light or infrared (such as the Geodimeter and Distomat) use Amplitude Modulation (AM).
questions.rankerTip: Microwave EDM (Tellurometer) = Frequency Modulation (FM). Light/IR EDM (Geodimeter/Distomat) = Amplitude Modulation (AM).

questions.question: Geodimeter uses which of the following waves as a carrier wave?
questions.explanation: Developed by Erik Bergstrand, the Geodimeter was the earliest electro-optical EDM and utilized modulated visible light waves (tungsten/mercury lamps or laser light) as carrier waves.
