bankQuestions.question: Where the plan is placed in third angle projection?
bankQuestions.explanation: In 3rd angle projection, the projection planes are assumed transparent: Top View (Plan) is placed above the Front View (Elevation). In 1st angle projection, the Plan is placed below the Elevation.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 3rd Angle: Plan is ABOVE elevation. 1st Angle: Plan is BELOW elevation.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Engineering Drawing Bank

bankQuestions.question: For thin chain line alternate long and short dashes are in proportion ranging from:
bankQuestions.explanation: In long-dashed dotted / thin chain lines (used for center lines and axes), long dashes are typically 9 to 12 mm and short dashes/dots are 1.5 to 2 mm, giving a proportion ranging from 6:1 to 4:1.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Chain line proportion of long to short dash is between 6:1 and 4:1.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Engineering Drawing Bank

bankQuestions.question: The type of Vernier in which the Vernier divisions are marked in the opposite direction of the main scale is:
bankQuestions.explanation: In a backward (retrograde) vernier, divisions are numbered in the direction opposite to the main scale, and n vernier divisions equal (n+1) main scale divisions (V > S).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Direct/Forward vernier: same direction, n V = (n - 1) S (V < S). Retrograde/Backward vernier: opposite direction, n V = (n + 1) S (V > S).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Engineering Drawing Bank

bankQuestions.question: To represent two units of measurement ....... scale is used.
bankQuestions.explanation: A plain (plane) scale is used to indicate two consecutive units of measurement (e.g., metres and decimetres, or kilometres and hectometres).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Plain scale represents 2 units (or a unit and its fractional subdivision).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Engineering Drawing Bank

bankQuestions.question: When the section plane is inclined to the axis of the cone and cuts all the generators, the section obtained is:
bankQuestions.explanation: When a cutting plane cuts all generators of a right circular cone at an angle greater than the semi-vertical angle α, the true shape of the section is an ellipse.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Section plane cuts ALL generators of a cone = Ellipse.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Engineering Drawing Bank

bankQuestions.question: If a line is parallel to any one of the reference planes and inclined to the other then:
options: Its projection on that plane to which it is parallel will show the true length
Its projection on that plane to which it is parallel will show the true inclination
bankQuestions.explanation: If a line is parallel to a plane of projection, its projection on that plane will faithfully show both its true length and its true inclination to the other reference plane.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Line parallel to a plane shows BOTH true length AND true inclination on that plane.
bankQuestions.topic: Projections - Lines Parallel to One Plane
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Engineering Drawing Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which is/are not the central conic/s?
bankQuestions.explanation: Both ellipses and hyperbolas possess a center of symmetry through which all chords are bisected, making them central conics. A parabola does not have a center of symmetry and is non-central.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Central conics = Ellipse and Hyperbola. Non-central conic = Parabola.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Engineering Drawing Bank

bankQuestions.question: The recommended method of Dimensioning of a sphere with diameter 50 mm is:
bankQuestions.explanation: According to BIS (IS 10714) and ISO drafting rules, spherical features are dimensioned by prefixing the symbol S before the diameter symbol ϕ, formatted as Sϕ50 (or SR25 for spherical radius).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Sphere dimensioning: Sϕ followed by diameter value (e.g. Sϕ50) or SR followed by radius (SR25).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Engineering Drawing Bank

bankQuestions.question: The continuous thin line connecting a dimensional value or some information relating to a feature in an engineering drawing is:
bankQuestions.explanation: A leader line is a continuous thin line with an arrowhead or dot pointing to a feature and an inclined/horizontal portion terminating at a note, dimension, or reference symbol.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Leader line connects an explanatory note, symbol, or dimension value to the feature on the drawing.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Engineering Drawing Bank

bankQuestions.question: The continuous thin ruled lines with short zig-zags within them are drawn to show:
bankQuestions.explanation: According to IS 10714 (Type D line), a continuous thin straight line with short zig-zags is designated to represent long break lines or limits of partial/interrupted views. Continuous wavy freehand lines (Type C) are used for short break lines.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Continuous thin with zig-zag (Type D) = Long break lines; Continuous thin wavy (Type C) = Short break lines.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Engineering Drawing Bank

bankQuestions.question: Vicat's apparatus is used to determine the:
bankQuestions.explanation: Vicat's apparatus is a standard testing instrument used for multiple cement tests: a 10 mm diameter plunger is used for the standard/normal consistency test (P), a 1 mm square needle for the initial setting time test, and an annular collar needle for the final setting time test.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Vicat plunger (10 mm) = Consistency (P); 1 mm square needle = Initial setting; Annular needle = Final setting.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: Chemically which rock is calcareous rock?
bankQuestions.explanation: Calcareous rocks have calcium carbonate (CaCO3) or lime as their predominant constituent. Marble and limestone are classic calcareous rocks. Granite and basalt are igneous/siliceous rocks.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Calcareous = Lime/CaCO3 (Limestone, Marble, Kankar); Siliceous = Silica (Granite, Basalt, Quartzite); Argillaceous = Clay/Alumina (Slate, Laterite).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: Weight of 1 bag of cement:
bankQuestions.explanation: In standard civil engineering practice across India, a commercial bag of cement weighs exactly 50 kg, with a nominal volume of approximately 34.7 to 35 litres (0.0347 m³). Standard density of cement is 1440 kg/m³.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 bag = 50 kg = 34.7 liters (0.0347 m³). Density = 1440 kg/m³. 20 bags = 1 Tonne (1000 kg).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: The central part of the tree is called:
bankQuestions.explanation: The innermost core or central longitudinal axis of an exogenous tree stem is called the Pith (or Medulla). It consists of cellular tissue that nourishes the tree in its sapling stage.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Order from center outward: Pith -> Heartwood -> Sapwood -> Cambium Layer -> Inner Bark -> Outer Bark.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: The most common material used as vehicle of a paint is:
bankQuestions.explanation: Linseed oil (raw, boiled, or double-boiled) is the standard and most widely used vehicle (drying oil) in oil paints, serving to hold pigment particles in suspension and forming a durable, protective film upon drying.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Vehicle (binder/carrier) = Linseed oil, Poppy oil, Tung oil. Most common = Linseed oil. Thinner/Solvent = Turpentine.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: The part of tree, which hold together the annual rings of Hardwood and Sap wood is:
bankQuestions.explanation: Medullary rays are cellular radial structures that extend perpendicularly from the pith towards the bark, holding the annular rings together and providing radial strength.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Medullary rays extend radially outward from pith to bark, locking annual rings together.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: The heating of limestone to redness in contact with air is known as:
bankQuestions.explanation: Calcination is the process of heating limestone (CaCO3) to red heat (approx. 800–900°C) in the presence of air to drive off carbon dioxide, producing quicklime (CaO).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: CaCO3 + Heat -> CaO + CO2 is Calcination. CaO + H2O -> Ca(OH)2 + Heat is Slaking.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: The compressive strength of fire-bricks varies from:
bankQuestions.explanation: Fire-clay/refractory bricks possess very high compressive resistance, conventionally cited in competitive exams as 200 to 220 N/mm² (derived from 200–220 kg/cm² or 2000-2200 N/cm² standards).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Fire bricks: compressive strength = 200 to 220 N/mm². Used for lining blast furnaces and kilns.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: The Kiln used for the manufacture of tile is:
bankQuestions.explanation: A Sialkot kiln is a specialized intermittent kiln commonly used for burning clay roofing and flooring tiles.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Sialkot kiln is specifically employed for tile manufacture; Rotary kiln is used for Portland cement clinker.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: The increase in volume of dry sand when water is added is called:
bankQuestions.explanation: Bulking of sand is the increase in bulk volume caused by surface tension films formed around sand particles when water is added (peaking typically between 4% and 6% moisture content).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Bulking peaks at 4% to 6% moisture content. Fine sand bulks more than coarse sand. Completely submerged sand has zero bulking.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: Brick containing cylindrical holes throughout their thickness:
bankQuestions.explanation: Perforated bricks contain cylindrical holes penetrating completely through their thickness (usually covering 30% to 45% of the gross face area), offering lightweight properties and enhanced thermal insulation.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Perforated bricks have holes throughout thickness (30-45% cross-section). Hollow bricks have larger cavities.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: The weight of Rose wood after seasoning is:
bankQuestions.explanation: Indian Rosewood is a heavy and dense hardwood with a seasoned unit weight of approximately 7.9 to 8.5 kN/m³ (7900 N/m³).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Rosewood unit weight after seasoning ≈ 7900 N/m³ (7.9 kN/m³). Teak is ≈ 6500 N/m³, Sal is ≈ 8500-9000 N/m³.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: The size of pin knot is:
bankQuestions.explanation: According to IS standards: Pin knot: Diameter ≤ 6.50 mm; Small knot: Diameter > 6.50 mm and ≤ 20 mm; Medium knot: Diameter > 20 mm and ≤ 40 mm; Large knot: Diameter > 40 mm.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Pin knot ≤ 6.5 mm; Small knot 6.5 - 20 mm; Medium knot 20 - 40 mm; Large knot > 40 mm.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: The alternate dry and wet conditions causes the development of ... in timber:
bankQuestions.explanation: Wet rot is caused by fungi attacking timber subjected to alternate wet and dry environments. Dry rot occurs in warm, damp, and unventilated conditions.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Alternate wet and dry conditions cause Wet Rot. Lack of ventilation with dampness causes Dry Rot.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which of the following tiles are conical in shape?
bankQuestions.explanation: Guna tiles are hollow conical/tapered cylindrical burnt clay tiles used in building vaulted roofs and domes.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Guna tiles = conical/tapered hollow tiles used for curved roofs and vault construction.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: The minimum compressive strength of lime mortar 1:3 with Class A lime at the end of 14 days is:
bankQuestions.explanation: As per IS 712, Class A (eminently hydraulic) lime mortar (1:3 mix) must attain a minimum compressive strength of 1.75 N/mm² at 14 days and 2.8 N/mm² at 28 days.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Class A hydraulic lime mortar (1:3): 14-day strength = 1.75 N/mm²; 28-day strength = 2.80 N/mm².
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which of the following bricks are used as aggregate for concrete in foundation, floors etc.?
bankQuestions.explanation: Fourth-class bricks (Jhama / overburnt bricks) are distorted and brittle for regular masonry, but their vitrified hardness makes them ideal when crushed for use as coarse aggregate in foundation and floor concrete.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Fourth-class / Jhama bricks = overburnt, brittle, used as crushed aggregate for concrete in foundations and road metalling.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: In which process in the manufacturing of brick the clay is brought to a proper degree of hardness?
bankQuestions.explanation: Tempering (kneading, often done in a pug mill) is the operation where clay is thoroughly mixed with water to give it the proper degree of plasticity and uniform hardness needed for moulding.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Preparation of brick earth: Unsoiling -> Digging -> Cleaning -> Weathering -> Blending -> Tempering (in Pug Mill).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which test is used to determine the rate of wear of stones?
bankQuestions.explanation: The attrition test (using Deval's attrition machine) measures the percentage wear of stones caused by mutual friction and rubbing.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Attrition test = wear & mutual rubbing; Impact test = toughness; Crushing test = compressive strength; Smith's test = presence of soluble/clayey matter.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which of the following is an igneous rock?
bankQuestions.explanation: Basalt is an extrusive (volcanic) igneous rock formed by the cooling of lava on the Earth's surface. (Slate and Gneiss are metamorphic; Kankar is sedimentary).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Igneous: Granite, Basalt, Trap, Diorite, Gabbro. Metamorphic: Marble, Slate, Gneiss, Quartzite. Sedimentary: Limestone, Sandstone, Kankar, Shale.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: Composition of alumina in brick earth:
bankQuestions.explanation: Standard brick earth contains 50–60% Silica, 20–30% Alumina, 5–6% Lime, and minor percentages of iron oxide and magnesia.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Brick earth composition mnemonic (SALIM): Silica (50-60%), Alumina (20-30%), Lime (5%), Iron oxide (5-6%), Magnesia (<1%).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: IS: Code of Super sulphated cement:
bankQuestions.explanation: IS 6909:1990 governs the specification for Supersulphated cement, manufactured by intergrinding blast furnace slag, calcium sulphate, and small amounts of Portland cement.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: IS 6909 = Supersulphated Cement; IS 269 = 33 Grade OPC; IS 8112 = 43 Grade OPC; IS 12269 = 53 Grade OPC; IS 455 = PSC; IS 1489 = PPC.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: Soundness tests of cement is carried out to determine:
bankQuestions.explanation: Soundness testing via the Le Chatelier apparatus detects excess uncombined free lime (CaO), which causes destructive delayed expansion upon hydration.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Le Chatelier method detects unsoundness due to free Lime only. Autoclave method detects unsoundness due to both Lime and Magnesia.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: Most commonly used solvent in oil paint is:
bankQuestions.explanation: Spirits of turpentine is the most common solvent (thinner) used in oil paints to make the paint thin, workable, and easily spreadable.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Turpentine is the principal solvent/thinner in oil paint; Linseed oil is the vehicle/carrier.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: The property by which lime will set in damp place:
bankQuestions.explanation: Hydraulicity is the capacity of hydraulic lime to set and harden in damp places or completely submerged under water without requiring atmospheric carbon dioxide.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Hydraulicity = ability of lime to set under water or in damp conditions (due to clay/silicates and aluminates).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: The defect is formed due to improper sawing of timber is:
bankQuestions.explanation: Diagonal grain is a manufacturing defect produced when logs are cut obliquely across the grain rather than parallel to the tree axis.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Defects due to conversion (sawing): Diagonal grain, Torn grain, Chip mark, Wane.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: The normal consistency of Portland cement is about:
bankQuestions.explanation: Standard consistency (P) of Ordinary Portland Cement typically ranges between 25% and 30% by weight of dry cement.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Standard consistency of OPC ≈ 25% to 30%. Initial & final setting time test uses 0.85P water; Soundness test uses 0.78P water.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: ... is manufactured in puddling process:
bankQuestions.explanation: Wrought iron (the purest commercial iron, <0.15% carbon) is manufactured from pig iron in a reverberatory puddling furnace.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Pig iron -> Blast furnace; Cast iron -> Cupola furnace; Wrought iron -> Puddling furnace; Steel -> Bessemer / Open Hearth / Electric Arc.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: In order to soften the iron, which heat treatment method is required?
bankQuestions.explanation: Annealing involves heating the metal to a specified temperature followed by very slow furnace cooling, which relieves internal stresses, refines grain structure, and softens the iron/steel.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Annealing softens steel and relieves internal stresses (slow cooling in furnace). Hardening increases hardness (rapid quenching).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: What is the process for increasing toughness and decreasing brittleness?
bankQuestions.explanation: Hardened steel is reheated below its lower critical transformation temperature and cooled; this reduces extreme brittleness and substantially increases toughness.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Tempering restores ductility and toughness in hardened steel while reducing extreme brittleness.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: The rocks formed due to pouring of magma at earth's surface are:
bankQuestions.explanation: Extrusive igneous rocks formed when magma pours out onto the surface as lava and cools rapidly are called Volcanic rocks (e.g., Basalt, Pumice).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: At surface (rapid cooling) = Volcanic rocks (Basalt); At shallow depth = Hypabyssal (Dolerite); At great depth (slow cooling) = Plutonic (Granite).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: The product obtained after slaking of quick lime is:
bankQuestions.explanation: The reaction of quicklime with water (CaO + H2O → Ca(OH)2 + Heat) is slaking, yielding calcium hydroxide, commercially called slaked lime or hydrated lime.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Quick lime (CaO) + Water -> Hydrated lime / Slaked lime [Ca(OH)2] + Heat.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: The defects in timber, which is due to over maturity or by poor ventilation during storage:
bankQuestions.explanation: Foxiness appears as red or yellow discolorations near the pith and heartwood, caused by fungal decay arising from overmaturity or unventilated storage.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Foxiness = reddish/yellow stain caused by overmaturity or poor ventilation during storage.
bankQuestions.topic: Timber - Defects due to Fungi & Storage
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: The main function of alumina in brick earth is:
bankQuestions.explanation: Alumina (Al2O3) is the essential ingredient in clay that provides plasticity, enabling the brick earth to be moulded into shape.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Alumina imparts plasticity for moulding. Silica prevents shrinkage, cracking, and warping. Iron oxide gives red color.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: Le-Chateliers flask is used for determining the:
bankQuestions.explanation: The Le Chatelier flask (using kerosene) is used to determine the specific gravity of cement (≈ 3.15). The Le Chatelier mould / apparatus is used to determine soundness.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Le Chatelier FLASK = Specific gravity test (using kerosene, value ≈ 3.15). Le Chatelier MOULD = Soundness test.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: Deciduous trees fall under the category of:
bankQuestions.explanation: Exogenous trees add outward annual rings each year and are classified into Conifers (needle-leaved evergreens) and Deciduous (broad-leaved hardwoods).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Exogenous trees grow outwards by adding annual rings; they include Conifers (softwoods) and Deciduous (hardwoods like Teak, Sal).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: Based on modulus of elasticity, timber used for construction purposes are classified as Group B when:
options: Modulus of elasticity in bending above 12.5 kN/mm²
Modulus of elasticity in bending above 5.6 kN/mm² and below 9.8 kN/mm²
Modulus of elasticity in bending above 9.8 kN/mm² and below 12.5 kN/mm²
Modulus of elasticity in bending below 5.6 kN/mm²
bankQuestions.explanation: According to IS 883: Group A: E > 12.5 kN/mm² (or > 12.6 kN/mm²); Group B: 9.8 kN/mm² < E ≤ 12.5 kN/mm²; Group C: 5.6 kN/mm² < E ≤ 9.8 kN/mm².
bankQuestions.rankerTip: IS 883 classification by Modulus of Elasticity (E): Group A: E > 12.5 kN/mm²; Group B: 9.8 to 12.5 kN/mm²; Group C: 5.6 to 9.8 kN/mm².
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: As per relevant Bureau of Indian Standard, the soundness of 43 grade Ordinary Portland Cement tested according to Le Chatelier apparatus shall not be more than:
bankQuestions.explanation: Per IS 8112 and IS 269, the maximum allowable expansion for OPC (grades 33, 43, 53) using the Le Chatelier method is 10 mm.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Soundness of OPC by Le Chatelier apparatus: Maximum expansion = 10 mm. By Autoclave test: Maximum expansion = 0.8%.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: The binding material used in Surkhi mortar is:
bankQuestions.explanation: In Surkhi mortar, Surkhi (powdered burnt clay) acts as a pozzolanic fine aggregate, while lime is the binding material.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: In Surkhi mortar: Lime is the binder; Surkhi is the pozzolanic fine aggregate substitute.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: The initial setting time of ordinary Portland cement shall not be:
bankQuestions.explanation: As per IS 269 / IS 456, the initial setting time of OPC shall not be less than 30 minutes, and the final setting time shall not exceed 600 minutes (10 hours).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: OPC setting times: Initial setting time ≥ 30 minutes; Final setting time ≤ 600 minutes (10 hours).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: Excess of silica makes the bricks:
bankQuestions.explanation: While silica prevents warping and shrinkage, an excess of silica destroys the cohesion of clay particles and renders the bricks brittle and weak when burnt.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Excess silica makes bricks brittle and weak on burning; excess alumina causes warping and shrinkage.
bankQuestions.topic: Bricks - Defects from Raw Material Excess
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: Igneous rocks are formed by the action of:
bankQuestions.explanation: Igneous rocks are primary rocks formed by the thermal action of extreme volcanic heat that liquefies rock into magma, which subsequently crystallizes upon cooling.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Igneous = Heat (cooling of molten magma/lava); Sedimentary = Weathering, deposition & compaction; Metamorphic = Heat and pressure alteration.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: Rapid hardening cement high percentage of:
bankQuestions.explanation: Rapid Hardening Cement gains high early strength due to a higher percentage of tricalcium silicate (C3S), achieved by increasing the lime content and grinding the clinker to a finer Blaine specific surface.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Rapid Hardening Cement has a higher lime content (resulting in higher C3S) and higher fineness than normal OPC.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: ... is a crack which is partly separate the annual rings:
bankQuestions.explanation: A curved crack that partly separates adjacent annual rings is a Cup shake. When the crack completely separates the rings in a full circle, it is called a Ring shake.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Cup shake = curved crack partly separating annual rings. Ring shake = complete circular separation of annual rings.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: The curvature formed the direction of length of timber is known as:
bankQuestions.explanation: Bow is the curvature formed in the direction of the length of the timber piece (face bend). Transverse curve across the face width is Cup.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Curvature along length = Bow. Curvature across width = Cup. Spiral distortion = Twist.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: The colour of a mineral in its powered form is known as:
bankQuestions.explanation: The streak is the characteristic color of a mineral's fine powder, determined by scraping the mineral against an unglazed porcelain streak plate.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Streak = color of powdered mineral on streak plate. Lustre = appearance of mineral surface in reflected light.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: The coarseness of the grains of a mineral is known as:
bankQuestions.explanation: Texture refers to the size, shape, and mutual arrangement of mineral grains (e.g., fine-grained, coarse-grained, porphyritic).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Texture = grain size and arrangement (fine, medium, coarse-grained). Fracture = surface appearance along a break.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: The board used for providing frog in bricks is known as:
bankQuestions.explanation: A Stock board is fixed with a raised wooden or metal projection (called a kick) that creates the indentation / frog on the brick bed during moulding.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Stock board (with kick projection) forms the frog. Pallet board supports the moulded green brick during transport.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: Swelling of bricks is known as:
bankQuestions.explanation: Bloating is the permanent spongy swelling of bricks caused by the entrapment of expanding gases from organic matter and sulfur during firing.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Bloating = spongy swelling due to trapped gas. Chuffs = deformation due to falling rain on hot bricks. Black core = unburnt carbon.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: The main corrosive resisting prime coat provided in steel:
bankQuestions.explanation: Red lead (Pb3O4) is the traditional anti-corrosive primer applied directly onto steel structures to protect against atmospheric rust and moisture.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Red lead primer is applied directly to bare steel for corrosion resistance; Zinc chromate is used for aluminium.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer / Surveyor Gr. II Bank

bankQuestions.question: A curved surface which of every point is perpendicular to the direction of gravity at the points is called:
bankQuestions.explanation: A level surface is defined as a curved surface on which every point is perpendicular (normal) to the direction of gravity (the plumb line) at that point. A still body of water undisturbed by tides or wind represents a level surface. A horizontal surface, in contrast, is tangential to a level surface at only one point.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Curved surface normal to plumb line at all points = Level surface. Plane tangential at one point = Horizontal surface.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Levelling Bank

bankQuestions.question: The surface parallel to the mean spheroidal surface of the earth:
bankQuestions.explanation: By definition, every level surface is parallel/concentric to the mean spheroidal surface of the earth (represented by Mean Sea Level or the geoid).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Surface concentric/parallel to mean spheroidal surface of earth = Level surface.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Levelling Bank

bankQuestions.question: A line normal to the plumb line of all points is known as:
bankQuestions.explanation: A level line is a line lying within a level surface and is normal to the plumb line at every point along its entire length. A horizontal line is tangential to the level line and perpendicular to the plumb line at only one specific point.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Line perpendicular to plumb line at ALL points = Level line. Perpendicular at ONLY ONE point = Horizontal line.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Levelling Bank

bankQuestions.question: When the points are apart, it may be necessary to set up the instrument several times. This type of levelling is known as:
bankQuestions.explanation: When two points are far apart and only their relative difference in elevation is required, the level is set up repeatedly at successive change points without taking intermediate sights. This rapid form of differential levelling is called Fly levelling (frequently used to connect a benchmark to a starting station or to check closure at the end of a day's work).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Fly levelling: rapid differential levelling taking only BS and FS to determine elevation difference between far-apart points.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Levelling Bank

bankQuestions.question: Correction for curvature for a distance of 1 km is:
bankQuestions.explanation: The curvature correction (Cc) formula is: Cc = d² / (2R) ≈ 0.07849 d² metres (with d in km). For d = 1 km: Cc = 0.07849 × (1)² = 0.07849 m (always subtractive from staff readings).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Curvature correction = 0.07849 d² m (subtractive). For 1 km, Cc = 0.07849 m.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Levelling Bank

bankQuestions.question: In levelling, correction for refraction is:
bankQuestions.explanation: Atmospheric refraction bends the line of sight downward towards the earth, making staff readings too small. The refraction correction (Cr) is additive and taken as roughly 1/7 of the curvature correction: Cr ≈ (1/7) Cc = (1/7) × 0.07849 d² ≈ 0.01121 d² m.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Refraction correction Cr = 0.01121 d² m = (1/7) Cc (additive).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Levelling Bank

bankQuestions.question: The refraction correction for a distance of 1 km is:
bankQuestions.explanation: Substituting d = 1 km into the refraction formula: Cr = 0.01121 × (1)² = 0.01121 m.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Refraction correction for 1 km is exactly 0.01121 m (additive).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Levelling Bank

bankQuestions.question: The combined correction for refraction and earth's curvature in levelling observations is:
bankQuestions.explanation: Combining curvature correction (subtractive) and refraction correction (additive): C = Cc − Cr = 0.07849 d² − 0.01121 d² = 0.06728 d² metres (subtractive).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Combined correction C = (6/7) × 0.07849 d² = 0.06728 d² m (always subtractive).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Levelling Bank

bankQuestions.question: In levelling, the effect of refraction may be taken as.... of that due to curvature:
bankQuestions.explanation: Under standard atmospheric conditions, light rays curve with a radius roughly seven times that of the earth's surface (R0 ≈ 7R). Therefore, refraction correction is approximately 1/7 (one-seventh) of the curvature correction.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Refraction effect is 1/7th of curvature effect. Combined effect is 6/7th of curvature effect.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Levelling Bank

bankQuestions.question: It is required to find the difference in elevation between two points A and B. During levelling, it is found that staff reading of B is more than the staff reading at A. It indicates that the point A is....the point B:
bankQuestions.explanation: Since the line of collimation is horizontal, staff readings are measured vertically down to the ground. A smaller staff reading indicates that the ground surface is closer to the line of sight (higher elevation). Reading at B > Reading at A ⇒ Elevation of A > Elevation of B. Thus, point A is higher than point B.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Higher staff reading = Lower ground elevation. Smaller staff reading = Higher ground elevation.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Levelling Bank

bankQuestions.question: The collimation method for obtaining the reduced levels of points does not provide check on:
bankQuestions.explanation: The arithmetic check in the Collimation (Height of Instrument) method is: ΣBS − ΣFS = Last RL − First RL. This formula provides no mathematical check on the intermediate sight (IS) readings or their reduced levels. In contrast, the Rise and Fall method checks intermediate sights via ΣRise − ΣFall = Last RL − First RL.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: HI / Collimation method provides NO arithmetic check on Intermediate Sights (IS). Rise & Fall method checks ALL sights (BS, FS, and IS).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Levelling Bank

bankQuestions.question: Permanent adjustments are carried out to:
options: Establish a fixed relationships between its fundamental axes
Establish temporary relationships between its fundamental axes
Establish variable relationships between its fundamental axes
bankQuestions.explanation: Permanent adjustments are made to set up and preserve fixed geometric relationships between the fundamental axes of the instrument (e.g., line of collimation parallel to bubble tube axis, vertical axis perpendicular to bubble axis) so they remain true across multiple setups.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Permanent adjustments = Establish fixed geometric relationships between fundamental lines/axes.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Levelling Bank

bankQuestions.question: Sensitiveness of a level tube is designated by of the level tube:
bankQuestions.explanation: The sensitiveness of a level tube is designated by the radius of curvature (R) of the upper internal surface of the vial, or by the angle subtended by an arc of one division (α = d/R). The larger the radius of curvature, the more sensitive the bubble tube.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Sensitiveness is directly designated by the internal Radius of Curvature (R) of the bubble tube.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Levelling Bank

bankQuestions.question: In profile levelling, the staff readings of two neighbourhood pegs 20m apart are 1.200 and 1.000 respectively. Therefore the proposed road had a:
bankQuestions.explanation: Staff reading at 1st peg = 1.200 m, at 2nd peg = 1.000 m. Difference in height = 1.200 − 1.000 = +0.200 m (reading decreases in forward direction, so ground is rising). Gradient = Rise / Distance = 0.200 / 20 = 1 / 100. Hence, Rising gradient of 1 in 100.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Reading drops from 1.200 to 1.000 => Rise = 0.2 m in 20 m => 0.2/20 = 1/100 Rising Gradient.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Levelling Bank

bankQuestions.question: The reduced level of a floor is 100.000, the staff reading on the floor is 1.500. From the same station the inverted staff reading taken on the bottom of roof slab is 1.800. The bottom level of roof slab is:
bankQuestions.explanation: Height of Instrument (HI) = RL of floor + Staff reading on floor = 100.000 + 1.500 = 101.500 m. For an inverted staff held against the underside of the slab: RL of bottom of roof slab = HI + Inverted staff reading = 101.500 + 1.800 = 103.300 m (Total = 100.000 + 1.500 + 1.800 = 103.300 m).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Under-roof / Inverted staff RL = RL of floor + Floor reading + Inverted staff reading = 100.000 + 1.500 + 1.800 = 103.300 m.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Levelling Bank

bankQuestions.question: All revenue survey maps are plotted with reference to the.... meridian
bankQuestions.explanation: True meridian lines remain constant and permanent over time (independent of magnetic declination variations). Therefore, government revenue survey maps and cadastral boundaries are invariably plotted with reference to the True Meridian.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Revenue survey maps and permanent cadastral boundaries are always plotted with reference to the True Meridian.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Compass Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: ..... meridian through a given point is the line in which the plane passing through the given point and north and south poles intersects the surface of the earth.
bankQuestions.explanation: By definition, the True (or Geographical) Meridian passing through a station is the line of intersection between the Earth's surface and the plane containing the station point and the geographic North and South poles.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Intersection of earth surface with the plane through station point and geographical poles = True or Geographical Meridian.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Compass Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: True or geographical meridians through the various stations
bankQuestions.explanation: Because the Earth is approximately spherical, true lines of longitude (true meridians) are not parallel; they converge from their maximum spacing at the equator to meet at the geographic poles.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: True meridians converge towards the poles and are widest at the equator.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Compass Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: True meridians converge at a point called.....
bankQuestions.explanation: All geographical (true) meridians converge and intersect at the Earth's Poles (North Pole and South Pole).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Convergence point of all true meridians is the geographic Pole.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Compass Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: A freely floating needle slightly gets inclined to the horizontal anywhere except on the equator, it is called
bankQuestions.explanation: The vertical angle of inclination that a freely suspended magnetic needle makes with the horizontal plane is called the magnetic dip (or angle of dip). Dip is 0° at the magnetic equator and increases to 90° at the magnetic poles.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Dip is 0° at the magnetic equator and 90° at the magnetic poles. Declination is horizontal angle; Dip is vertical angle.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Compass Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: If the fore bearing of a line is S 40° W, the back bearing equals
bankQuestions.explanation: In the Quadrantal Bearing (Reduced Bearing) system, the Back Bearing (BB) has the exact same numerical angle as the Fore Bearing (FB), with the cardinal quadrant letters reversed: FB = S 40° W ⇒ BB = N 40° E.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: For quadrantal bearings, change N ↔ S and E ↔ W without altering the numerical value.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Compass Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: If the bearings of two lines AB and BC are S 45° E and S 45° E, the ∠ABC equals
bankQuestions.explanation: Bearing of ray BA (Back Bearing of AB) = N 45° W. Bearing of ray BC (Fore Bearing of BC) = S 45° E. Because rays BA and BC point in directly opposing directions along the same line, the interior angle ∠ABC = 180°.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Equal forward bearings mean line ABC is straight, hence ∠ABC = 180°.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Compass Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: If the true bearing of a line is 127° and declination is 2° W, the magnetic bearing equals
bankQuestions.explanation: True Bearing (TB) = Magnetic Bearing (MB) − Declination (W). 127° = MB − 2° ⇒ MB = 127° + 2° = 129°.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: TB = MB ± Declination (+ for East, − for West). Therefore MB = TB + Declination(West).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Compass Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: If the bearing of two lines AB and CB are S 45° E and N 45° W, the angle ABC equals
bankQuestions.explanation: Back Bearing of AB (ray BA) = N 45° W. Bearing of ray BC (opposite to given ray CB = N 45° W) = S 45° E. Rays BA and BC form opposite directions along the straight line passing through B, so ∠ABC = 180°.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Notice given lines are AB and CB radiating at B. Ray BA = N 45° W, ray BC = S 45° E. Together they form a straight line (180°).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Compass Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: If bearing of OA = 20° and bearing of OB = 140°, then angle ∠AOB = …
bankQuestions.explanation: Since both lines radiate from the common vertex O: ∠AOB = Bearing(OB) − Bearing(OA) = 140° − 20° = 120°.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: For two lines radiating from the same station in WCB, Included Angle = Greater Bearing − Smaller Bearing.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Compass Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: If bearing of AB = N 50° E and bearing of AC = N 40° W, then ∠BAC = …
bankQuestions.explanation: Both lines radiate from common station A: Ray AB is 50° east of North, Ray AC is 40° west of North. ∠BAC = 50° + 40° = 90°.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: When lines radiate into adjacent NE and NW quadrants from the same station, angle = sum of angles from North.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Compass Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: If the whole circle bearing of a line is 210° 15', its reduced bearing is
bankQuestions.explanation: A WCB of 210° 15' lies in Quadrant III (South-West, between 180° and 270°): RB = WCB − 180° = 210° 15' − 180° = S 30° 15' W.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Quadrant III (180° to 270°): Reduced Bearing = S (WCB − 180°) W.
bankQuestions.topic: Compass Survey - WCB to RB Conversion
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Compass Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: If the whole circle bearing of a line is 180°, its reduced bearing is
bankQuestions.explanation: A Whole Circle Bearing of 180° points due South along the meridian, so its quadrantal notation is simply South (or S 0°).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 0°/360° = North, 90° = East, 180° = South, 270° = West.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Compass Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: In prismatic compass, the 360° or 0° of the Graduation is marked at the ..... end of the graduated circle
bankQuestions.explanation: In a prismatic compass, the graduated aluminum ring is attached to the needle and remains fixed to the magnetic meridian while the compass box rotates. The observer reads the ring through a prism located at the South end of the box when sighting North, so the 0°/360° graduation is marked at the South end.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Prismatic compass: 0°/360° is at South, 90° at West, 180° at North, 270° at East (graduations are inverted).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Compass Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: On the graduated ring of the prismatic compass 90° is marked at ......end of needle
bankQuestions.explanation: Graduations on a prismatic compass ring run clockwise from South (0°). Therefore: South = 0°/360°, West = 90°, North = 180°, East = 270°.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: In Prismatic Compass, 90° is at the West end, NOT East.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Compass Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: The angle which the line of force due to magnetic field at a point makes with the surface of the earth is known as
bankQuestions.explanation: The angle between the Earth's magnetic lines of force and the horizontal surface of the Earth at any given point is called the angle of dip (magnetic inclination).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Angle between magnetic lines of force and earth's horizontal surface = Dip (Magnetic Inclination).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Compass Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: The bearing of a line in the direction of progress of survey is known as
bankQuestions.explanation: The bearing of a survey line taken in the forward direction along which the survey is advancing is termed the Fore bearing (FB).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Direction of progress = Fore Bearing (FB). Reverse direction = Back Bearing (BB).
bankQuestions.topic: Compass Survey - Fore and Back Bearings
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Compass Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: When the magnetic bearing of the sun at noon is 185° 20', the magnetic declination will be
bankQuestions.explanation: At solar noon in the northern hemisphere, the Sun is on the true meridian due True South (TB = 180° 00'): Declination = TB − MB = 180° 00' − 185° 20' = −5° 20' ⇒ 5° 20' West.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: If MB at noon > 180°, declination is West. If MB at noon < 180°, declination is East.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Compass Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: The reduced bearing of a line is N 87° W. Its whole circle bearing (WCB) is
bankQuestions.explanation: N 87° W lies in the fourth quadrant (North-West): WCB = 360° − RB = 360° − 87° = 273°.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Quadrant IV (NW): WCB = 360° − RB.
bankQuestions.topic: Compass Survey - WCB to RB Conversion
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Compass Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: The reduced bearing of a line whose whole circle bearing is 270° is
bankQuestions.explanation: WCB = 270° is due West. Measured from North, it is 90° to the west (N 90° W). Measured from South, it is 90° to the west (S 90° W). Both describe the same bearing line.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 270° represents pure West, expressible as N 90° W or S 90° W.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Compass Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Fore bearing of a line AB is 154° and the back bearing is 334°, then local attraction at that place
bankQuestions.explanation: |Back Bearing − Fore Bearing| = 334° − 154° = 180°. Because the difference between FB and BB is exactly 180°, stations A and B are free from magnetic interference, meaning the local attraction is 0° (nil).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: If |BB − FB| = 180°, both stations are unaffected by local attraction (0° error).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Compass Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: If the quadrantal bearing of a line is N 69° 45' E, its whole circle bearing is....
bankQuestions.explanation: In the first quadrant (North-East), Whole Circle Bearing and Quadrantal Bearing are numerically identical: WCB = QB = 69° 45'.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: In NE quadrant (Quadrant I), WCB = QB.
bankQuestions.topic: Compass Survey - WCB to RB Conversion
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Compass Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: If the quadrantal bearing of a line is S 64° 10' W, its whole circle bearing is.....
bankQuestions.explanation: A bearing in the third quadrant (SW) has its WCB measured clockwise from North through South: WCB = 180° + QB = 180° + 64° 10' = 244° 10'.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: SW quadrant (Quadrant III): WCB = 180° + QB.
bankQuestions.topic: Compass Survey - WCB to RB Conversion
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Compass Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: In surveyor's compass .... points are marked with letters N and S and ..... points are marked with letters E and W
bankQuestions.explanation: In a Surveyor's Compass, the ring is graduated into four 0° to 90° quadrants. The 0° points are marked at North (N) and South (S), and the 90° points are marked at East (E) and West (W).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Surveyor's Compass: 0° at N & S, 90° at E & W. Prismatic Compass: 0° at S, 90° at W, 180° at N, 270° at E.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Compass Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Orientation by ___ is the most accurate method of orientation and is always to preferred.
bankQuestions.explanation: In plane table surveying, orientation by back-sighting (sighting along a previously drawn ray to a known preceding station) is the most accurate and reliable method because it is completely unaffected by local magnetic variations or metallic disturbances.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Orientation by backsighting is the most accurate method of orientation and is always preferred over magnetic orientation.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Planetable Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Centering may be done by means of a.
bankQuestions.explanation: The plumbing fork (or U-fork/U-frame), fitted with a plumb bob on its bottom arm, is the specific surveying accessory used to transfer the plotted ground station mark directly onto the drawing sheet on the plane table.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Plumbing fork (U-frame) with plumb bob is specifically used for centering the plane table over the ground station.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Planetable Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: The working edge of Alidade is known as
bankQuestions.explanation: The beveled, graduated working edge of a plane table alidade along which rays/lines of sight are ruled on the paper is called the fiducial edge.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: The ruling/working edge of an alidade is called the fiducial edge (beveled edge).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Planetable Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: The fiducial edge should be coincident with or parallel to the
bankQuestions.explanation: To prevent graphical plotting errors, the fiducial edge must be parallel to or lie within the vertical plane of sight formed by the alidade's sight vanes (eye vane and object vane).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: The fiducial edge of an alidade must be coincident with or parallel to the vertical plane of sight.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Planetable Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which method is used for balancing the traverse when angular and linear measurements are equally precise
bankQuestions.explanation: Bowditch's rule (compass rule) is applied to balance a closed traverse when linear and angular measurements have been carried out with equal precision. (The Transit rule is applied when angular measurements are more precise than linear measurements).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Equal precision in linear and angular measurements = Bowditch's rule. Angular more precise = Transit rule.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Traverse & Planetable Bank

bankQuestions.question: Bowditch rule is sometimes called
bankQuestions.explanation: Bowditch's rule is commonly known as the Compass rule because it was originally designed for traverses surveyed with a prismatic/surveyor's compass and chain.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Bowditch's rule is also known as the Compass rule.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Traverse & Planetable Bank

bankQuestions.question: Orientation by magnetic needle is sufficiently accurate, provided if there is no ___
bankQuestions.explanation: Orienting a plane table using a magnetic needle (trough compass) is only accurate if the station is completely free from local attraction (magnetic interference caused by power lines, iron pipes, steel structures, or magnetic mineral deposits).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Magnetic orientation fails or gives errors if local attraction is present in the vicinity.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Planetable Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: The first temporary adjustment to be done after setting up the plane table at any station will be
bankQuestions.explanation: The standard sequential order of operations in plane tabling is: Levelling → Centering → Orientation. Levelling is adjusted first so that subsequent horizontal adjustments do not tilt the board and disturb prior centering.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Strict sequence of operations: Levelling first, then Centering, then Orientation.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Planetable Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: In setting up a plane table at any station
options: Centering and levelling both are done simultaneously
bankQuestions.explanation: In actual field practice and according to standard technical exam answer keys, centering and levelling of a plane table are interdependent operations performed simultaneously by adjusting and embedding the tripod legs into the ground.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: In field practice, centering and levelling of the plane table are carried out simultaneously.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Planetable Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: ___ method is suitable for the survey of small areas which can be commanded from a single station
bankQuestions.explanation: The Radiation method is ideal when the survey area is relatively small, unobstructed, and all ground details can be clearly observed and directly measured from a single central instrument setup.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Radiation method: Small area commanded from a single central station. Intersection: Inaccessible or large undulating areas.
bankQuestions.topic: Planetable Survey - Methods of Plane Tabling
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Planetable Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Closing error of a traverse can be calculated by the formula ___, where ΣL is algebraic sum of latitude and ΣD is algebraic sum of departure
bankQuestions.explanation: In any closed traverse, the linear error of closure e is the hypotenuse formed by the total error in latitude (ΣL) and departure (ΣD): e = √((ΣL)² + (ΣD)²).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Closing error formula: e = √((ΣL)² + (ΣD)²). Direction of closing error: tan(θ) = (ΣD) / (ΣL).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Traverse & Planetable Bank

bankQuestions.question: If the WCB of a line is ___, the latitude of the line is positive
bankQuestions.explanation:
Latitude is defined as L = l · cos(θ), where θ is the Whole Circle Bearing (WCB). Latitude represents projection along the North-South axis and is positive (Northing) only in Quadrant I (0° < θ < 90°) and Quadrant IV (270° < θ < 360°).

For θ = 30° (Quadrant I): cos(30°) > 0 ⇒ Latitude is positive.
For θ = 90°: cos(90°) = 0 ⇒ Latitude is zero.
For θ = 135° (Quadrant II) & 180°: cos(θ) < 0 ⇒ Latitude is negative (Southing).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Latitude = l · cos(θ) (Positive in NE and NW quadrants: 0°-90° & 270°-360°). Departure = l · sin(θ) (Positive in NE and SE quadrants: 0°-180°).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Traverse & Planetable Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which process is used for the transmission of radio signals from the satellites into the GPS receiver for position determination?
bankQuestions.explanation: GPS positioning determines receiver coordinates by measuring pseudo-ranges (distances) from multiple satellites with known coordinates, which is the geometric process of trilateration.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: GPS position determination is based on Trilateration (distance intersections), not angular triangulation.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Among the following, which does not come under the components of GIS?
bankQuestions.explanation: The standard five components of a GIS are Hardware, Software, Data, People, and Methods/Procedures. A Compiler is not a core GIS component.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Core GIS components: Hardware, Software, Data, People, and Methods.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which acts as medium for transmitting information from the target to the sensor?
bankQuestions.explanation: In remote sensing fundamentals, the energy source (electromagnetic radiation) acts as the carrier medium transmitting information about the target to the receiving sensor.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Energy source / Electromagnetic radiation transmits spectral reflectance from target to sensor.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which normally includes attribute data?
bankQuestions.explanation: Unlike standalone geometric CAD or raw coordinates, GIS data integrates spatial geometry with descriptive tabular attribute data.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: GIS Data = Spatial Geometry + Tabular Attribute Data.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which is used to put the satellite into Earth Orbit?
bankQuestions.explanation: A rocket / launch vehicle (such as PSLV or GSLV) is used to transport and inject satellites into their targeted Earth orbits.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Launch Vehicle (PSLV, GSLV, Ariane) places satellites in orbit.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which was first Indian remote sensing satellite?
bankQuestions.explanation: Bhaskara-I (launched by ISRO in June 1979, designated Satellite for Earth Observation - SEO-I) was India's first experimental remote sensing satellite.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: First Indian experimental remote sensing satellite = Bhaskara-I (1979). First operational = IRS-1A (1988).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which indicates the object that being studied in remote sensing?
bankQuestions.explanation: In remote sensing systems, the physical entity, surface feature, or ground area under observation is called the target.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: The feature or phenomenon being sensed = Target.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Expansion of GIS:
bankQuestions.explanation: GIS stands for Geographic Information System.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: GIS = Geographic Information System.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: What is meant by the study of something without direct contact?
bankQuestions.explanation: Remote sensing is defined as acquiring information about an object or phenomenon without making physical contact with it.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Gathering data without physical contact = Remote Sensing.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which is an application of GPS for visually impaired in India?
bankQuestions.explanation: Drishti is a dedicated wireless sensor and GPS/GIS-based pedestrian navigation system developed in India for assisting the visually impaired.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Drishti = Indian GPS/wireless pedestrian navigation system for the blind.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which is an application of GPS for visually impaired?
bankQuestions.explanation: MOBIC stands for Mobility of Blind and Elderly People Interacting with Computers, an international GPS-based orientation and navigation aid.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: MOBIC = Mobility of Blind and Elderly People Interacting with Computers.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: How many operational satellites are available in GPS space segment?
bankQuestions.explanation: The baseline nominal design constellation of the GPS space segment consists of 24 operational satellites distributed evenly across 6 orbital planes.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Nominal GPS constellation = 24 satellites in 6 orbital planes (4 satellites per plane inclined at 55°).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Where are the master control stations of control segment located?
bankQuestions.explanation: The Master Control Station (MCS) of the GPS control segment is located at Schriever Space Force Base in Colorado (Colorado Springs, USA).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: GPS Master Control Station (MCS) = Schriever AFB, Colorado Springs, Colorado, USA.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which is the common choice of coordinate for specifying position in global geodesy?
bankQuestions.explanation: Geographic position on the global datum is standardly defined by Latitude, Longitude, and Elevation (ellipsoidal/orthometric height).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Universal geodetic coordinate triple = Latitude (φ), Longitude (λ), Elevation (h).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: What is orbital height for GPS?
bankQuestions.explanation: GPS satellites orbit in Medium Earth Orbit (MEO) at a nominal altitude of approximately 20,180 km (~20,200 km).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: GPS orbital altitude = 20,180 km (approx. 20,200 km), period ~ 11 hr 58 min.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: What is meant by GPS?
bankQuestions.explanation: GPS stands for Global Positioning System.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: NAVSTAR GPS = Navigation System with Timing And Ranging Global Positioning System.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which country developed GPS?
bankQuestions.explanation: The Global Positioning System (NAVSTAR GPS) was developed by the United States Department of Defense.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: GPS = USA. GLONASS = Russia. Galileo = European Union. NavIC/IRNSS = India. BeiDou = China.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: The system that uses the Sun as a source of electromagnetic energy and records the naturally radiated and reflected energy from the object is called:
bankQuestions.explanation: Passive remote sensing systems record radiation provided by natural sources (primarily the Sun or natural thermal emissions), whereas active systems supply their own source of energy (e.g., Radar/LiDAR).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Sun/Natural radiation = Passive remote sensing. Self-illuminating (Radar/LiDAR) = Active remote sensing.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Remote sensing uses which of the following waves in its procedure?
bankQuestions.explanation: Remote sensing operates by measuring and recording electromagnetic waves reflected or emitted from Earth's surface across various spectral bands.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Remote sensing carrier = Electro-magnetic waves (visible, infrared, microwave).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which program is used to determine position of new station with reference to two known points?
bankQuestions.explanation: The Free Station (Resection) program enables setting up the instrument at any unknown position and determining its coordinates by sighting two or more known control points.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Free station = occupying an arbitrary point and determining coordinates from known target sights.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which program is used to determine polygonal distance in total station?
bankQuestions.explanation: The Tie Distance (also called Missing Line Measurement / MLM) program computes the distance, elevation difference, and azimuth between successive points measured in a polygonal sequence.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Tie Distance / Missing Line Measurement = distance between any two target points without occupying them.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which is the total station with latest technology?
bankQuestions.explanation: Modern motorized robotic / automatic total stations (with automatic target recognition and motorized tracking) represent the state-of-the-art.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Automatic / Robotic total stations operate with auto-tracking servomotors.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: What is the disadvantage of total station?
bankQuestions.explanation: The high capital cost of the instrument and maintenance is its primary disadvantage.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Major disadvantage = High instrument cost and skilled personnel requirement.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: What is the advantage of total station?
options: direct observation of points not possible
bankQuestions.explanation: Eliminating manual reading/recording errors provides high-precision coordinates, resulting in greater accuracy in area and volume computations.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Total station advantage = Greater accuracy in coordinate, area, and volume computations.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which is fitted with a total station capable of storing 900 to 10000 points?
bankQuestions.explanation: Total stations are equipped with internal solid-state memory capable of storing between 900 and 10,000 coordinate points.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Onboard internal memory stores 900 to 10,000 survey points.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which are dedicated to the particular instrument and can store and process surveying observation?
bankQuestions.explanation: Electronic data recorders (data collectors / electronic field books) are dedicated units that record, store, and process survey observations.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Data recorder / Electronic field book stores observations and field codes digitally.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Faulty temperature and pressure measurement occurs by which source of error in EDM?
bankQuestions.explanation: Incorrect reading or entering of ambient atmospheric temperature and barometric pressure values into the EDM by the operator constitutes a personal (human) error.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Operator entering wrong temperature/pressure = Personal error in ppm atmospheric correction.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: In which conditions, the LCD screen of total station does not work?
bankQuestions.explanation: Liquid crystals in LCD screens lose their responsiveness and freeze in extreme cold temperatures.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Extreme cold freezes liquid crystal molecules, causing LCD display sluggishness or failure.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which instrument is used to find out the coordinates of a reflection and at the same time measuring the vertical angles?
bankQuestions.explanation: A total station measures the distance to a reflector/prism (reflection) and vertical/horizontal angles simultaneously to compute 3D coordinate positions.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Simultaneous prism distance + vertical angle + horizontal angle = Total Station.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which program is used for setting out points in total station?
bankQuestions.explanation: Stake out (or Setting Out) is the dedicated program used in the field to locate and mark predetermined coordinate points on the ground.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Setting out design coordinates on ground = Stake Out program.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which program is used for erecting perpendicular line to base line [in total station]?
bankQuestions.explanation: The Reference Line program in total station firmware is used to define a baseline and set out or measure points with chainage and perpendicular offset relative to that baseline.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Reference line program = chainage & perpendicular offset relative to a defined baseline.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: The data obtained from total station can be used in which among the following software directly?
bankQuestions.explanation: Surfer is a 3D surface modeling, gridding, and contour mapping software that directly accepts coordinate point files (X, Y, Z) exported from total stations.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Surfer = 3D surface modeling and contouring software using total station ASCII coordinate points.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which among the following doesn't indicate the basic calculation of the total station?
bankQuestions.explanation: The slope distance is directly measured by the instrument's EDM. Horizontal distance, vertical elevation difference, and (X, Y, Z) coordinates are derived calculations computed by the internal processor.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Slope distance is an observed measurement; horizontal distance and coordinates are calculated values.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which of the following indicates the correct set of the combination of total station?
bankQuestions.explanation: A total station specifically combines an electronic theodolite (electronic digital reading circles) with an EDM.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: The precise definition is Electronic Theodolite + EDM.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: When total station is sighted to the target, which of the operation acts first?
bankQuestions.explanation: Aligning the telescope onto the optical center of the retroreflector prism requires primary rotation/alignment along the optical axis.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Target sighting initiates with optical axis rotation toward the prism.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which of the following indicates the formula for converting slope distance to horizontal distance in total station?
bankQuestions.explanation: When the vertical angle is referenced as a zenith angle z, the horizontal distance H is related to the measured slope distance S by H = S sin(z).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Formula: H = S sin(z) and V = S cos(z), where z is the zenith angle.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Vertical angle is measured in the total station as:
bankQuestions.explanation: Modern total stations reference vertical angles from the zenith (0° directly overhead), measuring zenith angle Z (90° at the horizontal plane).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Zenith = 0° (overhead). Horizon = 90°. Nadir = 180° (directly below).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: In total station, data is stored in:
bankQuestions.explanation: The observed angles and distances in a total station are processed and held internally via its microprocessor and onboard data storage.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Primary internal storage and computation is managed directly by the onboard microprocessor.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Combination of electronic theodolite and EDM:
bankQuestions.explanation: A Total Station is an electronic surveying instrument that integrates an electronic transit theodolite with an electronic distance meter (EDM) and an onboard microprocessor.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Electronic Theodolite + EDM + Microprocessor = Total Station.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Microwave EDM instrument requires two instrument stations.
bankQuestions.explanation: Microwave EDM systems (e.g., Tellurometer) require an active transceiver unit at both ends of the line (a Master station and a Remote station), unlike optical EDMs which use a passive retroreflector/prism.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Microwave EDM requires two active operator stations (Master + Remote transceiver).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Geodimeter uses which of the following waves as a carrier wave?
bankQuestions.explanation: Developed by Erik Bergstrand, the Geodimeter was the earliest electro-optical EDM and utilized modulated visible light waves (tungsten/mercury lamps or laser light) as carrier waves.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Geodimeter = Visible light carrier wave. Tellurometer = Microwave carrier wave.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which type of modulation is used in the case of microwave instrument?
bankQuestions.explanation: Microwave electronic distance measurement (EDM) instruments (such as the Tellurometer) employ Frequency Modulation (FM), whereas electro-optical instruments using visible light or infrared (such as the Geodimeter and Distomat) use Amplitude Modulation (AM).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Microwave EDM (Tellurometer) = Frequency Modulation (FM). Light/IR EDM (Geodimeter/Distomat) = Amplitude Modulation (AM).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Modern Survey Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which method is useful for measuring precisely a number of horizontal angle from a single station point in theodolite instrument:
bankQuestions.explanation: The method of reiteration (direction method) is used to measure several angles from a single station by sighting surrounding stations in succession and closing the horizon on the starting station.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Multiple angles from single station = Reiteration (Direction) method.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Theodolite Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which method if the eccentricity of vernier is eliminated by reading both vernier in theodolite:
bankQuestions.explanation: The method of repetition eliminates errors due to eccentricity of verniers and centers by reading both verniers at every step and accumulating the angle around the circle.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Method of repetition eliminates: eccentricity of centers/verniers and graduation errors.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Theodolite Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which method is a single set of observations made for measuring a horizontal angle between any two point at a station:
bankQuestions.explanation: In the ordinary method, a single set of Face Left and Face Right observations is made to measure a horizontal angle between two points without accumulating angles.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Single set of observations between two points = Ordinary method.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Theodolite Bank

bankQuestions.question: What test is that the line of sight perpendicular to the horizontal axis in theodolite:
bankQuestions.explanation: The collimation in azimuth test (collimation test) ensures that the line of sight (line of collimation) is perpendicular to the horizontal (trunnion) axis.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Collimation test = Line of sight ⟂ Trunnion axis. Spire test = Trunnion axis ⟂ Vertical axis.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Theodolite Bank

bankQuestions.question: What test is that the vertical and horizontal cross hair lie in a plane perpendicular to the horizontal axis in theodolite:
bankQuestions.explanation: The cross hair ring test (diaphragm test) verifies that the vertical crosshair lies in a plane truly perpendicular to the horizontal (trunnion) axis.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Cross hair ring test = checks verticality of vertical crosshair.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Theodolite Bank

bankQuestions.question: What is the purpose of focusing in theodolite:
bankQuestions.explanation: Focusing the eyepiece and objective lens brings the target image accurately into the plane of the crosshairs, thereby eliminating parallax.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Focusing eyepiece + objective = Eliminates parallax error.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Theodolite Bank

bankQuestions.question: What is the term, while the vertical circle is on the left of the telescope and the target on the telescope is up in theodolite:
bankQuestions.explanation: When the vertical circle of the instrument is to the left of the observer and the altitude bubble is up, it is known as Face Left, or telescope normal / direct.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Vertical circle on left = Face Left = Telescope Normal / Direct.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Theodolite Bank

bankQuestions.question: What is the term, while the vertical circle is on the right of the telescope and the target on the telescope is down in theodolite:
bankQuestions.explanation: When the vertical circle of a theodolite is on the right of the observer and the bubble/target is down, it is known as Face Right, or telescope inverted / reversed.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Vertical circle on right = Face Right = Telescope Inverted.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Theodolite Bank

bankQuestions.question: What is called the horizontal arm in vernier frame of theodolite instrument:
