bankQuestions.explanation: If the plane table station lies on or near the circle circumscribing the three reference stations (the Great Circle), all rays pass through a common intersection regardless of orientation, making the solution impossible.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 3-point problem fails if station lies ON the Great Circle (circumscribing circle).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Technical Education

bankQuestions.question: Bessel's graphical method for solving the Three-Point Problem is based on the construction of an:
bankQuestions.explanation: Bessel's method is a purely graphical solution based on constructing an inscribed quadrilateral using auxiliary rays.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Bessel's method = Inscribed quadrilateral graphical solution.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: A major source of error in plane tabling that causes the greatest distortion in plotting is:
bankQuestions.explanation: Defective orientation introduces severe angular displacement across the entire map and is by far the most critical observational error in plane tabling.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Defective orientation causes maximum error in plane tabling.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Technical Education

bankQuestions.question: In large-scale plane table mapping (e.g., 1:100), an error in centering of 30 cm on the ground results in a plotting error of:
bankQuestions.explanation: Plotting error = Ground error / Scale = 300 mm / 100 = 3 mm. On a 1:100 map, 3 mm is significant, necessitating precise centering.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Error on paper = Ground error / Scale factor.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: A significant operational limitation of plane table surveying is that it:
options: Cannot be conducted during rainy or humid monsoon weather
Cannot determine boundaries of irregular plots
Requires highly expensive electronic computing batteries
bankQuestions.explanation: Plane table surveying uses exposed drawing sheets on site; rain, heavy dew, or high humidity warps and damages the paper, rendering field work impossible.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Plane table survey is unsuitable in wet, rainy, or windy climates.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: In plane table surveying, field observations and map plotting are carried out:
options: After numerical reduction of field books
bankQuestions.explanation: The hallmark of plane table surveying is that sighting, measuring, and plotting are done simultaneously on site, eliminating the need for a separate numerical field book.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Plane table: Field work and plotting done simultaneously.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: A curved surface on the earth which is at all points perpendicular to the direction of gravity (plumb line) is called a:
bankQuestions.explanation: A level surface is a curved surface concentric with the mean spheroid of the earth, where every point is perpendicular to the plumb line (gravity vector).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Level surface = Normal to plumb line at all points; Horizontal plane = Tangent to level surface.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The vertical distance of a point above or below an assumed datum surface is called its:
bankQuestions.explanation: The elevation or Reduced Level (RL) of a point is its vertical distance above or below the reference datum surface.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Elevation / RL = Vertical height of point above datum.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: In India, the reference datum for the Great Trigonometrical Survey (GTS) is Mean Sea Level (MSL) established at:
bankQuestions.explanation: GTS datum for all levelling in India is the Mean Sea Level determined by continuous tidal observations at Mumbai (formerly Bombay).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Indian GTS Datum = Mean Sea Level at Mumbai.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: The first staff reading taken after setting up a level at any instrument station is always a:
bankQuestions.explanation: A Back Sight (BS) is always the first sight taken after setting up the instrument, directed to a point of known elevation (Bench Mark or Change Point).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Back Sight (BS) = First sight taken on known RL point.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The last staff reading taken before moving a level to a new position is termed:
bankQuestions.explanation: A Fore Sight (FS) is the final sight taken on a point prior to picking up the instrument, signifying the conclusion of that instrument setup.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Fore Sight (FS) = Last staff reading from an instrument setup.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: A point on which both a Fore Sight and a Back Sight are observed to advance the line of levels is called a:
bankQuestions.explanation: A Change Point (CP) or Turning Point (TP) is a stable ground point on which a Fore Sight is read from the old station and a Back Sight is read from the new station.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Change Point = Both FS and BS taken on same point.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: In the Height of Instrument (Collimation) method of levelling, the Height of Instrument (HI) is computed as:
options: RL of Bench Mark + Back Sight (BS)
RL of Bench Mark - Back Sight (BS)
RL of Bench Mark + Fore Sight (FS)
RL of Bench Mark / Back Sight (BS)
bankQuestions.explanation: Height of Instrument (HI) = RL of Bench Mark + Back Sight (BS). The RL of any succeeding point = HI - (IS or FS).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: HI = RL + BS; RL = HI - Staff Reading.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Which arithmetical check applies to the Rise and Fall method of levelling?
bankQuestions.explanation: In the Rise and Fall method, the three-fold check is: ∑BS - ∑FS = ∑Rise - ∑Fall = Last RL - First RL. This provides a complete check on intermediate sights as well.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Rise & Fall check: ∑BS - ∑FS = ∑Rise - ∑Fall = Last RL - First RL.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: The correction for earth's curvature for a sight distance of 'd' kilometres is given by:
bankQuestions.explanation: The curvature of the earth causes the level line to drop below the horizontal line of collimation by Cc = d² / (2R) = 0.0785 d² m, which is always subtractive (-).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Curvature correction = - 0.0785 d² m (Always subtractive).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: Atmospheric refraction causes the line of sight to bend towards the earth, resulting in a refraction correction of:
bankQuestions.explanation: Refraction bends the ray downward, making staff readings appear smaller than actual. Correction Cr = + (1/7) Cc ≈ + 0.0112 d² m, which is additive (+).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Refraction correction Cr = + 0.0112 d² m (Additive, 1/7 of curvature).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The combined correction for curvature and refraction for a sight distance of 'd' km is:
bankQuestions.explanation: Combined correction C = Cc + Cr = - 0.0785 d² + 0.0112 d² = - 0.0673 d² metres.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Combined correction = - 0.0673 d² m (subtractive).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: Reciprocal levelling eliminates the errors caused by:
options: Curvature, refraction, and collimation error simultaneously
bankQuestions.explanation: By balancing readings taken reciprocally across wide rivers or ravines from both banks, reciprocal levelling completely cancels out curvature, atmospheric refraction, and collimation errors.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Reciprocal levelling cancels curvature, refraction, and collimation errors.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: When taking a staff reading on the underside of a bridge girder or roof ceiling (inverted staff), the RL of the point is calculated as:
bankQuestions.explanation: For an inverted staff, the staff reading is negative (-). Elevation = HI - (- Staff Reading) = HI + Staff Reading.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Inverted staff: RL = HI + Staff Reading (staff reading is treated as negative).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The sensitivity of a spirit bubble tube increases with:
options: An increase in the radius of curvature of the internal tube surface
An increase in the viscosity of the bubble liquid
A decrease in the length of the bubble
A smaller diameter of the glass tube
bankQuestions.explanation: Bubble sensitivity increases with a larger radius of curvature (R), longer bubble length, larger tube diameter, smoother glass finish, and lower liquid viscosity.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Sensitivity increases with larger radius of curvature and lower liquid viscosity.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: The vertical distance between two consecutive contour lines on a topographic map is known as:
bankQuestions.explanation: The vertical distance between two successive contour lines is called the contour interval. It is kept constant throughout a given map.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Contour interval = Vertical distance; Horizontal equivalent = Horizontal distance.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: Concentric closed contour lines with higher elevation values inside indicate a:
bankQuestions.explanation: Concentric closed contour loops with elevations increasing progressively toward the center represent a hill peak or mountain summit.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Values increase inward = Hill; Values decrease inward = Depression/Pond.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Concentric closed contour lines with lower elevation values toward the inside represent a:
bankQuestions.explanation: Concentric contours whose values decrease toward the center signify a depression, pond, lake basin, or crater.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Values decrease inward = Depression / Pond.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: Contour lines can unite to form a single continuous line only in the case of a:
bankQuestions.explanation: Contour lines of different elevations coalesce into a single line only where the terrain is a strictly vertical cliff wall.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Contours unite = Vertical cliff; Contours cross each other = Overhanging cliff.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: Contour lines can cross each other only in the exceptional case of an:
bankQuestions.explanation: Contours cross each other only in the case of an overhanging cliff or an underground cavern/cave.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Contours cross = Overhanging cliff or cave.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Contour lines cross ridge and valley lines at an angle of:
bankQuestions.explanation: Because water flows down the steepest path perpendicular to contours, drainage valley lines and watershed ridge lines always cross contour lines at right angles (90°).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Contours cross ridge and valley lines at right angles (90°).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: A level is set up and a Back Sight of 1.250 m is read on a Bench Mark of RL 105.000 m. If a Fore Sight of 2.100 m is read on station B, what is the RL of B?
bankQuestions.rankerTip: HI = RL + BS; Target RL = HI - FS.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: Calculate the combined correction for curvature and refraction for a sight distance of 2 km:
bankQuestions.explanation: Combined correction = - 0.0673 d² = - 0.0673 × (2)² = - 0.2692 metres.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Combined correction C = - 0.0673 d² m. Always subtractive!
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: A theodolite in which the telescope can be revolved through a complete revolution (180°) in the vertical plane about its horizontal axis is known as a:
bankQuestions.explanation: A transit theodolite is one whose telescope can be transited (plunged or reversed) by rotating it through a complete vertical circle about its trunnion axis.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Transit theodolite = Telescope can revolve 180° in vertical plane.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The least count of a standard vernier transit theodolite commonly used in engineering surveying is:
bankQuestions.explanation: A standard engineer's vernier theodolite has its main circle divided into degrees and 20-minute spaces, and the vernier divides 20 minutes into 60 parts, giving a least count of 20 seconds.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Standard Vernier Theodolite least count = 20 seconds.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: In a theodolite, the lower clamp screw and lower tangent screw are used to control the rotation of the:
bankQuestions.explanation: The lower clamp fixes the main horizontal graduated plate to the inner spindle; turning the lower tangent screw rotates the main scale slowly without altering the vernier reading.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Lower clamp fixes the main horizontal circle.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: The operation of revolving the telescope about the vertical axis in the horizontal plane is termed:
bankQuestions.explanation: Revolving the telescope in a horizontal plane about its vertical axis is called swinging. Right swing is clockwise; left swing is counter-clockwise.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Swinging = Horizontal rotation; Transiting = Vertical rotation.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Changing the face of the theodolite (observing on both Face Left and Face Right) completely eliminates:
options: Collimation error and horizontal axis tilt error
Errors due to non-verticality of vertical axis
bankQuestions.explanation: Taking the mean of Face Left and Face Right readings eliminates: (1) line of collimation not perpendicular to horizontal axis, (2) horizontal axis not perpendicular to vertical axis, and (3) index error of vertical circle.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Double face sighting cancels collimation and horizontal axis errors.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: Reading both opposite verniers (Vernier A and Vernier B) in a theodolite eliminates the error due to:
options: Eccentricity of the graduated circle and verniers
bankQuestions.explanation: Taking the average reading of two diametrically opposite verniers (A and B at 180° apart) eliminates error caused by eccentricity of the centers of the inner and outer spindles.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Reading opposite verniers eliminates eccentricity of circle.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: Which method of horizontal angle measurement is preferred when several stations radiate from a single instrument position?
bankQuestions.explanation: The reiteration method (method of series) is ideal when several angles are to be measured around a single station, ending with closing the horizon on the starting station.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Reiteration = Multiple angles around a central station.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The Repetition method of angle measurement with a theodolite is specifically adopted to eliminate:
options: Errors due to imperfect graduations of the circle
bankQuestions.explanation: In the repetition method, the angle is measured several times on successive parts of the graduated circle and divided by the number of repetitions, eliminating graduation errors.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Repetition method eliminates graduation errors of the circle.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: The projection of a survey line on the true North-South meridian line is called its:
bankQuestions.explanation: Latitude of a line is its orthographic projection on the reference North-South meridian. Northing is positive (+) and Southing is negative (-): Latitude = l cos θ.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Latitude = l cos θ (North-South projection); Departure = l sin θ (East-West projection).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: The projection of a survey line on the reference East-West line perpendicular to the meridian is called its:
bankQuestions.explanation: Departure is the projection of a survey line on the axis perpendicular to the meridian (East-West line). Easting is positive (+) and Westing is negative (-): Departure = l sin θ.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Departure = l sin θ.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: In Bowditch's rule for balancing a closed traverse, the correction applied to the latitude of any line is proportional to:
options: The square of the line length
bankQuestions.explanation: Under Bowditch's rule (Compass rule), correction to latitude of a line = Total error in latitude × (Length of that line / Perimeter of traverse).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Bowditch rule: Correction ∝ Length of line.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: In the Transit rule for balancing a theodolite traverse, corrections are distributed proportional to the:
options: Latitude or departure of the individual line
Square root of the line length
bankQuestions.explanation: The transit rule is used when angular measurements are more precise than linear measurements; corrections to latitude are proportional to the latitude of the line, and to departure proportional to departure.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Transit rule: Correction to latitude ∝ |Latitude|; Correction to departure ∝ |Departure|.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: In tacheometric surveying, an anallatic lens introduced between the objective and diaphragm is a:
options: Convex lens that makes the additive constant zero
Concave lens that doubles the multiplying constant
Plano-convex lens that corrects spherical aberration
bankQuestions.explanation: An anallatic lens (invented by Porro) is an internal convex lens placed between the object glass and eyepiece so that the vertex of the measuring angle falls at the center of the instrument, making additive constant C = (f + d) = 0.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Anallatic lens is CONVEX; makes additive constant C = 0.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The standard value of the multiplying constant (f / i) in an ordinary surveying tacheometer is:
bankQuestions.explanation: Tacheometers are manufactured so that the focal length f and stadia wire interval i have a ratio k = f / i = 100.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Multiplying constant k = 100; Additive constant C = 0 (with anallatic lens).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: When sighting a vertical staff with a tacheometer at an angle of elevation 'θ', the horizontal distance 'D' is given by:
options: k s cos² θ + C cos θ
k s sin² θ + C sin θ
bankQuestions.explanation: For inclined line of sight with staff held vertically: Horizontal distance D = k s cos² θ + C cos θ, where s is staff intercept.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Horizontal distance: D = k s cos² θ + C cos θ.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: For a standard 30-metre chain, the radius 'R' of a 1-degree curve is approximately:
bankQuestions.explanation: R = (30 × 180) / (π × 1°) = 1718.87 m ≈ 1719 m. Radius R = 1719 / D metres for a 30 m chain.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 30 m chain: R = 1719 / D; 20 m chain: R = 1146 / D.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: For a 20-metre chain, the radius 'R' of a 1-degree curve is approximately:
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 20 m chain: R = 1146 / D.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Rankine's method for setting out circular curves using a theodolite and tape is based on:
bankQuestions.explanation: Rankine's method of tangential angles uses the theodolite to lay off deflection angles δ = 1718.87 (c / R) minutes and a chain or tape to measure chord lengths.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Rankine's method = Deflection angle method (theodolite and tape).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: In a horizontal line of sight using an anallatic tacheometer (k = 100, C = 0), the staff intercept 's' is read as 1.00 m. What is the horizontal distance to the staff?
bankQuestions.rankerTip: With anallatic lens, C = 0; D = 100 × s.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: For a standard 30 m chain, what is the approximate radius of curvature 'R' for a 1° circular curve?
bankQuestions.explanation: For a 30 m chain, Radius R ≈ 1718.9 / D = 1719 / 1 ≈ 1719 metres.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Formula: R = 1719 / D (30 m chain); R = 1146 / D (20 m chain).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: A Total Station combines in a single integrated electronic instrument:
options: Electronic theodolite, EDM, microprocessor, and data collector
Dumpy level, optical square, and GPS antenna
Plane table, alidade, and prismatic compass
bankQuestions.explanation: A Total Station integrates an electronic digital theodolite, an electro-optical distance meter (EDM), an internal microprocessor, and electronic storage memory in a single unit.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Total Station = Electronic Theodolite + EDM + Microprocessor + Data Logger.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The carrier waves utilized in infrared Electronic Distance Measurement (EDM) instruments are produced by:
bankQuestions.explanation: Modern compact infrared EDMs use a Gallium Arsenide (GaAs) semiconductor diode to emit infrared carrier waves of wavelength approx 0.9 micrometres.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Infrared EDM uses Gallium Arsenide (GaAs) diode.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: The corner-cube retro-reflector prism used with Total Stations reflects incoming light rays:
options: Strictly parallel to the incident path regardless of alignment angle
bankQuestions.explanation: A corner-cube prism has three mutually perpendicular reflecting surfaces that return the reflected beam exactly parallel to the incoming beam, even if the prism is slightly misaligned.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Corner cube retro-reflector returns beam parallel to incident path.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Town Planning Surveyor

bankQuestions.question: The onboard software program 'REM' in a Total Station stands for:
bankQuestions.explanation: REM stands for Remote Elevation Measurement. It allows measuring the height of inaccessible points (e.g., overhead high-tension power lines, building tops) without placing a prism on the target.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: REM = Remote Elevation Measurement (inaccessible heights).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The onboard program 'MLM' in a Total Station is used to determine:
options: Distance and gradient between two remote target points without setting up at either (Missing Line Measurement)
bankQuestions.explanation: MLM stands for Missing Line Measurement. It computes the horizontal distance, slope distance, and slope percentage between any two target prisms sighted from the instrument.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: MLM = Missing Line Measurement (distance between two targets).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: The process of setting up a Total Station at an arbitrary uncoordinated station and determining its coordinates by sighting two or more known reference stations is called:
bankQuestions.explanation: Free Station or Resection allows the surveyor to set up the Total Station anywhere with good visibility and compute the instrument station coordinates by sighting 2 or more known control points.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Free Station / Resection = Determines instrument coordinates from known targets.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Town Planning Surveyor

bankQuestions.question: The Space Segment of the Global Positioning System (GPS / NAVSTAR) consists of a nominal constellation of:
options: 24 operational satellites arranged in 6 orbital planes
bankQuestions.explanation: The baseline GPS space segment consists of at least 24 operational satellites distributed in 6 orbital planes inclined at 55° to the equator at an altitude of 20,200 km.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: GPS constellation = Minimum 24 satellites in 6 orbital planes at 20,200 km altitude.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: To determine the 3D position (X, Y, Z coordinates) and eliminate receiver clock error, a GPS receiver requires signals from a minimum of:
bankQuestions.explanation: Four satellites are needed: three to resolve the spatial coordinates (X, Y, Z) via trilateration, and the fourth to solve for receiver clock bias error.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Minimum 4 satellites needed for 3D GPS positioning.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: The fundamental positioning principle on which GPS functions is:
bankQuestions.explanation: GPS positioning is based on satellite trilateration, where distances (pseudo-ranges) from satellites to the receiver are computed using signal travel time (Distance = Speed of Light × Time).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: GPS works on the principle of Trilateration (distance measurement).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Town Planning Surveyor

bankQuestions.question: India's independent regional satellite navigation system developed by ISRO is named:
bankQuestions.explanation: NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation), officially Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (IRNSS), is ISRO's constellation of 7 satellites providing regional positioning.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: India's satellite navigation system = NavIC (IRNSS, 7 satellites).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Differential GPS (DGPS) achieves high accuracy by:
options: Using a stationary base receiver at a known point to transmit error corrections to a rover receiver
Using multiple frequencies on a single mobile unit
bankQuestions.explanation: DGPS uses a base station at an established benchmark to calculate atmospheric and orbital pseudo-range errors and transmits real-time differential corrections to mobile rover receivers.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: DGPS uses a known base station to transmit real-time corrections to a rover.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: Real-Time Kinematic (RTK) GPS surveying achieves centimeter-level precision primarily by measuring:
bankQuestions.explanation: RTK achieves centimeter accuracy by tracking carrier phase cycles (L1/L2 wavelengths of ~19 cm and ~24 cm) in real time between base and rover receivers.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: RTK GPS uses carrier-phase measurements for centimeter precision.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Town Planning Surveyor

bankQuestions.question: In Geographic Information Systems (GIS), the two primary spatial data models are:
bankQuestions.explanation: Spatial data in GIS is represented either as Vector data (points, lines, polygons defined by coordinates) or Raster data (regular grid of cells/pixels with values).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: GIS spatial data = Vector (points/lines/polygons) and Raster (grid cells).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: In remote sensing, a sensor that generates its own source of electromagnetic energy to illuminate the target is called an:
bankQuestions.explanation: Active sensors (e.g., Radar, LiDAR) provide their own illumination source and measure the backscattered energy, operating day or night independent of sunlight.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Active sensors (LiDAR, Radar) emit own energy; Passive sensors rely on solar light.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: A polar planimeter is an instrument used exclusively for measuring the:
options: Area of irregular figures plotted on paper
bankQuestions.explanation: A planimeter (invented by Amsler) is a mechanical drafting instrument used for integrating and calculating the surface area of irregular two-dimensional plane figures on maps.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Planimeter = Measures irregular area on paper.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Town Planning Surveyor

bankQuestions.question: The area formula for an Amsler polar planimeter is given by:
bankQuestions.explanation: Planimeter formula: A = M (F - I ± 10N + C), where M is multiplying constant, F and I are final and initial wheel readings, N is number of revolutions of counting disc, and C is zero circle constant (added only when anchor point is inside the figure).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Planimeter area: A = M (F - I ± 10N + C). C is added when anchor point is inside.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The box sextant is a reflecting survey instrument that measures horizontal and vertical angles up to a maximum of:
bankQuestions.explanation: Although the graduated arc of a box sextant is one-sixth of a circle (60°), by the principle of double reflection it can measure angles up to twice this arc, i.e., up to 120°.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Box sextant measures angles up to 120° (Double reflection principle).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: The Abney level is a lightweight handheld instrument combining a spirit level and a:
options: Clinometer graduated arc for measuring vertical angles and slopes
bankQuestions.explanation: An Abney level combines a sighting tube, a semi-circular graduated arc (clinometer), and a reversible spirit bubble to measure slopes, gradients, and vertical angles.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Abney level = Measures vertical angles, slopes, and road gradients.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Town Planning Surveyor

bankQuestions.question: A Ceylon Ghat Tracer is specifically employed in field surveying for:
options: Setting out road gradients and hill railway alignments
bankQuestions.explanation: The Ceylon Ghat Tracer is a simple instrument used for setting out gradients and locating grade contours for roads, bridle paths, and railways in mountainous hill country (ghats).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Ceylon Ghat Tracer = Setting out road and railway gradients in hilly ghats.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: A Pantograph is a drafting instrument constructed on the geometric principle of a:
options: Parallelogram of articulated linkages for enlarging or reducing plans
bankQuestions.explanation: A pantograph consists of four jointed wooden or brass bars connected in a parallelogram, used to mechanically enlarge or reduce plans and maps to scale.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Pantograph = Enlarging and reducing drawings mechanically (parallelogram linkages).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD, which function key is used to toggle Ortho mode On or Off?
bankQuestions.explanation: F8 toggles Ortho mode, which restricts cursor movement strictly to horizontal and vertical directions (0°, 90°, 180°, and 270°).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: F8 = Ortho mode (horizontal/vertical lines only).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Which function key toggles Object Snap (OSNAP) On or Off in AutoCAD?
bankQuestions.explanation: F3 turns Object Snap (OSNAP) on or off, allowing the cursor to lock onto precise geometric points like endpoints, midpoints, and centers.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: F3 = OSNAP toggle; F11 = Object Snap Tracking toggle.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD, the coordinate format '@50,30' represents which coordinate entry method?
bankQuestions.explanation: The '@' symbol denotes relative coordinates measured from the last point entered. '@50,30' specifies 50 units along X and 30 units along Y from the previous position.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: '@X,Y' = Relative Cartesian; '@dist<angle' = Relative Polar; 'X,Y' = Absolute.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Civil

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD, the coordinate entry format '@100<45' specifies:
options: A point at a distance of 100 units at an angle of 45° counter-clockwise from positive X-axis
A point at coordinates X=100, Y=45
A point 45 units away at 100° slope
bankQuestions.explanation: '@100<45' is relative polar coordinate syntax specifying a distance of 100 units at an angle of 45° measured counter-clockwise from the positive horizontal X axis.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Relative Polar: @distance<angle. Standard angles measure counter-clockwise.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Which AutoCAD command allows drawing a continuous sequence of line or arc segments that behaves as a single unified object?
bankQuestions.explanation: PLINE (Polyline) creates a 2D polyline consisting of connected line or arc segments treated as a single unified selectable entity.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: PLINE creates a single continuous entity; LINE creates independent segments.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: Which modify command in AutoCAD rounds off the intersection of two lines with a specified circular arc radius?
bankQuestions.explanation: FILLET rounds or fillets the edges of two intersecting lines or objects with an arc of specified radius. A fillet with radius 0 creates a clean sharp corner.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: FILLET = Rounded corners with radius R (R=0 gives sharp corner); CHAMFER = Beveled angled corner.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Civil

bankQuestions.question: To trim objects in AutoCAD, which keyboard shortcut command is used?
bankQuestions.explanation: TR (TRIM) trims objects to meet the cutting edges of other intersecting objects.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: TR = TRIM; EX = EXTEND; O = OFFSET; F = FILLET.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD, which command creates concentric circles, parallel lines, and parallel curves at a specified distance?
bankQuestions.explanation: The OFFSET command creates a new object whose shape parallels the original at a designated offset distance or through a specified point.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: OFFSET (O) creates parallel lines or concentric circles.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: Which AutoCAD command breaks a compound entity like a block, polyline, or dimension into its constituent basic geometry?
bankQuestions.explanation: EXPLODE (shortcut X) deconstructs complex compound objects such as polylines, blocks, hatches, and dimensions into their independent primitive elements.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: EXPLODE (X) breaks blocks and polylines into individual components.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Civil

bankQuestions.question: What is the function of the Defpoints layer created automatically in an AutoCAD drawing?
options: It stores dimension definition points and does not print or plot
It holds the default title block
bankQuestions.explanation: The Defpoints layer is created automatically by AutoCAD when dimensions are inserted. Entities on this layer are visible on screen but are non-plottable (never print).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Defpoints layer never plots/prints.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Which command in AutoCAD removes unused named objects such as unused layers, blocks, and linetypes to purge drawing database size?
bankQuestions.explanation: PURGE (PU) removes unused definitions such as empty layers, unreferenced blocks, dimension styles, and linetypes to reduce file size and clean the database.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: PURGE (PU) deletes unused blocks, layers, and styles.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD, the default extension for a drawing template file is:
bankQuestions.explanation: .dwt is the file format for AutoCAD Drawing Templates containing preset units, layers, borders, and styles. .dwg is a standard drawing file.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: .dwt = Drawing Template; .dwg = Drawing file; .dxf = Drawing Exchange Format.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Civil

bankQuestions.question: Which AutoCAD function key toggles the Grid Display on or off?
bankQuestions.explanation: F7 toggles the background drafting grid display On or Off in the drawing area.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: F7 = Grid display; F9 = Snap mode.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Which AutoCAD command writes an existing internal block or selected geometry to an external .dwg file on disk?
bankQuestions.explanation: WBLOCK (Write Block) saves selected entities or an existing internal block as an independent external .dwg drawing file on disk for use across projects.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: BLOCK = Internal to drawing; WBLOCK = External .dwg file.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD, which command is used to display the DesignCenter palette?
bankQuestions.explanation: Ctrl + 2 (or command ADCENTER) opens AutoCAD DesignCenter, which enables browsing and dragging blocks, layers, and styles from other drawings.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Ctrl+1 = Properties; Ctrl+2 = DesignCenter; Ctrl+3 = Tool Palettes; Ctrl+9 = Command Line.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Civil

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD, the command 'HATCH' is used to:
options: Fill an enclosed boundary with a crosshatch pattern, solid color, or gradient
bankQuestions.explanation: HATCH (H) fills an enclosed area or selected boundary objects with a specified hatch pattern (e.g. ANSI31, AR-CONC), solid fill, or gradient.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: HATCH (H) fills enclosed areas with standard drafting patterns.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The STRETCH command in AutoCAD requires selecting objects using which selection window method?
options: Crossing Window (green window dragged from right to left)
Standard Window (blue window left to right)
bankQuestions.explanation: STRETCH (S) requires a Crossing Window or Crossing Polygon to capture vertices that need to be stretched while leaving non-selected vertices anchored.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: STRETCH requires a Crossing Window (green window).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: Which system variable in AutoCAD prevents mirrored text from appearing backwards/inverted when using the MIRROR command?
bankQuestions.explanation: Setting system variable MIRRTEXT = 0 retains text readability (direction) when mirroring objects, preventing the letters from being flipped backwards.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: MIRRTEXT = 0 keeps text readable when mirroring; MIRRTEXT = 1 mirrors text letters.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Civil

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD layout space, which command is used to create floating viewports showing model space geometry?
bankQuestions.explanation: MVIEW (Make View) or VPORTS creates rectangular or polygonal layout viewports in Paper Space to display and scale views of the Model Space drawing.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: MVIEW / VPORTS creates viewports in paper space layouts.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Which command in AutoCAD regenerates the entire drawing and recalculates screen coordinates to smooth out pixelated circles and arcs?
bankQuestions.explanation: REGEN (Regenerate) regenerates the entire drawing from drawing database coordinates, recalculating screen display coordinates to render smooth curves.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: REGEN (RE) recalculates drawing display coordinates; REDRAW only cleans screen blips.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: In Kerala land measurements, 1 Cent of land is equivalent to approximately:
bankQuestions.explanation: 1 Cent = 1/100 of an Acre = 40.4686 m² ≈ 40.47 m² = 435.6 sq ft.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 Cent = 40.47 m² = 435.6 sq ft; 100 Cents = 1 Acre = 4046.86 m².
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: How many acres are there in 1 Hectare?
bankQuestions.explanation: 1 Hectare = 10,000 m² = 2.471 Acres = 247.1 Cents.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 Hectare = 10,000 m² = 2.471 Acres.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: One Metric Horsepower (HP) is equivalent to:
bankQuestions.explanation: 1 Metric HP = 75 kg·m/s = 735.49875 Watts ≈ 735.5 W. In the British imperial system, 1 HP = 550 ft·lb/s = 746 Watts.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Metric HP = 735.5 W; British HP = 746 W.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: The relation between Celsius (°C), Fahrenheit (°F), and Kelvin (K) temperature scales is given by:
bankQuestions.explanation: The standard fundamental thermometric conversion relation is C / 5 = (F - 32) / 9 = (K - 273.15) / 5.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: At what temperature do the Celsius and Fahrenheit temperature scales read identical values?
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Celsius and Fahrenheit scales are equal at -40°.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: The commercial unit of electrical energy, 1 kilowatt-hour (1 kWh or 1 unit), equals:
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 unit of electricity = 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ Joules.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: The density of standard structural steel is approximately:
bankQuestions.explanation: The nominal density of structural steel is 7850 kg/m³ (7.85 g/cm³). Plain concrete is ~2400 kg/m³ and water is 1000 kg/m³.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Steel density = 7850 kg/m³; RCC = 2500 kg/m³; Water = 1000 kg/m³.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The mechanical advantage (MA) of an ideal simple machine is defined as the ratio of:
options: Distance moved by effort to distance moved by load
bankQuestions.explanation: Mechanical Advantage (MA) = Load (W) / Effort (P). Velocity Ratio (VR) = Distance moved by effort / Distance moved by load.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: MA = Load / Effort; VR = Effort Distance / Load Distance; Efficiency η = MA / VR.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: A wheelbarrow is an example of which class of lever?
options: Second class lever (Load is between Fulcrum and Effort)
bankQuestions.explanation: In a second class lever, the load is situated between the fulcrum and effort (e.g. wheelbarrow, nutcracker, bottle opener). Its MA is always > 1.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Class 1: Fulcrum in middle (crowbar, scissors); Class 2: Load in middle (wheelbarrow); Class 3: Effort in middle (tongs).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: What is the area of a right-angled triangle with base 12 cm and hypotenuse 13 cm?
bankQuestions.explanation: By Pythagoras theorem, height = √(13² - 12²) = √(169 - 144) = √25 = 5 cm. Area = 1/2 × base × height = 1/2 × 12 × 5 = 30 cm².
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Pythagorean triplet (5, 12, 13). Area = 1/2 × 12 × 5 = 30 cm².
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The volume of a right circular cone of radius 'r' and height 'h' is given by:
bankQuestions.explanation: The volume of a cone is one-third the volume of a cylinder with the same base and height: V = (1/3) π r² h.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Cone volume = 1/3 π r² h; Cylinder = π r² h; Sphere = 4/3 π r³.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: The total surface area of a solid hemisphere of radius 'r' is:
bankQuestions.explanation: Curved surface area = 2 π r²; Flat circular base area = π r². Total surface area = 2 π r² + π r² = 3 π r².
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Solid hemisphere: Curved area = 2πr²; Total area = 3πr².
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: The sum of all interior angles of a regular hexagon is:
bankQuestions.explanation: Sum of interior angles of polygon = (n - 2) × 180°. For a hexagon (n = 6): (6 - 2) × 180° = 4 × 180° = 720°.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Interior angles sum = (n - 2) × 180°. Hexagon (n=6) = 720°; Pentagon (n=5) = 540°.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The trigonometric expression (1 + tan² θ) is identically equal to:
bankQuestions.explanation: Standard trigonometric identity: 1 + tan² θ = sec² θ. Similarly: sin² θ + cos² θ = 1, and 1 + cot² θ = cosec² θ.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 + tan² θ = sec² θ; 1 + cot² θ = cosec² θ; sin² θ + cos² θ = 1.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: The property of a metal that enables it to be drawn into thin wires without breaking is known as:
bankQuestions.explanation: Ductility is the mechanical property that permits a material to undergo significant plastic deformation under tensile stress, allowing it to be drawn into wires.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Ductility = Drawn into wires; Malleability = Hammered into thin sheets.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: Which heat treatment process is carried out to relieve internal stresses and soften hardened steel?
bankQuestions.explanation: Annealing involves heating steel to above its critical temperature, soaking, and slowly cooling in the furnace to soften it, refine grain structure, and relieve internal stresses.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Annealing = Softens metal and relieves internal stress; Tempering = Reduces brittleness.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Latent heat of fusion of ice at standard atmospheric pressure is:
bankQuestions.explanation: The latent heat of fusion of ice is 80 calories per gram (approx. 336 kJ/kg). The latent heat of vaporization of water is 540 cal/g (2260 kJ/kg).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Latent heat of fusion of ice = 80 cal/g; Vaporization of water = 540 cal/g.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: Two resistors of 6 ohms and 3 ohms are connected in parallel. What is their equivalent resistance?
bankQuestions.explanation: For parallel resistors: 1 / R_eq = 1/R1 + 1/R2 = 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/6 + 2/6 = 3/6 = 1/2. Therefore, R_eq = 2 ohms.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Parallel resistors: R = (R1 × R2) / (R1 + R2) = (6 × 3) / (6 + 3) = 18 / 9 = 2 Ω.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: A body of mass 10 kg is lifted to a height of 5 metres. What is its potential energy? (Take g = 9.8 m/s²)
bankQuestions.explanation: Potential Energy (PE) = m × g × h = 10 kg × 9.8 m/s² × 5 m = 490 Joules.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The speed of a train traveling at 72 km/h expressed in metres per second (m/s) is:
bankQuestions.explanation: To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18: 72 × (5 / 18) = 4 × 5 = 20 m/s.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: km/h to m/s: Multiply by 5/18. 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: Convert a vehicle velocity of 108 km/h into metres per second (m/s):
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Conversion factor from km/h to m/s is 5/18.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Granite and basalt are examples of which geological class of building stones?
bankQuestions.explanation: Granite (plutonic) and basalt (volcanic) are formed by the cooling and solidification of molten magma or lava, classifying them as igneous rocks.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Granite & Basalt = Igneous; Sandstone & Limestone = Sedimentary; Marble & Slate = Metamorphic.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Marble is formed through the metamorphic recrystallization of:
bankQuestions.explanation: Marble is a metamorphic rock formed when sedimentary limestone or dolomite undergoes intense heat and pressure recrystallization.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Limestone metamorphism -> Marble; Sandstone metamorphism -> Quartzite; Shale -> Slate.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: On Mohs Scale of Mineral Hardness, which mineral has a hardness rating of 1 (softest) and which has 10 (hardest)?
bankQuestions.explanation: Mohs hardness scale ranges from 1 for Talc (softest mineral) to 10 for Diamond (hardest naturally occurring substance).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Mohs scale: 1 Talc, 2 Gypsum, 3 Calcite, 7 Quartz, 9 Corundum, 10 Diamond.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: A good building stone should have a maximum percentage of water absorption after 24 hours of immersion not exceeding:
bankQuestions.explanation: A sound building stone should not absorb more than 5% of its dry weight in water after 24 hours immersion. Stones absorbing over 10% are rejected.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Building stone water absorption must be ≤ 5%.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The standard modular dimensions of a building brick as prescribed by the Bureau of Indian Standards (IS 1077) are:
bankQuestions.explanation: The standard modular brick size is 190 mm × 90 mm × 90 mm (19 cm × 9 cm × 9 cm). With a 10 mm mortar joint, nominal size is 200 mm × 100 mm × 100 mm.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Standard modular brick = 190 × 90 × 90 mm; Nominal size with mortar = 200 × 100 × 100 mm.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: The primary constituent of good brick earth responsible for preventing shrinkage, cracking, and warping is:
bankQuestions.explanation: Silica constitutes 50-60% of brick earth. It prevents cracking, shrinking, and warping of raw bricks during drying and preserves their shape.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Silica (50-60%) prevents shrinkage and cracking; Alumina (20-30%) imparts plasticity.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: In brick manufacturing, what is the role of alumina (clay)?
options: It imparts plasticity to the earth for easy moulding
It imparts deep cherry red color
It fuses silica at high temperatures
bankQuestions.explanation: Alumina (20-30%) is the principal clay constituent that gives plasticity to the soil so it can be moulded into shape without crumbling.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Alumina imparts plasticity. Excess alumina causes shrinkage and warping on drying.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The depression or indentation provided on the top face of a modular brick is called the:
bankQuestions.explanation: The shallow depression formed on the top face of a hand-moulded brick (depth 10 mm to 20 mm) is called the frog. It creates a key for mortar and displays the maker's name.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Frog = Indentation on top face of brick (10-20 mm depth) to key mortar.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: A First Class brick must possess a minimum compressive crushing strength of:
bankQuestions.explanation: As per IS 1077, First Class bricks must have a minimum crushing strength of 10.5 N/mm² and water absorption ≤ 20%. Second Class requires 7.0 N/mm².
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Class I brick strength ≥ 10.5 N/mm²; Class II ≥ 7.0 N/mm²; Class III ≥ 3.5 N/mm².
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: Which brick bond consists of alternate courses of headers and stretchers and is considered the strongest bond in brick masonry?
bankQuestions.explanation: English bond features alternate courses of headers and stretchers with a queen closer placed next to the quoin header. It is the strongest and most widely used masonry bond.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: English bond = Alternate courses of headers and stretchers (Strongest bond).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: In brick masonry, a brick cut longitudinally into two equal halves of width 45 mm is known as a:
bankQuestions.explanation: A Queen closer is obtained by cutting a standard brick along its entire longitudinal centerline, resulting in two pieces of dimensions 190 mm × 45 mm × 90 mm.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Queen closer = Cut along length; King closer = Triangular cut from header midpoint to stretcher midpoint.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: Fat lime (quick lime) is obtained by the calcination of:
bankQuestions.explanation: Fat lime (also known as rich lime, white lime, or high calcium lime) is produced by calcining pure limestone containing 95% or more calcium carbonate.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Fat lime = From pure limestone; slakes vigorously, used for whitewashing.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: Which ingredient is added during the final grinding of cement clinker to retard its flash setting time?
bankQuestions.explanation: Gypsum (raw calcium sulphate, 2% to 3%) is ground with clinker to react with tricalcium aluminate (C₃A), preventing flash setting and extending the initial setting time.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Gypsum retards cement flash setting, ensuring initial setting time ≥ 30 mins.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Which Bogue's compound in Portland cement hydrates rapidly and is primarily responsible for early strength development (within the first 7 days)?
bankQuestions.explanation: Tricalcium silicate (C₃S, 40-50%) hydrates rapidly and generates high early strength during the first 7 to 14 days.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: C₃S = Early strength (7 days); C₂S = Progressive ultimate strength (28+ days).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: The standard initial and final setting times of Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC) as per IS 269 are:
bankQuestions.explanation: Standard OPC must have an initial setting time of not less than 30 minutes and a final setting time of not more than 600 minutes (10 hours).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: OPC setting times: Initial ≥ 30 mins; Final ≤ 600 mins (10 hrs).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: Soundness of cement (expansion caused by unslaked free lime) is tested using which laboratory apparatus?
bankQuestions.explanation: Soundness of cement due to free lime is measured using the Le Chatelier split-cylinder apparatus (expansion must not exceed 10 mm for OPC).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Le Chatelier = Soundness (free lime); Vicat = Consistency & setting times.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The standard volumetric mix proportion for M20 grade concrete in nominal mixes is:
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: The phenomenon where sand increases in volume due to the formation of a surface tension water film around sand grains is called:
bankQuestions.explanation: Bulking of sand is the increase in bulk volume of damp fine aggregate caused by surface tension films pushing particles apart. Maximum bulking (20-30%) occurs at 4% to 5% moisture.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Bulking of sand is maximum (20-30%) at 4% to 5% moisture content.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: Steel is universally used as reinforcement in concrete (RCC) primarily because:
options: Steel and concrete have almost identical coefficients of thermal expansion
Steel is cheaper than all other metals
Steel resists tensile stress without bond adhesion
bankQuestions.explanation: Steel and concrete expand and contract together without bond separation because their coefficients of thermal expansion are virtually identical (approx 12 × 10⁻⁶ / °C).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Steel and concrete have nearly identical thermal expansion coefficients.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The central core or innermost fibrous column of an exogenous tree trunk is called the:
bankQuestions.explanation: The pith (or medulla) is the central dark core of the tree formed in the first year of growth, consisting of cellular tissue.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Pith = Central core; Heartwood = Dense inner wood; Sapwood = Outer living wood.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: The defect in timber characterized by radial splits widening from the bark toward the center is called:
bankQuestions.explanation: Star shakes are radial cracks that are wider at the bark and narrow toward the pith, caused by severe frost or intense solar heat shrinking outer wood.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Star shake = Widest at bark; Heart shake = Widest at pith; Cup shake = Along growth rings.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: Dry rot in seasoned timber is caused by fungal attack that reduces the wood to dry powder, commonly occurring in:
options: Damp, unventilated, and dark locations (fungus Merulius lacrymans)
Continuous full submersion in fresh water
bankQuestions.explanation: Dry rot is caused by wood-destroying fungi (chiefly Merulius lacrymans) in damp, stagnant, dark, poorly ventilated conditions, converting wood into dry powdery dust.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Dry rot = Caused by fungus in damp unventilated areas, turns wood to dry powder.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The relationship between Duty (D in hectares/cumec), Delta (Δ in metres), and Base period (B in days) is given by:
bankQuestions.explanation: Delta Δ (depth in metres) = (8.64 × B) / D, where B is base period in days and D is duty in hectares/cumec. If Δ is in cm: Δ = 864 B / D.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Δ = 8.64 B / D (in metres); Δ = 864 B / D (in centimetres).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: In irrigation engineering, a hydraulic structure where a canal is carried over a natural drainage stream with the drainage High Flood Level (HFL) remaining well below the canal bed is called an:
bankQuestions.explanation: An Aqueduct carries a canal above a drainage stream where the stream flows freely under gravity with its HFL below the canal bed trough.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Canal over stream (free flow) = Aqueduct; Stream over canal (free flow) = Superpassage.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: According to the Indian Roads Congress (IRC), what is the standard carriageway width for a two-lane road without raised kerbs?
bankQuestions.explanation: IRC specifies: Single lane = 3.75 m; Two lane without kerbs = 7.0 m; Two lane with raised kerbs = 7.5 m; Intermediate lane = 5.5 m.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 2-lane without kerb = 7.0 m; 2-lane with kerb = 7.5 m; Single lane = 3.75 m.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The transverse slope provided on the road surface to drain off rainwater towards the side drains is called:
bankQuestions.explanation: Camber is the convexity or cross-fall provided to the road carriageway surface to rapidly drain surface runoff into gutters.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Camber = Cross slope for drainage; Super-elevation = Banking on curves against centrifugal force.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: A Revised Estimate for a civil engineering work is required when the original sanctioned estimate is likely to be exceeded by more than:
bankQuestions.explanation: A Revised Estimate is prepared when the original sanctioned estimate is exceeded by more than 5%, or when the expenditure on materials deviates by more than 10%.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Revised estimate required if cost exceeds sanctioned estimate by > 5%.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: In civil engineering quantity takeoff, what is the standard unit of measurement for plastering and pointing work?
bankQuestions.explanation: Surface finish works such as plastering, pointing, whitewashing, and painting are measured in superficial area: Square metres (m²).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Plastering/Painting/DPC = m²; Brickwork/Earthwork/Concrete = m³.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: If a crop has a base period 'B' of 140 days and the canal duty 'D' is 1000 hectares/cumec, calculate the total delta (depth of water Δ) required:
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Formula: Δ = 8.64 B / D metres = 864 B / D centimetres.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: A survey distance of 180 m was measured using a nominal 20 m metric chain. On testing against a standard steel tape, the chain was found to be 4 cm too long. What is the corrected true distance?
bankQuestions.explanation: True Distance = (Actual Length of Chain / Nominal Length) × Measured Distance = (20.04 / 20) × 180 = 180.36 m. Since the chain is too long, the recorded distance is too short and the correction is positive (+).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Correction is positive when chain is too long. Formula: True = (L'/L) × Measured.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala Water Authority (KWA) Tracer / Overseer

bankQuestions.question: A land parcel was measured with a chain that was 2% too short. If the calculated area from the field notes was 1050 m², what is the true area of the parcel?
bankQuestions.explanation: True Area = (L' / L)² × Measured Area = (0.980)² × 1050 = 1008.4 m². When a chain is too short, the measured area is greater than the true area.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: True Area = (L'/L)² × Measured Area. If chain is short, true area is smaller.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD / Irrigation)

bankQuestions.question: On an engineering survey plan, a line of length 2 cm represents an actual ground distance of 100 metres. What is the Representative Fraction (R.F.) of this drawing?
bankQuestions.explanation: Representative Fraction (R.F.) = Map Distance / Ground Distance = 2 cm / (100 × 100 cm) = 2 / 10000 = 1:5000.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: R.F. numerator is always 1 with identical units in numerator and denominator.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Town Planning Surveyor

bankQuestions.question: In chaining along sloping ground, the horizontal difference in elevation 'h' between chain ends over a slope length of 30 m is 5 m. What is the slope correction to be deducted?
bankQuestions.explanation: Slope correction Ch = h² / (2L) = (5)² / (2 × 30) = 25 / 60 = 0.417 m. Slope correction is always subtractive (negative).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Slope correction Ch ≈ h² / (2L). Always subtract from sloping distance.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tradesman (Survey) / Technical Education

bankQuestions.question: A steel tape of length 30 m standardized under a tension of 80 N is pulled with a field tension of 160 N. Given cross-sectional area A = 3 mm² and E = 2 × 10⁵ N/mm², what is the pull correction?
bankQuestions.explanation: Pull correction Cp = (P - P₀) L / (A E) = (160 - 80) × 30 / (3 × 200000) = (80 × 30) / 600000 = + 0.0040 m. Since applied pull exceeds standard pull, correction is positive.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Cp = (P - P₀) L / (AE). Positive when P > P₀.
bankQuestions.examName: NCVT / CTS All India Trade Test (Surveyor & Draftsman Civil)

bankQuestions.question: The Whole Circle Bearing (WCB) of a survey line is recorded as 162° 00'. What is its corresponding Quadrantal Bearing (Reduced Bearing)?
bankQuestions.explanation: For WCB = 162° 00', the line falls in Quadrant 2. Converting gives Quadrantal Bearing = S 18° 00' E.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Quadrant 1: N θ E; Quadrant 2: S (180°-θ) E; Quadrant 3: S (θ-180°) W; Quadrant 4: N (360°-θ) W.
bankQuestions.examName: NCVT / CTS All India Trade Test (Surveyor & Draftsman Civil)

bankQuestions.question: The magnetic bearing of a baseline is observed as 142° 45'. If the magnetic declination at the survey station is 6° 15' West, calculate the true bearing of the line:
bankQuestions.explanation: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing - Declination (West) = 142° 45' - 6° 15' = 136° 30'. Add East declination, subtract West declination.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing ± Declination (Add East, Subtract West).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tradesman (Survey) / Technical Education

bankQuestions.question: If the Fore Bearing (FB) of line PQ is observed as 341° 30', what is the Back Bearing (BB) of the same line in Whole Circle Bearing?
bankQuestions.explanation: Back Bearing = Fore Bearing ± 180°. Since FB (341° 30') is greater than 180°, BB = 341° 30' - 180° = 161° 30'.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala Water Authority (KWA) Tracer / Overseer

bankQuestions.question: In a closed polygon compass traverse having 8 sides, what is the theoretical sum of all interior angles?
bankQuestions.explanation: Theoretical sum of interior angles for a polygon of n sides = (2n - 4) × 90° = (n - 2) × 180°. For n = 8: (2 × 8 - 4) × 90° = (12) × 90° = 1080°.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Sum of interior angles = (2n - 4) × 90°; Sum of exterior angles = (2n + 4) × 90°.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD / Irrigation)

bankQuestions.question: What is the combined correction for earth's curvature and atmospheric refraction for a staff sight distance of 1.2 km?
bankQuestions.explanation: Combined correction C = - 0.0673 d² = - 0.0673 × (1.2)² = - 0.0969 m. It is always subtractive from the staff reading.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Combined correction C = - 0.0673 d² m (subtractive). Curvature is -0.0785 d², Refraction is +0.0112 d².
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala Water Authority (KWA) Tracer / Overseer

bankQuestions.question: A level is set up and a BS of 1.220 m is read on a Bench Mark of RL 155.000 m. An inverted staff reading of 2.330 m is observed on the soffit of a bridge girder. What is the RL of the bridge soffit?
bankQuestions.explanation: HI = BM RL + BS = 155.000 + 1.220 = 156.220 m. For an inverted staff, reading is negative: RL = HI - (- 2.330) = HI + 2.330 = 156.220 + 2.330 = 158.550 m.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Inverted staff: RL = HI + Staff Reading.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD / Irrigation)

bankQuestions.question: For a standard 30-metre chain, what is the radius of curvature 'R' of a 1-degree circular curve?
bankQuestions.explanation: For a 30 m chain, R = 1718.87 / D ≈ 1719 / 1 ≈ 1719 m. For a 20 m chain, R = 1146 / D.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 30 m chain: R = 1719 / D; 20 m chain: R = 1146 / D.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala Water Authority (KWA) Tracer / Overseer

bankQuestions.question: In a horizontal sight using an anallatic tacheometer with multiplying constant k = 100 and additive constant C = 0, the staff intercept 's' is read as 1.05 m. What is the horizontal distance from instrument to staff?
bankQuestions.explanation: Distance formula D = k s + C = (100 × 1.05) + 0 = 105 m. Anallatic lens eliminates the additive constant C.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: With anallatic lens, D = 100 × s.
bankQuestions.examName: NCVT / CTS All India Trade Test (Surveyor & Draftsman Civil)

bankQuestions.question: A traverse line AB has length 225 m and reduced bearing N 30° E. What are the consecutive coordinates (Latitude and Departure) of the line?
bankQuestions.explanation: Latitude = l cos θ = 225 × cos 30° = 225 × 0.866 = + 194.86 m (Northing). Departure = l sin θ = 225 × sin 30° = 225 × 0.5 = + 112.50 m (Easting).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Latitude = l cos θ; Departure = l sin θ. In NE quadrant, both are positive.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: A residential plot in Kerala has an area of 100 Cents. What is its exact equivalent area in square metres (m²)?
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 Cent = 40.47 m²; 100 Cents = 1 Acre = 4046.86 m².
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala Water Authority (KWA) Tracer / Overseer

bankQuestions.question: Convert a temperature reading of 50°C on the Celsius scale into degrees Fahrenheit (°F):
bankQuestions.rankerTip: C / 5 = (F - 32) / 9. Multiply by 1.8 and add 32.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD / Irrigation)

bankQuestions.question: Two electrical resistors of 10 Ω and 12 Ω are connected in parallel across a circuit. What is the equivalent resistance of the combination?
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Parallel resistance: R = (R1 × R2) / (R1 + R2). Always less than individual resistors.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: A seasonal crop has a base period 'B' of 135 days and the duty of canal water 'D' is 1400 hectares/cumec. Calculate the total depth of water (Delta Δ) required by the crop:
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Δ = 8.64 B / D (in metres); Δ = 864 B / D (in centimetres).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tradesman (Survey) / Technical Education

bankQuestions.question: In the manufacturing of quality building bricks, the constituent Alumina (20-30%) is essential because it:
options: imparts plasticity to the earth for moulding into shape
acts as an accelerator for cement hydration
bankQuestions.explanation: In good brick earth, Alumina (20-30%) imparts plasticity to the earth for moulding into shape.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Silica prevents shrinkage; Alumina gives plasticity; Iron oxide gives red color.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD / Irrigation)

bankQuestions.question: Which Bogue's compound in Portland cement is primarily responsible for fastest reaction with water causing flash setting and high heat of hydration?
bankQuestions.explanation: Tricalcium Aluminate (C₃A) is characterized by fastest reaction with water causing flash setting and high heat of hydration.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: C₃S = Early strength; C₂S = Progressive ultimate strength; C₃A = Flash setting.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Town Planning Surveyor

bankQuestions.question: In the manufacturing of quality building bricks, the constituent Magnesia (<1%) is essential because it:
options: imparts a yellowish tint and reduces shrinkage
acts as an accelerator for cement hydration
bankQuestions.explanation: In good brick earth, Magnesia (<1%) imparts a yellowish tint and reduces shrinkage.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Silica prevents shrinkage; Alumina gives plasticity; Iron oxide gives red color.
bankQuestions.examName: NCVT / CTS All India Trade Test (Surveyor & Draftsman Civil)

bankQuestions.question: Which Bogue's compound in Portland cement is primarily responsible for slow hydration, providing progressive ultimate strength after 14 to 28 days?
bankQuestions.explanation: Dicalcium Silicate (C₂S) is characterized by slow hydration, providing progressive ultimate strength after 14 to 28 days.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: C₃S = Early strength; C₂S = Progressive ultimate strength; C₃A = Flash setting.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: In the manufacturing of quality building bricks, the constituent Lime (<5%) is essential because it:
options: acts as a flux to fuse silica particles during burning
acts as an accelerator for cement hydration
bankQuestions.explanation: In good brick earth, Lime (<5%) acts as a flux to fuse silica particles during burning.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Silica prevents shrinkage; Alumina gives plasticity; Iron oxide gives red color.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD / Irrigation)

bankQuestions.question: Which Bogue's compound in Portland cement is primarily responsible for rapid hydration and development of early strength within 7 to 14 days?
bankQuestions.explanation: Tricalcium Silicate (C₃S) is characterized by rapid hydration and development of early strength within 7 to 14 days.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: C₃S = Early strength; C₂S = Progressive ultimate strength; C₃A = Flash setting.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Town Planning Surveyor

bankQuestions.question: In the manufacturing of quality building bricks, the constituent Silica (50-60%) is essential because it:
options: prevents shrinkage, warping, and cracking during drying
acts as an accelerator for cement hydration
bankQuestions.explanation: In good brick earth, Silica (50-60%) prevents shrinkage, warping, and cracking during drying.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Silica prevents shrinkage; Alumina gives plasticity; Iron oxide gives red color.
bankQuestions.examName: NCVT / CTS All India Trade Test (Surveyor & Draftsman Civil)

bankQuestions.question: Which Bogue's compound in Portland cement is primarily responsible for poor cementing value and lowest contribution to concrete strength?
bankQuestions.explanation: Tetracalcium Aluminoferrite (C₄AF) is characterized by poor cementing value and lowest contribution to concrete strength.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: C₃S = Early strength; C₂S = Progressive ultimate strength; C₃A = Flash setting.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Which survey classification is based on the nature of the field and deals with large water bodies, sounding, and navigation charts?
bankQuestions.explanation: Hydrographic surveying deals with bodies of water for navigation, water supply, harbor works, and sounding to determine underwater depth contours.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Hydrographic survey = Water bodies, tides, soundings, and shorelines.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Surveys conducted to fix boundaries of municipalities, taluks, and village administrative units are termed:
bankQuestions.explanation: Cadastral surveys are legal boundary surveys carried out to establish property boundaries, village boundaries, revenue records, and land transfer documents.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Cadastral survey = Revenue boundaries, land parcels, and property ownership records.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala Land Records Technical Exam

bankQuestions.question: In survey networks, a well-conditioned triangle is defined as one whose angles are strictly between:
bankQuestions.explanation: A well-conditioned triangle has angles between 30° and 120°. An equilateral triangle with all angles 60° is the most ideal well-conditioned triangle.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Ideal well-conditioned triangle = Equilateral (60°). Limits = 30° to 120°.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Surveyor (Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: The main survey line running through the centre of the entire area upon which the framework of triangles is built is called the:
bankQuestions.explanation: The baseline is the longest and most central survey line on which the skeleton framework of the entire survey network is laid down.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Base line = Longest and most critical chain line, measured with highest accuracy.
bankQuestions.examName: KPSC Draftsman Gr. II / Technical Education

bankQuestions.question: A survey line run to check the positional accuracy of the framework and plotting is called a:
bankQuestions.explanation: A check line (also known as a proof line) is measured from the apex of a triangle to an opposite side to verify the accuracy of the framework and fieldwork.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Check line / Proof line = Confirms accuracy of the framework.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II

bankQuestions.question: The primary purpose of running a tie line in chain surveying is to:
options: Locate interior detailed features and check framework
bankQuestions.explanation: Tie lines connect tie stations on main lines to enable the pickup of interior topological details (trees, buildings, fences) without using overly long offsets.
