options: A fine mapping pricker with a needle point protected by a bone or wood handle
A drawing compass divider with blunt point
bankQuestions.explanation: A fine mapping pricker creates a tiny clean puncture without tearing paper fibres.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Fine pricker makes a clean, minute puncture without paper tearing.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In plane table surveying, what is an "orientation ray"?
options: A sightline drawn between two stations used specifically to align and orient the board at subsequent setups
A ray pointing to magnetic South
A ray drawn without an alidade
bankQuestions.explanation: An orientation ray joins two setup stations and serves as the baseline for backsighting orientation.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Orientation ray = Sightline connecting two stations used for backsighting.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the advantage of using a metal-mounted plane table sheet (aluminum foil sandwiched between paper layers)?
options: It provides extreme dimensional stability under all humidity and temperature conditions, virtually eliminating expansion and contraction
It is magnetic and holds pins
bankQuestions.explanation: Foil-interleaved paper (metal-mounted paper) prevents humidity expansion, preserving precision.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Metal-mounted paper has near-zero expansion, eliminating humidity distortion.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In plane table surveying, what is meant by "graphic resection"?
options: Fixing the position of the occupied instrument station on the sheet by sighting already plotted control stations without numerical calculations
bankQuestions.explanation: Graphic resection locates the instrument station entirely on the drawing board by sighting known stations.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Graphic resection fixes station position on the drawing board graphically.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the role of the "compass groove" provided in some plane table boards?
options: A recessed slot along one edge of the board designed to snugly hold the trough compass parallel to the board edge
bankQuestions.explanation: A recessed wooden groove holds the trough compass firmly against the board edge for rapid orientation.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Compass groove holds trough compass flush with board edge.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In the Two-Point Problem, why is an auxiliary station D selected?
options: To provide an initial setup where a trial orientation line can be established before occupying station C
To measure the height of the hill
To provide shelter for the crew
bankQuestions.explanation: Occupying auxiliary station D provides a trial line of sight to calibrate board orientation at station C.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Auxiliary station D establishes trial orientation line in 2-point problem.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In Lehmann's method of solving the Three-Point Problem, what is the meaning of "great circle"?
options: The circle circumscribing the three known ground control stations A, B, and C
The zero circle of a planimeter
The edge of the circular compass
bankQuestions.explanation: The circumscribed circle passing through ground stations A, B, and C is the great circle.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Great circle = Circumscribed circle through control stations A, B, C.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Why does Lehmann's method fail if the plane table is positioned on the circumscribed circle through stations A, B, and C?
options: Because the subtended angles from all points on the circumference are identical, making the position mathematically indeterminate
Because the magnetic needle ceases to swing
Because the sun blinds the alidade
bankQuestions.explanation: By the inscribed angle theorem, angles subtended by chords AC and BC are identical at every point on the circumference.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Circumscribed circle creates indeterminate geometry; 3-point problem fails.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: According to Lehmann's rules, if the station is inside the great triangle ABC, where does true point p lie?
options: Strictly inside the triangle of error
bankQuestions.explanation: Lehmann's rule: If the station is inside the great triangle, the true point lies inside the triangle of error.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Station inside great triangle -> Point p is INSIDE triangle of error.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: According to Lehmann's rules, if the station is outside the great triangle ABC, where does true point p lie?
options: Strictly outside the triangle of error
bankQuestions.explanation: Lehmann's rule: If the station is outside the great triangle, the true point lies outside the triangle of error.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Station outside great triangle -> Point p is OUTSIDE triangle of error.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: According to Lehmann's rules, what is the lateral relationship between true point p and the three rays?
options: Point p lies either all to the right or all to the left of the three rays when looking along them towards the stations
Point p alternates between left and right
Point p lies on ray B
Point p lies between the shortest rays
bankQuestions.explanation: Facing the stations, point p must lie consistently to the right or consistently to the left of all three rays.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Point p lies all to the right or all to the left of the three rays.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: According to Lehmann's rules, how does the distance of true point p from any resection ray relate to ground distance?
options: Distance of p from each ray is directly proportional to the ground distance from the table to that station
bankQuestions.explanation: Angular orientation error causes lateral ray displacement proportional to ray length: Distance from ray ∝ Ground distance.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Distance from ray is PROPORTIONAL to ground distance to station.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In plane table traversing, how are line lengths between stations measured?
options: Using a metric tape, steel band, or tacheometric stadia readings with a telescopic alidade
bankQuestions.explanation: Traverse line lengths are measured with steel tapes or tacheometrically using stadia hairs on a telescopic alidade.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Traverse lengths measured with tape/steel band or tacheometric stadia.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the primary check on an open plane table traverse connecting two established control points?
options: The plotted position of the closing station must coincide with its known plotted position on the sheet
The sum of line lengths must equal 1000 m
bankQuestions.explanation: The closing ray and distance must land exactly on the pre-plotted control mark on the sheet.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Open connecting traverse check: Final plotted position must match known control point.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the purpose of the spring clips used on plane table boards?
options: To clamp the edges of the drawing paper firmly to the board without puncturing the working area with pin holes
To clip the alidade to the board
bankQuestions.explanation: Spring board clips hold paper edges securely without leaving holes or tearing the working surface.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Spring clips secure paper edges without damaging the working surface.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Why should the observer never rotate the plane table to take sights to different ground features?
options: Rotating the table destroys the established orientation and ruins the parallelism of the entire survey
It makes the tripod legs unscrew
It causes the alidade to magnetize
bankQuestions.explanation: Once oriented, the table must remain clamped and motionless; the surveyor walks around the table to sight.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: NEVER rotate an oriented table; walk around the table to take sights!
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In differential levelling, what is the definition of "line of collimation"?
options: An imaginary line passing through the intersection of the cross-hairs and the optical centre of the objective lens and its continuation
The line along the top of the telescope tube
The axis of the bubble tube
bankQuestions.explanation: Line of collimation is the optical sightline joining the reticle cross-hair intersection to the objective lens optical centre.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Line of collimation = Line joining cross-hairs intersection and optical centre of objective.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: How does the "axis of the telescope" differ from the "line of collimation"?
options: The axis of the telescope connects the optical centres of the objective lens and eyepiece lens
They are always at 90° to each other
The axis of the telescope is curved
The line of collimation is vertical
bankQuestions.explanation: Axis of the telescope joins the optical centre of the objective to the optical centre of the eyepiece.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Axis of telescope joins optical centres of objective and eyepiece.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the "axis of the bubble tube" in a spirit level?
options: The imaginary line tangential to the longitudinal curved inner surface of the vial at its central graduation mark
The line joining the two leveling screws
bankQuestions.explanation: The bubble tube axis is the tangent to the longitudinal curve at the centre of the bubble tube scale.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Axis of bubble tube = Tangent to longitudinal curve at centre of tube.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In a perfectly adjusted dumpy level, what is the geometric relationship between the line of collimation and the bubble tube axis?
options: The line of collimation must be strictly parallel to the axis of the bubble tube
They must coincide with the vertical axis
bankQuestions.explanation: When the bubble is in the centre, the line of collimation must be strictly horizontal, meaning it must be parallel to the bubble axis.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Line of collimation must be PARALLEL to the bubble tube axis.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In a dumpy level, what is the relationship between the bubble tube axis and the vertical spindle axis?
options: The axis of the bubble tube must be strictly perpendicular to the vertical axis of rotation
bankQuestions.explanation: When the bubble axis is perpendicular to the vertical axis, the bubble remains centered throughout a complete 360° horizontal rotation.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Bubble tube axis must be PERPENDICULAR to the vertical axis of rotation.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the purpose of the "two-peg test" in dumpy level calibration?
options: To detect and adjust collimation error by verifying whether the line of collimation is truly horizontal when the bubble is centered
To measure the sensitivity of the bubble
bankQuestions.explanation: The two-peg test checks whether the line of collimation is parallel to the bubble tube axis, detecting collimation error.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Two-peg test: Detects and eliminates collimation error in a level.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In the two-peg test, why is the instrument first set up midway between peg A and peg B?
options: Because equal sight distances automatically cancel out collimation error, curvature, and refraction, giving the true height difference
Because it is easier to walk
To protect the instrument from sun
bankQuestions.explanation: When distances to A and B are equal (D1 = D2), collimation error e affects both readings equally (a + e, b + e), so true difference h = a - b.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Midway setup: Equal sights cancel collimation error, yielding TRUE height difference.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What type of level features a telescope that can be tilted slightly in the vertical plane using a fine micrometer screw without moving the vertical axis?
bankQuestions.explanation: In a tilting level, the telescope is pivoted on a horizontal axis and fine-tilted by a micrometer screw to centre the bubble before each reading.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Tilting level: Micrometer tilting screw centres bubble before each reading.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is an "automatic level" (auto level) and how does it maintain a horizontal line of sight?
options: It incorporates an optical-mechanical pendulum compensator that automatically levels the line of sight when the circular bubble is roughly centered
It has an internal gyroscope motor
bankQuestions.explanation: An auto level uses a suspended prism/mirror compensator that swings under gravity to automatically align the line of sight horizontally.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Auto level: Pendulum compensator automatically levels the line of sight.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the purpose of the damping device (air or magnetic damper) in an automatic level compensator?
options: To quickly damp oscillations of the suspended pendulum prism and bring it to rest in seconds
bankQuestions.explanation: Without damping, the suspended pendulum would oscillate for minutes; air or eddy-current magnetic dampers bring it to rest in seconds.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Compensator damper halts pendulum oscillations quickly.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is a "digital level"?
options: An electronic level that scans a bar-coded levelling staff via an internal CCD sensor, displays digital staff readings, and records data electronically
A level that uses laser beams only
bankQuestions.explanation: Digital levels scan bar-coded staves electronically, eliminating human observation blunders and recording data directly.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Digital level: Electronic CCD reading of bar-coded staff; eliminates human reading errors.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the "least count" of a standard Sopwith metric levelling staff?
bankQuestions.explanation: A standard metric Sopwith staff has alternate black and white painted blocks and spaces of 5 mm height, giving a direct least count of 5 mm (estimable to 1 mm).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Sopwith staff least count = 5 mm (0.005 m).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: On a standard 4-metre metric Sopwith levelling staff, what do the black and white stripes indicate?
options: Each black painted rectangle has a height of 5 mm, and each white space between them has a height of 5 mm
Black is 1 cm, white is 2 cm
Black is 1 mm, white is 1 mm
bankQuestions.explanation: The graduations are divided into 5 mm blocks: the bottom of a black block represents an even number of centimetres, and top represents 5 mm.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Sopwith staff: 5 mm black blocks and 5 mm white spaces.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the purpose of "waving the staff" (staff rocking) during levelling observation?
options: To rock the staff slowly back and forth through the vertical to identify the true minimum reading, which occurs when the staff is strictly vertical
To dry the staff in rain
bankQuestions.explanation: When tilted away or towards the level, staff readings increase; the minimum reading observed during rocking represents the true vertical position.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Waving the staff: The MINIMUM staff reading observed is the true vertical reading.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: When should staff waving NOT be practiced?
options: When using a staff fitted with a spherical circular bull's-eye level bubble held strictly plumb
bankQuestions.explanation: A circular bubble mounted on the staff confirms verticality directly, making rocking unnecessary and potentially introducing base displacement.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Do not rock staff when a circular bull's-eye level bubble is fitted and centered.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the primary objective of "reciprocal levelling"?
options: To determine the true height difference between two stations separated by a wide obstacle (river or ravine) where the level cannot be placed midway
To measure the width of a river
To find the magnetic meridian across water
To balance the tripod on a boat
bankQuestions.explanation: Reciprocal levelling takes readings from both banks of a wide water body to determine true elevation difference without midway setup.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Reciprocal levelling: Wide obstacles (rivers/ravines); eliminates collimation and curvature errors.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which errors are COMPLETELY eliminated by reciprocal levelling?
options: Collimation error of the instrument, Earth's curvature error, and constant atmospheric refraction error
bankQuestions.explanation: By observing from both banks and taking the mean of elevation differences, instrumental collimation error, curvature, and constant refraction cancel out.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Reciprocal levelling eliminates collimation error, curvature, and constant refraction.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which error is NOT completely eliminated by reciprocal levelling?
options: Variable and unequal atmospheric refraction occurring at different times between the two setups
bankQuestions.explanation: If atmospheric refraction over the water changes significantly between the morning reading and afternoon reading, the difference is not canceled.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Unequal / fluctuating atmospheric refraction is NOT eliminated by reciprocal levelling.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In reciprocal levelling between stations A and B across a river, the readings are: Instrument near A: Staff on A = 1.500 m, Staff on B = 2.800 m. Instrument near B: Staff on A = 0.900 m, Staff on B = 2.200 m. What is the true difference in elevation?
options: 1.300 metres (B is lower than A by 1.300 m)
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the sensitivity of a spirit level bubble tube defined as?
options: The angular rotation of the bubble axis (in seconds or radians) required to cause the bubble to move through one standard division of the scale (usually 2 mm)
The length of the glass vial
The freezing temperature of the liquid
The thickness of the glass wall
bankQuestions.explanation: Sensitivity is the angular tilt (in arc-seconds) corresponding to a 1-division (2 mm) displacement of the bubble: α = s / (n·D) = d / R.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Sensitivity = Angular tilt per 1 scale division (usually 2 mm) of bubble movement.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which of the following modifications will INCREASE the sensitivity of a spirit level bubble tube?
options: Increasing the internal radius of curvature R of the tube vial
Decreasing the length of the bubble
Increasing the viscosity of the liquid
bankQuestions.explanation: Sensitivity increases with: 1. Larger radius of curvature R; 2. Larger tube diameter; 3. Longer bubble; 4. Lower liquid viscosity and surface tension.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Sensitivity increases with LARGER radius of curvature R and LOWER liquid viscosity.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What liquid is filled inside standard precision spirit level bubble tubes, and why?
options: Synthetic alcohol, chloroform, or purified petroleum ether because of low freezing point, low viscosity, and low surface tension
bankQuestions.explanation: Alcohol and ether have low freezing points (will not freeze in winter), low viscosity (bubble moves freely), and low surface tension.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Bubble tube liquid: Purified alcohol or ether (low viscosity, low freezing point).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In differential levelling, what is the "profile levelling" (longitudinal levelling)?
options: The operation of taking levels along the established centerline of a proposed route (road, railway, canal, or pipeline) to determine ground profile
Finding the height of a tree
bankQuestions.explanation: Profile levelling determines elevations of points at regular intervals along the centerline of a proposed engineering alignment.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Profile levelling = Levelling along the centerline of a proposed route (road, rail, canal).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is "cross-section levelling" in route surveys?
options: Taking levels along lines perpendicular to the centerline at regular chainages to determine transverse ground profile for earthwork computation
bankQuestions.explanation: Cross-sections are run at 90° to the centerline to obtain transverse ground slopes for computing cut and fill earthwork quantities.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Cross-section levelling = Levels taken perpendicular to route centerline for earthworks.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is a "contour line" in surveying?
options: An imaginary line on the ground surface connecting all points having the exact same elevation (reduced level) above datum
A boundary line of a land parcel
A line of sight through a level
bankQuestions.explanation: A contour line connects points of equal elevation above a datum surface.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Contour line = Imaginary line connecting points of equal elevation.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is "contour interval"?
options: The constant vertical distance in elevation between two consecutive contour lines on a map
The horizontal distance between two contours
The thickness of the contour pen line
The time interval between two contour surveys
bankQuestions.explanation: Contour interval is strictly the vertical height difference between consecutive contours; it remains uniform throughout a given map.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Contour interval = Vertical elevation difference between consecutive contour lines (CONSTANT).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is "horizontal equivalent" in contouring?
options: The horizontal distance between two consecutive contour lines on the ground surface
bankQuestions.explanation: Horizontal equivalent is the horizontal ground distance between adjacent contours. It varies with terrain slope (narrow on steep slopes, wide on gentle slopes).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Horizontal equivalent = Horizontal distance between contours (VARIES with ground slope).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: How does the horizontal equivalent vary with the steepness of the ground slope for a fixed contour interval?
options: It is smaller (contours closer together) on steep slopes and larger (contours further apart) on gentle slopes
It is larger on steep slopes
It is zero on flat ground
bankQuestions.explanation: On steep slopes, elevation changes rapidly over short horizontal distance, bringing contours close together.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Steep slope = Contours CLOSE together (small horizontal equivalent). Gentle slope = Contours FAR apart.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What do concentric closed contour lines with elevation values INCREASING towards the centre represent?
options: A hill, knoll, or mountain peak
bankQuestions.explanation: Concentric closed contours where higher numbers are inside represent a hill summit.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Concentric closed contours increasing INWARD = HILL.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What do concentric closed contour lines with elevation values DECREASING towards the centre represent?
options: A depression, pond, lake, or crater without outlet
bankQuestions.explanation: Concentric closed contours where lower elevations lie inside represent a depression or pond.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Concentric closed contours decreasing INWARD = DEPRESSION / POND.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What do V-shaped contour lines with the apex of the "V" pointing UPHILL (towards higher elevations) indicate?
options: A valley, ravine, or stream course (the stream flows down along the valley line)
bankQuestions.explanation: Valley contours form V-shapes pointing uphill towards higher contours. The stream line runs through the points of the V.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: V-shaped contours pointing UPHILL = VALLEY line (stream).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What do U-shaped contour lines with the convex rounded loop of the "U" pointing DOWNHILL (towards lower elevations) indicate?
options: A ridge line, watershed, or spur
bankQuestions.explanation: Ridge contours form U-shaped loops with the convex nose pointing downhill towards lower elevations.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: U-shaped contours pointing DOWNHILL = RIDGE / SPUR line.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: At what angle do contour lines cross a ridge line or a valley line?
bankQuestions.explanation: Because ridge and valley lines represent directions of maximum slope, contour lines must cross them perpendicularly at 90°.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Contours cross ridge and valley lines at RIGHT ANGLES (90°).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Under what exceptional topographical condition can two contour lines cross each other on a map?
options: An overhanging cliff or a natural cave / overhanging rock shelter
bankQuestions.explanation: Contours can only cross where a single vertical line pierces the ground surface at more than one elevation, as in an overhanging cliff or cave.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Contours CROSS each other ONLY at an OVERHANGING CLIFF or CAVE.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What topographic feature is represented when several contour lines merge into a single combined line on a map?
bankQuestions.explanation: A perfectly vertical cliff wall contains multiple elevations along the same vertical plane, causing contours to merge into a single line.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Several contours merging into ONE line = VERTICAL CLIFF.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is a "saddle" or "col" in contour topography?
options: A dip or pass between two adjacent mountain peaks, characterized by four sets of contours (two hills and two valleys meeting)
The top of a vertical cliff
bankQuestions.explanation: A saddle (col) is a low point on a ridge between two peaks; contours form two facing hills and two drainage gaps on opposite sides.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Saddle / Col = Mountain pass between two peaks.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the "direct method" of contouring?
options: Locating points of exact contour elevations on the physical ground using a level and staff, marking them with pegs, and surveying them
bankQuestions.explanation: In the direct method, the surveyor guides the staffman to find points having the exact contour reduced level and surveys their positions.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Direct method: Exact contour points found on ground with level and staff (accurate but slow).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which indirect method of contouring is best suited for small, flat, or gently undulating plots of land?
bankQuestions.explanation: In the grid (squares) method, the site is divided into a grid of squares (5 m to 20 m), corner levels taken, and contours interpolated.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Method of squares (Grid method): Small, flat, or gently undulating sites.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which indirect method of contouring is most suitable for route surveys (highways, railways, canals)?
bankQuestions.explanation: Cross-sections set out at regular intervals perpendicular to the centerline capture lateral topography efficiently for route corridors.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Cross-section method: Route surveys (roads, railways, canals).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which indirect method of contouring is most effective in steep, rugged, and mountainous terrain?
bankQuestions.explanation: A tacheometer set up at a command summit takes radial sights and stadia readings in all directions without climbing every slope.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Radial line / Tacheometric method: Steep, rugged, mountainous terrain.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In computing reservoir water storage capacity from a contour map, which formula represents the Trapezoidal (End Area) formula?
bankQuestions.explanation: Trapezoidal formula for reservoir volume: V = (h/2) [A0 + An + 2(A1 + A2 + ... + An-1)], where h is contour interval and A are contour areas.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Trapezoidal volume: V = (h/2) [A0 + An + 2(sum of intermediate areas)].
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In computing reservoir capacity from contours, what is the Prismoidal formula (Simpson's rule for volume)?
bankQuestions.explanation: Prismoidal formula: V = (h/3) [(A0 + An) + 4(A1 + A3 + ...) + 2(A2 + A4 + ...)], where h is contour interval.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Prismoidal formula: V = (h/3) [First + Last + 4(odd) + 2(even)].
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What mathematical condition must be satisfied to apply the Prismoidal formula to contour areas?
options: There must be an ODD number of contour areas (an even number of contour intervals)
There must be an EVEN number of areas
bankQuestions.explanation: Like Simpson's 1/3 rule, the prismoidal formula pairs cross-sectional areas in triplets, requiring an odd number of areas.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Prismoidal formula requires an ODD number of contour areas (even number of intervals).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: How does the volume of a reservoir calculated by the Trapezoidal rule compare with that calculated by the Prismoidal rule for convex ground slopes?
options: The Trapezoidal rule always yields a LARGER volume than the Prismoidal rule (Prismoidal correction is subtractive)
bankQuestions.explanation: Because trapezoids replace parabolic convex contours with straight chords, the trapezoidal volume overestimates true storage.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Trapezoidal volume is GREATER than Prismoidal volume; Prismoidal correction is subtractive.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is an "Abney level" primarily used for in civil and forest engineering?
options: Measuring vertical angles of slope, measuring gradients, and tracing uniform gradient contour lines on hill roads
bankQuestions.explanation: An Abney level is a handheld pocket instrument with a graduated semicircular arc and spirit level for measuring vertical angles and tracing slopes.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Abney level: Handheld clinometer for measuring slope angles and tracing hill road gradients.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is a "Ceylon ghat tracer" used for in hill road surveys?
options: Setting out and tracing uniform gradients (e.g. 1 in 20 or 1 in 30) along steep hill slopes for proposed ghat roads
bankQuestions.explanation: A Ceylon ghat tracer features a perforated sighting box and rack-graduated weight used specifically to locate guide pegs at a fixed slope gradient.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Ceylon ghat tracer: Sets out uniform gradients on steep hill slopes for ghat roads.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is a "box sextant" and what optical principle does it employ?
options: A compact pocket sextant that measures horizontal and vertical angles up to 120° based on the principle of double reflection
A wooden box with a level tube
A box used to carry arrows
A device to test concrete cubes
bankQuestions.explanation: A box sextant is a handheld pocket instrument using two mirrors (index glass and horizon glass) to measure angles up to 120° by double reflection.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Box sextant: Handheld instrument measuring angles up to 120° by DOUBLE REFLECTION.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is a "pantograph" used for in surveying office practice?
options: A mechanical linkage instrument based on parallel motion used for enlarging, reducing, or copying map drawings to a desired scale
An instrument for reading bar codes
A device to measure paper weight
bankQuestions.explanation: A pantograph consists of four articulated bars forming a parallelogram; tracing a drawing moves a pencil to reproduce it at scaled enlargement or reduction.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Pantograph = Mechanical instrument for enlarging, reducing, or copying drawings.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: How does an "eidograph" compare to a "pantograph" in drawing office practice?
options: An eidograph is a superior and more precise instrument for enlarging and reducing maps, consisting of a single central beam and two parallel arms
An eidograph is smaller than a pencil
bankQuestions.explanation: The eidograph uses a central bar and wire pulleys, providing greater rigidity, smoother motion, and superior precision over the loose multi-jointed pantograph.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Eidograph: More precise and rigid map-enlarging/reducing instrument than pantograph.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In differential levelling, why is it essential to keep the Back Sight and Fore Sight distances approximately equal from each instrument setup?
options: Because equal sight distances completely cancel out collimation error, Earth curvature error, and atmospheric refraction error
To save walking time for the staffman
Because the telescope has a fixed range
bankQuestions.explanation: Balancing BS and FS distances (D_BS = D_FS) ensures that equal errors affect both readings and subtract out completely: Δh = (BS + e) - (FS + e) = BS - FS.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Equal BS and FS distances cancel collimation error, curvature, and refraction!
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What type of paper grain orientation is preferred when mounting drawing paper on a plane table board?
options: Grain running parallel to the longer dimension of the board to minimize transverse expansion
bankQuestions.explanation: Paper expands more across the grain than along it; aligning grain with the longer side minimizes total distortion.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Align paper grain with longer board dimension.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is "Whatman paper" and why is it prized in plane table field mapping?
options: A premium linen-based hand-made drawing paper with superior dimensional stability and erasure resistance
bankQuestions.explanation: Whatman paper resists atmospheric humidity stretching and withstands repeated erasure without fraying.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Whatman paper: Premium drawing paper with high dimensional stability.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Why should plane table field sheets be protected with a paper mask having a cut-out window for working?
options: To keep the rest of the sheet clean from dust, perspiration, and graphite smudges during field work
To prevent wind from blowing the table away
bankQuestions.explanation: Covering the board with a paper mask exposes only the active working area, keeping the rest clean.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Use a paper mask with a working window to keep field sheets clean.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: When surveying a building boundary with a plane table, how are accessible corners located by Radiation?
options: By sighting each corner through the alidade, drawing rays, measuring tape distances, and scaling them along the rays
By sighting through the building walls
By setting the table on the roof
By using an Indian clinometer only
bankQuestions.explanation: Radiation sights every corner from the command station and scales measured tape distances along each ray.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Building corners by radiation: Sight corner + Measure distance + Scale along ray.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: How is an inaccessible corner of a building located if direct taping is blocked by a boundary wall?
options: By the Intersection method from two accessible plane table stations
By tearing down the boundary wall
By throwing the alidade over the wall
bankQuestions.explanation: Intersecting rays from two stations fix the corner graphically without measuring distance to it.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Inaccessible building corners are fixed by Intersection.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: If the plane table station lies within the triangle formed by three ground stations A, B, C, where does true point p lie?
options: Strictly inside the triangle of error
bankQuestions.explanation: Lehmann's rule: If the station is inside the great triangle, the true point lies inside the triangle of error.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Station inside great triangle -> Point p is INSIDE triangle of error.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: If the plane table station lies outside the triangle formed by three ground stations, where does true point p lie?
options: Strictly outside the triangle of error
bankQuestions.explanation: Lehmann's rule: If the station is outside the great triangle, the true point lies outside the triangle of error.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Station outside great triangle -> Point p is OUTSIDE triangle of error.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: According to Lehmann's rules, if the station is outside the great triangle, how is point p placed relative to the rays?
options: In such a position that it lies either all to the right or all to the left of the three rays when looking along them towards the stations
On the circumference of ray B
bankQuestions.explanation: Facing the stations, point p must lie consistently to the right or consistently to the left of all three rays.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Point p must lie all to the right or all to the left of the three rays.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: According to Lehmann's rules, how does the distance of point p from any ray relate to ground distance?
options: Its perpendicular distance from each ray is proportional to the distance of the corresponding ground station from the table
bankQuestions.explanation: Angular orientation error causes lateral ray displacement proportional to ray length: Distance from ray ∝ Ground distance.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Distance from ray is PROPORTIONAL to ground distance to station.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the "distance to the visible horizon" formula (in km) from an observation point of height h (in metres) above sea level?
bankQuestions.explanation: Combined correction is h = 0.0673 d², so distance to horizon d = √(h / 0.0673) ≈ 3.855 √h kilometres.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Distance to horizon: d = √(h / 0.0673) ≈ 3.855 √h km.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: If a lighthouse light is 49 metres above sea level, what is its distance to the visible horizon for an observer at sea level?
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Horizon distance = 3.855 × √49 = 27 km.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: If an observer at sea level sees a ship mast of height 16 m disappearing over the horizon, how far away is the ship?
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the radius of curvature R of a spirit level bubble tube having length of one division l = 2 mm and sensitivity α = 20 seconds?
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the sensitivity α in seconds of a bubble tube having radius of curvature R = 25 m and division length l = 2 mm?
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In profile levelling, what are "plus stations" (fractional stations)?
options: Intermediate stations established at breaks in ground slope between regular 20 m or 30 m chainage pegs
Stations where staff reading is positive
bankQuestions.explanation: Plus stations are points located between regular chain pegs to record significant ground features (ditches, culverts, ridges).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Plus stations = Intermediate points between regular chainage intervals.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In road cross-section levelling, how are offset distances booked in the field book?
options: As fractional entries with staff reading above the line and offset distance below the line (e.g. 1.85 / 10.0 L)
In separate columns for every metre
bankQuestions.explanation: Cross-section levels are booked as fractions: Staff Reading / Offset Distance from centerline (L for left, R for right).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Cross-section booking: Reading / Offset (e.g. 1.85 / 10 L).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In levelling across a pond or lake with calm still water, how can the Reduced Level of the opposite bank be determined accurately without setting up in water?
options: By taking staff reading on the water surface on near bank, since still water surface forms a true level surface
By swimming across with a dumpy level
By running reciprocal levelling with an Abney level
By dropping a plumb bob into the mud
bankQuestions.explanation: The water surface of a calm lake is an equipotential level surface; its elevation is constant at all perimeter points.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Calm water surface forms a true level surface; levels can be transferred across water.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is a "fly level" (fly levelling)?
options: A rapid reconnaissance differential levelling run to check the accuracy of benchmarks or close a loop without taking intermediate sights
bankQuestions.explanation: Fly levelling takes only Back Sights and Fore Sights to connect benchmarks or verify closure rapidly without picking up intermediate ground points.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Fly levelling: Rapid differential levelling using ONLY Back Sights and Fore Sights.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is "check levelling"?
options: Levelling run at the end of a day's work from the final station back to the starting benchmark to check closing accuracy
Checking the level with a spirit level
bankQuestions.explanation: Check levelling reruns the line rapidly back to the origin BM to ensure that no blunders occurred during the day's work.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Check levelling = Rapid fly levelling back to starting BM to verify closing error.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the allowable closing error in ordinary engineering levelling over a distance of K kilometres?
bankQuestions.explanation: For ordinary engineering levelling, permissible closing error is E = ± 0.025 √K metres (25 mm per √km).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Ordinary levelling error tolerance = ± 0.025 √K m (25 √K mm).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the allowable closing error in precise levelling over a distance of K kilometres?
bankQuestions.explanation: Precise geodetic levelling requires closing error within E = ± 0.004 to ± 0.006 √K metres.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Precise levelling tolerance = ± 0.004 to ± 0.006 √K m (4 to 6 √K mm).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In levelling, what is the effect of the levelling staff not being held strictly vertical (staff tilted forward or backward)?
options: The reading observed on the staff is always GREATER than the true vertical reading (cumulative positive error)
The reading is smaller than true
bankQuestions.explanation: A tilted staff acts as the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle, so the cross-hair intercepts a higher number than true vertical.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Tilted staff reading is ALWAYS TOO LARGE (Positive error).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What error is introduced into levelling if the tripod settles or sinks into soft mud between the Back Sight and Fore Sight readings?
options: The Height of Instrument drops, causing subsequent staff readings to be too small and calculated RLs to be too high
The line of collimation tilts upward
bankQuestions.explanation: Tripod settlement lowers the line of sight, so the fore sight reading is smaller than it should be, falsely elevating the next benchmark.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Tripod settlement lowers HI, making Fore Sight reading too small.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the purpose of using a "foot plate" (staff shoe or trivet) under the levelling staff on soft ground?
options: To provide a firm, stable metal base that prevents the staff from sinking into the ground at Change Points
To protect the staff numbers from mud
To increase staff height by 1 m
bankQuestions.explanation: A triangular iron foot plate with three spikes beds firmly into soft soil, providing an unyielding turning point for the staff.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Foot plate (staff shoe) prevents staff from sinking into soft ground at Change Points.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In contouring, what is "contour gradient"?
options: A line lying on the ground surface maintaining a constant, uniform slope or inclination with the horizontal
The contour interval divided by map scale
The steepest line down a mountain
The line joining two hill tops
bankQuestions.explanation: A contour gradient is a line on the ground having a specified uniform slope (e.g. 1 in 30), traced for laying out roads or canals.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Contour gradient = Line maintaining a constant uniform slope on the ground.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What minor surveying instrument is specifically designed to locate and peg out a contour gradient along a hill slope?
options: Ceylon ghat tracer or Abney level
bankQuestions.explanation: The Ceylon ghat tracer or Abney level is set to the desired gradient (e.g. 1 in 25) and sighted to locate successive pegs on the hillside.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Ceylon ghat tracer / Abney level sets out contour gradients on hill slopes.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the vertical distance between the water surface of a reservoir and the top edge of the dam crest called?
bankQuestions.explanation: Freeboard is the vertical safety margin provided between maximum reservoir flood level and the dam crest to prevent wave overtopping.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Freeboard = Vertical margin between maximum water level and dam crest.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In reservoir capacity surveys, what does the "dead storage" represent?
options: The volume of water stored below the sill level of the lowest sluice or outlet that cannot be drawn out by gravity
The water stored above the spillway
bankQuestions.explanation: Dead storage is the bottom volume of the reservoir below the lowest outlet gate, reserved to accumulate incoming silt over the dam lifetime.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Dead storage = Water volume below lowest outlet, reserved for silt accumulation.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In reservoir capacity surveys, what does "live storage" (useful storage) represent?
options: The effective volume of water stored between the lowest outlet sill level and the full reservoir level (F.R.L.) available for use
The volume above the dam crest
bankQuestions.explanation: Live storage is the active, usable water volume between minimum drawdown level and full reservoir level (FRL).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Live storage = Usable storage between lowest outlet and Full Reservoir Level (FRL).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What defines a "transit theodolite" as distinguished from a non-transit theodolite?
options: The telescope can be revolved through a complete revolution (180°) in a vertical plane about its horizontal axis
It has two verniers on the plate
It can be mounted on a wooden tripod
bankQuestions.explanation: In a transit theodolite, the telescope can be transited (plunged) end-for-end through 180° in the vertical plane about its trunnion axis.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Transit theodolite: Telescope rotates through 180° in a vertical plane about its horizontal axis.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: How is the nominal size of a surveying theodolite specified?
options: By the diameter of the graduated horizontal circle on the lower plate
By the length of the telescope tube
By the height of the tripod
By the focal length of the objective lens
bankQuestions.explanation: Theodolites are designated by the diameter of their lower graduated circle (e.g., 10 cm, 12 cm, 15 cm theodolite). 8 to 12 cm is standard for engineering surveys.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Theodolite size = Diameter of graduated horizontal circle on lower plate.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In a transit theodolite, what is the "vertical axis"?
options: The axis about which the telescope rotates in a horizontal plane (the central axis of inner and outer spindles)
The axis through the trunnion pins
bankQuestions.explanation: The vertical axis is the primary vertical rotation axis of the instrument about which the telescope swings horizontally.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Vertical axis: Axis about which the instrument rotates horizontally.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In a transit theodolite, what is the "horizontal axis" (trunnion axis)?
options: The horizontal axis resting in the A-frame standards about which the telescope rotates in a vertical plane
The line along the plate level vial
bankQuestions.explanation: The horizontal (trunnion) axis rests on the A-frame standards, allowing the telescope to tilt up and down in the vertical plane.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Horizontal axis (trunnion axis): Axis about which the telescope rotates vertically.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the first fundamental axis relationship in a transit theodolite?
options: The axis of the plate levels must be strictly perpendicular to the vertical axis of the theodolite
The telescope axis must be parallel to the tripod legs
The horizontal axis must be parallel to the vertical axis
The line of collimation must be inclined at 45°
bankQuestions.explanation: Plate level axis ⊥ Vertical axis ensures that when plate bubbles are centered, the vertical axis is truly vertical.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Axis of plate levels must be PERPENDICULAR to vertical axis.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the second fundamental axis relationship in a transit theodolite?
options: The line of collimation must be strictly perpendicular to the horizontal trunnion axis
The line of collimation must be parallel to the vertical axis
The plate level must be parallel to the telescope
The altitude bubble must be perpendicular to vertical axis
bankQuestions.explanation: Line of collimation ⊥ Horizontal axis ensures that transiting the telescope sweeps a true great circle without conical distortion.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Line of collimation must be PERPENDICULAR to horizontal trunnion axis.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the third fundamental axis relationship in a transit theodolite?
options: The horizontal trunnion axis must be strictly perpendicular to the vertical axis
The horizontal axis must be parallel to the plate level
The altitude bubble must be at 45° to vertical axis
The vertical axis must coincide with the line of sight
bankQuestions.explanation: Horizontal axis ⊥ Vertical axis ensures that when the vertical axis is plumb, the telescope rotates in a strictly vertical plane.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Horizontal axis must be PERPENDICULAR to the vertical axis.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In a transit theodolite, which component carries the verniers A and B and the telescope standards?
bankQuestions.explanation: The upper plate carries verniers A and B, two plate bubble vials, the vertical standards supporting the telescope, and the upper clamp.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Upper plate carries verniers A and B, standards, and telescope.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In a transit theodolite, which component carries the main 0° to 360° graduated horizontal circle?
bankQuestions.explanation: The lower plate carries the beveled horizontal circle graduated continuously from 0° to 360° clockwise in degrees and minutes.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Lower plate carries the main 0° to 360° graduated horizontal circle.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: When measuring horizontal angles with a theodolite, what operation does the "upper clamp" control?
options: It clamps the upper vernier plate to the lower graduated circle plate, locking their relative angular reading
It clamps the lower plate to the tribrach
bankQuestions.explanation: Tightening the upper clamp locks the upper and lower plates together so they rotate as one unit.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Upper clamp locks upper vernier plate to lower circle plate.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: When measuring horizontal angles, what operation does the "lower clamp" control?
options: It clamps the lower graduated circle plate to the outer spindle and leveling head tribrach
It clamps the telescope in vertical tilt
It clamps the plumb bob string
bankQuestions.explanation: Tightening the lower clamp prevents the lower graduated circle from turning relative to the ground.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Lower clamp locks the lower graduated plate to the leveling head.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is "Face Left" (Circle Left) observation in theodolite surveying?
options: An observation taken when the vertical graduated circle is situated on the left of the observer looking through the telescope
Looking towards the left side of the road
Holding the levelling staff with the left hand
bankQuestions.explanation: Face Left means the vertical circle of the instrument is to the observer's left while sighting through the eyepiece.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Face Left = Vertical circle is to the LEFT of the observer.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is "Face Right" (Circle Right) observation in theodolite surveying?
options: An observation taken when the vertical graduated circle is situated on the right of the observer looking through the telescope
Looking towards the right side of the road
bankQuestions.explanation: Face Right means the vertical circle lies to the observer's right while sighting.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Face Right = Vertical circle is to the RIGHT of the observer.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the operational procedure to change the face of a theodolite from Face Left to Face Right?
options: Transit (plunge) the telescope through 180° vertically, and swing the theodolite through 180° horizontally
Unscrew the telescope and turn it around
Step around to the other side of the tripod
bankQuestions.explanation: Changing face requires two motions: 1. Transiting (plunging) the telescope vertically through 180°; 2. Swinging the instrument horizontally through 180°.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Change face: Transit telescope 180° vertically + Swing instrument 180° horizontally.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which instrumental errors are completely eliminated by taking the mean of Face Left and Face Right observations of horizontal angles?
options: Collimation error in azimuth and horizontal axis tilt error (lack of perpendicularity between trunnion axis and vertical axis)
bankQuestions.explanation: Because collimation error and trunnion axis tilt produce opposite signs on Face Left and Face Right, their average cancels both errors.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Mean of Face Left and Face Right cancels collimation error and horizontal axis tilt.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which instrumental error is eliminated by reading both opposite verniers A and B and taking their mean?
options: Error due to eccentricity of the graduated circle and vernier plates
bankQuestions.explanation: Eccentricity (when the center of the vernier plate does not coincide with the center of the graduated ring) is canceled by averaging verniers A and B (spaced 180° apart).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Reading both verniers A and B (180° apart) eliminates ECCENTRICITY of the circle.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In theodolite angle measurement, what is the "method of repetition"?
options: A method where the angle is added continuously on the graduated circle a specified number of times (e.g. 3 or 6 times) and the final reading divided by n
Repeating the same angle on different days
bankQuestions.explanation: Repetition accumulates the angle n times along the circle, increasing angular precision beyond the vernier least count and eliminating graduation errors.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Method of repetition: Angle added n times on circle, final reading divided by n.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: When is the "method of reiteration" (direction method) preferred over the method of repetition?
options: When several horizontal angles are to be measured to multiple radiating stations from a single instrument station
When measuring a single isolated angle with high precision
bankQuestions.explanation: Reiteration sights each station in continuous succession around the circle, closing the horizon on the starting station. It is ideal for multiple radiating rays.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Method of reiteration: Multiple radiating lines measured from a single setup.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In theodolite traversing, what is the "closing of horizon" check in the reiteration method?
options: Sighting back to the initial starting station after a complete round; the final reading on station 1 must match the initial zero reading (360° or 0°)
bankQuestions.explanation: After swinging through all stations, returning to station A should read exactly 360° 00' 00" (or 0°); any discrepancy is the horizon closing error.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Closing the horizon: Final reading on initial station must equal initial reading (0°/360°).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the "least count" of a standard vernier transit theodolite commonly used in engineering surveys in India?
bankQuestions.explanation: Standard Indian engineering transit theodolites have lower circles divided into degrees and 20-minute divisions, read by verniers to a least count of 20 seconds.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Least count of standard engineering vernier theodolite = 20 seconds (20").
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In tacheometry, what is a "tacheometer"?
options: A transit theodolite fitted with a stadia reticle (two stadia hairs) and an anallatic lens
A magnetic compass with a mirror
bankQuestions.explanation: A tacheometer is a transit theodolite equipped with horizontal stadia wires and an internal anallatic lens for optical distance measurement.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Tacheometer = Transit theodolite fitted with stadia diaphragm and anallatic lens.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In tacheometric surveying, what is the "stadia intercept" s on a levelling staff?
options: The difference between the upper stadia hair reading and the lower stadia hair reading (s = top - bottom)
The reading of the central cross-hair
The height of the staff off the ground
The sum of all three hair readings
bankQuestions.explanation: Stadia intercept s is the length of staff intercepted between the upper and lower stadia lines: s = S_top - S_bottom.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Stadia intercept s = Upper hair reading - Lower hair reading.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the standard value of the multiplying constant K = f / i in a surveying tacheometer?
bankQuestions.explanation: Tacheometers are manufactured so that focal length f divided by stadia hair interval i equals exactly 100.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Tacheometric multiplying constant K = f / i = 100.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the "anallatic lens" and who invented it?
options: An internal convex lens placed between the objective and diaphragm that brings the optical vertex to the vertical axis, making additive constant C = 0; invented by Porro
A concave lens invented by Newton
A cylindrical lens invented by Galileo
bankQuestions.explanation: Invented by Porro in 1823, the anallatic lens makes the additive constant (f + d) equal to zero, so horizontal distance D = 100 × s directly.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Anallatic lens: Invented by Porro; makes additive constant C = 0.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the horizontal distance D formula for a horizontal sight with an anallatic tacheometer (K = 100, C = 0) and staff intercept s?
bankQuestions.explanation: Since D = K·s + C, when K = 100 and C = 0, D = 100 × s.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Horizontal distance D = 100 × s (when K = 100, C = 0).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In tacheometry with an anallatic tacheometer, if the upper hair reads 2.450 m and lower hair reads 1.650 m on a vertical staff on level ground, what is the horizontal distance?
bankQuestions.explanation: Intercept s = 2.450 - 1.650 = 0.800 m. Horizontal distance D = 100 × s = 100 × 0.800 = 80.00 metres.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: For an inclined sight of angle θ with staff held strictly vertical, what is the formula for horizontal distance D using an anallatic tacheometer?
bankQuestions.explanation: For an inclined line of sight with vertical staff, the horizontal distance is D = K·s·cos² θ + C·cos θ = 100 s cos² θ.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Horizontal distance for inclined sight: D = 100 s cos² θ.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: For an inclined sight of angle θ with staff held vertical, what is the formula for vertical height difference V between the instrument trunnion axis and central hair mark?
options: V = 100 × s × 0.5 sin 2θ (or 100 s · sin θ · cos θ)
bankQuestions.explanation: Vertical component V = D · tan θ = (100 s cos² θ) · tan θ = 100 s sin θ cos θ = 0.5 × 100 s sin 2θ.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Vertical component V = 50 s sin 2θ = 100 s sin θ cos θ.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In the tangential method of tacheometry, what type of levelling staff is used?
options: An ordinary levelling staff without stadia lines, where vertical angles are sighted to two fixed targets on the staff
bankQuestions.explanation: The tangential method requires no stadia hairs; vertical angles are measured to two distinct marks on a normal staff.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Tangential tacheometry: Measures vertical angles to two targets on a normal staff.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is a "subtense bar" in tacheometric distance measurement?
options: A precision horizontal bar (usually 2.000 m long) of invar alloy mounted horizontally on a tripod perpendicular to the sightline
A bar to test theodolite levels
bankQuestions.explanation: A subtense bar is a 2-metre horizontal invar bar with targets at both ends. Sighting both targets measures the small horizontal angle α, giving D = 1.0 / tan(α/2).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Subtense bar = 2-metre horizontal invar bar for precision optical distance measurement.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In railway and highway geometry, what is a "simple circular curve"?
options: A single arc of a circle connecting two intersecting straight tangents with a uniform radius throughout
A curve made of two ellipses
A straight line on a slope
bankQuestions.explanation: A simple circular curve consists of a single circular arc of constant radius R connecting two straight alignments.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Simple circular curve: Single arc of constant radius R connecting two straights.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In highway geometry, what is a "compound curve"?
options: A curve composed of two or more circular arcs of different radii curving in the SAME direction with a common tangent at their junction point
A curve curving in opposite directions
A curve with a spiral and parabola
A straight road with two junctions
bankQuestions.explanation: A compound curve consists of two or more consecutive circular arcs of different radii curving in the same direction sharing a common tangent.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Compound curve: Two or more arcs of different radii curving in the SAME direction.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In highway geometry, what is a "reverse curve" (serpentine curve)?
options: A curve composed of two circular arcs of equal or different radii curving in OPPOSITE directions with a common tangent at their junction point
A curve curving in the same direction
bankQuestions.explanation: A reverse curve consists of two arcs turning in opposite directions (left then right) with a common point of reverse curvature (PRC).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Reverse curve: Two arcs curving in OPPOSITE directions with a common tangent.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Why are reverse curves strictly avoided on high-speed highways and mainline railway tracks?
options: Because the instantaneous reversal of centrifugal force causes severe passenger discomfort, vehicle swaying, and cant reversal difficulties
Because asphalt cracks on reverse curves
bankQuestions.explanation: At the point of reverse curvature, centrifugal force instantly flips direction, making superelevation runoff dangerous at high speed.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Reverse curves are avoided on high-speed roads/rail due to dangerous centrifugal force reversal.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is a "transition curve" (easement curve)?
options: A curve of non-uniform radius that transitions gradually from infinity (R = ∞) at the tangent to the full radius (R) of the circular curve
A curve that connects two mountains
A vertical curve over a bridge
bankQuestions.explanation: Transition curves provide a gradual introduction of curvature and superelevation, preventing sudden centrifugal shock.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Transition curve: Radius decreases gradually from infinity at tangent to R at circular arc.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which geometric curves are commonly adopted as transition curves in Indian railway and highway engineering?
options: Cubic parabola, Clothoid (Euler spiral), and Bernoulli's lemniscate
bankQuestions.explanation: Indian Railways and IRC standards adopt the cubic parabola and clothoid (Euler spiral) where curvature increases linearly with length.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Transition curves: Cubic parabola, Clothoid (Euler spiral), and Lemniscate.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In a simple circular curve with radius R and deflection angle Δ, what is the formula for the tangent length T?
bankQuestions.explanation: The length of each tangent from Point of Curve T1 (or T2) to Point of Intersection V is T = R tan(Δ/2).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Tangent length T = R tan(Δ / 2).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In a simple circular curve of radius R and deflection angle Δ, what is the formula for curve length L?
bankQuestions.explanation: Arc length of a circular curve is L = R × Δ(in radians) = (π R Δ) / 180°.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Curve length L = (π R Δ) / 180°.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In a simple circular curve of radius R and deflection angle Δ, what is the formula for the long chord length C?
bankQuestions.explanation: The straight chord joining T1 and T2 is C = 2 R sin(Δ/2).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Long chord C = 2 R sin(Δ / 2).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In a simple circular curve, what is the formula for the "apex distance" (external distance E)?
bankQuestions.explanation: The distance from intersection point V to the midpoint of the curve is E = R (sec(Δ/2) - 1).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Apex distance E = R [sec(Δ / 2) - 1].
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In a simple circular curve, what is the formula for the "mid-ordinate" (versed sine M)?
bankQuestions.explanation: The distance from midpoint of the long chord to the midpoint of the curve is M = R (1 - cos(Δ/2)).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Mid-ordinate M = R [1 - cos(Δ / 2)].
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In Rankine's method of tangential deflection angles for setting out circular curves, what is the formula for the deflection angle δ in minutes for a chord length c (in metres) on a curve of radius R (in metres)?
bankQuestions.explanation: Since δ = (c / 2R) radians = (c / 2R) × (180 × 60 / π) = (1718.87 × c) / R minutes.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Rankine's deflection angle: δ = (1718.9 × c) / R minutes.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In setting out a circular curve using the "two-theodolite method", which field measurement is completely dispensed with?
options: Linear measurement with tape or chain is completely eliminated
bankQuestions.explanation: In the two-theodolite method, two theodolites at T1 and T2 sight intersecting tangential rays simultaneously, eliminating all linear chaining.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Two-theodolite method: Zero linear chaining needed; points fixed purely by intersecting angles.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is a "summit curve" (crest curve) in highway vertical alignment?
options: A vertical curve with convexity upwards connecting an ascending gradient to a descending gradient
A vertical sag curve under a bridge
bankQuestions.explanation: A summit curve has positive convexity upward, joining an upgrade to a downgrade where headlight and stopping sight distances are critical.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Summit curve = Vertical curve with convexity UPWARDS (crest).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is a "valley curve" (sag curve) in highway vertical alignment?
options: A vertical curve with concavity upwards connecting a descending gradient to an ascending gradient
A circular curve in a deep valley
A hairpin bend on a hill road
A transition spiral on a bridge
bankQuestions.explanation: A valley (sag) curve dips downward, connecting a downgrade to an upgrade, where headlight beam distance and rider comfort are design limits.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Valley curve = Vertical curve with concavity UPWARDS (sag).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In plane table cartography, what conventional color is standardized for representing roads and metalled highways?
bankQuestions.explanation: On standard surveying topographical plans, roads and cart tracks are tinted with burnt sienna or crimson red.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Roads and highways are tinted with burnt sienna / red.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In plane table cartography, what conventional color is used for water bodies such as lakes, ponds, canals, and rivers?
bankQuestions.explanation: Water features, shorelines, canals, and reservoirs are universally depicted in blue tint.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Water bodies are tinted in Prussian blue / cyan.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In plane table cartography, what conventional color is standardized for cultivated agricultural fields?
bankQuestions.explanation: Cultivated agricultural land is colored with yellow ochre or pale wash of gamboge.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Cultivated land is tinted in yellow ochre.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In plane table cartography, what conventional color is standardized for wooded forest land and orchards?
bankQuestions.explanation: Forests, tree groves, jungles, and parks are depicted in standard green wash.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Forests and vegetation are tinted in green.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In plane table cartography, what conventional color is used for masonry buildings and concrete structures?
bankQuestions.explanation: Masonry buildings and pucca structures are outlined in black and hatched or tinted in crimson lake.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Masonry buildings are tinted in crimson lake / red.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the standard convention for representing a boundary pillar on a plane table cadastral field plan?
options: A neat small solid circle or triangle inscribed inside a square with its pillar identification number
bankQuestions.explanation: Cadastral boundary stones are drawn as small squares or circles enclosing a dot, labeled with the demarcation boundary pillar number.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Boundary pillars are drawn as small squares/circles with identification numbers.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the purpose of the "title block" drawn on a completed plane table survey sheet?
options: To provide essential metadata including project title, locality, scale, date, surveyor name, and reference datum
To cover a damaged corner of the paper
To protect the paper from fire
bankQuestions.explanation: The title block at the lower right corner records project name, cadastral district/village, graphic scale, surveyor signature, and date.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Title block records project name, locality, scale, surveyor, and date.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the primary function of the "north line" drawn on a plane table drawing sheet?
options: To show both True North and Magnetic North along with the observed magnetic declination and date
To point to the nearest railway station
To divide the drawing into halves
