bankQuestions.explanation: The north arrow displays true north and magnetic north arrows with the specific declination and epoch date.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: North line displays True and Magnetic North with declination and date.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In plane table surveying, how are contour lines drawn on the field sheet?
options: As smooth continuous curves drawn in burnt sienna brown ink with their elevations written in breaks along the lines
bankQuestions.explanation: Contours are inked in burnt sienna brown, with values written in gaps along the line facing uphill.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Contours are drawn in burnt sienna brown ink with elevations in breaks.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Why are contour elevation numbers on a plane table map always written facing the uphill direction?
options: So that anyone reading the map can immediately tell the uphill direction from the text orientation
To avoid running out of ink
bankQuestions.explanation: Writing contour labels facing uphill allows readers to perceive relief slope instantly without searching for other numbers.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Contour elevation labels face uphill for instant slope interpretation.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In plane table resection, what is "Lehmann's rule of proportional distances"?
options: The perpendicular distance of the true station point p from any resection ray is proportional to the ground distance to that respective station
The longest ray has zero distance
The distance is inversely proportional to board width
bankQuestions.explanation: Because angular orientation errors cause lateral ray displacement equal to distance × error, offset distance from ray ∝ Ground distance.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Offset from ray is proportional to ground distance to the station.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In plane table resection, what is "Lehmann's rule of consistent side"?
options: The true station point p must lie either completely to the right or completely to the left of all three resection rays when facing the ground stations
Point p must lie on the middle ray
Point p alternates between left and right
Point p is outside all triangles
bankQuestions.explanation: Facing the stations, point p lies consistently to the right of all three rays or consistently to the left of all three rays.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Point p lies all to the right or all to the left of the three rays.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the primary danger when performing resection from three control stations that lie on a circle with the instrument on the same circle?
options: The resection method fails completely because infinite trial positions satisfy the sightings (danger circle / great circle failure)
The paper will burn from sunlight
The tripod legs will sink into the ground
bankQuestions.explanation: If the instrument lies on the circumscribed circle through A, B, and C, the geometry is indeterminate and resection fails completely.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Great circle / danger circle failure: Table on circumference -> Infinite solutions.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In the Two-Point Problem, why is a preliminary auxiliary station D needed?
options: To establish a trial line on the sheet to resolve the unknown orientation before occupying the actual station
To measure the elevation of station C
To provide shade for the drawing board
bankQuestions.explanation: With only two points, orientation cannot be checked directly; auxiliary station D provides a trial line of sight.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Auxiliary station D provides a trial line to resolve orientation in the 2-point problem.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the mechanical method of solving the Three-Point Problem also called?
bankQuestions.explanation: The mechanical method uses transparent tracing paper to plot three rays and shift them over the map points.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Mechanical method = Tracing paper method.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In Bessel's graphical solution of the Three-Point Problem, what is the geometric construction employed?
bankQuestions.explanation: Bessel's method solves the three-point problem graphically by constructing an inscribed quadrilateral.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Bessel's method = Inscribed quadrilateral solution.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the advantage of plane table surveying when preparing architectural site layout plans?
options: Building outlines, pavements, trees, and underground utility covers are plotted and checked on-site with zero omitted features
It can be done in dark rooms
bankQuestions.explanation: Simultaneous field observation and plotting ensures all site details and boundary clearances are recorded authentically.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Plane tabling ensures zero omitted features on architectural site plans.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the main limitation of an untreated cloth or linen measuring tape when used with a plane table?
options: It stretches significantly under tension, shrinks when wet, and twists easily, reducing distance accuracy
bankQuestions.explanation: Untreated linen tapes stretch under pull and shrink in humidity, causing distance errors.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Linen tape stretches under pull and shrinks in moisture; only for rough offsets.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What type of tape provides the best accuracy for measuring radiation lines in plane table surveying?
options: A high-grade synthetic fiberglass or metallic tape (linen interwoven with phosphor bronze wires)
bankQuestions.explanation: Metallic tapes (varnished linen interwoven with bronze wires) resist stretching and provide dependable distance measurements.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Metallic or fiberglass tapes provide durable, non-stretching distance measurement.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the maximum recommended radiation sight distance with a plain alidade on a 1:1000 scale plane table map?
bankQuestions.explanation: Beyond 100 to 150 m, open sights without optical magnification suffer from inaccurate bisection and taped distance errors.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Plain alidade radiation limit: 100 to 150 m on 1:1000 maps.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In differential levelling, what is the "collimation error" of a level?
options: The vertical angular inclination between the line of collimation and the axis of the bubble tube
The friction in the focusing screw
The bending of the tripod leg
bankQuestions.explanation: Collimation error occurs when the line of sight is not strictly parallel to the bubble tube axis, causing tilted lines of sight.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Collimation error = Lack of parallelism between line of collimation and bubble tube axis.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: How does equalizing Back Sight and Fore Sight distances eliminate collimation error?
options: Because the line of sight rises or falls by the same vertical amount over equal distances, canceling completely when subtracting readings
Because it reduces sight distance to zero
bankQuestions.explanation: If collimation error angle is e, staff error is D·tan e. With equal sights, Δh = (BS + e·D) - (FS + e·D) = BS - FS.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Equal sight distances cancel collimation error: Δh = BS - FS.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In differential levelling, what is a "bench mark run"?
options: A line of levels run specifically to establish or verify the elevation of a new permanent bench mark from a known GTS bench mark
bankQuestions.explanation: A bench mark run is a precision differential levelling circuit connecting an existing datum BM to a newly established BM.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Bench mark run = Differential levelling line connecting two bench marks.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the "parallactic error" (parallax) in a level telescope and how is it completely eliminated?
options: Apparent movement between cross-hairs and image caused by image not falling in reticle plane; eliminated by focusing eyepiece then objective lens
bankQuestions.explanation: Parallax occurs when the real image from the objective does not form on the reticle plane. It is removed by focusing eyepiece sharply on cross-hairs, then focusing objective on target.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Parallax elimination: Focus eyepiece on cross-hairs first, then focus objective on target.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In the two-peg test, the instrument is set up at C midway between pegs A and B (distance = 60 m). Readings are A = 1.800 m, B = 1.400 m. What is the true elevation difference between A and B?
options: 0.400 metres (B is higher than A by 0.400 m)
bankQuestions.explanation: With equal sights from the midway setup, collimation error cancels: True difference h = 1.800 - 1.400 = 0.400 m (B is 0.400 m higher).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: True difference from midway setup = 1.800 - 1.400 = 0.400 m.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In the two-peg test, the instrument is next set up near peg B. Readings are B = 1.300 m, A = 1.750 m. If true difference is 0.400 m, what should the correct reading on A be, and is the collimation error up or down?
options: Correct reading on A = 1.700 m; line of collimation is inclined UPWARDS by 0.050 m
Correct reading = 1.750 m; error is zero
bankQuestions.explanation: Reading on B has zero error (instrument at B). True reading on A = Reading on B + 0.400 = 1.300 + 0.400 = 1.700 m. Since observed A is 1.750 m, line of sight is tilted UP by 0.050 m.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Correct reading on A = 1.300 + 0.400 = 1.700 m; Collimation error = +0.050 m (upward).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: How is the collimation error adjusted mechanically in a dumpy level after the two-peg test?
options: By shifting the horizontal cross-hair vertically using the diaphragm capstan screws until it reads the true reading on the distant staff
By adjusting the leveling foot screws
bankQuestions.explanation: With the bubble centered, the diaphragm screws are adjusted to raise or lower the cross-hair to the calculated true staff reading.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Adjust diaphragm capstan screws to align horizontal cross-hair with true staff reading.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In a tilting level, how is collimation error adjusted after the two-peg test?
options: The telescope is set to the true staff reading using the tilting micrometer screw, and the bubble is centered using its vial adjusting screws
bankQuestions.explanation: In a tilting level, the telescope is directed to the true reading with the micrometer screw, then the bubble vial screws are adjusted to bring the bubble to center.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Tilting level adjustment: Sight true reading with tilting screw, then center bubble using vial screws.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the purpose of the "tribrach" on a modern levelling instrument?
options: The triangular three-armed casting that carries the three leveling foot screws and the circular bull's-eye bubble
The glass reticle inside the telescope
The metal case of the tripod
bankQuestions.explanation: The tribrach is the three-armed base plate carrying the foot screws and circular bubble for leveling the instrument.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Tribrach = Triangular base carrying the three leveling foot screws.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the "trivet" (foot plate) of a dumpy level?
options: The lower plate of the leveling head with three depressions for foot screw tips that screws directly onto the tripod head
bankQuestions.explanation: The trivet is the lower fixed base plate that attaches to the tripod head and supports the leveling foot screws.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Trivet = Lower plate of leveling head that screws onto the tripod.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the purpose of the "circular bubble" (bull's-eye level) on an automatic level?
options: For rough initial leveling of the instrument so that the pendulum compensator swings freely within its operating working range
bankQuestions.explanation: The circular bubble brings the instrument within the ±15' working range of the pendulum compensator.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Circular bubble brings auto level within compensator working range (±15').
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What happens if an automatic level is set up with its circular bubble outside the black ring mark?
options: The compensator prism hits its mechanical limit stops and CANNOT level the line of sight, producing severe observation errors
bankQuestions.explanation: If outside the bubble ring, the suspended compensator rests against its physical travel limit, disabling auto-leveling.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Compensator cannot function if circular bubble is outside its target ring.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the purpose of the "compensator check button" (or push button) on an automatic level?
options: To slightly tap or displace the suspended compensator prism to verify that it swings freely and returns to the exact same reading
bankQuestions.explanation: Pressing the compensator button displaces the prism; when released, the image must twitch and return to the identical reading, proving it is not stuck.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Compensator button verifies that the pendulum prism swings freely and is not stuck.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In bar-coded levelling staves used with digital levels, what material is used for precision invar staves?
options: A continuous invar alloy ribbon under spring tension mounted in an aluminum staff frame to eliminate thermal expansion
bankQuestions.explanation: Precision digital levelling staves mount an invar alloy band under spring tension to prevent temperature expansion errors.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Precision digital staves use an invar alloy band under spring tension.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the primary operational advantage of a digital level over a traditional optical dumpy level?
options: It eliminates human staff reading errors, eliminates booking and transcription mistakes, and automatically computes reduced levels and closures
It operates in complete darkness without illumination
It does not require a tripod
bankQuestions.explanation: Digital levels scan barcodes automatically, eliminating misreadings, inverted numbers, and manual arithmetic blunders.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Digital levels eliminate human reading, booking, and arithmetic mistakes.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In a transit theodolite, what is the "centering error"?
options: The error introduced when the vertical axis of the instrument does not pass exactly through the ground station peg center
The error of the altitude bubble
The tilt of the trunnion axis
bankQuestions.explanation: Centering error occurs when the plumb bob point does not hang directly over the center punch mark on the station peg.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Centering error = Instrument vertical axis not plumb over ground station peg.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: How does an error in centering a theodolite affect horizontal angle measurements?
options: The angular error is inversely proportional to sight distance; it is severe for short sights and negligible for long sights
It is proportional to sight distance
It is constant for all distances
bankQuestions.explanation: Centering displacement e produces angular error δ ≈ e / D. Shorter sight distances D magnify the angular deviation.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Centering error impact is INVERSELY proportional to sight distance (critical for short sights!).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In theodolite angle observation, what is "double centering" (double sighting or double transiting)?
options: Prolonging a straight survey line AB to C by sighting B on Face Left, transiting to C1, then sighting B on Face Right, transiting to C2, and taking the midpoint of C1 and C2
bankQuestions.explanation: Double transiting (prolonging a line with Face Left and Face Right) completely eliminates collimation error when extending straight lines.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Double transiting: Prolongs lines with Face Left and Face Right, taking the midpoint to eliminate collimation error.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the "spire test" (or horizontal axis test) in the permanent adjustment of a transit theodolite?
options: Testing whether the horizontal trunnion axis is strictly perpendicular to the vertical axis by sighting a high spire or church steeple
Testing the optical sharpness of the objective lens
bankQuestions.explanation: The spire test sights a high point on Face Left, depresses to ground mark, then reverses face and checks if the depressed line coincides.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Spire test: Tests perpendicularity of horizontal axis to vertical axis.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: How is the horizontal trunnion axis adjusted mechanically if the spire test reveals an error?
options: By raising or lowering the adjustable bearing block of the trunnion axis on one of the standards using capstan screws
By sliding the plate level vial
bankQuestions.explanation: One standard features an adjustable trunnion bearing; turning its capstan screws levels the trunnion axis.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Trunnion axis adjustment: Adjust capstan screw on the movable standard bearing block.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the "collimation in azimuth test" (or line of collimation test) in a transit theodolite?
options: Testing whether the line of collimation is strictly perpendicular to the horizontal trunnion axis
Testing if the telescope is horizontal
bankQuestions.explanation: The collimation test checks whether the line of sight is at 90° to the horizontal axis so that transiting sweeps a flat plane.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Collimation test: Verifies line of collimation ⊥ horizontal axis.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: How is collimation error in azimuth adjusted mechanically in a transit theodolite?
options: By moving the vertical cross-hair laterally using the left and right diaphragm capstan screws
bankQuestions.explanation: Left and right capstan screws on the reticle shift the vertical cross-hair sideways to center it on the true sightline.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Adjust lateral diaphragm capstan screws to center vertical cross-hair.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In theodolite traversing, what are "consecutive coordinates"?
options: The latitude (l cos θ) and departure (l sin θ) of each traverse station with respect to the immediately preceding station
The total coordinates from the origin
bankQuestions.explanation: Consecutive coordinates (latitude and departure) define the relative position of each station with respect to the previous station.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Consecutive coordinates = Latitude and Departure relative to previous station.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What are "independent coordinates" (total coordinates) in theodolite traversing?
options: The total Northing and Easting of each traverse station computed with respect to a single fixed origin
Coordinates that do not depend on angles
bankQuestions.explanation: Independent coordinates are cumulative total Northings and Eastings calculated from a single coordinate origin.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Independent coordinates = Total Northing and Easting from common origin.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is "Gale's traverse table"?
options: A standardized tabular sheet used to systematically calculate, balance, and plot theodolite traverse coordinates
bankQuestions.explanation: Gale's traverse system tabulates line lengths, bearings, raw latitudes/departures, closing error corrections, and total coordinates.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Gale's table systematically computes and balances traverse coordinates.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In balancing a theodolite traverse by Bowditch's rule, what is the correction applied to the latitude of line AB of length l?
options: Correction = - Total closing error in latitude × (Length of line AB / Total perimeter of traverse)
Correction = Total error / Number of sides
Correction = Total error × Latitude of AB
bankQuestions.explanation: Bowditch latitude correction: C_L = - ΣL × (l / Σl), where ΣL is total latitude closing error and Σl is total perimeter.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Bowditch latitude correction = - ΣL × (l / Perimeter).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In balancing a theodolite traverse by Bowditch's rule, what is the correction applied to the departure of line AB of length l?
options: Correction = - Total closing error in departure × (Length of line AB / Total perimeter of traverse)
Correction = Total error / Number of sides
Correction = Total error × Departure of AB
bankQuestions.explanation: Bowditch departure correction: C_D = - ΣD × (l / Σl), where ΣD is total departure closing error and Σl is perimeter.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Bowditch departure correction = - ΣD × (l / Perimeter).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In balancing a theodolite traverse by the Transit rule, what is the correction applied to the latitude of line AB?
options: Correction = - Total closing error in latitude × (|Latitude of AB| / Sum of all absolute latitudes)
Correction = - Total error × (Length of AB / Perimeter)
bankQuestions.explanation: Transit rule latitude correction: C_L = - ΣL × (|L_AB| / Σ|L|).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Transit rule: Correction proportional to latitude itself: - ΣL × (|L| / Σ|L|).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In balancing a theodolite traverse by the Transit rule, what is the correction applied to the departure of line AB?
options: Correction = - Total closing error in departure × (|Departure of AB| / Sum of all absolute departures)
Correction = - Total error × (Length of AB / Perimeter)
Correction = Total error / Number of sides
bankQuestions.explanation: Transit rule departure correction: C_D = - ΣD × (|D_AB| / Σ|D|).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Transit rule: Correction proportional to departure itself: - ΣD × (|D| / Σ|D|).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the formula for the linear closing error e of a theodolite traverse?
bankQuestions.explanation: By Pythagoras theorem, the linear closing error hypotenuse is e = √[(ΣL)² + (ΣD)²].
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Linear closing error: e = √[(ΣL)² + (ΣD)²].
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the direction (reduced bearing θ) of the closing error in a traverse?
bankQuestions.explanation: The direction of the closing error vector satisfies tan θ = Departure Error / Latitude Error = |ΣD / ΣL|.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Closing error bearing: tan θ = |ΣD / ΣL|.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In theodolite traversing, what are "omitted measurements"?
options: Quantities (such as length or bearing of one or more lines) that could not be measured directly in the field and are computed trigonometrically
Mistakes where surveyor forgot to read staff
Points left out of the drawing
bankQuestions.explanation: Omitted measurements occur when obstacles prevent direct measurement of a length or bearing, which is then solved using ΣL = 0 and ΣD = 0.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Omitted measurements = Missing line lengths or bearings solved via ΣL = 0 and ΣD = 0.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the maximum number of unknown quantities (lengths or bearings) that can be computed mathematically in a closed theodolite traverse?
options: At most two unknown parts (e.g. length and bearing of one line, or lengths of two lines, or bearings of two lines)
bankQuestions.explanation: Because a closed traverse provides only two independent equilibrium equations (ΣL = 0 and ΣD = 0), at most two unknowns can be determined.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: At most TWO unknown parts can be solved in a closed traverse (from ΣL = 0 and ΣD = 0).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In tacheometry, how is the multiplying constant K = f / i verified in the field?
options: By measuring horizontal base distances (e.g. 50 m, 100 m, 150 m) with an invar tape, taking staff intercepts, and calculating K = (D2 - D1) / (s2 - s1)
bankQuestions.explanation: Plot known taped distances D1, D2 and observe intercepts s1, s2: K = (D2 - D1) / (s2 - s1).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Field calibration: K = (D2 - D1) / (s2 - s1).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In tacheometry, how is the additive constant C = (f + d) verified in the field?
options: By substituting the calculated multiplying constant K into D = K·s + C for known taped baseline distances
By measuring telescope tube length with a ruler
bankQuestions.explanation: With known D and calibrated K, additive constant is C = D - K·s.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Additive constant: C = D - K·s.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the "degree of curve" D defined as in Indian Railway practice (using a 30-metre chord)?
options: The central angle (in degrees) subtended at the center of the curve by a standard chord of 30 metres length (D = 1718.9 / R)
The angle subtended by a 1-metre chord
The total deflection angle of the curve
bankQuestions.explanation: In 30 m chord definition: sin(D/2) = 15 / R. For large radii, (D/2) × (π/180) ≈ 15 / R, so D = 30 × (180 / π) / R = 1718.9 / R degrees.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Degree of curve (30 m chord): D = 1718.9 / R (or R = 1718.9 / D).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In highway engineering using a 20-metre chord, what is the relationship between degree of curve D and radius R?
bankQuestions.explanation: For a 20-metre chord: D = 20 × (180 / π) / R = 1145.9 / R degrees.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Degree of curve (20 m chord): D = 1146 / R (or R = 1146 / D).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: If a railway curve has a degree of curve D = 2° based on a 30-metre chord, what is its radius R?
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: If a highway curve has a degree of curve D = 3° based on a 20-metre chord, what is its radius R?
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In setting out a circular curve, what is the "Point of Curve" (P.C.) or Point of Commencement T1?
options: The starting point of the circular curve where the alignment transitions from the rear straight tangent to the circular arc
The point of intersection of tangents
bankQuestions.explanation: Point of Curve (T1 or PC) marks the transition from the backward tangent into the circular curve: Chainage of T1 = Chainage of PI - Tangent Length T.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Point of Curve (PC / T1): Beginning of curve; Chainage of T1 = Chainage of PI - T.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In setting out a circular curve, what is the "Point of Tangency" (P.T.) T2?
options: The terminal point of the circular curve where the alignment transitions from the circular arc into the forward straight tangent
The middle of the long chord
bankQuestions.explanation: Point of Tangency (T2 or PT) marks the transition from circular curve into the forward tangent: Chainage of T2 = Chainage of T1 + Curve Length L.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Point of Tangency (PT / T2): End of curve; Chainage of T2 = Chainage of T1 + L.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: If the chainage of the Point of Intersection (P.I.) is 1250.00 m and tangent length T is 180.00 m, what is the chainage of the Point of Curve T1?
bankQuestions.explanation: Chainage of T1 = Chainage of PI - Tangent Length T = 1250.00 - 180.00 = 1070.00 m.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: If the chainage of T1 is 1070.00 m and the calculated length of the curve L is 314.16 m, what is the chainage of the Point of Tangency T2?
bankQuestions.explanation: Chainage of T2 = Chainage of T1 + Curve Length L = 1070.00 + 314.16 = 1384.16 m. Note: NEVER add tangent length to PI to get T2!
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Chainage of T2 = Chainage of T1 + L = 1070 + 314.16 = 1384.16 m.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Why must the chainage of Point of Tangency T2 NEVER be calculated by adding tangent length T to the chainage of Point of Intersection (P.I.)?
options: Because the road alignment follows the shorter curved arc (T1 to T2), not the two longer straight tangents through PI
Because the chain expands on curves
Because PI is always in a river
bankQuestions.explanation: The route goes along the curve L, not via PI: True path length = T1 + L, which is shorter than traversing 2 tangents (2T).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Always add curve length L to T1 to get T2 (Chainage of T2 = Chainage of T1 + L).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the "shift of a circular curve" S when transitioning with a transition curve of length L and circular radius R?
bankQuestions.explanation: To insert a transition curve, the circular arc is shifted inward radially by an amount S = L² / (24 R).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Shift of circular curve: S = L² / (24 R).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In plane table traversing, what is an "interior angle traverse"?
options: A traverse where internal angles between adjacent lines are plotted by bisection from each station
A traverse that measures vertical angles
bankQuestions.explanation: In an interior angle traverse, the table is oriented by backsight along each traverse leg and interior angles plotted.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Interior angle traverse plots interior angles at each station setup.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the purpose of drawing diagonal grid lines across a plane table field sheet before taking it to the field?
options: To provide a permanent reference grid to detect, measure, and correct any future shrinkage or distortion of the paper
To create square boxes for notes
bankQuestions.explanation: A pre-drawn coordinate grid expands and shrinks with the sheet, enabling accurate mathematical scaling and distortion monitoring.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Coordinate grid lines on sheet monitor and correct paper shrinkage distortion.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What type of eraser is recommended for erasing pencil lines on a plane table drawing sheet without tearing the surface fibres?
options: A soft kneaded art gum or vinyl eraser used with a metal erasing shield
bankQuestions.explanation: Soft vinyl or kneaded art erasers remove graphite cleanly without abrading or scuffing delicate paper fibres.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Use soft vinyl erasers with an erasing shield to protect paper surface.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In plane table surveying, what is an "erasing shield"?
options: A thin sheet of flexible stainless steel with precise slots and holes to expose only the exact pencil line to be erased
A shield to protect against rain
A wooden guard for the board
bankQuestions.explanation: An erasing shield masks surrounding drawing details, allowing the surveyor to erase a single erroneous line cleanly.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Erasing shield masks surrounding work, allowing isolated line erasure.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the recommended height of a plane table board above the ground when set up for comfortable working by an average surveyor?
options: Approximately at elbow level (about 1.0 to 1.2 metres above ground)
bankQuestions.explanation: Setting the table at elbow height allows the surveyor to lean comfortably over the board for sighting and plotting without stooping.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Table setup height: Elbow height (approx. 1.0 to 1.2 m above ground).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Why should the tripod legs of a plane table be spread sufficiently wide apart (forming an angle of roughly 60° with the ground)?
options: To ensure maximum lateral stability, lower the centre of gravity, and prevent tipping under wind pressure
To allow the surveyor to sit under the table
bankQuestions.explanation: A broad triangular stance lowers the center of gravity and resists torsional flexing from wind gusts.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Spread tripod legs to ~60° with ground for maximum stability against wind.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In plane tabling on a steep hillside, how should the three tripod legs be positioned for safety and stability?
options: Two legs placed downhill and one leg placed uphill firmly embedded into the slope
Two legs uphill and one downhill
All three legs in a straight line
bankQuestions.explanation: Placing two legs downhill and one uphill forms a wide stable base that prevents the instrument from toppling downhill.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: On steep slopes: Place TWO legs downhill and ONE leg uphill.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the function of the "leg clamp screws" (wing nuts) on an adjustable extension tripod for a plane table?
options: To securely clamp the sliding telescopic wooden or aluminum legs at the desired extension height
bankQuestions.explanation: Leg wing nuts tighten the extension sliding segments, establishing a rigid tripod height on uneven ground.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Leg clamp wing nuts lock telescopic tripod legs at the desired height.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In plane table surveying, how is a circle or curved boundary wall plotted in the field?
options: By radiating rays to multiple closely spaced perimeter points along the curve and joining them with an irregular French curve
By drawing a circle with a compass from an estimated center
By treating it as a single straight line
bankQuestions.explanation: Irregular curved boundaries are mapped by plotting frequent radiation points and joining them smoothly using French curves.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Curved boundaries: Radiate multiple points along the curve, join with French curves.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is a "French curve" used for in plane table drawing office practice?
options: A plastic template with varying smooth mathematical curves used to ink non-circular curved boundaries and contours
A device to measure angles in France
A level tube filled with wine
bankQuestions.explanation: French curves are plastic drafting templates with smooth transitions used to draw continuous irregular curves and contours.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: French curve = Drafting template for inking irregular smooth curves and contours.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the "beam compass" (trammel) used for in large-scale plane table plotting?
options: Drawing circular arcs and large intersecting radius circles that exceed the reach of standard drafting compasses
bankQuestions.explanation: A beam compass consists of a long rigid bar with sliding divider points used to prick or swing large control radius arcs.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Beam compass = Long-reach bar compass for drawing large radius arcs and base circles.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In plane tabling, why should the surveyor avoid wearing magnetic steel buttons or belt buckles while orienting with a trough compass?
options: Because personal ferromagnetic items held near the board edge will deflect the sensitive magnetic needle, causing orientation error
Because they will scratch the timber
Because they will tear the paper
bankQuestions.explanation: Personal iron items (belt buckles, pocket knives, steel buttons) act as local attraction sources when standing near the trough compass.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Avoid steel belt buckles or pocket knives near the trough compass to prevent orientation error.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: How does a topographer verify that the plane table has not been accidentally disturbed or rotated during a day's work at a station?
options: By periodically placing the alidade back along a reference baseline ray and checking if the distant sighting target remains bisected
By checking the time on a watch
By measuring the height of the board
bankQuestions.explanation: Periodically checking the sightline to a distant reference beacon confirms that orientation has not shifted during work.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Verify orientation stability by frequently re-sighting a distant reference station.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In plane table surveying, what is an "auxiliary ray" used for?
options: A supplementary line drawn to check the intersection of other rays or locate minor intermediate topographic features
A ray drawn in gold ink
bankQuestions.explanation: Auxiliary rays provide secondary checks or detail bisections across the active mapping zone.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Auxiliary ray = Supplementary ray for checking intersections or locating minor detail.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the purpose of the "centering score" (cross mark) engraved on the brass plate under a plane table board?
options: It marks the exact central vertical axis of the mounting socket directly above which the board rotates
bankQuestions.explanation: The central socket mark aligns the board with the vertical axis of the tripod head.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Socket center mark indicates the rotational vertical axis of the table.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In plane table surveying, what is meant by "scale of the survey"?
options: The ratio between distances measured on the drawing paper and the corresponding true horizontal distances on the ground
The weight of the drawing board
The graduations on the leveling staff
The range of the alidade telescope
bankQuestions.explanation: Map scale is the fixed representative fraction (e.g. 1:1000 or 1 cm = 10 m) relating map dimensions to ground dimensions.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Scale = Ratio between map distance and true ground distance.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: On a plane table survey conducted at a scale of 1:500, what distance on the ground is represented by 1 centimetre on the drawing sheet?
bankQuestions.explanation: 1 cm on map = 500 cm on ground = 5 metres.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: On a plane table survey conducted at a scale of 1:2000, what distance on the ground is represented by 1 centimetre on paper?
bankQuestions.explanation: 1 cm on map = 2000 cm on ground = 20 metres.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: On a plane table survey conducted at a scale of 1:250, what distance on the ground is represented by 2 millimetres on paper?
bankQuestions.explanation: 2 mm on map = 2 × 250 mm = 500 mm = 0.50 m.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the primary factor dictating the choice of scale for a plane table topographic survey?
options: The purpose of the survey, the extent of the area, and the finest degree of detail required to be depicted
The length of the tripod legs
The size of the surveyor's car
bankQuestions.explanation: Survey scale is chosen based on intended application (cadastral vs regional), area extent, and resolution of detail required.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Scale selection depends on survey purpose, extent of terrain, and required detail resolution.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In plane table surveying, what is an "optical plummet"?
options: A right-angled optical sighting prism inside the alidade or tribrach providing a line of sight straight down to the station peg mark
A magnifying glass for reading scales
bankQuestions.explanation: An optical plummet directs line of sight vertically downward through a 90° prism, allowing wind-proof centering over the peg mark.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Optical plummet: Optical sighting system for wind-free, precision station centering.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Why is an optical plummet vastly superior to a plumb bob on windy, exposed mountain summits?
options: It is completely immune to wind swing and turbulence that make a suspended plumb bob oscillate continuously
bankQuestions.explanation: A plumb bob swings wildly in mountain winds, whereas an optical plummet sightline is unaffected by air currents.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Optical plummet is immune to wind gusts, providing stable centering on windy terrain.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In plane tabling, what is meant by "working from whole to part"?
options: Establishing a widely spaced, highly accurate primary control network across the entire tract first, and then filling in interior details
Starting from the edge of the paper
Surveying the whole country in one day
Measuring all trees before measuring roads
bankQuestions.explanation: Working from whole to part confines errors within major control triangles, preventing cumulative error accumulation.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Working from whole to part: Major primary control framework first, interior details second.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What happens if a plane tabler violates the principle of "working from whole to part" and builds the map by adding small local surveys consecutively?
options: Small local plotting and orientation errors accumulate and magnify continuously, resulting in massive distortion at the outer perimeter
The survey finishes twice as fast
bankQuestions.explanation: Working from part to whole accumulates small errors without constraint, distorting the entire map.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Working from part to whole accumulates and magnifies errors across the survey.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In plane table surveying, how should field pencil rays be drawn to keep the finished map sheet clean?
options: Draw only short ray dashes near the expected position of the object rather than ruling continuous lines across the entire board
Draw thick dark lines across the whole paper
Draw rays in red wax crayon
bankQuestions.explanation: Ruling short dashes near the anticipated target position keeps the central sheet uncluttered and smudge-free.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Draw short ray dashes near target location to avoid cluttering the field sheet.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the role of an "indexing letter or number" placed next to each ray dash during field plane tabling?
options: To identify which ground object that particular ray was sighted towards, preventing confusion when plotting multiple features
bankQuestions.explanation: Labeling each ray dash (e.g. Tree 1, Well, Corner A) prevents misidentifying rays when intersecting from the second station.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Label ray dashes with feature names/numbers to avoid misidentification during intersection.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In plane table intersection, what is the best practice for bisecting a distant ranging rod with the alidade?
options: Bisect the lowest visible point of the rod near the ground mark to avoid vertical inclination errors
Bisect the top of the flag
Bisect the shadow of the rod
bankQuestions.explanation: Sighting near the base eliminates aiming errors caused by out-of-plumb rods.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Bisect the lowest visible point of the ranging rod near the ground.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In plane table surveying, what is an "edge-bound field sheet"?
options: A drawing sheet whose edges are wrapped around the edges of the board and pasted or taped underneath to prevent edge lifting by wind
A sheet bound in a book
A sheet with a steel border
bankQuestions.explanation: Taping or folding paper edges beneath the board prevents strong winds from getting under the paper and tearing it.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Fold and secure sheet edges beneath the board to resist wind lift.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the function of the "compass lifter" screw on a trough compass box?
options: To gently lower the magnetic needle onto the pivot for observation and lift it securely against the glass lid when not in use
bankQuestions.explanation: The lifting screw raises the needle off the sharp pivot, preventing jewel bearing damage during transit.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Compass lifter locks needle against glass to protect the pivot during transport.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the recommended method to remove static electric charges from a plane table drawing sheet on very dry windy days?
options: Gently wipe the paper surface with a clean, slightly damp cotton cloth or touch a grounded metal object to the board
Heat the board with a flame
bankQuestions.explanation: A slightly damp cloth discharges electrostatic buildup without wetting the paper fibres.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Gently wipe paper with a slightly damp cloth to dissipate static charges.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In precision levelling, what is the "collimation error" per metre of sight distance?
options: e = (Observed staff reading - True staff reading) / Sight distance
bankQuestions.explanation: Collimation error per unit distance is the angular tilt slope e = Δh_error / D.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Collimation error rate e = Staff reading error / Sight distance.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the purpose of using two levelling staves alternately (staff A and staff B) in precision differential levelling runs?
options: To leapfrog staves at alternate change points, speeding up progress while canceling zero-point calibration differences between staves
To have a spare staff if one breaks
To allow two staffmen to race
bankQuestions.explanation: Leapfrogging two staves (A and B) ensures that each staff appears an equal number of times as Back Sight and Fore Sight, canceling zero-offset differences.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Leapfrogging two staves cancels zero-point index error between the two staves.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In differential levelling, what is a "bench mark pillar"?
options: A solid concrete or granite pillar embedded deep below frost and moisture depth with a spherical brass rivet on top marking true elevation
A pillar of bricks on grass
bankQuestions.explanation: Permanent GTS benchmark pillars are founded on deep stable strata to resist seasonal soil heave.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Benchmark pillar: Deeply founded concrete/granite monument with top spherical brass rivet.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is a "spherical brass rivet" (datum plug) on a permanent benchmark used for?
options: To provide a single, well-defined point of contact for the flat base of the levelling staff without rocking or wobble
bankQuestions.explanation: A rounded brass rivet ensures that a flat staff base rests tangentially on a single distinct point of contact.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Spherical brass rivet provides a stable, wobble-free single point of contact for the staff.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In differential levelling, what is meant by "balancing sights"?
options: Keeping the length of the Back Sight distance equal to the length of the Fore Sight distance from each setup station
Balancing the level on one tripod leg
Keeping the staff reading at 2.000 m
bankQuestions.explanation: Balancing sights (D_BS = D_FS) ensures that collimation error, curvature, and constant refraction cancel completely.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Balancing sights = Equalizing Back Sight and Fore Sight distances.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the maximum permissible difference between cumulative Back Sight distances and cumulative Fore Sight distances in first-order geodetic levelling?
options: Not more than 2 to 5 metres over an entire section run
bankQuestions.explanation: First-order geodetic standards require cumulative sight distance differences to remain under 2 to 5 m to ensure complete error cancellation.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: First-order levelling: Cumulative BS and FS distance difference must be under 2 to 5 m.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In differential levelling, why should observations NEVER be taken during midday hours when the sun is blazing and ground heat shimmer is intense?
options: Because boiling heat shimmer and atmospheric boiling cause severe optical refraction fluctuations that blur cross-hairs and produce large random errors
Because the staff expands by 10 metres
Because the tripod will catch fire
Because the level bubble will freeze
bankQuestions.explanation: Intense solar radiation creates turbulent thermal air convection near the ground, causing shimmering images and fluctuating refraction.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Avoid levelling during midday heat shimmer; thermal turbulence causes severe refraction errors.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What time of day provides the most stable atmospheric conditions for high-precision differential levelling?
options: Early morning hours just after sunrise and late afternoon hours before sunset (overcast calm skies are ideal)
bankQuestions.explanation: Early mornings and overcast days have uniform air density and minimal thermal gradients, minimizing refraction errors.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Best levelling conditions: Early morning or calm overcast days with zero heat shimmer.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the purpose of an "umbrella" in precision differential levelling with a dumpy or auto level?
options: To shield the level from direct solar radiation, preventing differential thermal expansion of the telescope tube and bubble vial
To protect the surveyor from sunburn
bankQuestions.explanation: Uneven sunlight on one side of a metal telescope tube causes differential expansion, tilting the line of collimation and displacing the bubble.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Survey umbrella prevents uneven solar heating and thermal tube warping.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is "differential thermal expansion" of a levelling telescope?
options: The warping of the telescope barrel when one side is heated by direct sunlight while the other is in shade, deflecting the line of collimation
The boiling of the spirit level fluid
The cracking of the tripod legs
bankQuestions.explanation: Direct sun expands the sunny side of the brass barrel, curving the telescope slightly and introducing collimation error.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Differential solar heating curves the telescope barrel, introducing temporary collimation error.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In differential levelling, what is the "zero error" (index error) of a levelling staff?
options: The error caused when the brass shoe at the base of the staff has worn down, so the zero mark does not coincide with the true staff bottom
An error in reading zero on the staff
bankQuestions.explanation: Shoe wear erodes the base, so readings are slightly too large: Measured reading = True height + wear error.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Staff zero error: Wear on the bottom brass shoe causes all readings on that staff to be too large.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: How does the staff zero error affect the calculated elevation difference between two points if the same staff is used for both Back Sight and Fore Sight?
options: It cancels out completely, because the constant base wear error is subtracted: Δh = (BS + e) - (FS + e) = BS - FS
It makes the final RL too high
It makes the final RL too low
bankQuestions.explanation: Using the identical staff for both sights subtracts the constant base error, leaving the true height difference intact.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Staff base wear error cancels completely when the SAME staff is used for BS and FS.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What happens to the staff zero error if two different staves with different base wear are used for Back Sight and Fore Sight?
options: The difference between their base errors accumulates systematically into every setup
bankQuestions.explanation: If staff A has wear e1 and staff B has wear e2, the difference (e1 - e2) accumulates systematically unless staves are leapfrogged.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Different staff base wear errors do not cancel unless staves are leapfrogged at alternate change points.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In profile levelling, how are the horizontal and vertical scales customarily chosen when drawing the ground profile on graph paper?
options: The vertical scale is exaggerated (typically 10 times larger than the horizontal scale) to make relief variations clearly discernible
Vertical scale is 10 times smaller than horizontal scale
bankQuestions.explanation: Vertical exaggeration (e.g. Horizontal 1:1000, Vertical 1:100) accentuates gentle slopes and undulations for design of road/rail formations.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Vertical scale in profile drawing is exaggerated (usually 10 times) to accentuate relief.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the "formation level" (subgrade level) in highway and railway engineering profile drawings?
options: The proposed finished ground level of the road or railway bed upon which paving or ballast is placed
The natural ground level before excavation
bankQuestions.explanation: Formation level is the engineered design elevation of the earthwork formation (subgrade) along the route.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Formation level = Engineered design elevation of the finished subgrade bed.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In road earthwork drawings, what does "depth of cutting" at a given chainage represent?
options: The vertical height by which the existing natural ground level exceeds the proposed formation level (Cutting = Existing RL - Formation RL)
bankQuestions.explanation: When existing ground is higher than proposed formation level, material must be cut: Cutting = Existing RL - Formation RL.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Depth of cutting = Existing Ground RL - Formation RL (when ground is higher).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In road earthwork drawings, what does "height of banking" (height of filling or embankment) represent?
options: The vertical height by which the proposed formation level exceeds the existing natural ground level (Filling = Formation RL - Existing RL)
The height of the bridge pier
bankQuestions.explanation: When proposed formation level is higher than existing ground, earth must be filled: Filling = Formation RL - Existing RL.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Height of filling = Formation RL - Existing Ground RL (when formation is higher).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is a "grade stake" in construction levelling?
options: A wooden peg driven into the ground whose top (or a mark on its side) indicates the exact grade or elevation to which earthwork must be cut or filled
A stake used to tie cows
bankQuestions.explanation: Grade stakes guide earthmoving contractors by showing the exact finish elevation or required depth of cut/fill.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Grade stake = Peg indicating design elevation for earthwork cutting or filling.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is a "boning rod" (traveler) used for in trench and pipeline excavation levelling?
options: A T-shaped wooden rod of fixed height sighted across sight rails to check the uniform excavation depth and invert level of a sewer trench
bankQuestions.explanation: Boning rods are T-shaped sighting timbers held in trenches to verify that the excavation floor follows the design gradient between sight rails.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Boning rod (T-rod) verifies trench excavation depth and sewer pipe gradient between sight rails.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is a "sight rail" in sewer construction levelling?
options: A horizontal timber board fixed across a trench between two uprights at a known height above the proposed sewer pipe invert level
bankQuestions.explanation: Sight rails are horizontal boards clamped across trench uprights at a uniform height above sewer pipe invert to guide boning rods.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Sight rail = Horizontal timber rail fixed across trench at known height above pipe invert.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the primary function of the leather carrying case provided with a high quality surveying alidade?
options: To protect the delicate sighting vanes, bubble vial, and beveled fiducial edge from bending and impacts during field transit
To act as a seat for the surveyor
bankQuestions.explanation: The fitted leather or wooden case cushions the alidade against accidental knocks that would bend vanes or dent the ruling edge.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Fitted carrying case protects alidade vanes and fiducial edge from distortion.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In plane table surveying, what is an "edge-clipped sheet"?
options: A drawing sheet held to the board by multiple spring clips distributed along the margins rather than driven pins
bankQuestions.explanation: Spring clips hold paper firmly around margins without penetrating or weakening the paper body.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Edge-clipped sheet uses spring clips along margins, avoiding pin punctures.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: How does an observer identify which ray corresponds to which ground station when multiple radiating lines are drafted from a single setup?
options: By lightly marking the ground station name or number in pencil at the end of each ray dash
By drawing rays in different colors
By measuring the angle of the sun
bankQuestions.explanation: Neatly annotating station identifiers beside ray ends prevents confusion when drawing intersecting rays from other stations.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Annotate station labels at ray ends to prevent misidentification during intersection.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the recommended diameter of a station pin hole pricked on a precision plane table drawing sheet?
options: Less than 0.2 millimetres (a fine puncture made with a sharp needle point)
bankQuestions.explanation: Fine punctures under 0.2 mm preserve geometric accuracy to within drafting limits on large scale maps.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Station pin pricks must be finer than 0.2 mm.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Why should the observer avoid sliding the alidade heavily across the drawing paper surface?
options: Dragging the heavy metal blade creates grey graphite smudges and abrades delicate pencil linework
Because it will break the tripod
bankQuestions.explanation: Lifting the alidade and placing it down carefully avoids dragging graphite smudges across the sheet.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Lift and place the alidade gently; do not drag it across graphite lines.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the function of the "dusting brush" (drafting brush) used by a plane tabler?
options: To gently sweep eraser crumbs and grit off the paper without smudging graphite pencil marks with the hand
To clean the plumb bob string
bankQuestions.explanation: A soft horsehair dusting brush sweeps eraser crumbs away cleanly without skin oils or perspiration contacting the paper.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Drafting brush removes eraser crumbs without skin oils smudging the drawing.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In plane table surveying, how are buildings plotted when only two corners can be seen directly from the instrument stations?
options: Plot the two visible corners by intersection or radiation, then measure the remaining wall lengths with tape and plot by perpendicular construction
Ignore the unseen parts of the building
bankQuestions.explanation: Intersecting two corners establishes alignment; remaining rectangular walls are taped directly and constructed geometrically.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Fix two corners graphically, then complete building geometry using taped dimensions.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the purpose of drawing a "scale bar" (graphic bar scale) in the margin of every plane table field sheet?
options: To enable true distance scaling even after the paper has shrunk or expanded with seasonal humidity changes
To measure the thickness of pencils
bankQuestions.explanation: Because graphic bar scales expand and contract with the paper sheet, they maintain exact scaling under all weather conditions.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Graphic scale expands and contracts with paper, preserving correct distance scaling.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the standard symbol for a "trigonometrical station" on a plane table cadastral map?
options: A small triangle with a central dot and its trigonometric identification number and elevation
bankQuestions.explanation: Trigonometrical control stations are represented by a neat equilateral triangle enclosing a central dot (Δ).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Trigonometrical station symbol: Small triangle with central dot (Δ).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In plane table surveying, what is an "index diagram" drawn in the margin of the sheet?
options: A small key map showing the relationship of the current sheet to adjoining neighboring survey sheets of the tract
A plan of the survey camp
bankQuestions.explanation: An index diagram is a 3×3 or 2×2 grid showing the sheet numbers of all adjacent maps to assist in sheet edge matching.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Index diagram shows sheet layout and numbers of adjoining map sheets.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In precision levelling, what is the "sight distance" limit typically enforced to prevent severe refraction and curvature errors?
options: Not more than 50 to 90 metres per sight
bankQuestions.explanation: Restricting sight lengths to 50–90 m limits refraction shimmer and ensures crisp bisection of millimeter staff divisions.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Precision levelling sight distance limit: 50 to 90 m.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the effect of wind pressure on the levelling staff during observation?
options: Wind vibrates and tilts the staff, making it difficult for the staffman to hold it plumb and causing unsteady readings
Wind bends the line of collimation downward
Wind increases the reduced level of the benchmark
bankQuestions.explanation: Strong winds create sail effects on 4-metre staves, vibrating the image and causing out-of-plumb reading errors.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Wind vibrates and tilts levelling staves, degrading reading precision.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the purpose of using a "staff brace" (bipod support legs) on a levelling staff?
options: Two light adjustable struts attached to the rear of the staff to steady it rigidly and keep it strictly vertical in windy weather
To turn the staff into a tripod
bankQuestions.explanation: Bipod staff struts support the tall rod rigidly in two directions, holding the circular bubble centered without hand tremor.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Bipod staff struts steady the rod rigidly in wind, holding it plumb.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In levelling across a deep valley where a single sight is impossible, what method is adopted?
options: Continuous differential levelling following a zig-zag path along the slope with balanced change points
Dropping a plumb bob on a 500 m rope
Using a bar-coded staff upside down
bankQuestions.explanation: Zig-zag differential levelling steps up and down slopes with balanced Back Sight and Fore Sight distances.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Step differential levelling with balanced sights traverses deep valleys accurately.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is an "arbitrary datum" and when is it legitimately adopted in engineering levelling?
options: An assumed reference plane (such as RL = 100.000 m) chosen for small localized construction surveys where connection to national MSL is not required
A datum that changes every hour
A datum defined by satellite orbit
bankQuestions.explanation: For small isolated building sites or drainage trenches, assuming an arbitrary datum of 100.000 m simplifies height differences.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Arbitrary datum (e.g. RL = 100.00 m) is adopted for small localized engineering surveys.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In differential levelling, what is a "flying bench mark"?
options: A temporary benchmark established rapidly during fly levelling to provide a quick reference point
A floating buoy in the sea
bankQuestions.explanation: A flying benchmark is a temporary reference mark established during rapid reconnaissance or fly levelling.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Flying bench mark = Temporary reference mark established during fly levelling.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the purpose of the "objective sunshade" fitted on a dumpy level telescope?
options: To prevent direct glare from entering the objective lens and shield the lens from rain drops and stray side light
bankQuestions.explanation: The cylindrical sunshade hood blocks direct sun glare that would wash out reticle contrast.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Objective sunshade shields lens from sun glare, raindrops, and flare.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the "focal length" of a level telescope objective lens typically found in standard engineering dumpy levels?
bankQuestions.explanation: Standard surveying dumpy level objectives have focal lengths of 25 to 35 cm, providing 20× to 32× optical magnification.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Level objective focal length: 250 to 350 mm (magnification 20× to 32×).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In differential levelling, what is meant by "optical magnification" of the telescope?
options: The ratio of the angle subtended by the virtual image at the eye to the angle subtended by the object viewed directly
The diameter of the objective lens
bankQuestions.explanation: Magnification m = f_objective / f_eyepiece; higher magnification resolves fine staff graduations over long distances.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Magnification = Ratio of visual angle of image to that of object (typically 24× to 32×).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the "field of view" of a surveying level telescope?
options: The angular width of the space visible through the telescope when looking through the eyepiece (typically about 1° to 1.5°)
The area of the grass field
The diameter of the tripod head
bankQuestions.explanation: Field of view is the circular angular scene visible through the optics, usually around 1° to 1°30' (spanning ~1.7 to 2.5 m at 100 m).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Field of view = Angular extent of visible scene through eyepiece (typically 1° to 1.5°).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the "aperture" of a level telescope objective lens?
options: The clear effective diameter of the objective lens that admits light into the telescope barrel (typically 35 to 45 mm)
The diameter of the foot screw
bankQuestions.explanation: Aperture is the light-gathering diameter of the front glass element; larger aperture yields brighter, sharper images in dim light.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Objective aperture = Clear diameter of front lens (typically 35 to 45 mm).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the purpose of the "internal focusing lens" found in modern surveying telescopes?
options: A double-concave lens moved along the optical axis by the focusing rack, allowing focusing without changing telescope overall length
A lens that balances the tripod
bankQuestions.explanation: An internal focusing negative lens slides inside a sealed barrel, keeping overall length constant and preventing dust/moisture entry.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Internal focusing lens: Constant telescope tube length; seals optics against dust and moisture.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In a transit theodolite, what is the "reversal method" used during permanent plate level adjustment?
options: Reversing the plate levels through 180° horizontally to double the error and adjusting half the bubble deviation with foot screws and half with capstan screws
Changing face from left to right
bankQuestions.explanation: Reversing 180° doubles the tilt: half the bubble displacement is corrected by the leveling foot screws, and the remaining half by the vial capstan screws.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Plate level adjustment: Half corrected by foot screws, half by bubble vial capstan screws.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the "plate level axis" in a transit theodolite?
options: The longitudinal line tangential to the curved upper surface of the plate bubble vial at its center mark
The line along the compass needle
bankQuestions.explanation: The plate level axis is the central tangent line to the internal curvature of the spirit level vial on the upper plate.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Plate level axis = Tangent to longitudinal curvature of vial at its center.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Why does a transit theodolite have two plate level vials placed mutually perpendicular to each other?
options: To permit simultaneous leveling in two perpendicular directions without rotating the upper plate continuously
To have a spare level if one breaks
To balance the weight of the standards
bankQuestions.explanation: Two mutually perpendicular plate vials allow rapid leveling by manipulating foot screws parallel to each vial.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Two perpendicular plate vials enable rapid two-axis leveling.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In leveling a theodolite with three foot screws, what is the rule for rotating the first pair of foot screws?
options: Rotate both foot screws simultaneously either both inwards or both outwards with thumb and forefinger
Rotate both screws in the same clockwise direction
Rotate only one screw while holding the other
bankQuestions.explanation: Align the vial parallel to two screws and turn both screws equally either both inward or both outward.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Leveling foot screws: Turn first pair simultaneously both inwards or both outwards.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In leveling with three foot screws, how is the third foot screw operated?
options: Turn the telescope through 90° so the vial is perpendicular to the first pair, and use ONLY the third screw to center the bubble
bankQuestions.explanation: After leveling across screws 1 and 2, turn the plate 90° over the third screw and manipulate only the third screw.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Turn plate 90° and level using ONLY the third foot screw.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the purpose of the "shifting head" (centering device) fitted to a theodolite leveling tribrach?
options: To allow the entire upper instrument to slide horizontally over the tripod head by a few centimetres for fine centering over the peg
bankQuestions.explanation: A shifting head permits 20 to 30 mm of horizontal planar translation to center the plumb bob precisely over the punch mark.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Shifting head: Translates the theodolite horizontally for precise station centering.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the "index error of the vertical circle" in a theodolite?
options: The residual angle indicated on the vertical circle verniers when the line of collimation is strictly horizontal
The error in reading vernier A
The tilt of the trunnion axis
bankQuestions.explanation: When the line of sight is truly horizontal, the vertical circle should read exactly 0° 00' 00"; any offset is the vertical index error.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Vertical index error = Offset reading on vertical circle when line of sight is horizontal.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: How is the index error of the vertical circle completely eliminated during field observations?
options: By observing vertical angles on both Face Left and Face Right and taking their mean
bankQuestions.explanation: Vertical circle readings have opposite algebraic signs on Face Left and Face Right: averaging Face Left and Face Right cancels index error.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Mean of Face Left and Face Right observations eliminates vertical index error completely.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In theodolite angle measurement, what is "vernier eccentricity"?
options: The geometric offset between the center of rotation of the vernier plate and the center of the graduated circle
A loose screw on the plate
bankQuestions.explanation: Eccentricity occurs when the centers of the inner and outer spindles do not coincide geometrically.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Vernier eccentricity = Non-coincidence of centers of graduated circle and vernier plate.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Why are verniers A and B placed at exact diametrically opposite positions (180° apart) on a theodolite plate?
options: So that taking the mean of readings from vernier A and vernier B completely cancels the effect of circle eccentricity
To allow two surveyors to read at once
bankQuestions.explanation: Eccentricity increases the reading on one vernier by e and decreases it on the opposite vernier by e; averaging A and B cancels e.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Mean of diametrical verniers A and B (180° apart) eliminates circle eccentricity.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records
