bankQuestions.question: What is an "Automatic Target Recognition" (ATR) system on a motorized robotic Total Station?
options: An optical sensor that detects the reflected laser from a prism and automatically points the cross-hairs exactly at the prism center
bankQuestions.explanation: ATR uses a CMOS sensor to image the returned laser spot and drives motorized servomotors to center cross-hairs onto the prism automatically.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: ATR (Automatic Target Recognition): Motorized fine aiming onto prism centers.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In GNSS surveying, what is an "ephemeris"?
options: A set of precise mathematical orbital parameters transmitted by each satellite that allows the receiver to calculate the satellite's exact 3D position in space at any instant
The serial number of the receiver
bankQuestions.explanation: Broadcast ephemeris data provides Keplerian orbital parameters, allowing the receiver to compute satellite positions at signal transmission time.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Ephemeris = Orbit parameters used by receiver to calculate exact satellite positions in space.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the "almanac" in a GPS broadcast navigation message?
options: Coarse orbital information for the ENTIRE satellite constellation used by receivers to rapidly find and acquire available satellites upon startup
bankQuestions.explanation: The almanac contains rough orbital data for all 31 satellites, helping the receiver predict which satellites are above the local horizon.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Almanac = Coarse constellation orbital data for fast satellite acquisition upon startup.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In satellite positioning, what is "Selective Availability" (SA)?
options: An intentional degradation of civilian GPS accuracy introduced by the US military, which was turned off permanently in May 2000
A system to choose satellite channels
bankQuestions.explanation: Selective Availability intentionally dithered satellite clocks to degrade civilian accuracy to 100 m; it was turned off in May 2000.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Selective Availability (SA) was intentional accuracy degradation, turned off in May 2000.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is "NTRIP" in modern RTK GNSS surveying?
options: Networked Transport of RTCM via Internet Protocol: streaming real-time differential GNSS corrections over mobile cellular internet to rovers
bankQuestions.explanation: NTRIP streams RTCM differential corrections from CORS networks over mobile internet (4G/5G) directly to rover data collectors.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: NTRIP streams real-time RTCM corrections to rovers over cellular internet.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the "Virtual Reference Station" (VRS) technique in CORS GNSS networks?
options: The central network server creates an artificial, non-existent base station located virtually right next to the rover, delivering localized corrections with zero baseline distance
A drone acting as a base
A base station on a hill
bankQuestions.explanation: VRS interpolates network corrections to synthesize a virtual base station next to the rover, eliminating distance-dependent baseline errors.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: VRS (Virtual Reference Station): Synthesizes an artificial base next to rover, eliminating baseline errors.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In GIS, what is a "Triangulated Irregular Network" (TIN)?
options: A vector-based digital elevation model representing a continuous terrain surface as a network of non-overlapping contiguous triangles
bankQuestions.explanation: A TIN connects irregularly spaced elevation mass points into a seamless mesh of Delaunay triangles, capturing breaklines efficiently.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: TIN = Vector digital elevation model composed of contiguous Delaunay triangles.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is a "Digital Elevation Model" (DEM)?
options: A digital representation of ground surface topography consisting of an array of bare-earth elevation values at regular grid intervals
A digital photograph of a mountain
bankQuestions.explanation: A DEM is a bare-earth raster grid where each pixel stores the elevation of the terrain above datum, excluding vegetation and buildings.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: DEM (Digital Elevation Model): Bare-earth raster grid storing terrain elevations.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is a "Digital Surface Model" (DSM)?
options: A digital elevation model that captures the elevations of the uppermost reflective surface, including tree canopies, roofs, and man-made structures
bankQuestions.explanation: Unlike a DEM (bare ground), a DSM includes tops of buildings, power lines, and tree canopies.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: DSM includes vegetation canopies and buildings; DEM represents bare ground.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In hydrographic surveying, what is a "sounding line" (lead line)?
options: A graduated hemp, nylon, or wire line attached to a streamlined lead weight used to measure water depths by hand sounding
A telephone wire across a river
bankQuestions.explanation: A lead line features a conical lead sinker (3 to 10 kg) attached to a non-stretching graduated cord for manual depth measurement.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Lead line = Graduated cord with lead sinker for manual water depth measurement.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the purpose of the hollow cavity filled with tallow (grease) in the bottom of a lead sinker used in hydrography?
options: To bring up samples of the seabed material (sand, mud, shells) adhering to the sticky tallow to determine sea bottom nature
To prevent the lead from rusting
bankQuestions.explanation: Arming the lead with tallow captures seabed specimens (sand, silt, gravel) to classify holding ground for ship anchorage.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Tallow in lead sinker cavity captures seabed sediment samples (arming the lead).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In hydrographic surveying, what is a "station pointer"?
options: A three-armed circular protractor (one central fixed arm and two movable graduated arms) used to plot boat positions from two simultaneous horizontal sextant angles
bankQuestions.explanation: A station pointer solves the Three-Point Resection Problem mechanically: setting the two sextant angles aligns all three arms with shoreline stations.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Station pointer = Three-armed protractor for plotting boat positions from two sextant angles.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is "Chart Datum" (Sounding Datum) in nautical navigation hydrography?
options: The reference water level (usually Lowest Astronomical Tide LAT) below which water depths on navigation charts are referenced so depths are safe at all tides
bankQuestions.explanation: Chart Datum is set at Lowest Astronomical Tide so charted depths represent the minimum water depth a mariner will encounter.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Chart Datum = Lowest Astronomical Tide (LAT); charted depths are safe at all tides.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD, what does the WCS acronym stand for?
bankQuestions.explanation: WCS is AutoCAD's fixed, Cartesian reference coordinate system where X is horizontal, Y is vertical, and Z is perpendicular.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: WCS = World Coordinate System (fixed Cartesian frame).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD, what is the UCS (User Coordinate System)?
options: A movable, customizable Cartesian coordinate system oriented by the user to simplify 2D and 3D drafting on inclined planes
bankQuestions.explanation: UCS allows the user to relocate origin and rotate axes to align with drawing geometry on any working plane.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: UCS = User Coordinate System (relocatable, customizable coordinate frame).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD coordinate entry, how is an "Absolute Cartesian Coordinate" entered at the command prompt?
bankQuestions.explanation: Absolute coordinates are entered directly as X,Y measured from the origin (0,0).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Absolute Cartesian: X,Y measured directly from (0,0).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD, how is a "Relative Cartesian Coordinate" entered relative to the last point picked?
bankQuestions.explanation: The @ symbol denotes relative displacement from the previous point: @deltaX,deltaY.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Relative Cartesian: @deltaX,deltaY.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD, how is a "Relative Polar Coordinate" entered relative to the last point picked?
bankQuestions.explanation: Polar coordinates specify distance and counter-clockwise angle from positive X-axis using @dist<angle.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Relative Polar: @distance<angle.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the function of the F3 key on the keyboard in AutoCAD?
options: Toggles running Object Snaps (OSNAP) On and Off
bankQuestions.explanation: F3 toggles running OSNAP (Endpoint, Midpoint, Center) mode.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: F3 = OSNAP toggle (On/Off).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the fundamental difference between an object created with the LINE command and one created with the PLINE (Polyline) command?
options: LINE creates separate, disconnected individual line segments, whereas PLINE creates a single contiguous, connected 2D entity that can include arcs and width
LINE has thickness while PLINE does not
bankQuestions.explanation: A polyline is a single unified object consisting of connected linear and arc segments with assignable start/end widths.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: LINE = Independent individual segments. PLINE = Single connected continuous entity.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which AutoCAD command converts a series of connected individual LINE and ARC segments into a single unified POLYLINE?
bankQuestions.explanation: The JOIN command (or PEDIT -> Join) merges collinear touching endpoints into a continuous polyline.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: JOIN / PEDIT Join converts touching line segments into a polyline.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which AutoCAD command breaks a complex compound object (such as a polyline, dimension, hatch, or block) into its component basic geometry?
bankQuestions.explanation: EXPLODE disassembles polylines into individual lines/arcs, and blocks into basic primitive geometries.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: EXPLODE breaks polylines, blocks, and hatches into primitive elements.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD, what is the special characteristic of the "Defpoints" layer?
options: It is created automatically when dimensions are inserted and objects on it NEVER plot or print on paper
It is the default layer for text
It deletes all lines on it
bankQuestions.explanation: The Defpoints layer holds dimension definition points and is hard-coded never to plot or print.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Defpoints layer holds dimension points and NEVER plots/prints on paper.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the difference between turning a layer "Off" versus "Freezing" a layer in AutoCAD?
options: Turning a layer Off hides it visually but AutoCAD still regenerates it mathematically; Freezing a layer completely suppresses it from memory and regeneration, dramatically improving computer performance
bankQuestions.explanation: Frozen layers are skipped during REGEN and redraw, freeing memory and boosting display speed on large drawing files.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Freeze suppresses layers from display and memory regeneration; Off only hides visually.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What does the MIRRTEXT system variable control in AutoCAD when using the MIRROR command?
options: MIRRTEXT = 0 preserves normal text orientation (readable), while MIRRTEXT = 1 creates a backwards mirror image of the text
bankQuestions.explanation: When MIRRTEXT is 0, mirrored text remains upright and legible from left to right; when 1, text is mirrored backwards.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: MIRRTEXT = 0 keeps mirrored text readable; MIRRTEXT = 1 mirrors text backwards.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What does the FILEDIA system variable control in AutoCAD when set to 0 versus 1?
options: FILEDIA = 1 displays standard Windows file navigation dialog boxes; FILEDIA = 0 suppresses dialogs and prompts for file paths at the command line
bankQuestions.explanation: When FILEDIA is 0, OPEN and SAVEAS prompt on the command line instead of opening file explorer dialogs.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: FILEDIA = 1 opens file dialog windows; FILEDIA = 0 forces command line prompts.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which component of a transit theodolite carries the lower clamping screw and the lower tangent screw?
bankQuestions.explanation: The lower plate carries the main circular scale graduated from 0 to 360 degrees and is fixed or rotated via the lower clamp and lower tangent screw.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Lower plate = main graduated scale, lower clamp/tangent. Upper plate = verniers, upper clamp/tangent.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: If the bubble of the plate level of a theodolite remains central during a complete 360 degree rotation of the instrument, what condition is confirmed?
options: The vertical axis is truly vertical
The line of collimation is horizontal
The trunnion axis is perpendicular to vertical axis
bankQuestions.explanation: When the plate levels stay centered for all positions around the circle, the vertical axis of rotation is confirmed to be truly vertical.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Centering of plate bubble throughout 360° rotation proves the vertical axis is truly vertical.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the purpose of the optical plummet provided in modern theodolites?
options: Centering the theodolite precisely over the ground station mark without using a plumb bob
bankQuestions.explanation: An optical plummet directs the line of sight vertically downward through the vertical axis to center the instrument accurately over a ground peg even in windy weather.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Optical plummet replaces the plumb bob for precise instrument centering.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which error in theodolite observations is eliminated by taking the mean of Face Left and Face Right observations?
options: Horizontal collimation error and horizontal axis non-perpendicularity error
Error due to non-verticality of vertical axis
Error due to slip in clamp screws
bankQuestions.explanation: Face Left and Face Right reversal eliminates index error of vertical circle, horizontal collimation error, and error due to trunnion axis inclination.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Double centering / Face reversal eliminates collimation and horizontal axis inclination errors.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Why cannot the error due to non-verticality of the vertical axis of a theodolite be eliminated by Face Left and Face Right observations?
options: Because the vertical axis remains in the same tilted position in space regardless of telescope reversal
Because vernier readings cancel it out
Because tangent screws compensate it automatically
bankQuestions.explanation: If the vertical axis is not vertical, reversing the face rotates the telescope about the same tilted axis; hence the tilt error cannot be canceled out by averaging.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Non-verticality of vertical axis cannot be eliminated by face reversal; only careful releveling cures it.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In the repetition method of measuring horizontal angles with a theodolite, what is the main advantage over single measurement?
options: Personal graduation reading errors are reduced and vernier reading errors are divided by the number of repetitions
Traverse closing error is made zero
bankQuestions.explanation: In repetition, the angle is added continuously on the graduated limb, and the final reading is divided by n, reducing reading errors to 1/n of the single vernier least count.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Repetition divides graduation and reading error by n.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which method of horizontal angle measurement with a theodolite is particularly preferred when several angles are to be measured from a single central station to surrounding stations?
bankQuestions.explanation: The reiteration method measures successive directions around the horizon from an initial reference station back to the reference station to close the horizon.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Reiteration (direction method) is ideal when measuring multiple angles from one central station.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In the reiteration method of measuring angles, what is the check called when the telescope is finally sighted back on the starting station?
bankQuestions.explanation: Sighting back to the initial reference station after sweeping around all stations is called closing the horizon; the reading should match the initial reading (360° or 0°).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Closing the horizon is the closure check in reiteration method.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the deflection angle in a theodolite traverse?
options: The angle which a survey line makes with the prolongation of the preceding survey line
The angle between the magnetic meridian and true meridian
The angle between two adjacent traverse lines measured clockwise
bankQuestions.explanation: A deflection angle is the angle through which a forward line deviates to the right (clockwise) or left (counterclockwise) from the extension of the preceding line.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Deflection angle is measured from the prolongation of the previous line to the forward line.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In a closed traverse with N sides, what is the theoretical sum of the deflection angles if the traverse proceeds around a closed loop?
bankQuestions.explanation: The algebraic sum of the deflection angles of a closed polygon traverse is always equal to 360 degrees (with right deflections taken positive and left taken negative).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Algebraic sum of deflection angles in a closed polygon = 360°.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In traverse computations, what is the latitude of a line defined as?
options: The orthographic projection of the line onto the north-south reference meridian
The orthographic projection of the line onto the east-west reference line
The distance from the instrument station to the origin
The bearing of the line measured clockwise from south
bankQuestions.explanation: The latitude of a survey line is its projection along the north-south direction, computed as L = l * cos(bearing).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Latitude = Northing/Southing = l cos θ. Departure = Easting/Westing = l sin θ.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In traverse computations, what is the departure of a line defined as?
options: The orthographic projection of the line onto the east-west reference line perpendicular to the meridian
The projection of the line onto the north-south axis
The length of the closing line
The error of closure per unit perimeter
bankQuestions.explanation: The departure of a survey line is its projection along the east-west axis perpendicular to the reference meridian, given by D = l * sin(bearing).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Departure is the projection on the East-West axis (perpendicular to meridian).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In which quadrant are both the latitude and departure of a survey line mathematically negative?
bankQuestions.explanation: In the third quadrant (South-West), southing means negative latitude and westing means negative departure.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Quadrant signs: NE (+,+), SE (-,+), SW (-,-), NW (+,-).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In which quadrant is the latitude positive and the departure negative?
bankQuestions.explanation: In the fourth quadrant (North-West), latitude is Northing (positive) and departure is Westing (negative).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: NW quadrant: Latitude is positive (+), Departure is negative (-).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the condition for mathematical geometric closure of a closed traverse with respect to latitudes and departures?
options: Sum of latitudes = 0 and sum of departures = 0
Sum of latitudes = sum of departures
Sum of latitudes > 0 and sum of departures < 0
Sum of latitudes + sum of departures = perimeter
bankQuestions.explanation: For a perfectly closed traverse returning to the starting point, the algebraic sum of all latitudes must equal zero and the algebraic sum of all departures must equal zero.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Closed traverse closure condition: ΣL = 0 and ΣD = 0.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: When the algebraic sums of latitudes (ΣL) and departures (ΣD) are not zero, how is the linear closing error (e) calculated?
bankQuestions.explanation: The linear error of closure is the hypotenuse of the right triangle formed by the residual latitude error and departure error: e = √((ΣL)^2 + (ΣD)^2).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Linear closing error e = √((ΣL)² + (ΣD)²). Direction tan θ = (ΣD)/(ΣL).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: According to Bowditch rule (compass rule), how is the correction in latitude of any traverse line distributed?
options: Total latitude closing error x (length of that line / perimeter of traverse)
Total latitude closing error / number of stations
Total latitude closing error x (latitude of that line / sum of latitudes)
Equally to all lines regardless of length
bankQuestions.explanation: Bowditch rule distributes errors proportionally to the length of each survey line: Correction in latitude = (Total ΣL) * (l / Σl).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Bowditch: Correction proportional to length of line (l / P). Assumes linear and angular precision equal.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: On what basic assumption is Bowditch rule (compass rule) of traverse balancing formulated?
options: Accidental errors in linear measurements are proportional to √l and in angular measurements are inversely proportional to √l
Angular measurements are much more precise than linear measurements
bankQuestions.explanation: Bowditch rule assumes linear errors vary as √l and angular errors vary as 1/√l, meaning linear and angular measurements have equal precision.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Bowditch assumption: Linear errors ∝ √l, angular errors ∝ 1/√l (equal precision).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: When angular measurements in a theodolite traverse are significantly more accurate than chain/tape linear measurements, which balancing rule is preferred?
bankQuestions.explanation: The Transit rule is applied when angular measurements are more precise than linear measurements; corrections are made proportional to the latitude/departure of the line.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Transit rule: applied when angles are measured with greater precision than lengths.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: According to the Transit rule, what is the correction applied to the departure of a traverse line?
options: Total departure closing error x (departure of that line / arithmetic sum of all departures)
Total departure closing error x (length of that line / perimeter)
Total departure closing error / number of lines
Total departure closing error x (latitude of that line / sum of latitudes)
bankQuestions.explanation: Transit rule states: Correction to departure of a line = Total departure error * (departure of the line / sum of departures without sign).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Transit rule correction = Total error * (Departure of line / Arithmetic sum of departures).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In Gale traverse table, what are the consecutive coordinates of a station?
options: The latitude and departure of the station with respect to the immediately preceding station
The coordinates of the station with respect to the common origin of the survey
The reduced levels of the station
The deflection angles of the station
bankQuestions.explanation: Consecutive coordinates (dependent coordinates) are the latitude and departure of a station referred to the preceding station as origin.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Consecutive coordinates = latitude & departure from previous station. Independent coordinates = total coordinates from common origin.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In Gale traverse table, what are independent coordinates (or total coordinates) of a station?
options: The coordinates of the station calculated with respect to a single common origin for the entire survey
The latitude and departure of the line joining adjacent stations
The coordinates measured on an arbitrary local grid without bearing
The slope distances measured by EDM
bankQuestions.explanation: Independent coordinates (or total coordinates) express the position of every station with respect to a single common rectangular coordinate origin.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Total coordinates (independent coordinates) are referred to one common coordinate datum origin.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is an anallatic lens in a tacheometer?
options: An additional convex lens fitted between the objective and the eyepiece to make the additive constant zero
A concave lens placed in front of the objective to magnify distant objects
A special eyepiece prism for steep sightings
A filter lens to reduce glare
bankQuestions.explanation: An anallatic lens (invented by Porro) is a convex lens placed between the objective and eyepiece that brings the optical center to the vertical axis, making c = (f + d) = 0.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Anallatic lens makes additive constant (c = f + d) equal to ZERO.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In an ordinary tacheometer without an anallatic lens, what is the typical value of the additive constant (c = f + d)?
options: 30 cm to 45 cm (0.3 m to 0.45 m)
bankQuestions.explanation: For an external focussing telescope without an anallatic lens, the additive constant (f + d) generally ranges between 30 cm and 45 cm (0.3 to 0.45 m). For internal focussing, it is 8 to 15 cm.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Additive constant c without anallatic lens is typically 30 to 45 cm; with anallatic lens it is ZERO.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the standard value of the multiplying constant (k = f / i) of a standard survey tacheometer?
bankQuestions.explanation: The multiplying constant k is the ratio of focal length (f) to stadia wire interval (i), designed by manufacturers to be exactly 100.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Multiplying constant k = f / i = 100.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: When the line of sight of a tacheometer is horizontal and the staff is held vertical, what is the formula for horizontal distance D?
options: D = k * s * cos θ + c
D = k * s * cos^2 θ + c * cos θ
bankQuestions.explanation: For a horizontal line of sight, the horizontal distance D = k*s + c, where k is multiplying constant, s is staff intercept, and c is additive constant.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Horizontal sight: D = k s + c. If anallatic, D = 100 s.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: When the line of sight of a tacheometer is inclined at an angle θ to the horizontal and the staff is held vertical, what is the horizontal distance D?
options: D = k * s * cos^2 θ + c * cos θ
D = k * s * sin^2 θ + c * sin θ
D = k * s * cos θ + c
D = k * s * tan θ + c
bankQuestions.explanation: When the staff is held vertical on an inclined sight, D = k * s * cos^2(θ) + c * cos(θ).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Inclined sight with vertical staff: D = k s cos² θ + c cos θ.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: When the line of sight of a tacheometer is inclined at an angle θ and the staff is held vertical, what is the vertical component V?
options: V = (1/2) * k * s * sin(2θ) + c * sin θ
V = k * s * cos^2 θ + c * sin θ
V = k * s * tan θ + c
V = k * s * sin^2 θ + c * cos θ
bankQuestions.explanation: Vertical component V = k * s * sin θ * cos θ + c * sin θ = (1/2) * k * s * sin(2θ) + c * sin θ.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Vertical component V = 0.5 k s sin(2θ) + c sin θ.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In tacheometry, what is the staff intercept (s)?
options: The difference between the upper stadia hair reading and the lower stadia hair reading on the staff
The reading of the central horizontal hair
The height of the instrument axis above the station peg
The total length of the levelling staff
bankQuestions.explanation: The staff intercept s is the distance between the two outer stadia hairs as read on the graduated levelling staff (s = Upper reading - Lower reading).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Staff intercept s = Upper stadia hair reading - Lower stadia hair reading.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the subtense bar used for in surveying?
options: Measuring horizontal distances by sighting a fixed-length horizontal bar and measuring the horizontal angle subtended at the instrument
Setting out right angles on the ground
Measuring vertical angles to mountain peaks
Finding the magnetic bearing of survey lines
bankQuestions.explanation: A subtense bar has two targets set at a fixed distance (usually 2 or 3 meters) apart on an invar bar; measuring the horizontal angle subtended yields the horizontal distance directly without slope corrections.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Subtense bar has fixed horizontal length; horizontal angle subtended gives distance directly.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What major advantage does the subtense bar method have over stadia tacheometry?
options: Atmospheric refraction affects both ends equally because sight lines are horizontal, eliminating vertical refraction errors
It can measure distances up to 50 km in a single sight
bankQuestions.explanation: Since the subtense bar is mounted horizontally, the sight lines are in the horizontal plane, so vertical atmospheric refraction cancels out completely.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Subtense bar is immune to vertical refraction errors because sights are in the horizontal plane.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the tangential method of tacheometry?
options: A method of measuring distance and elevation using an ordinary theodolite without stadia hairs by taking two vertical angles to two targets on a staff
Measuring angles using the lower tangent screw
Setting out circular curves using tangent offsets
bankQuestions.explanation: Tangential tacheometry uses a theodolite with ordinary crosshairs (no stadia lines). Two vertical angles are observed to two distinct vanes/targets on the staff.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Tangential method uses an ordinary theodolite without stadia hairs; observes 2 vertical angles.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In tangential tacheometry, if two vertical angles α1 and α2 are observed to targets on a staff separated by height s, and both angles are angles of elevation (α1 > α2), what is the horizontal distance D?
bankQuestions.explanation: When both sights are angles of elevation: h1 = D tan α1 and h2 = D tan α2. Then s = h1 - h2 = D(tan α1 - tan α2), so D = s / (tan α1 - tan α2).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Both angles elevation: D = s / (tan α1 - tan α2). One elevation, one depression: D = s / (tan α1 + tan α2).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In tangential tacheometry, if one angle is an angle of elevation (α1) and the other is an angle of depression (α2), what is the horizontal distance D?
bankQuestions.explanation: When one vane is above the horizontal line of sight and the other below: s = h1 + h2 = D(tan α1 + tan α2), therefore D = s / (tan α1 + tan α2).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: One elevation, one depression: D = s / (tan α1 + tan α2).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In a simple circular curve, what is the relation between the intersection angle (I) and the deflection angle (Δ)?
bankQuestions.explanation: The intersection angle I between the two straights and the deflection angle Δ through which the forward straight deflects satisfy I + Δ = 180° (I = 180° - Δ).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Intersection angle I + Deflection angle Δ = 180°.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the formula for the tangent length (T) of a simple circular curve of radius R and deflection angle Δ?
bankQuestions.explanation: From the tangent triangle formed by vertex and curve center, Tangent length T = R * tan(Δ / 2).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Tangent length T = R tan(Δ/2).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the formula for the length of curve (L) of a circular curve of radius R and deflection angle Δ (in degrees)?
bankQuestions.explanation: Length of arc L = 2 * π * R * (Δ / 360°) = (π * R * Δ) / 180°.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Curve length L = (π R Δ) / 180.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the formula for the length of the long chord (C) of a circular curve of radius R and deflection angle Δ?
bankQuestions.explanation: The long chord connects the point of curvature (T1) and point of tangency (T2). Half the chord is R * sin(Δ/2), so long chord C = 2R * sin(Δ/2).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Long chord C = 2R sin(Δ/2).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the formula for the apex distance (external distance, E) of a circular curve of radius R and deflection angle Δ?
bankQuestions.explanation: Apex distance is the distance from vertex V to the midpoint of the curve: E = R * sec(Δ/2) - R = R * (sec(Δ/2) - 1).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Apex distance E = R [sec(Δ/2) - 1].
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the formula for the mid-ordinate (versine of the curve, M) of a circular curve of radius R and deflection angle Δ?
bankQuestions.explanation: The mid-ordinate M is the distance from the midpoint of the long chord to the apex of the curve: M = R - R * cos(Δ/2) = R * (1 - cos(Δ/2)).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Mid-ordinate M = R [1 - cos(Δ/2)].
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In terms of radius R and long chord C, what is the approximate expression for the mid-ordinate (M) of a flat curve?
bankQuestions.explanation: By series expansion or Pythagorean approximation, the mid-ordinate of a flat circular curve is given by M = C^2 / (8R).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Approximate mid-ordinate M = C² / (8R).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the relation between the radius R and the degree of curve D for a 30-meter chain / arc?
bankQuestions.explanation: For a 30m arc: Arc length = 30m = (π * R * D) / 180°, which gives R = (30 * 180) / (π * D) = 1718.87 / D ≈ 1719 / D.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Degree of curve: R = 1719 / D for 30m chain; R = 1146 / D for 20m chain.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the definition of the degree of curve (D) based on the chord definition?
options: The angle subtended at the center of the curve by a standard chord of 20 m or 30 m length
The angle subtended by the full long chord
The total deflection angle of the curve
The angle subtended by a 100 m arc
bankQuestions.explanation: Under the chord definition, the degree of curve D is the angle subtended at the center of the curve by a chord of standard length (20m or 30m).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Degree of curve = angle subtended at center by a standard chord (20m or 30m).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In Rankine method of tangential angles (deflection angles) for setting out circular curves, what is the tangential angle δ for a sub-chord of length c (in minutes of arc)?
bankQuestions.explanation: The tangential deflection angle δ in minutes is given by δ = (180 * 60 / 2π) * (c / R) = 1718.87 * (c / R) minutes.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Rankine deflection angle δ = 1718.9 x (c / R) minutes.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In Rankine method of setting out a circular curve, what is the total deflection angle (Δn) for any station n with respect to the initial tangent?
options: The sum of all individual deflection angles up to that station (Δn = δ1 + δ2 + ... + δn)
The average of all deflection angles
Half of the first deflection angle
The total deflection angle of the entire curve
bankQuestions.explanation: The total deflection angle for the nth peg from the point of curve is the algebraic sum of all preceding individual deflection angles: Δn = δ1 + δ2 + ... + δn.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Total deflection angle for nth peg: Δn = Σδ.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In Rankine method of curve setting, what is the final check on the total deflection angle to the Point of Tangency (T2)?
options: The total deflection angle to T2 must be exactly equal to half the total deflection angle of the curve (Δ / 2)
It must equal the full deflection angle Δ
It must equal 180 degrees minus Δ
bankQuestions.explanation: The total angle subtended between the initial tangent and the long chord to T2 is mathematically equal to Δ / 2. This serves as the primary angular check.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Final check in Rankine method: Total deflection angle to T2 = Δ / 2.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which curve setting method requires NO linear measurement with chain or tape on the curve and uses two theodolites set at T1 and T2?
bankQuestions.explanation: In the two-theodolite method, one theodolite is set at T1 and another at T2. Sights are directed simultaneously according to computed deflection angles, locating pegs at the intersection of lines of sight without chaining.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Two-theodolite method requires NO linear chain measurements on the ground; uses intersection of sights.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: When setting out a circular curve by offsets from the long chord, what is the offset (Ox) at a distance x from the midpoint of the long chord?
bankQuestions.explanation: The exact formula for the offset from long chord at distance x from mid-point is Ox = √(R^2 - x^2) - (R - O0), where O0 is the mid-ordinate.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Offset from long chord: Ox = √(R² - x²) - (R - O0). Approx: Ox ≈ O0 - x²/(2R).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In setting out a curve by offsets from chords produced, what is the offset for the first point (O1) from the initial tangent for a chord of length c1?
bankQuestions.explanation: The first offset from the tangent is O1 = c1^2 / (2R). Subsequent intermediate offsets are On = cn * (cn-1 + cn) / (2R).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: First offset from tangent: O1 = c1² / (2R). Subsequent regular offset: O = c² / R.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In setting out a curve by offsets from chords produced, if all chords have the same regular length c, what is each intermediate offset (On)?
bankQuestions.explanation: When successive chords are of equal regular length c, the intermediate offset is On = c * (c + c) / (2R) = c^2 / R.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Regular chord offset: On = c² / R (twice the first offset from tangent).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is a compound curve in surveying?
options: A curve consisting of two or more circular arcs of different radii bending in the same direction with a common tangent at their junction
A curve consisting of two arcs bending in opposite directions
A curve combining a straight line and a parabola
A circular curve combined with an ellipse
bankQuestions.explanation: A compound curve consists of two or more circular curves of different radii curving in the SAME direction with a common tangent at their point of compound curvature (PCC).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Compound curve: different radii, bending in SAME direction, common tangent.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is a reverse curve (or serpentine curve)?
options: A curve consisting of two circular arcs of equal or unequal radii bending in opposite directions with a common tangent at their junction
A curve where radius decreases continuously to zero
A curve that doubles back on itself by 180 degrees
A curve used exclusively in vertical profiles
bankQuestions.explanation: A reverse curve consists of two circular arcs curving in OPPOSITE directions with a common tangent at their point of reverse curvature (PRC).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Reverse curve: arcs bending in OPPOSITE directions with a common tangent (PRC).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Why are reverse curves strictly avoided on high-speed railway mainlines and expressways?
options: Because the sudden reversal of cant (superelevation) and centrifugal force causes severe passenger discomfort and risk of derailment
Because they cannot be set out with a theodolite
Because they require too much land
bankQuestions.explanation: At the point of reverse curvature, superelevation must transition instantaneously from one side to the other, causing sudden lateral jerk dangerous at high speeds.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Reverse curves avoided on high speeds due to dangerous abrupt reversal of cant and centrifugal force.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the primary function of a transition curve introduced between a straight tangent and a circular curve?
options: To introduce centrifugal force and superelevation gradually, preventing sudden lateral shocks
To increase the speed beyond the design limit
To shorten the length of the road
bankQuestions.explanation: Transition curves provide a gradual increase in curvature (from 0 to 1/R) and a gradual rise of superelevation, ensuring smooth motion without sudden jerks.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Transition curves introduce curvature (1/R) and superelevation gradually.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What ideal mathematical property defines the Euler spiral (clothoid) as a transition curve?
options: Its radius of curvature is inversely proportional to its distance along the curve from the origin (l * r = constant)
Its radius of curvature is constant throughout
Its deflection angle is proportional to the square root of distance
bankQuestions.explanation: In an ideal transition spiral (clothoid), the radius r at any point is inversely proportional to the distance l from the start: l * r = constant.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Clothoid / Euler spiral: l x r = constant. Curvature increases linearly with length.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which transition curve shape is most commonly adopted on Indian railways and road highways?
bankQuestions.explanation: The cubic parabola (for small deflection angles) and clothoid spiral are standard in railway and highway engineering.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Cubic parabola and spiral are the standard transition curves adopted in practice.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the formula for the shift (S) of a circular curve when a transition curve of length L is introduced for a curve of radius R?
bankQuestions.explanation: To accommodate a transition curve of length L, the circular arc is shifted inward by an amount S = L^2 / (24R).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Shift of circular curve S = L² / (24R).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: At what point does the shift (S) bisect the transition curve?
options: At the midpoint of the transition curve (L / 2)
At the beginning of the transition curve
At the junction with the circular curve
At one-third of the transition length
bankQuestions.explanation: The shifted circular curve passes through a point where the transition curve is bisected by the shift at distance L / 2.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: The shift S bisects the transition curve at its midpoint (L / 2).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the formula for the length of a transition curve (L) based on the permissible rate of change of radial acceleration (c)?
bankQuestions.explanation: From kinematics, the rate of change of centrifugal acceleration is a/t = (v^2/R)/(L/v) = v^3 / (LR) = c, giving L = v^3 / (c * R).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Transition length by rate of radial acceleration: L = v³ / (c R). Permissible c = 0.3 to 0.75 m/s³.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What type of curve is provided at the intersection of two different gradients on a highway or railway?
bankQuestions.explanation: Vertical curves are provided at grade changes to smooth out vertical profile transitions. A parabola is preferred for vertical curves due to its constant rate of change of grade.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Vertical curves are parabolic to maintain a constant rate of change of grade.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is a summit curve (crest curve) in highway engineering?
options: A vertical curve with convexity upwards, formed when an ascending gradient meets a descending gradient
A vertical curve with concavity upwards
A curve at the highest mountain pass with zero gradient
A curve designed for drainage only
bankQuestions.explanation: A summit curve has its convexity upwards (e.g., +g1 meets -g2). The primary design criterion is providing adequate Stopping Sight Distance (SSD).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Summit curve: convexity upwards (+g1 meets -g2). Governed by Stopping Sight Distance.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is a valley curve (sag curve) in highway engineering?
options: A vertical curve with convexity downwards (concavity upwards), formed when a descending gradient meets an ascending gradient
A curve located inside an underground tunnel
A horizontal curve in a river valley
A curve with zero drainage slope
bankQuestions.explanation: A valley curve has convexity downwards (e.g., -g1 meets +g2). Primary design criteria are headlight sight distance at night and passenger comfort.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Valley curve: concavity upwards. Governed by headlight sight distance and comfort.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Why is a simple parabola preferred over a circle for vertical curves on highways?
options: Because a parabola has a constant rate of change of grade, providing uniform vertical acceleration and easiest field computation
Because a parabola has shorter length than a circle
Because a parabola requires no sight distance
Because circular curves cannot be vertical
bankQuestions.explanation: The second derivative d²y/dx² of a parabola y = kx² is constant, which means the rate of change of grade is perfectly constant throughout the curve.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Parabola has constant rate of change of grade (uniform vertical acceleration).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In theodolite surveying, what is meant by "centering" the instrument?
options: Placing the vertical axis of the theodolite exactly vertically over the station mark on the ground
Aligning the line of sight with true north
Bringing the plate bubble to the center of its run
Focusing the objective on the crosshairs
bankQuestions.explanation: Centering is the operation of bringing the vertical axis of the theodolite exactly over the center of the station peg using a plumb bob or optical plummet.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Centering = placing the vertical axis exactly over the ground station mark.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the operation of rotating the telescope of a theodolite about its horizontal axis in a vertical plane through 180 degrees called?
bankQuestions.explanation: Transiting (plunging) is the process of rotating the telescope through 180 degrees about its horizontal (trunnion) axis in the vertical plane.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Transiting / plunging = rotating telescope 180° about horizontal axis.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the operation of rotating the telescope of a theodolite about its vertical axis in a horizontal plane called?
bankQuestions.explanation: Swinging is rotating the theodolite telescope about its vertical axis in the horizontal plane. A clockwise rotation is called a right swing.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Swinging = rotating telescope in a horizontal plane about vertical axis.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What does "Face Left" observation mean in theodolite surveying?
options: The vertical circle of the instrument is to the left of the observer while sighting
The observer is standing to the left of the tripod
The horizontal angle is measured towards the left
The telescope is transited to the left
bankQuestions.explanation: Face Left (or circle left) means the vertical graduated circle is situated to the left hand of the observer sighting through the telescope.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Face Left: vertical circle is on the observer's left hand side.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What does "Face Right" observation mean in theodolite surveying?
options: The vertical circle of the instrument is to the right of the observer while sighting
The telescope points towards the right quadrant
The horizontal clamp is tightened on the right
bankQuestions.explanation: Face Right (or circle right) means the vertical graduated circle is situated to the right hand of the observer.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Face Right: vertical circle is on the observer's right hand side.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: How does an observer change from Face Left to Face Right with a theodolite?
options: Transit the telescope through 180 degrees and then swing it horizontally through 180 degrees
Loosen the tripod legs and rotate the entire stand
Unscrew the telescope and turn it upside down
Rotate the vernier plate only by 90 degrees
bankQuestions.explanation: To change face, transit (plunge) the telescope through 180° in the vertical plane, then swing the instrument 180° horizontally.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Change face: Transit telescope 180° + Swing horizontally 180°.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the index error of the vertical circle in a theodolite?
options: The vertical circle vernier does not read exactly zero when the line of collimation is truly horizontal
The horizontal scale reads 180 degrees instead of zero
bankQuestions.explanation: Index error is the residual reading on the vertical circle when the telescope bubble is leveled and the line of sight is horizontal. It is eliminated by taking the mean of Face Left and Face Right.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Index error = non-zero reading on vertical circle when line of sight is horizontal.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In a theodolite, the trunnion axis is another name for which axis?
bankQuestions.explanation: The horizontal axis on which the telescope rotates vertically is called the trunnion axis.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Trunnion axis = Horizontal axis of the theodolite.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the line of collimation in a surveying telescope?
options: The imaginary line passing through the intersection of the crosshairs and the optical center of the objective lens
The physical axis of the brass telescope barrel
The line passing through the eyepiece and the eye of observer
The line parallel to the bubble tube
bankQuestions.explanation: The line of collimation is the line joining the intersection of crosshairs with the optical center of the objective and its continuation into space.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Line of collimation = Line joining crosshairs intersection and optical center of objective.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the line of sight in a surveying telescope?
options: The line passing through the intersection of crosshairs and optical center of objective, without necessarily being horizontal
A line that is always strictly horizontal
The line along the top of the telescope barrel
The line connecting both plate levels
bankQuestions.explanation: The line of sight is the straight line passing through the crosshairs intersection and optical center of the objective. When horizontal, it is called the line of collimation.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Line of sight = ray from crosshairs through optical center of objective.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In permanent adjustment of a theodolite, what is the Spire test used to check and adjust?
options: Perpendicularity of the horizontal axis to the vertical axis
Perpendicularity of plate bubble to vertical axis
bankQuestions.explanation: The Spire test (sighting a high point like a church spire with Face Left and Face Right and depressing to ground marks) checks if the horizontal axis is perpendicular to the vertical axis.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Spire test: checks horizontal axis is perpendicular to vertical axis.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the condition verified in the plate level test of a theodolite?
options: The axes of the plate levels must be perpendicular to the vertical axis
The line of collimation must be parallel to the vertical axis
The trunnion axis must be parallel to the horizontal plate
bankQuestions.explanation: The plate level test ensures that the longitudinal axis of each plate level tube is perpendicular to the vertical axis of the theodolite.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Plate level test: Plate level axes perpendicular to vertical axis.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In theodolite traversing, what are included angles?
options: The interior or exterior angles between two survey lines measured clockwise from the back station to the forward station
The angles between the magnetic needle and the traverse line
The vertical angles measured to tops of pegs
The angles between traverse lines and true North
bankQuestions.explanation: Included angles are measured directly between adjacent traverse lines, conventionally measured clockwise from the back station to the forward station.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Included angles are measured clockwise from back station to forward station.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In a closed traverse running clockwise, the measured interior angles must sum to which theoretical value?
bankQuestions.explanation: For an N-sided closed polygon, the sum of all interior angles is always (2N - 4) * 90° or (N - 2) * 180°.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Sum of interior angles = (2N - 4) x 90° = (N - 2) x 180°.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In a closed polygon traverse running clockwise, what is the theoretical sum of the exterior angles?
bankQuestions.explanation: For an N-sided polygon, the sum of all exterior angles is always (2N + 4) * 90° or (N + 2) * 180°.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Sum of exterior angles = (2N + 4) x 90° = (N + 2) x 180°.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is an open traverse suitable for in surveying?
options: Long linear surveys such as roads, railways, highways, pipelines, and canal routes
Surveying city commercial plots with boundary walls
Measuring the area of an agricultural farm
bankQuestions.explanation: An open traverse extends continuously without returning to its start point or closing onto a known station, used for routes of roads, railways, canals, and pipelines.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Open traverse: used for linear engineering projects (roads, railways, canals).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: How can an open traverse be checked for accuracy in the field when it cannot close back onto itself?
options: By taking bearings to prominent distant control points (cut-off lines or tie lines) or ending at a known trigonometrical station
By measuring each line twice with the same tape
By assuming latitudes sum to zero
bankQuestions.explanation: Checks on open traverses include sighting prominent reference marks from multiple stations (cut-off lines) or connecting to existing geodetic control points (connecting traverse).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Open traverse checks: Cut-off lines, tie lines, or connecting to known geodetic stations.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the formula for the radius R of a circular curve if its degree of curve is D degrees based on a 100-foot chord?
bankQuestions.explanation: For a 100-foot chord: R = (100 * 180) / (π * D) = 5729.58 / D feet.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: For 100-ft chord: R = 5730 / D feet.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In curve geometry, what is the point of curvature (PC or T1)?
options: The beginning point of the curve where the alignment transitions from the straight tangent into the circular arc
The point where two tangents intersect
The end point of the circular curve
The center of the circular curve
bankQuestions.explanation: Point of Curvature (PC or T1) is the point of commencement where the alignment changes from the rear straight tangent to the circular arc.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Point of Curvature (PC / T1) = starting point of curve.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In curve geometry, what is the point of tangency (PT or T2)?
options: The end point of the circular curve where it rejoins the forward straight tangent
The intersection of the two tangents
The midpoint of the circular curve
bankQuestions.explanation: Point of Tangency (PT or T2) is the termination point where the circular arc ends and merges into the forward tangent.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Point of Tangency (PT / T2) = ending point of curve.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: If the chainage of the intersection point (V) is known, how is the chainage of the Point of Curvature (T1) calculated?
options: Chainage of T1 = Chainage of V - Tangent length (T)
Chainage of T1 = Chainage of V + Tangent length (T)
Chainage of T1 = Chainage of V - Length of curve (L)
Chainage of T1 = Chainage of V / 2
bankQuestions.explanation: Since T1 lies on the rear tangent before the vertex V at a distance equal to tangent length T, Chainage of T1 = Chainage of V - T.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Chainage of T1 = Chainage of V - Tangent length (T).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: How is the chainage of the Point of Tangency (T2) correctly calculated?
options: Chainage of T2 = Chainage of T1 + Length of curve (L)
Chainage of T2 = Chainage of V + Tangent length (T)
Chainage of T2 = Chainage of V + Length of curve (L)
Chainage of T2 = Chainage of T1 + Tangent length (T)
bankQuestions.explanation: Chainage is measured along the actual traveled curve path: Chainage of T2 = Chainage of T1 + Curve length (L). Note: Never add T to V to find T2!
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Chainage of T2 = Chainage of T1 + Curve length L (NOT Chainage of V + T).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What type of sensor is incorporated in a modern Total Station to automatically sense and correct for physical instrument tilt in both longitudinal and transverse directions?
bankQuestions.explanation: A dual-axis tilt compensator monitors inclinations along both the line of sight and trunnion axis, applying electronic corrections to horizontal and vertical angles in real time.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Dual-axis compensator senses tilt along both axes and automatically corrects angular readings.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the optical operating principle of the cube-corner retroreflector prism used with Total Stations?
options: Internal reflection from three mutually perpendicular reflective faces directs the beam back strictly parallel to the incoming path
Diffraction grating splits light into spectral colors
Refraction through a convex lens focuses rays on a focal plane
Polarization filters rotate light waves by 90 degrees
bankQuestions.explanation: A cube-corner prism has three mutually perpendicular internal reflecting faces. Any incoming light ray undergoes triple reflection and exits along a path strictly parallel to the incoming beam.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Cube-corner prism reflects incoming EDM light back exactly parallel to the incoming path.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Why does a Total Station prism have an inherent prism constant (such as -30 mm)?
options: Because the optical apex of the glass prism does not coincide physically with the vertical plumb line of the prism holder mounting thread
Because glass slows down the speed of light
Because the laser beam expands with distance
bankQuestions.explanation: The theoretical reflection point within the glass prism is physically offset from the vertical plumb axis of the prism pole mounting adapter, necessitating a calibration offset constant.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Prism constant arises because the optical center of the prism does not coincide with the mechanical mounting axis.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In EDM distance measurement, what happens to the velocity of the modulated electromagnetic light wave as it travels through atmospheric air compared to a vacuum?
options: Its velocity decreases depending on ambient air temperature, pressure, and humidity
Its velocity increases due to atmospheric refraction
Its velocity remains strictly identical to the speed of light in vacuum
Its velocity fluctuates with the earth magnetic field
bankQuestions.explanation: The velocity of light in air is v = c / n, where n is the refractive index of air (n > 1). As temperature, pressure, and humidity change, n varies, requiring ppm corrections.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Light travels slower in air than in vacuum (v = c / n); ppm correction accounts for this.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In Total Station operations, what does the atmospheric correction unit "ppm" stand for?
options: Parts per million (millimeters of correction per kilometer of distance)
bankQuestions.explanation: ppm stands for parts per million. A correction of 1 ppm equals 1 mm per 1,000,000 mm (i.e., 1 mm per 1 km of measured slope distance).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 ppm = 1 mm correction per 1 km of measured distance.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which two atmospheric parameters must be entered into a Total Station before starting high-precision EDM distance measurements?
options: Ambient temperature and atmospheric barometric pressure
bankQuestions.explanation: Atmospheric pressure and dry-bulb temperature have the most significant impact on the refractive index of air, dictating the ppm atmospheric velocity correction.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Temperature and barometric pressure are entered to apply the atmospheric ppm correction.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the primary difference between phase-shift EDM measurement and pulsed time-of-flight EDM measurement in a Total Station?
options: Phase-shift measures the phase angle difference of continuous modulated waves, whereas pulsed EDM measures the travel time of discrete high-energy laser pulses
Phase-shift uses sound waves while pulsed uses radio waves
Phase-shift works without reflectors while pulsed requires prisms
Pulsed EDM is restricted to distances under 5 meters
bankQuestions.explanation: Phase-shift EDMs emit continuous waves modulated at multiple frequencies and compute distance from phase differences; pulsed EDMs measure the round-trip transit time (t) of laser pulses: d = c*t/2.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Phase-shift measures phase difference of continuous waves; Pulsed measures travel time of discrete pulses.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which onboard program of a Total Station allows determining the unknown coordinates of the instrument station by sighting two or more known control benchmarks?
bankQuestions.explanation: Resection (or Free Stationing) computes the coordinates and orientation of an arbitrarily placed Total Station by observing angles and distances to two or more known control points.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Resection calculates unknown instrument station coordinates from sightings to known control points.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which onboard function of a Total Station is used to determine the height of an overhead high-tension electric cable where a prism cannot be physically placed?
bankQuestions.explanation: In REM, a prism is placed directly below the overhead object on the ground; after measuring the base distance, tilting the telescope up to the object gives its height and elevation.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: REM (Remote Elevation Measurement) measures heights of inaccessible overhead points.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which onboard function of a Total Station calculates the horizontal distance, slope distance, and gradient between two remote target points without occupying either point?
bankQuestions.explanation: MLM (Missing Line Measurement) measures the vector (horizontal distance, slope distance, height difference, and azimuth) between two target points sighted from the instrument.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: MLM computes distance and slope between two target points without occupying them.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In setting out construction works using a Total Station, what is the "Stake-out" mode used for?
options: Guiding the rodman to stake ground pegs at pre-calculated design coordinate positions
Measuring the boundary area of a polygon
Downloading raw coordinate points to a flash drive
Measuring the height of the instrument tripod
bankQuestions.explanation: Stake-out mode compares design coordinates with current measured positions, displaying the horizontal angle to turn and distance to move forward/backward.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Stake-out guides the rodman to exact design coordinate locations on the ground.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is reflectorless EDM measurement in modern Total Stations?
options: Measuring distances directly to natural object surfaces (concrete, rock, brick) using a narrow focused visible laser without a reflecting prism
Measuring distances by sound echo reflection
bankQuestions.explanation: Reflectorless EDM uses a collimated visible laser diode to measure distances directly against natural surfaces without requiring a retroreflector prism.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Reflectorless EDM measures directly to natural surfaces without needing a prism.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the tracking mode (coarse tracking) in a Total Station EDM used for?
options: Rapid continuous distance updates (several times per second) for moving prism poles during stake-out, at slightly reduced precision
bankQuestions.explanation: Tracking mode updates distances every 0.1 to 0.3 seconds to track a moving prism pole during stake-out, trading off the extreme precision of fine mode for speed.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Tracking mode offers rapid continuous distance measurement for moving rodmen during stake-out.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is a robotic Total Station (motorized Total Station)?
options: A Total Station equipped with servo motors and active target tracking that can be operated by a single surveyor at the prism pole via radio remote control
bankQuestions.explanation: A robotic Total Station uses motorized drives and automatic target recognition (ATR) to track the prism automatically, allowing one-man operation from the rod.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Robotic Total Station tracks the prism automatically, enabling single-person surveying.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the function of Automatic Target Recognition (ATR) in motorized Total Stations?
options: Optically detecting the center of the target prism and pointing the telescope crosshairs onto it automatically without manual sighting
bankQuestions.explanation: ATR emits an infrared spot toward the prism and senses the reflected beam on a CMOS/CCD sensor to center the crosshairs onto the prism automatically.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: ATR automatically points the telescope exactly at the center of the reflector prism.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the minimum number of GNSS satellites that a GPS receiver must track simultaneously to determine an unambiguous 3D position (X, Y, Z) and receiver clock offset?
bankQuestions.explanation: Four satellite ranges are required to solve for four mathematical unknowns: three Cartesian coordinates (X, Y, Z) and the receiver clock bias (Δt).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Minimum 4 satellites are needed for a 3D position fix (X, Y, Z, and clock bias).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Why are atomic clocks (rubidium or cesium standards) mounted on GNSS satellites rather than in ground user receivers?
options: To provide exceptionally stable timekeeping on the satellites, while inexpensive quartz clocks in user receivers are synchronized by solving for clock error as a fourth unknown
Because atomic clocks cannot function in atmospheric pressure
Because quartz crystals fail in space radiation
bankQuestions.explanation: Satellites carry highly stable atomic clocks (rubidium/cesium) for nanosecond timing. Inexpensive quartz clocks in receivers are synchronized using the 4th satellite observation.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Satellites carry atomic clocks; user receivers use quartz clocks synchronized via the 4th satellite.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the nominal orbital altitude of the satellites in the NAVSTAR GPS constellation above the Earth surface?
bankQuestions.explanation: NAVSTAR GPS satellites orbit at an altitude of approximately 20,180 to 20,200 km in Medium Earth Orbit (MEO) with an orbital period of 11 hours and 58 minutes.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: GPS satellites orbit at ~20,200 km altitude (MEO) with an orbital period of ~12 hours.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: How many orbital planes are used in the baseline design of the NAVSTAR GPS space segment constellation?
options: 6 orbital planes inclined at 55 degrees to the equator
bankQuestions.explanation: The GPS constellation comprises 6 orbital planes inclined at 55° to the equator, spaced 60° apart, ensuring at least 4 satellites are visible anywhere on Earth.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: GPS constellation: 6 orbital planes inclined at 55° with 4+ satellites per plane.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the primary carrier frequency of the GPS L1 signal?
bankQuestions.explanation: The GPS L1 carrier frequency is 1575.42 MHz (wavelength ~19.05 cm), derived from the fundamental atomic standard frequency of 10.23 MHz (154 x 10.23 MHz).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: GPS L1 frequency = 1575.42 MHz. L2 = 1227.60 MHz. L5 = 1176.45 MHz.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the carrier frequency of the GPS L2 signal?
bankQuestions.explanation: The GPS L2 carrier frequency is 1227.60 MHz (120 x 10.23 MHz, wavelength ~24.42 cm).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: GPS L2 frequency = 1227.60 MHz.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the name of the civilian pseudorandom noise (PRN) code modulated onto the GPS L1 carrier wave?
bankQuestions.explanation: The C/A (Coarse/Acquisition) code is a 1.023 MHz civilian PRN code repeated every 1 millisecond, modulated onto the L1 carrier.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Civilian GPS code is C/A code (Coarse/Acquisition) on L1 at 1.023 MHz.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the name of the Russian satellite navigation system equivalent to USA GPS?
bankQuestions.explanation: GLONASS (Global Navigation Satellite System) is operated by the Russian Federation, using 24 satellites in 3 orbital planes at ~19,100 km altitude.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: GLONASS is the Russian global navigation satellite system.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the name of the civilian satellite navigation system developed by the European Union?
bankQuestions.explanation: Galileo is the European Union global navigation satellite system, operated for civilian and commercial navigation with high precision.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Galileo is the European Union GNSS constellation.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the official operational name of India regional navigation satellite system (IRNSS)?
bankQuestions.explanation: NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation), developed by ISRO, is India regional navigation satellite system covering India and a region extending 1,500 km around it.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: NavIC is India regional satellite navigation system (IRNSS) developed by ISRO.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is GAGAN in Indian aviation and spatial positioning?
options: GPS Aided GEO Augmented Navigation (a Satellite-Based Augmentation System - SBAS)
A GIS software platform developed by ISRO
bankQuestions.explanation: GAGAN is India SBAS (Satellite-Based Augmentation System), developed by ISRO and AAI to provide differential GPS corrections over Indian airspace.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: GAGAN is India Satellite-Based Augmentation System (SBAS) for GPS corrections.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the primary operational mechanism of Differential GPS (DGPS)?
options: A base station at known coordinates calculates pseudorange errors and broadcasts real-time corrections to roving receivers
Using two satellites instead of four
Measuring ground distances with a laser tape simultaneously
bankQuestions.explanation: In DGPS, a stationary base receiver at known coordinates computes differences between true and measured pseudoranges (PRC) and broadcasts them to rovers to cancel common errors.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: DGPS uses a base receiver at a known station to broadcast range corrections to rovers.
