bankQuestions.question: Which AutoCAD command is used to create a smooth, curved line fitted through or near a set of specified control points (NURBS curve)?
bankQuestions.explanation: The SPLINE command creates Non-Uniform Rational B-Spline (NURBS) curves, creating smooth mathematical curves passing through or influenced by control vertices.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: SPLINE creates smooth NURBS curves through specified points.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which option of the CIRCLE command creates a circle that is tangent to two existing drawing objects and has a specified radius?
bankQuestions.explanation: TTR prompts the user to select two objects to which the circle will be tangent and then prompts for the desired radius.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: TTR = Tangent, Tangent, Radius option of CIRCLE command.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What are the two primary geometric options available when constructing a regular polygon using the POLYGON command in AutoCAD?
options: Inscribed in circle and Circumscribed about circle
bankQuestions.explanation: POLYGON can be created either Inscribed in an imaginary circle (vertices touch the circle) or Circumscribed about an imaginary circle (midpoints of sides touch the circle), or by specifying Edge length.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: POLYGON options: Inscribed in circle, Circumscribed about circle, or Edge.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the maximum number of sides that can be specified for a regular polygon using the POLYGON command in AutoCAD?
bankQuestions.explanation: The POLYGON command allows the number of sides to range from 3 (minimum, a triangle) up to 1024 (maximum).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: POLYGON sides: minimum = 3, maximum = 1024.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which AutoCAD command creates a filled solid circle or hollow ring with inner and outer diameters?
bankQuestions.explanation: The DONUT command draws filled rings or solid circular dots (if the inside diameter is specified as 0).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: DONUT creates filled rings or solid filled dots (if inside diameter = 0).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which system variable controls the display style (shape) of point objects created by the POINT command in AutoCAD?
bankQuestions.explanation: PDMODE controls the appearance of POINT objects (e.g., 0 = dot, 1 = none, 2 = cross +, 3 = X, 4 = tick, 34 = circle with cross). Configured visually via DDPTYPE.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: PDMODE controls point shape/style; PDSIZE controls point display size.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which system variable in AutoCAD controls the display size of point objects?
bankQuestions.explanation: PDSIZE sets the display size for point objects. A positive value sets absolute size in drawing units; a negative value sets size as a percentage of the screen viewport.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: PDSIZE sets point object display size (negative = percentage of screen).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What does an "Associative Hatch" mean in AutoCAD?
options: The hatch pattern automatically updates and conforms to the new boundary shape when the surrounding boundary objects are edited or stretched
The hatch is permanently locked and cannot be deleted
The hatch pattern changes color on hover
The hatch links to an external image file
bankQuestions.explanation: An associative hatch is dynamically linked to its bounding entities; if the boundary is stretched, moved, or trimmed, the hatch boundary updates automatically.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Associative hatch dynamically updates when its boundary is modified.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is a "REGION" in AutoCAD and how is it created?
options: A 2D enclosed planar surface object created from closed coplanar loops of lines/polylines that possesses physical properties such as area, centroid, and moments of inertia
bankQuestions.explanation: The REGION command converts closed coplanar boundary shapes into 2D solid planar regions from which engineering area mass properties can be extracted using MASSPROP.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: REGION creates a 2D closed planar solid with physical mass properties (area, centroid).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which AutoCAD command calculates and displays the mass properties (area, perimeter, bounding box, centroid, and moments of inertia) of 2D regions and 3D solids?
bankQuestions.explanation: MASSPROP computes and reports the analytical geometric and mass properties (area, perimeter, centroid coordinates, moments of inertia, radii of gyration) of regions and solids.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: MASSPROP computes area, centroid, and moments of inertia for regions and 3D solids.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD text creation, what is the special code string entered in single-line text to insert the degree symbol (°)?
bankQuestions.explanation: In AutoCAD DTEXT and MTEXT, %%d inserts the degree symbol (°). %%c inserts the diameter symbol (Ø), %%p inserts plus/minus (±), and %%u toggles underline.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Text symbols: %%d = degree (°), %%c = diameter (Ø), %%p = plus/minus (±), %%u = underline.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD text creation, what is the special code string entered to insert the diameter symbol (Ø)?
bankQuestions.explanation: The control code %%c inserts the diameter symbol (Ø).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: %%c inserts the diameter symbol (Ø).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD text creation, what is the special code string entered to insert the plus/minus tolerance symbol (±)?
bankQuestions.explanation: The control code %%p inserts the plus/minus symbol (±).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: %%p inserts the plus/minus symbol (±).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD object selection, what is the difference between a Window selection (dragged left-to-right) and a Crossing selection (dragged right-to-left)?
options: Window selection (blue box) selects ONLY objects entirely enclosed within the rectangle; Crossing selection (green dashed box) selects all objects enclosed OR crossed by the rectangle boundary
Window selection selects text only; Crossing selects lines only
Window selection deletes objects; Crossing copies them
They are strictly identical in operation
bankQuestions.explanation: Dragging left-to-right creates a Window (blue box with solid border) that selects only objects completely inside. Dragging right-to-left creates a Crossing window (green box with dashed border) that selects all objects inside or intersected by it.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Left-to-right (blue window) = Enclosed only. Right-to-left (green crossing) = Enclosed OR touched.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which selection method in AutoCAD allows selecting objects by drawing a continuous freehand polyline path that selects every object it touches or crosses?
bankQuestions.explanation: The Fence option allows the user to draw an open multi-segment line; any object touched or crossed by the fence line is immediately added to the selection set.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Fence (F) selects all objects crossed by an open polyline path.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which AutoCAD modify command requires a Crossing selection window (or crossing polygon) to select the vertices of objects to be displaced while keeping unmoved portions attached?
bankQuestions.explanation: The STRETCH command stretches geometry by moving vertices and endpoints that fall inside a Crossing selection window, while keeping points outside the window fixed in place.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: STRETCH must use a Crossing window (or Crossing polygon) to capture vertices.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: While using the TRIM command in modern AutoCAD, which modifier key can be held down to temporarily switch the command into EXTEND mode without exiting?
bankQuestions.explanation: Holding down the Shift key while using the TRIM command temporarily turns it into the EXTEND command (and vice versa).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Holding Shift toggles between TRIM and EXTEND dynamically.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What occurs when using the FILLET command with the Fillet Radius set to 0 (zero)?
options: It cleans and trims or extends two intersecting or non-parallel lines to form a clean, sharp 90-degree or corner vertex without creating an arc
bankQuestions.explanation: Setting FILLET radius to 0 is a standard CAD drafting technique to quickly close corners into sharp geometric intersections without rounding.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: FILLET with Radius = 0 creates a clean sharp corner without an arc.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which option of the CHAMFER command allows setting the bevel cut using a specified distance along the first line and an angle for the second line?
bankQuestions.explanation: The Angle option prompts for a chamfer distance along the first line and an angular bevel cut (in degrees) to meet the second line.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: CHAMFER Angle option uses distance on 1st line + angle for 2nd line.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is an "Associative Array" in AutoCAD?
options: An array where all cloned elements remain grouped as a single intelligent parametric entity whose rows, columns, counts, and spacings can be dynamically edited at any later time
An array linked to a Microsoft Excel file
An array that cannot be moved
bankQuestions.explanation: Associative arrays treat arrayed items as a single object with grips and properties; modifying the number of items or spacing updates the entire pattern parametrically.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Associative arrays can be dynamically edited (rows, spacing) as a single parametric entity.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which three types of arrays can be created using the ARRAY command in AutoCAD?
options: Rectangular array, Polar array, and Path array
bankQuestions.explanation: Modern AutoCAD supports Rectangular arrays (rows and columns), Polar arrays (circular around a center point), and Path arrays (distributed evenly along an open or closed path curve).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Three ARRAY types: Rectangular, Polar, and Path.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What does the DIVIDE command do to an entity (such as a line, arc, or polyline) in AutoCAD?
options: Places POINT objects or blocks at equal length intervals along the object, dividing it into a specified number of equal segments without physically cutting it
Cuts the entity physically into separate pieces
Halves the thickness of the line
bankQuestions.explanation: DIVIDE places point markers or blocks along an entity to mark equal divisions; it does NOT break or split the physical entity into separate pieces.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: DIVIDE places POINT markers at equal intervals; it does not cut the entity.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the difference between the DIVIDE command and the MEASURE command in AutoCAD?
options: DIVIDE divides an entity into a specified NUMBER of equal segments; MEASURE places points along an entity at a specified SEGMENT LENGTH starting from one end
DIVIDE cuts the line while MEASURE measures its length
MEASURE opens a ruler while DIVIDE is for math
They do the exact same thing
bankQuestions.explanation: DIVIDE prompts for the number of segments (n). MEASURE prompts for a specified segment length (d) and places markers every d units, with any leftover remainder at the far end.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: DIVIDE = specify number of segments. MEASURE = specify segment length.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What does the PURGE command do in AutoCAD?
options: Removes unused named objects (such as unused layers, blocks, dimension styles, linetypes, text styles) from the drawing database, reducing file size
Deletes all objects currently visible on screen
bankQuestions.explanation: PURGE scrubs the drawing database of unreferenced definitions (layers with no objects, unused blocks/styles), significantly shrinking file size and cleaning up templates.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: PURGE removes unused layers, blocks, and styles to shrink file size.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the function of the MATCHPROP command in AutoCAD?
options: Copies property attributes (such as layer, color, linetype, lineweight, hatch pattern, text style) from a selected source object to one or more destination objects
Aligns the origins of two files
bankQuestions.explanation: MATCHPROP (Painter tool) applies the properties (layer, color, linetype, lineweight, transparency) of a selected source entity to destination entities.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: MATCHPROP copies properties (layer, linetype, color) from one object to others.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which Object Snap (OSNAP) mode snaps to the exact center point of a circle, arc, or ellipse in AutoCAD?
bankQuestions.explanation: CENter snaps to the center of a circle, arc, or ellipse.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: CENter snaps to the center of circles, arcs, and ellipses.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which Object Snap mode snaps to the four cardinal points (0°, 90°, 180°, and 270°) of a circle, arc, or ellipse in AutoCAD?
bankQuestions.explanation: QUADrant snaps to the closest cardinal quadrant point (top, bottom, left, right) of a circle, arc, or ellipse.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: QUADrant snaps to the 0°, 90°, 180°, or 270° cardinal points of circles/ellipses.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which Object Snap mode is specifically used to snap to a POINT object created by the POINT, DIVIDE, or MEASURE commands?
bankQuestions.explanation: NODe snaps specifically to point objects, dimension definition points, or dimension text origins.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: NODe snaps to POINT entities (created by POINT, DIVIDE, MEASURE).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which Object Snap mode snaps to the insertion base point of text, blocks, attributes, or shape definitions in AutoCAD?
bankQuestions.explanation: INsertion snaps to the insertion point of text, mtext, blocks, and attributes.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: INsertion (INS) snaps to insertion points of text and blocks.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which system variable in AutoCAD stores the running Object Snap settings as a sum of bitcodes?
bankQuestions.explanation: OSMODE stores the sum of bitcodes for active running OSNAPs (e.g., 1 for Endpoint, 2 for Midpoint, 4 for Center, 8 for Node, 16 for Quadrant, 32 for Intersection). Setting OSMODE to 0 turns off all running snaps.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: OSMODE stores the active OSNAP bitcodes (1=END, 2=MID, 4=CEN, 8=NOD, 16=QUA, 32=INT).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD, what happens to objects that are drawn on a layer that is currently "Locked"?
options: They remain visible and can be snapped to and plotted, but cannot be modified, moved, trimmed, or deleted
They cannot be printed on paper
bankQuestions.explanation: Locked layers prevent accidental editing: objects remain visible, snap points remain active, and they print normally, but editing commands cannot alter them.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Locked layers prevent modification/deletion, but objects remain visible, snappable, and printable.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the unique property of Layer "0" in AutoCAD when objects drawn on it are included in a BLOCK definition?
options: When the block is inserted onto another layer, the Layer 0 objects automatically adopt the color, linetype, and lineweight of that target layer
bankQuestions.explanation: Layer 0 is the universal block authoring layer. Objects drawn on Layer 0 with color ByLayer inherit the layer properties of whichever layer the block reference is placed on.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Objects created on Layer 0 in a block inherit the properties of the layer where the block is inserted.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the primary difference between the BLOCK command and the WBLOCK command in AutoCAD?
options: BLOCK creates an internal block definition stored only inside the current drawing file; WBLOCK (Write Block) exports the geometry as an independent, standalone DWG drawing file on the hard drive
BLOCK is for 2D while WBLOCK is for 3D
WBLOCK can only be used by administrators
BLOCK is temporary while WBLOCK is permanent
bankQuestions.explanation: BLOCK saves block definitions internally within the current drawing. WBLOCK writes the block or selected entities out to an external DWG file accessible by any drawing.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: BLOCK = internal to current DWG. WBLOCK = external standalone DWG file.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which command in AutoCAD is used to create editable alphanumeric text tags (attributes) that attach to a block definition?
bankQuestions.explanation: ATTDEF creates attribute definitions (with Tag, Prompt, and Default value) that attach metadata fields to block definitions.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: ATTDEF creates attribute definitions for blocks.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which command is used to edit the attribute values of an already inserted block reference in AutoCAD?
bankQuestions.explanation: Double-clicking a block reference with attributes or typing EATTEDIT opens the Enhanced Attribute Editor to modify attribute string values.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: EATTEDIT edits attribute values of inserted block references.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD external references (Xrefs), what is the difference between an "Attachment" Xref and an "Overlay" Xref?
options: An Attachment Xref is nested and travels along when the host drawing is referenced into a third drawing; an Overlay Xref is NOT nested and is ignored by third drawings, preventing circular reference errors
Attachment merges objects while Overlay keeps them separate
Overlay embeds the file permanently while Attachment links it
bankQuestions.explanation: Attachment includes the Xref in subsequent nesting (drawing C sees Xref A attached to B). Overlay does not follow nesting, preventing circular referencing loops.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Attachment propagates with nested xrefs; Overlay is ignored in nested drawings (prevents circular loops).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which AutoCAD dimensioning command measures distance parallel to an inclined or skewed line rather than strictly horizontal or vertical?
bankQuestions.explanation: DIMLINEAR measures only true horizontal or vertical distances; DIMALIGNED measures the true true oblique distance parallel to the baseline of the two picked points.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: DIMALIGNED measures true distance parallel to an inclined line; DIMLINEAR is horizontal/vertical only.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which dimensioning command in AutoCAD creates a series of chained, end-to-end continuous dimensions starting from the second extension line of the previous dimension?
bankQuestions.explanation: DIMCONTINUE creates a string of chained dimensions that share adjacent extension lines, continuing sequentially from the last dimension created.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: DIMCONTINUE creates chained end-to-end continuous dimensions.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which dimensioning command in AutoCAD creates a series of stacked, parallel dimensions measured from a common reference baseline datum?
bankQuestions.explanation: DIMBASELINE generates stacked parallel dimensions originating from a single common baseline extension line, automatically spaced by the baseline spacing setting.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: DIMBASELINE creates stacked dimensions originating from a common base datum line.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the function of the MVIEW (or VPORTS) command in Paper Space (Layout)?
options: Creates rectangular or polygonal floating viewports on the paper layout that display views of the geometry created in Model Space
Switches the screen monitor to 3D mode
Exports drawing sheets to MP4 video
Prints drawings directly to a plotter
bankQuestions.explanation: MVIEW creates floating viewports in layout sheets, acting as windows looking into Model Space with independent scales, layers, and view angles.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: MVIEW creates floating viewports in paper space layouts.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD, what does the system variable TILEMODE control when set to 1 versus 0?
options: TILEMODE = 1 activates Model Space with tiled viewports; TILEMODE = 0 activates Paper Space layouts with floating viewports
bankQuestions.explanation: When TILEMODE is 1, the Model tab is active. Setting TILEMODE to 0 switches to the Paper Space layout environment.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: TILEMODE = 1 (Model Space); TILEMODE = 0 (Paper Space Layout).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the primary difference between a CTB plot style table and an STB plot style table in AutoCAD plotting?
options: CTB (Color-dependent) assigns plot properties like pen width based strictly on the object color index (ACI 1-255); STB (Named plot style) assigns plot styles by name independently of color
CTB is for black and white while STB is for color
CTB works only with ink plotters while STB works with laser printers
bankQuestions.explanation: In CTB tables, object color determines printed line thickness and screening. In STB tables, plot styles are named styles assigned directly to layers or objects regardless of display color.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: CTB = Color-dependent plot style (color determines pen width). STB = Named plot style.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the native binary file format extension used by AutoCAD to store drawing files?
bankQuestions.explanation: .dwg (Drawing) is the proprietary binary file format developed by Autodesk to store two- and three-dimensional design data and metadata.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: .dwg is AutoCAD native drawing format.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the file format extension for an AutoCAD Drawing Template file used as a starting seed for new drawings?
bankQuestions.explanation: .dwt is the Drawing Template format, storing preset layers, text styles, dimension styles, units, and title blocks for starting new projects.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: .dwt is the AutoCAD Drawing Template file extension.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the file format extension for the open Drawing Exchange Format developed by Autodesk to enable interoperability across different CAD and GIS software programs?
bankQuestions.explanation: .dxf (Drawing Exchange Format) is an open ASCII or binary data file format created by Autodesk to enable data interoperability between AutoCAD and other CAD/GIS software.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: .dxf is the open CAD exchange format for interoperability across software.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What does the .bak file automatically created in the same folder as an AutoCAD drawing represent?
options: A backup copy of the previous version of the drawing file saved prior to the most recent save operation
bankQuestions.explanation: AutoCAD creates a .bak (Backup) file every time a drawing is manually saved, storing the state of the drawing as it was before that save. Renaming .bak to .dwg recovers the previous state.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: .bak is an automatic backup file of the previous saved version of the DWG.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD Express Tools, what does the BURST command do when executed on a block containing attributes?
options: Explodes the block while preserving the current visible attribute values as ordinary editable text entities
Restores attributes to their default tag labels
Converts the block into a 3D solid
bankQuestions.explanation: Standard EXPLODE reverts attributes back to their original tag names (e.g., TAG_NAME). BURST explodes the block while keeping the actual text values entered by the user.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: BURST explodes a block while maintaining the current attribute values as plain text.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which AutoCAD command allows editing the properties, geometry, vertices, and width of an existing 2D Polyline?
bankQuestions.explanation: The PEDIT command provides options to Close, Open, Join, change Width, Fit curve, Spline curve, and Edit individual vertices of 2D polylines.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: PEDIT edits polyline properties, joins segments, and changes vertex widths.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which option in the PEDIT command closes an open polyline by drawing a straight segment from its last endpoint back to its start point?
bankQuestions.explanation: The Close option in PEDIT connects the start and endpoints of an open polyline with a closing segment.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: PEDIT -> Close joins the start and end of an open polyline.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which AutoCAD Express Tool converts lines, arcs, and polylines with non-zero Z elevations into flat 2D entities with elevation Z = 0?
bankQuestions.explanation: FLATTEN projects 3D geometry onto the current viewing plane, forcing all Z-coordinate elevations to zero to fix unwanted 3D snapping issues.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: FLATTEN forces all selected 3D geometry onto the 2D plane (Z = 0).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the function of AutoCAD DesignCenter (ADC, accessible via Ctrl+2)?
options: Browsing drawings, folders, and networks to drag and drop blocks, layers, styles, and linetypes from other drawings into the current drawing
bankQuestions.explanation: AutoCAD DesignCenter (Ctrl+2) allows users to explore and reuse content (blocks, layers, linetypes, dimension styles) from existing DWG files.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: DesignCenter (Ctrl+2) copies blocks, layers, and styles across drawing files.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the function of AutoCAD Tool Palettes (accessible via Ctrl+3)?
options: Providing tabbed graphic panels of commonly used blocks, hatching patterns, and customized drawing tools for quick drag-and-drop insertion
bankQuestions.explanation: Tool Palettes (Ctrl+3) organize frequently used blocks, hatch patterns, commands, and drawing materials into organized tabbed toolbars.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Tool Palettes (Ctrl+3) provides quick drag-and-drop access to blocks, hatches, and tools.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which AutoCAD command allows editing the internal definition of a block directly inside the dedicated Block Editor environment?
bankQuestions.explanation: BEDIT opens the selected block in the dedicated Block Editor environment where dynamic parameters, actions, and geometry can be modified.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: BEDIT opens the Block Editor window to modify block geometry and dynamic parameters.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD Dynamic Blocks, what is a "Visibility Parameter"?
options: A parameter that allows creating multiple visual states or variations of a block within a single definition, toggling parts visible or hidden
A setting that changes the screen contrast
A tool for measuring line transparency
bankQuestions.explanation: A Visibility parameter defines different visibility states in a block, allowing the user to switch between different graphic views (e.g. door swing angles) using a drop-down grip.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Visibility Parameter allows multiple display states/views in a single dynamic block.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the function of the WIPEOUT command in AutoCAD?
options: Creates a polygonal boundary that masks or hides underlying objects using the current background screen color
Deletes all layers in the drawing
bankQuestions.explanation: WIPEOUT generates a blank masking region that obscures objects beneath it, commonly placed behind text notes or detail tags to keep drawings legible without trimming lines.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: WIPEOUT masks underlying geometry with a blank background polygon.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which system variable controls whether the boundary frame of a WIPEOUT object is displayed on screen and plotted on paper?
bankQuestions.explanation: WIPEOUTFRAME: 0 = frames hidden and not plotted; 1 = frames displayed and plotted; 2 = frames displayed on screen but NOT plotted on paper.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: WIPEOUTFRAME controls visibility and plotting of wipeout borders (0=off, 1=on, 2=screen only).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is a "FIELD" in AutoCAD annotation text?
options: A dynamic text placeholder linked to drawing properties (such as polyline area, file name, plot date) that updates automatically when the property changes
An empty area of land in GIS
A text box for writing long paragraphs
bankQuestions.explanation: Fields are intelligent text expressions that display variable data (e.g. parcel area, title block dates, author name); typing REGEN updates fields when drawing geometry changes.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: FIELD inserts dynamic text linked to drawing data (e.g. area, date) that auto-updates.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which command in AutoCAD creates a formatted grid table of rows and columns that supports mathematical formulas and data linking to Microsoft Excel?
bankQuestions.explanation: The TABLE command creates native AutoCAD tables with cells that support text, block symbols, arithmetic formulas (SUM, AVERAGE), and dynamic links to Excel spreadsheets.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: TABLE creates formatted tabular grids supporting formulas and Excel links.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the function of the QTEXT (Quick Text) system variable in AutoCAD?
options: When turned ON, it replaces text strings with rectangular bounding boxes to drastically accelerate screen redraw and pan speeds in large drawings
It types text automatically using voice recognition
It translates English text into regional languages
It checks grammatical errors in notes
bankQuestions.explanation: QTEXT (Quick Text) replaces text rendering with simple rectangular outlines. When enabled, regeneration of large architectural plans with heavy text occurs much faster.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: QTEXT ON displays text as rectangular boxes to speed up screen regeneration.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the difference between an AutoCAD .SHX font and a Windows .TTF font in CAD drawings?
options: SHX fonts are compiled vector stroke fonts native to AutoCAD that regenerate and plot very quickly; TTF (TrueType) fonts are Windows outline fonts that support diverse typographical styles
SHX fonts contain images while TTF fonts contain audio
SHX fonts cannot be printed on paper
TTF fonts can only be used in Microsoft Word
bankQuestions.explanation: SHX fonts are proprietary stroke-based shape files optimized for CAD drawing speed; TrueType (.ttf) fonts are scalable Windows fonts used when publication styling is required.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: SHX = native compiled CAD stroke fonts (fast plotting). TTF = Windows TrueType outline fonts.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which AutoCAD command allows finding and replacing text strings across Model Space, Paper Space layouts, and block attribute values?
bankQuestions.explanation: The FIND command opens the Find and Replace dialog to search, locate, and replace specific text strings across drawing annotations, dimensions, and block attributes.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: FIND searches and replaces text across drawings and block attributes.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the function of the AUDIT command in AutoCAD?
options: Evaluates the integrity of the active drawing database, detecting internal data errors and giving the option to fix them
Audits financial accounts of the company
Checks if the software license is genuine
Counts the total number of blocks in the drawing
bankQuestions.explanation: AUDIT inspects the active drawing database for internal data corruption or broken entity links and repairs errors when "Fix any errors detected" is set to Yes.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: AUDIT diagnoses and repairs database errors in the currently open DWG drawing.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the function of the RECOVER command in AutoCAD?
options: Opens and repairs a severely damaged or corrupted drawing file that fails to open normally using the standard OPEN command
Restores files deleted from the Windows Recycle Bin
bankQuestions.explanation: RECOVER repairs and opens corrupted DWG files that crash during standard file opening by rebuilding corrupted database tables.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: RECOVER repairs and opens damaged DWG files that cannot open normally.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the function of the PLAN command in AutoCAD?
options: Restores the top orthogonal plan view (looking down along the positive Z-axis) of the current UCS, a specified UCS, or the World Coordinate System
Creates a civil layout drawing automatically
Changes the printer sheet size to A1
bankQuestions.explanation: The PLAN command switches the current viewport view to a top plan view (looking directly down on the X-Y plane) aligned with the active UCS or WCS.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: PLAN switches the viewport to a top orthogonal plan view of the current coordinate system.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which command in AutoCAD is used to assign named viewports in Model Space for multi-view drafting?
bankQuestions.explanation: In Model Space, the VPORTS command splits the drawing window into multiple tiled viewport panes (e.g. Top, Front, Isometric) to aid drafting from different angles simultaneously.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: VPORTS creates tiled viewports in Model Space (or floating viewports in layouts).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What does "VP Freeze" (Viewport Freeze) in the AutoCAD Layer Properties Manager do?
options: Freezes selected layers ONLY within the active layout viewport while leaving them fully visible in other viewports and Model Space
Freezes layers across all drawings on the network
bankQuestions.explanation: Viewport Freeze allows setting different layer visibility states for different viewports on the same layout sheet without affecting the master model.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: VP Freeze hides layers in a specific layout viewport only.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which command in AutoCAD creates a Revision Cloud composed of continuous connected arc segments?
bankQuestions.explanation: The REVCLOUD command creates revision clouds around drawing changes, with customizable minimum/maximum arc lengths and calligraphy brush styles.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: REVCLOUD creates revision clouds made of continuous arcs to highlight drawing changes.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What does the SKETCH command in AutoCAD allow the user to do?
options: Draws freehand line segments by tracking cursor movement across the screen as if drawing with a pencil
bankQuestions.explanation: The SKETCH command enables freehand drawing: moving the pointing device traces a sequence of short line or polyline segments on the screen.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: SKETCH enables freehand line drafting following cursor movements.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the function of the LTSCALE system variable in AutoCAD?
options: Sets the global linetype scale factor for all dotted, dashed, and hidden linetypes throughout the drawing
Sets the font size of linear dimensions
Sets the thickness of solid walls
bankQuestions.explanation: LTSCALE controls the global scaling of dashes and spaces for broken linetypes (HIDDEN, DASHED, CENTER) across the entire drawing.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: LTSCALE sets the global scaling factor for linetypes (dash/space lengths).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What does the PSLTSCALE system variable control in AutoCAD Paper Space layouts?
options: When PSLTSCALE = 1, linetype dash lengths appear identical on paper regardless of the magnification scale of individual viewports
It controls the printer paper thickness
It sets the line weight in millimeters
It locks the layout viewport zoom
bankQuestions.explanation: PSLTSCALE (Paper Space Linetype Scale): When set to 1, dash lengths on printed sheets remain uniform across viewports having different zoom scales (e.g., 1:20 and 1:100).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: PSLTSCALE = 1 maintains uniform linetype dash spacing across viewports of different scales.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the function of the ISOPLANE command (or F5 shortcut) in AutoCAD?
options: Switches the active isometric drawing plane between Top, Left, and Right when isometric snap is enabled
bankQuestions.explanation: ISOPLANE sets the active plane for 2D isometric drawing (Left: 90° and 150°, Top: 30° and 150°, Right: 30° and 90°).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: ISOPLANE switches the 2D isometric drafting plane (Top, Left, Right).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: How is an isometric circle (isocircle) correctly drawn in AutoCAD when isometric drafting mode is active?
options: By using the ELLIPSE command and selecting the Isocircle (I) sub-option
By using the CIRCLE command directly
By drawing a polygon with 100 sides
bankQuestions.explanation: In isometric projection, a circle appears as an ellipse. Running ELLIPSE and typing "I" for Isocircle orients an ellipse correctly according to the current Isoplane.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Isometric circles are drawn using ELLIPSE -> Isocircle (I) option.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the function of the BATTMAN command in AutoCAD?
options: Block Attribute Manager: manages attribute tags, prompts, default values, and display order across all insertions of a block definition
A utility to test battery power
bankQuestions.explanation: BATTMAN (Block Attribute Manager) allows editing attribute definitions in blocks, updating existing block instances, and reordering attribute prompts.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: BATTMAN = Block Attribute Manager (manages attribute order and definitions).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the function of the ATTEXT (Attribute Extraction) command in AutoCAD?
options: Extracts block attribute data into external structured text or CSV files for spreadsheet and database analysis
bankQuestions.explanation: ATTEXT (and DATAEXTRACTION) extracts attribute data and object properties from blocks into external files (TXT, CSV, XLS) for bill of quantities (BOQ) generation.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: ATTEXT extracts attribute data from drawings into external text/CSV files.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the function of the ALIGN command in AutoCAD?
options: Moves, rotates, and optionally scales 2D or 3D objects to align with other target objects using 1, 2, or 3 pairs of source and destination points in a single operation
Aligns text paragraphs to the left margin
Lines up icons on the desktop
Aligns paper in the printer tray
bankQuestions.explanation: The ALIGN command aligns objects with target geometry by specifying source and destination alignment points, with an option to scale 2D objects to match target dimensions.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: ALIGN moves, rotates, and scales objects to match target geometry in one command.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What does the LENGTHEN command in AutoCAD do to open lines and arcs?
options: Changes the length of objects and the included angle of arcs using Delta, Percent, Total length, or Dynamic dragging options
bankQuestions.explanation: The LENGTHEN command edits the length of lines/open polylines and included angles of arcs: Delta adds a length, Percent scales length, Total sets absolute final length.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: LENGTHEN modifies the length of lines and arc angles (Delta, Percent, Total, Dynamic).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which component of a digital computer CPU performs mathematical arithmetic operations and logical comparisons?
bankQuestions.explanation: The Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) is the CPU sub-component responsible for all elementary arithmetic calculations (addition, subtraction) and logical evaluations (AND, OR, NOT).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) executes mathematical and logical operations in the CPU.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the primary function of the Control Unit (CU) inside a computer Central Processing Unit?
options: Directing and coordinating the operations of all computer components by fetching instructions, decoding them, and managing data flow
bankQuestions.explanation: The Control Unit (CU) orchestrates the execution of instructions: it fetches instructions from memory, decodes them, and directs the ALU, registers, and buses.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Control Unit (CU) fetches, decodes, and orchestrates instruction execution in the CPU.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Why is RAM (Random Access Memory) characterized as "volatile" memory?
options: Because all data stored in it is instantly lost when the computer power is switched off
Because it is made of radioactive materials
Because its memory chips overheat easily
Because it can be stolen over the internet
bankQuestions.explanation: Volatile memory requires continuous electrical power to maintain its state. When power is removed, RAM contents are wiped immediately.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: RAM is volatile memory: data is lost immediately when power is turned off.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is ROM (Read-Only Memory) primarily used for on a computer motherboard?
options: Storing essential permanent boot firmware (such as BIOS or UEFI) that boots the hardware during power-on
bankQuestions.explanation: ROM is non-volatile memory that permanently holds the BIOS/UEFI firmware necessary to initialize hardware components and load the operating system during startup.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: ROM is non-volatile memory holding the system boot firmware (BIOS/UEFI).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: How many bits make up one Byte of digital data?
bankQuestions.explanation: A byte consists of exactly 8 binary digits (bits). A group of 4 bits is called a nibble.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 Byte = 8 bits. 1 Nibble = 4 bits.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In digital computing binary storage, how many Bytes are in one Kilobyte (KB)?
bankQuestions.explanation: In computer architecture based on binary addressing, 1 KB = 2^10 = 1024 Bytes. In decimal SI notation, 1 kB = 1000 Bytes.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 Kilobyte (KB) = 1024 Bytes. 1 Megabyte (MB) = 1024 KB. 1 Gigabyte (GB) = 1024 MB.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which computer storage device utilizes non-volatile flash memory chips with NO moving mechanical parts, providing ultra-fast read/write speeds for CAD operations?
bankQuestions.explanation: Solid State Drives (SSDs) use NAND flash memory rather than spinning magnetic platters, eliminating seek time and drastically accelerating CAD file loading.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: SSDs use flash memory with no moving parts, delivering superior read/write speeds.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is a "Plotter" in computer hardware, and why is it preferred over ordinary desktop printers in civil engineering offices?
options: A specialized large-format output device designed to print high-precision vector line drawings, site maps, and blueprints onto large paper rolls (A0, A1, A2)
A device that enters GPS coordinates
A specialized monitor with touch pen
A digitizing camera for aerial mapping
bankQuestions.explanation: Plotters print high-resolution vector architectural drawings and cadastral survey plans on large sheets up to A0 size (841 x 1189 mm) or continuous roll paper.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Plotter = large-format output device for printing architectural and survey plans (A0/A1).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the function of a Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) with dedicated VRAM in a CAD workstation?
options: Accelerating 2D/3D graphics rendering, model rotation, wireframe shading, and viewport pan/zoom without overloading the main CPU
Connecting the computer to the internet
Saving files to USB flash drives
bankQuestions.explanation: A dedicated GPU processes complex vector rendering, texture mapping, and 3D viewport rotations in real time, freeing the CPU for program logic.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: GPU accelerates 2D/3D graphics rendering and viewport manipulation in CAD.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is an Operating System (OS)?
options: System software that manages computer hardware resources, memory, files, processes, and provides a user interface and runtime environment for application software
An application for drawing survey plans
A physical electronic circuit inside the keyboard
bankQuestions.explanation: The operating system (e.g. Windows, Linux) manages hardware resources (CPU, RAM, storage, peripherals) and provides services for application programs like AutoCAD.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Operating System manages computer hardware, memory, files, and runs applications.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the standard physical addressing length of a network hardware MAC (Media Access Control) address?
bankQuestions.explanation: A MAC address is a unique 48-bit hardware identifier burned into network interface cards (NIC), written as 12 hexadecimal digits (e.g., 00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: MAC address is a 48-bit (6-byte) unique hardware physical address.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the address length of an IPv4 (Internet Protocol version 4) address?
options: 32 bits (expressed as 4 decimal octets separated by dots, e.g., 192.168.1.1)
bankQuestions.explanation: IPv4 addresses are 32 bits in length, typically written in dotted-decimal format comprising four 8-bit octets (e.g. 192.168.0.1).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: IPv4 address = 32 bits (4 octets). IPv6 address = 128 bits.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What type of network connects computers and peripherals within a localized geographical area such as a single office building, survey lab, or school campus?
bankQuestions.explanation: A Local Area Network (LAN) interconnects computers, plotters, and servers within a limited room, building, or campus.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: LAN (Local Area Network) connects computers in a single building or office.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is a WAN (Wide Area Network)?
options: A telecommunications network spanning large geographical areas, connecting cities, states, or countries across continents (e.g., the Internet)
A network inside a single home
A Bluetooth connection between a phone and headset
A network connecting two computers with a USB cable
bankQuestions.explanation: A Wide Area Network (WAN) connects geographically dispersed local networks across cities or countries. The Internet is the world largest public WAN.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: WAN (Wide Area Network) spans broad geographic areas across cities and countries.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the function of a Router in computer networking?
options: Directing and forwarding data packets between different IP networks based on destination IP addresses and routing tables
Converting AC voltage to DC power
bankQuestions.explanation: A router operates at Layer 3 (Network Layer) of the OSI model, inspecting packet destination IP addresses to forward traffic between distinct networks.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Router forwards data packets between different networks based on IP addresses.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the function of the DNS (Domain Name System) on the Internet?
options: Translating human-readable domain names (such as www.keralapsc.gov.in) into numerical IP addresses (such as 164.100.150.10)
bankQuestions.explanation: DNS functions as the phonebook of the Internet, translating user-friendly domain names into machine-readable IP addresses required for network routing.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: DNS translates human-readable domain names into numerical IP addresses.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is a "Digitizer" (or graphics tablet with puck) historically used for in CAD mapping offices?
options: Tracing existing paper land survey maps and blueprints by hand using an electronic crosshair puck to convert line features into digital CAD coordinates
bankQuestions.explanation: A digitizer tablet has an embedded electromagnetic wire grid. Tracing over a paper map taped to the tablet records digital coordinate points directly into AutoCAD.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Digitizer tablets were used to trace paper survey maps into digital CAD drawings.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which file system is standardly used by the modern Microsoft Windows operating system, supporting file permissions, journaling, and large drives?
bankQuestions.explanation: NTFS is the proprietary journaling file system used by modern Windows, supporting access control lists (permissions), encryption, and massive partition sizes.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: NTFS is the primary file system for modern Windows installations.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the function of the Windows shortcut key combination "Ctrl + Z"?
options: Undo the most recent action or command
bankQuestions.explanation: Ctrl + Z is the universal keyboard shortcut to Undo the last operation.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Ctrl + Z = Undo. Ctrl + Y = Redo. Ctrl + S = Save.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the function of the OOPS command in AutoCAD?
options: Restores objects deleted by the most recent ERASE command without undoing any intervening drawing or editing actions performed since
Undoes all commands from the entire session
bankQuestions.explanation: OOPS specifically restores entities removed by the last ERASE command, even if you have created other geometry in the meantime. Unlike UNDO, it does not rollback intervening work.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: OOPS restores objects deleted by the last ERASE command without undoing intervening actions.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD, what happens when an object grip is clicked to turn "hot" (red) and the Spacebar or Enter key is pressed repeatedly?
options: It cycles through the five grip editing modes: STRETCH, MOVE, ROTATE, SCALE, and MIRROR
It switches between model space and paper space
It opens the print dialog box
bankQuestions.explanation: Clicking a grip activates it. Pressing Spacebar cycles through the built-in grip modes in sequence: Stretch -> Move -> Rotate -> Scale -> Mirror.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Spacebar cycles through grip modes: Stretch, Move, Rotate, Scale, Mirror.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What does the VIEWRES command control in AutoCAD?
options: The display smoothness and resolution of circles, arcs, and ellipses by adjusting the number of line chords used to approximate them on screen
The physical pixel resolution of the computer monitor
bankQuestions.explanation: VIEWRES sets the circle zoom percentage (1 to 20,000). A higher value makes circles appear perfectly round on screen rather than segmented multi-sided polygons.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: VIEWRES controls the display resolution/smoothness of circles and arcs on screen.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the difference between REDRAW and REGEN in AutoCAD?
options: REDRAW merely refreshes the current display screen to clean up blip marks; REGEN completely recomputes the entire drawing database from floating-point math coordinates
REDRAW prints the drawing; REGEN saves it to disk
REDRAW is for 3D; REGEN is for 2D
bankQuestions.explanation: REDRAW simply repaints the current screen buffer (fast). REGEN recalculates all entity coordinates mathematically from the database and updates the display list (slower).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: REDRAW repaints the screen; REGEN recalculates the drawing database mathematically.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD Parametric drafting, what does the "Coincident" geometric constraint enforce?
options: Constrains two points to remain pinned together, or constrains a point to remain on a line, arc, or curve
Forces two lines to have identical lengths
Forces two circles to be concentric
Locks an object at a fixed coordinate
bankQuestions.explanation: The Coincident constraint binds two points together, or constrains a point to lie continuously along a curve or extended line.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Coincident constraint locks two points together or keeps a point on a curve.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD Parametric drafting, what does the "Collinear" geometric constraint enforce?
options: Constrains two or more straight line segments to lie along the exact same infinite straight line path
Constrains lines to be equal in length
Constrains lines to have the same layer color
bankQuestions.explanation: The Collinear constraint ensures that two or more selected line segments remain aligned along the same common infinite line of action.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Collinear constraint forces multiple line segments to lie along the same straight line.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD Parametric drafting, what does the "Concentric" geometric constraint enforce?
options: Constrains two or more circles, arcs, or ellipses to share the exact same center point
Forces circles to have the same radius
Forces arcs to have the same sweep angle
bankQuestions.explanation: The Concentric constraint locks the center points of two or more circular/elliptical arcs together so they remain concentric.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Concentric constraint forces circles and arcs to share the exact same center point.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD Parametric drafting, what does the "Fix" geometric constraint enforce?
options: Locks a specified geometric point or curve at its fixed coordinate location in space so it cannot move or rotate
bankQuestions.explanation: The Fix constraint anchors a point or curve in place relative to the WCS, preventing it from being moved or resized by other parametric constraints.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Fix constraint anchors a point or curve at a fixed coordinate location.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD Parametric drafting, what does the "Equal" geometric constraint enforce?
options: Constrains selected lines to have equal length, or selected circles/arcs to have equal radius
Forces two layers to have equal transparency
Sets text height equal to dimension height
bankQuestions.explanation: The Equal constraint resizes lines to maintain identical lengths, or circles/arcs to maintain identical radii.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Equal constraint maintains identical lengths for lines or identical radii for circles/arcs.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the function of the DIMREASSOCIATE command in AutoCAD?
options: Reassociates disassociated dimensions with geometric vertices on objects so dimensions update dynamically when geometry is modified
Converts linear dimensions into aligned dimensions
bankQuestions.explanation: DIMREASSOCIATE re-links orphaned dimension extension lines to object snap points so associative dimensioning functionality is restored.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: DIMREASSOCIATE links disconnected dimensions back to object vertices.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the function of the "Background Mask" property in AutoCAD Multiline Text (MTEXT)?
options: Opaquely masks drawing lines and objects behind the text box using the background color, ensuring text readability without trimming underlying lines
Draws a border box around the text
bankQuestions.explanation: Background Mask places an opaque mask behind MTEXT so lines passing through the text box are obscured, keeping annotations legible without cutting lines.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Background Mask in MTEXT obscures lines behind text for clear legibility.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which AutoCAD command allows setting up and modifying Multileader styles (controlling leader line type, landing distance, and arrowhead shape)?
bankQuestions.explanation: MLEADERSTYLE opens the Multileader Style Manager to define leader line characteristics (straight/spline), landing offsets, arrowhead types, and content format.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: MLEADERSTYLE configures multileader appearance, landing distances, and arrowheads.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which network topology connects all client computers to a single central network switch or hub?
bankQuestions.explanation: In a Star topology, every network node has a dedicated cable running to a central switch. A cable break only affects that single node, making it the most common LAN topology.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Star topology connects all network nodes to a single central switch or hub.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which network topology uses a single continuous central coaxial backbone cable terminated with resistors at both ends?
bankQuestions.explanation: A Bus topology connects all devices along a single shared cable (backbone) with terminators at both ends to prevent signal reflections.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Bus topology uses a single shared backbone cable with terminators at both ends.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which network topology provides maximum redundancy and fault tolerance by connecting every computer directly to every other computer via dedicated links?
bankQuestions.explanation: In a full mesh topology, every node has a point-to-point connection to every other node, providing total fault tolerance at high cabling cost.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Mesh topology provides highest redundancy by linking every node directly to all others.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In the 7-layer OSI networking reference model, which layer is responsible for logical routing of packets and IP addressing?
bankQuestions.explanation: Layer 3 (Network Layer) handles packet routing, logical IP addressing, and path determination across interconnected networks.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Network Layer (Layer 3) handles IP addressing and packet routing.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In the 7-layer OSI model, which layer handles physical MAC addressing and frames?
bankQuestions.explanation: Layer 2 (Data Link Layer) organizes data into frames, handles hardware MAC addressing, and performs error detection across a single local link.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Data Link Layer (Layer 2) handles MAC addressing, frames, and switches.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In the 7-layer OSI model, which layer ensures reliable end-to-end data delivery, flow control, and port numbers (such as TCP and UDP)?
bankQuestions.explanation: Layer 4 (Transport Layer) provides transparent, reliable end-to-end data transfer between hosts using TCP or connectionless UDP, managing port numbers.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Transport Layer (Layer 4) handles end-to-end reliable delivery (TCP/UDP) and ports.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the standard transmission medium used for Gigabit Ethernet LAN cables terminated with RJ-45 modular connectors?
options: Unshielded Twisted Pair (UTP) copper cable (Cat5e or Cat6)
bankQuestions.explanation: Cat5e and Cat6 Unshielded Twisted Pair (UTP) cables consisting of 4 twisted pairs of copper wires terminated with 8P8C (RJ-45) connectors are standard for Ethernet LANs.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: UTP Cat5e/Cat6 cables with RJ-45 connectors are standard for office Ethernet LANs.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Which transmission cable transmits data as light pulses through a thin glass or plastic core, providing complete immunity to electromagnetic interference (EMI)?
bankQuestions.explanation: Fiber optic cables transmit light pulses via total internal reflection inside silica glass fibers, offering immense bandwidth over long distances without electrical interference.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Fiber optic cables transmit light pulses through glass cores and are completely immune to EMI.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is a "Firewall" in computer network security?
options: A hardware device or software program that monitors and filters incoming and outgoing network traffic based on predetermined security rules
A physical fireproof safe to store backup hard disks
An air cooling system for server racks
A surge protector for power plugs
bankQuestions.explanation: A firewall acts as a security barrier between a trusted internal network and untrusted external networks (the Internet), inspecting packets and blocking unauthorized access.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Firewall monitors and filters network traffic according to security rules.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What type of malicious computer software masquerades as legitimate software but carries hidden malicious code that compromises security when run?
bankQuestions.explanation: A Trojan horse disguises itself as a useful, benign application (e.g. a drawing utility or game) to trick the user into installing it, thereby creating a backdoor.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Trojan Horse disguises itself as legitimate software to deliver a malicious payload.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What type of malware self-replicates and spreads across computer networks automatically WITHOUT needing to attach itself to an existing host file or program?
bankQuestions.explanation: A computer worm is a standalone malicious program that replicates itself over network connections without requiring human intervention or a host carrier file.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Worm is a standalone self-replicating malware spreading automatically over networks.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is "Ransomware" in cybersecurity?
options: Malware that encrypts user data files and demands an extortion payment in exchange for the decryption key
Software that speeds up computer performance
A tool for recovering lost CAD drawings
bankQuestions.explanation: Ransomware maliciously encrypts files, locking victims out of their documents, drawings, and databases until a ransom is paid.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Ransomware encrypts victim files and extorts money for the decryption key.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the function of an Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) in a computer CAD workstation setup?
options: Providing instantaneous battery backup power during mains electricity failure to prevent sudden computer shutdown and drawing file corruption
Backing up files to Google Drive
bankQuestions.explanation: A UPS provides emergency battery backup power when the main electrical supply fails, allowing draftsmen sufficient time to save open DWG files and shut down cleanly.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: UPS provides battery backup during power outages, preventing loss of unsaved CAD work.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD Parametric drafting, what does the "Tangent" geometric constraint enforce?
options: Constrains two curves (or a line and a curve) to maintain tangency to each other at their point of intersection
Forces two lines to intersect at 45 degrees
Forces an arc to touch the X-axis
bankQuestions.explanation: The Tangent constraint maintains tangency between two curves (circles, arcs, ellipses, splines) or between a straight line and a curve.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Tangent constraint locks curves/lines to remain tangent at their meeting point.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD Parametric drafting, what does the "Parallel" geometric constraint enforce?
options: Constrains selected straight line segments to remain strictly parallel to each other
Forces lines to have the same length
Forces lines to lie on the same layer
bankQuestions.explanation: The Parallel constraint constrains two or more straight lines to maintain equal angular slope, ensuring they never intersect.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Parallel constraint ensures two or more lines remain strictly parallel.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD Parametric drafting, what does the "Perpendicular" geometric constraint enforce?
options: Constrains two straight lines to maintain an exact 90-degree orthogonal angle between them
Forces lines to cross at their midpoints
Forces lines to be vertical only
Forces lines to touch at endpoints
bankQuestions.explanation: The Perpendicular constraint locks two lines at a constant 90° angle relative to each other.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Perpendicular constraint maintains a 90° angle between two lines.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In AutoCAD Parametric drafting, what does the "Symmetric" geometric constraint enforce?
options: Constrains two objects or points to maintain symmetrical positions relative to a designated symmetry centerline
Mirrors objects and deletes the originals
bankQuestions.explanation: The Symmetric constraint maintains geometric symmetry of selected objects or constraint points about a chosen symmetry line.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Symmetric constraint forces geometry to remain mirror-symmetric about an axis.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the function of the APERTURE system variable in AutoCAD?
options: Controls the size (in pixels) of the Object Snap target box that appears inside the crosshairs when snapping to objects
bankQuestions.explanation: APERTURE sets the display size in pixels of the object snap selection target box that hovers at the cursor crosshairs.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: APERTURE sets the pixel size of the OSNAP target box.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What does the PICKFIRST system variable in AutoCAD control?
options: Noun/verb selection: when PICKFIRST = 1, objects can be selected before issuing an editing command; when 0, commands must be issued before selecting objects
The first color in the palette
bankQuestions.explanation: PICKFIRST controls noun/verb selection. With PICKFIRST = 1 (default), you can pick objects first and then type commands like MOVE or ERASE.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: PICKFIRST = 1 allows selecting objects first before typing commands (noun/verb).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What does the BLIPMODE system variable control in classic AutoCAD?
options: Controls whether temporary tiny marker crosses (blips) appear on the screen at points clicked with the pointing device
bankQuestions.explanation: BLIPMODE controls whether small plus marker crosses ("blips") are left on screen on mouse clicks. When ON, typing REDRAW removes the blip marks.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: BLIPMODE displays temporary tick marks on mouse clicks; cleaned by REDRAW.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the function of the DRAGMODE system variable in AutoCAD?
options: Controls whether objects are displayed dynamically in real time while being dragged during commands like MOVE, COPY, and SCALE
bankQuestions.explanation: DRAGMODE controls dynamic dragging preview. When set to Auto (2), AutoCAD shows full real-time graphic dragging of entities as the mouse moves.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: DRAGMODE controls dynamic visual preview during MOVE, COPY, and SCALE dragging.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What does the CURSORSIZE system variable control in AutoCAD?
options: The size of the crosshair cursor expressed as a percentage of the total screen display size (from 1 to 100 percent)
The size of the mouse arrow pointer
The font size of the command line
bankQuestions.explanation: CURSORSIZE determines the length of crosshairs across the drawing window. Setting CURSORSIZE to 100 extends crosshairs completely across the screen.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: CURSORSIZE = 100 gives full-screen crosshairs across the drawing area.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In computer networking, which device operates at Layer 2 (Data Link Layer) to inspect incoming frames and forward them specifically to the destination port based on MAC addresses?
bankQuestions.explanation: A network switch learns MAC addresses on each physical port and directs incoming data frames only to the intended destination node, avoiding collision domains.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Network Switch operates at Layer 2, forwarding frames based on hardware MAC addresses.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the fundamental difference between a network Hub and a network Switch?
options: A Hub blindly broadcasts all incoming data packets out to every connected port (Layer 1); a Switch inspects MAC addresses and forwards frames only to the specific destination port (Layer 2)
A Hub connects to fiber optic while a switch connects to copper
A Hub has built-in Wi-Fi while a switch does not
bankQuestions.explanation: A hub is a multiport repeater that copies all electrical signals to every port, wasting bandwidth. A switch selectively routes frames to the intended recipient.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Hub broadcasts traffic to all ports; Switch forwards selectively to the destination MAC port.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In the Internet TCP/IP protocol suite, what is the well-known default port number used for unencrypted HTTP web browsing traffic?
bankQuestions.explanation: Port 80 is the standard port assigned to unencrypted HTTP web traffic. Port 443 is used for secure encrypted HTTPS connections.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: HTTP = Port 80. HTTPS = Port 443. FTP = Port 21. SMTP = Port 25.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In the Internet TCP/IP protocol suite, what is the default port number used for secure encrypted HTTPS web browsing traffic?
bankQuestions.explanation: Port 443 is the standard port for HTTPS (HTTP over TLS/SSL) encrypted communications.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: HTTPS uses Port 443 for encrypted web browsing.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the function of the DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) service on a local network?
options: Automatically assigning IP addresses, subnet masks, default gateways, and DNS servers to client computers connecting to the network
Backing up files to external servers
bankQuestions.explanation: DHCP dynamically allocates IP configuration parameters from an address pool to client devices upon connection, eliminating manual static IP configuration.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: DHCP automatically leases IP addresses and network configuration to connected devices.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is a "Computer Virus" and how does it spread compared to a standalone worm?
options: A piece of malicious code that requires a human action to run and attaches itself to an existing host executable file to propagate
A physical insect inside the CPU heatsink
A software program that speeds up internet
bankQuestions.explanation: A virus requires an existing host file or carrier document and user execution to replicate and spread, unlike a worm which self-replicates across networks.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Virus requires a host file and user execution to propagate; worms spread autonomously.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is "Phishing" in internet cybersecurity?
options: A social engineering fraud where deceptive emails or fake websites impersonate trustworthy institutions to trick victims into revealing passwords or credit card details
A method of repairing damaged network cables
bankQuestions.explanation: Phishing tricks individuals into providing sensitive personal authentication credentials by masquerading as banks, universities, or government agencies.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Phishing = deceptive social engineering scams tricking users into revealing passwords.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the purpose of defragmentation (Disk Defragmenter) on traditional Hard Disk Drives (HDDs)?
options: Reorganizing fragmented file clusters into contiguous physical sectors on disk tracks to speed up read access times
bankQuestions.explanation: Defragmentation consolidates scattered file pieces into contiguous disk clusters, minimizing drive head movement and boosting HDD file retrieval speed.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Defragmentation arranges file clusters contiguously on HDDs to reduce read head seek time.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Why is traditional disk defragmentation NOT recommended for Solid State Drives (SSDs)?
options: SSDs have instantaneous random access with zero mechanical seek time, and defragmenting causes unnecessary write cycles that prematurely wear out flash memory cells
bankQuestions.explanation: SSDs retrieve non-contiguous memory blocks without mechanical seek delay; defragmenting writes gigabytes of unnecessary data, consuming finite flash endurance cycles.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Do NOT defragment SSDs; it wears out flash memory cells without providing speed benefits.
