bankQuestions.question: In the centre-line method of building estimation, what deduction is made from the total centre-line length for each T-junction of cross walls?
options: Half the breadth of the wall (b / 2)
Twice the breadth of the wall (2 b)
bankQuestions.explanation: At each T-junction where a cross-wall meets a main wall, a deduction equal to half the wall breadth (b/2) is made from the total centre-line length.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: At L-corners: No deduction. At T-junctions: Deduct b/2 per junction. At X-cross junctions: Deduct full breadth (b).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: Why is no deduction made at corner (L-junction) wall intersections in the centre-line method of estimation?
options: Because the overlap area on the inner side exactly balances the omitted triangular area on the outer side
Because corner walls are always thinner
bankQuestions.explanation: At a rectangular L-corner, the excess area counted on the outer corner perfectly balances the deficient area inside, meaning the centerline length yields the exact correct net volume.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Centerline method: 0 deduction at L-corners; b/2 deduction at T-junctions.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In the long-wall and short-wall method of estimating, how is the length of a long wall from out-to-out calculated from its centre-to-centre length?
options: Centre-to-centre length + Half breadth of wall at each end (Total + One breadth)
bankQuestions.explanation: Length of long wall (out-to-out) = Centre-to-centre length + (Breadth of footing / 2) + (Breadth of footing / 2) = Centre-to-centre length + Breadth of wall.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Long wall length = c/c length + 1 breadth. Short wall length = c/c length - 1 breadth.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What type of preliminary estimate is prepared by multiplying the total plinth area of a proposed building by the prevailing plinth area rate in that locality?
bankQuestions.explanation: A plinth area estimate is an approximate estimate prepared by multiplying the external covered plinth area by the predetermined plinth area rate of comparable structures.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Plinth area is based on external wall dimensions at floor level.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: When is a Revised Estimate prepared for an engineering project under CPWD/PWD rules?
options: When the original sanctioned estimate is likely to be exceeded by more than 5% or expenditure exceeds administrative sanction by 10%
When minor alterations are made without cost impact
When a contractor leaves the site midway
bankQuestions.explanation: A revised estimate must be framed when the original sanctioned cost is exceeded by more than 5%, or when substantial material deviations from the approved design occur.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Revised estimate is required when cost exceeds original estimate by > 5% or expenditure exceeds administrative sanction by > 10%.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is an additional estimate framed to cover new works found necessary while an original project is under execution called?
bankQuestions.explanation: A supplementary estimate is prepared for additional works that were not included in the original sanctioned estimate but become necessary during project progress.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Supplementary estimate covers new extra work; Revised estimate updates an existing exceeded budget.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What percentage of the estimated capital cost of a building is typically provided for annual repairs and maintenance in PWD norms?
bankQuestions.explanation: Annual maintenance and repair estimates for public buildings are usually framed at 1.5% to 2% of the original capital construction cost.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Annual repair provision = 1.5% to 2% of capital cost.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the monetary deposit required from a contractor along with their tender submission as a guarantee of good faith called?
bankQuestions.explanation: Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) is an upfront deposit (usually 1% to 2% of estimated project value) submitted with the tender to show bona fide intent.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: EMD is 1% to 2% (returned to unsuccessful bidders); Security Deposit is 10% (kept until defects liability period ends).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the typical percentage of the contract value retained as Security Deposit (SD) to guarantee satisfactory completion of the work?
bankQuestions.explanation: Security Deposit is typically 10% of total contract value (or accumulated via deductions from running bills) to cover potential contractor defaults during construction and defects period.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Security deposit = 10% of total work cost.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In which contract system does the contractor agree to carry out each item of work at rates quoted in a bill of quantities?
bankQuestions.explanation: In an item rate contract (schedule contract), the contractor quotes individual rates for each item of work listed in the bill of quantities, paid based on actual measured quantities.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Item rate contract is the most widely adopted contract system in civil engineering departments.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In rate analysis of construction items, what percentage of the material and labour cost is normally included for contractor's profit?
bankQuestions.explanation: Standard PWD analysis of rates includes 10% on the net cost of materials and labour as contractor's profit.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Contractor's profit = 10%; Water charges = 1.5%; Overhead charges = 2.5% to 5%.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What percentage is added to civil engineering estimates to cover unforeseen contingencies?
bankQuestions.explanation: A provision of 3% to 5% of estimated cost is added to cover unforeseen expenditures and incidental site expenses termed contingencies.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Contingencies = 3% to 5%; Workcharged establishment = 1.5% to 2%.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the value of a dismantled building material at the end of its useful lifespan, less the cost of demolition and removal, called?
bankQuestions.explanation: Scrap value is the salvageable junk value of dismantled materials (such as scrap steel, old bricks, timber) after the useful life of the building is over, typically estimated at 10% of initial construction cost.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Scrap value is realized after dismantling (usually ~10%); Salvage value is realized without dismantling.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the value of a utility structure at the end of its utility period without being broken up or dismantled termed?
bankQuestions.explanation: Salvage value is the estimated value of an asset at the end of its useful working life when sold as a working unit without being dismantled.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Salvage = sold intact; Scrap = sold as demolished junk.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the original capital cost of an asset minus its accumulated depreciation up to that date called?
bankQuestions.explanation: Book value is the accounting value of a property recorded in ledger books, defined as original cost minus total depreciation to date.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Book value decreases every year; at the end of useful life, book value equals scrap value.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In valuation, what is Year's Purchase (YP) defined as for a property yielding net annual return at an interest rate 'i' (expressed as a fraction)?
bankQuestions.explanation: Year's Purchase (YP) is the capital sum required to be invested at a given interest rate 'i' to produce a net income of 1 Rupee per year, given by YP = 1 / i (or 100 / R where R is interest percentage).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: YP = 1 / i; Capitalized value = Net annual income * Year's Purchase.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: A property yields a net annual income of Rs. 12,000. If the prevailing rate of interest is 6%, what is its capitalized value?
bankQuestions.explanation: Capitalized value = Net Annual Income * Year's Purchase = 12,000 * (100 / 6) = 12,000 * 16.667 = Rs. 2,00,000.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Capitalized value = Net income / interest rate = 12,000 / 0.06 = Rs. 2,00,000.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In the straight-line method of depreciation, what is the annual depreciation formula for an asset with original cost C, scrap value S, and useful life n years?
bankQuestions.explanation: In the straight-line method, depreciation is assumed uniform throughout the life of the asset: Annual depreciation D = (C - S) / n.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Straight-line depreciation assigns equal wear-and-tear loss to each year.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is a fund created by setting aside periodic payments at compound interest so that the accumulated sum equals the cost of asset replacement at the end of its useful life called?
bankQuestions.explanation: A sinking fund is a fund accumulated over time by regular equal annual deposits earning compound interest, intended to replace the property or repay a loan when its useful life expires.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Annual sinking fund instalment: I = S * i / [ (1 + i)^n - 1 ].
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the right of a property owner to enjoy light, air, or passage across another person's adjoining land without obstruction called?
bankQuestions.explanation: An easement is a non-possessory legal right acquired by an owner over the adjoining land of another (such as right to light, air, support, or pathway).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Under the Indian Easements Act, uninterrupted continuous enjoyment for 20 years creates a prescriptive easement right.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What type of lease confers property tenure for a specified fixed duration of 99 years or more, after which possession reverts to the lessor?
bankQuestions.explanation: In a leasehold property, the lessee possesses the land for a specified period (e.g., 99 years) subject to payment of lease rent, with ownership returning to the freeholder upon expiry.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Freehold owner has absolute perpetual ownership; leaseholder holds property for a fixed lease term.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In rent fixation for government residential buildings, the standard rent is generally calculated as what percentage of the total capital cost of the building?
bankQuestions.explanation: Standard rent is typically fixed at 6% to 8% (sometimes up to 10% including municipal taxes and maintenance) of the total capital cost of the building and land.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Standard net return is typically assessed at 6% to 8% per annum on capital cost.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In an analysis of rates for brick masonry in 1:6 cement mortar, what volume of dry mortar is approximately required for 1 cubic metre of finished brickwork?
bankQuestions.explanation: For 1 m³ of brick masonry using standard modular bricks, approximately 0.25 to 0.30 m³ of dry mortar is required (typically taken as 0.30 m³ to account for wastage and frog filling).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Rule of thumb: 1 m³ brickwork requires ~500 modular bricks and ~0.30 m³ dry mortar.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: How many standard modular bricks of size 190 mm x 90 mm x 90 mm are required to construct 1 cubic metre of brick masonry?
bankQuestions.explanation: Nominal modular brick size with mortar joint is 200 mm x 100 mm x 100 mm = 0.2 m x 0.1 m x 0.1 m = 0.002 m³. Therefore, 1 / 0.002 = 500 bricks are required per cubic metre.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Standard modular brickwork: exactly 500 bricks per m³.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the standard weight of one bag of ordinary Portland cement (OPC) in India?
bankQuestions.explanation: In India, one commercial bag of cement contains exactly 50 kg of cement, with a loose volume of approximately 0.0347 m³ (34.7 litres or 35 litres).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 bag = 50 kg = 34.7 litres = 0.0347 m³. Density of cement = 1440 kg/m³.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the nominal density of ordinary Portland cement commonly adopted for material estimation?
bankQuestions.explanation: The standard nominal bulk density of ordinary Portland cement is taken as 1440 kg/m³ in Indian practice.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Density of cement = 1440 kg/m³; Steel = 7850 kg/m³; Water = 1000 kg/m³; Plain concrete = 2400 kg/m³; RCC = 2500 kg/m³.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the density of structural mild steel adopted in quantity surveying calculations?
bankQuestions.explanation: The density of structural steel and reinforcement bars is standardly taken as 7850 kg/m³ (78.5 kN/m³).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Weight of 1 m length of steel rebar = (d² / 162) kg.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the thickness of a standard one-brick wall constructed using traditional modular bricks (nominal size 200 mm x 100 mm x 100 mm)?
bankQuestions.explanation: Nominal modular brick size with mortar is 200 mm x 100 mm x 100 mm; thus, a one-brick thick wall has a nominal thickness of 200 mm (20 cm).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Half-brick wall = 10 cm; One-brick wall = 20 cm; One-and-a-half brick wall = 30 cm.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In an earthwork excavation estimate, what is the horizontal distance over which excavated soil is conveyed called?
bankQuestions.explanation: Lead is the horizontal distance over which excavated earth is moved from the excavation pit to the disposal site, standardly measured in units of 30 metres (or 50 m in modern codes).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Lead = Horizontal distance (standard 30 m or 50 m); Lift = Vertical height (standard 1.5 m).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In standard earthwork estimation schedules, what is the default initial lift specified for ordinary excavation?
bankQuestions.explanation: The standard initial lift included in ordinary earthwork rates without extra charge is 1.5 metres of vertical height.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Initial lead = 30 m (or 50 m); initial lift = 1.5 m.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the process of trimming, dressing, and compacting the excavated subgrade surface to true slope and level before laying road metal called?
bankQuestions.explanation: Subgrade preparation involves cutting, filling, camber shaping, and rolling the excavated earth foundation to the specified longitudinal grade and transverse profile.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Subgrade preparation ensures the foundation bed conforms to design level and compaction.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: In quantity surveying, what is a detailed list of all work items with descriptions, units, and quantities without rates called?
bankQuestions.explanation: A Bill of Quantities (BOQ) is a tender document containing item descriptions and calculated quantities prepared by the quantity surveyor for contractors to price.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: BOQ contains quantities for bidders to insert their rates; SOR is the departmental master schedule of standard rates.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the document containing standard approved labor, material, and machinery rates maintained by government engineering departments (like PWD) called?
bankQuestions.explanation: A Schedule of Rates (SOR or DSR for Delhi Schedule of Rates) is an official compilation of current standardized rates for various construction operations in a state or region.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: SOR / DSR is updated periodically to reflect changing market costs of material and labor.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records

bankQuestions.question: What is the small depression (usually 10 to 20 mm deep) molded on the top face of a clay brick called?
bankQuestions.explanation: The frog is an indentation on the top face of a brick that forms a key for mortar and displays the brick manufacturer's trademark.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Bricks are always laid with frog facing upward so that mortar fills the frog to form a shear key.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II / Land Records
